How to read this file — gold, silver & PGM

How to read a card

  • 2nd 3×? (the chip on each card): after a first 3× in years 1–5, is there room for another 3× by about year 10? Yes = a believable path (big or growing resource, several assets, growth paid from cash flow); partly = capped or dependent on the metal price; little = the first re-rating is most of the value. Judged per share at today's market value. It is not about cash: months of cash left are on the card's Financials tab (where it exists) and in the funding line. Full explanation on the rankings page under table B.
  • Financials (tab on the card, pilot on 39 companies so far): the last 8 quarters and 3 fiscal years read from the original financial statements on the company's own website (no data feed), simplified to the lines that matter — cash, burn, months of cash left, what went into the ground vs overhead, money raised and share count, and for producers revenue, margin and free cash flow. Every column links to the PDF it came from; every quarter is checked (opening cash + net flow = closing cash). The findings feed the runway and risk notes; there is no separate score.
  • Management (chip on each card, full review in the card's Management tab): the people graded A–D on track record (what they built, sold or ran before, misses included), fit (have they done this exact job: same stage, deposit type, region) and candour (a dated promises-vs-delivery log). A★ tier 1 · B solid, or unproven but clean — the default · C real weaknesses · D a pattern of failing shareholders. Neutral by default: the odds move only with evidence, full weight for explorers and developers, half for producers. A fourth score, skin in the game (1–5, in the Management tab), is the team's own money at risk — a conviction signal that never moves the odds but breaks near-ties in list B; a team that gets paid while shareholders lose scores 1. Reviewed 5 Oct 2026, refreshed every Saturday.
  • Bucket (the colour bar): the archetype — cheap defined ounces needs at least an Indicated resource plus a study; grade / discovery is drill-bit optionality, however cheap it screens; quality / jurisdiction is de-risked and priced for it; scale & financing is a big asset whose gate is the cheque; producer / cash flow holds names with revenue, anchored on EV/EBITDA, AISC margin and EV per M&I ounce instead of NPV/capex.
  • Gate: the one thing that has to go right. Differentiator: what the company has that peers don't. When those two are the same fact seen from two sides, that is usually the most honest thing to know about the name.
  • Funding & next catalyst (top of every card): cash, debt, burn, next dated event, and a verdict — funded / partly / not funded to that event — with the gap in money and months. The verdict is about the next catalyst, not the mine build.
  • Anchor: EV per ounce, stated by category (Inferred / Indicated / Reserve); for producers EV/EBITDA and margin. Always read against the confidence category — an Inferred ounce is not a cheap ounce, it is an unproven one.
  • Rule screen (Rick Rule's developer test): after-tax IRR ≥ 25–30% at a conservative price, NPV ≥ 2–3× capex, payback ≲ 3 years, 8–10% discount rate. Few names pass at their own deck; the Numbers tab shows where each one passes and where it doesn't. In gold it bites differently: most 2025–26 studies use decks far below spot and a 5% discount rate where the copper file sits at 8% — re-run NPV : capex at the study's downside case and haircut for the rate before comparing across the two tabs.
  • Risk 1–5: chance of permanent loss or no re-rate inside a 3–5 year horizon (1 lowest). Risk and ranking are deliberately separate — a 4 can top the multi-bagger list if the price pays for the risk.
  • Cost curve (producers only): where the company's all-in sustaining cost sits among the world's primary gold or silver mines, cheapest on the left. Lower half = cheaper than most of the world's output — the mines that keep earning when prices fall. The dot is 2026, the ring 2025; the Numbers tab shows the figure used and the method. Moving from the lower to the upper half with no proven fix is a sell trigger.
  • Metal badge beside the name (Au · Ag · Au·Ag · Mn) and the matching filter row: silver's share of revenue (producers) or of in-situ value at a stated ratio (developers) — never AgEq, which hides the split behind each company's own price ratio.
  • Shareholder structure is on every card but never scored: insider ownership is a tell, not a criterion. Shares bought with cash at market are a vote; options and RSUs are pay; settlement shares are a negotiation.
  • 💸 Pick: a personal flag with an event-driven entry plan on the card (Entry plan & Watch tab). Picks do not enter the rankings.
  • News tab and the file-level News section: the company's own releases for the current and previous month, linked to its site, with a grey note where a release changes the card.

Figures are mixed-date and sit on each study's own metal-price deck and discount rate — read anchors and NPV/capex as shapes, not decimal-precise rankings. Research shorthand, not investment advice. The rankings page uses the same scales.

Gold-specific gates to watch for

  • Nugget effect / grade continuity — visible-gold systems are hard to model; Inferred → Indicated conversion is the real test, not the headline intercept.
  • Capex re-baselining — any study dated 2021–23 resets materially; the reset, not the gold price, decides a developer's financing.
  • Metallurgy — refractory vs. free-milling decides capex and recovery; ask early.
  • By-product decks — AgEq/AuEq conversions vary wildly between companies; strip back to the primary metal before comparing.

Thesis

Agnico Eagle is the highest-quality senior gold producer: 11 mines, 3.45 Moz in 2025 (record) and 1.68 Moz in H1 2026, ~85% of Q2 2026 ounces from Canada (Detour Lake 24%, Canadian Malartic 16%, Meadowbank 12%, Meliadine 11%, LaRonde 9.5%, Macassa 9.4%) plus Kittila (Finland, 7%), Fosterville (Australia, 5%) and Pinos Altos (Mexico, 2%). Q2 2026 AISC US$1,459/oz (TCC US$1,054) against US$4,483 realised gave a ~73% EBITDA margin, record FCF of US$1.335B and record shareholder returns of US$625M; H1 FCF US$2.07B. 2026 guidance 3.3–3.5 Moz (low end after the 1 Jul Barnat wall failure, which also costs up to ~150 koz/yr in 2027–28), AISC US$1,400–1,550, capex raised to US$2.6–2.8B for Hope Bay (sanctioned 19 May 2026: US$2.4B, 435 koz/yr from 2030, IRR 19% at US$3,600). Balance sheet: net cash US$3.27B, US$197M debt, ~US$2B undrawn revolver, Fitch A-/Moody's A3. Reserves 55.4 Moz (+2%; ~16 yrs) plus 3.5 Moz at Ikkari after the ~C$3.4B Central Lapland consolidation (Rupert, Aurion, Fingold; closed Apr–Jun 2026). Returns: US$1.80/sh dividend (~1%), US$2B NCIB (US$550M bought in H1 at ~US$186), ≥40% of FCF paid out. Management: CEO Ammar Al-Joundi (since 2022), Executive Chair Sean Boyd (CEO 1998–2022), CFO Jamie Porter; three fatalities in 12 months triggered a global safety reset. Valuation US$93.0B / EV ~US$89.7B = 8.85× TTM EBITDA, 15.7× P/E, 4.9% FCF yield; consensus Buy (22 analysts), average target US$215.96 (+18%).

CEO & President Ammar Al-Joundi (CEO since 23 Feb 2022 after the Kirkland Lake merger; President 2015–22; Agnico CFO 2010–12; Barrick CFO 2012–15 after ~11 years at Barrick; FY2025 total compensation US$17.6M, mostly RSUs/PSUs). Executive Chair Sean Boyd (CEO 1998–2022; built Agnico from ~240 koz to 3.5 Moz; still a public face — the 29 Sep 2026 Mining Forum Americas presentation is attributed to him in Investing.com's transcript, which mislabels him 'CEO'). CFO Jamie Porter (since Apr 2023), COO Dominique Girard, EVP/COO Ontario Natasha Vaz. No CEO/CFO changes found in 2025–26; AGM 1 May 2026 re-elected the board. Track record: 11 mines built in ~20 years with in-house teams (Meliadine, Amaruq, Odyssey on schedule), Kirkland Lake MOE (2022) and Yamana's Canadian assets (2023, 100% of Malartic) integrated smoothly, debt cut by ~US$1B in 2025, production/share ~3× over 20 yrs (Boyd). Blemishes: three fatalities in 12 months (Fosterville Dec 2025, Canadian Malartic Apr 2026, Upper Beaver May 2026) → 'global safety reset'; Barnat wall failure in a known weak-structure zone; Hope Bay's Doris operation was suspended after the 2021 TMAC acquisition before this year's re-sanction (background from training knowledge, not re-verified). Guidance credibility high: 2025 guidance met; Q2 2026 beat budget.

The Gate

Turn a flat 3.3–3.5 Moz producer into ~4.5–5 Moz by 2031 without unit-cost drift — i.e. deliver the four-project build-out (Odyssey, Hope Bay, Detour UG, Upper Beaver; mgmt: '+1.5 Moz from 2030') on time and budget while AISC stays ~US$1,400–1,600/oz and ≥40% of FCF keeps going back to shareholders.

Production is flat at 3.3–3.5 Moz through 2028 and the Barnat wall failure takes up to ~150 koz a year out of 2027–28. The growth (+~1.5 Moz) arrives mostly from 2030, at the edge of a 3–5 year horizon. What the market pays ~9× EBITDA for is that delivery plus a ≥40% FCF payout.

  3. Hope Bay: US$2.4B initial capex held (2027 spend ~US$797M) through the 2027 sealift, first gold in 2030, design rate 2032.
  4. Costs: 2026 AISC inside US$1,400–1,550 (H1 US$1,471) and 2027 guidance not above ~US$1,600 despite 3–4% labour inflation, diesel and Finland's 2.5% royalty.
  5. Capital returns: H2 2026 payout keeps ≥40% of FCF (H1 ~48%) and net cash stays >US$2B through the Hope Bay peak.

Lower half and steady: ~36th in 2025 (US$1,339) → ~31st now, as peers inflated faster. AISC is still up ~14% year on year on gold-linked royalties, labour and diesel.

How to read it: picture every primary gold mine in the world lined up from cheapest to most expensive to run (all-in sustaining cost per ounce, weighted by output). The percentile is the share of world output that costs less; the middle line splits the cheaper half from the costlier half. Lower-half mines keep earning when the metal price falls. Dot = 2026, ring = 2025. Gold curve: Metals Focus / World Gold Council, Q1 2026 (average US$1,785/oz; the quartile lines are estimates). Approximate — it ranks the names, it is not decimal-precise.

Risk score1/5Permanent-loss risk is as low as it gets in gold equities: net cash US$3.27B, A-/A3 ratings, ~US$2B undrawn revolver, AISC ~US$1,460 vs ~US$4,160 spot (≈65% margin), 16-yr reserves across 11 mines with ~85% of output in Canada, and modelled FCF still positive (~US$1.3–1.6B) at US$3,000 gold — no single mine, country or financing event can impair the equity. Valuation modelColumns use 3.8 Moz by ~2030 × (0.95 × gold − US$1,000) × 8–10×.Volume: 3.3 Moz sold/yr (2026 low end, 2027–28 flat after Barnat; growth excluded from price columns). EBITDA cost per oz calibrated to actuals: (realised − adjusted EBITDA/oz sold) = US$1,206 in Q2 2026 (US$4,483 realised, US$2,738M on 835,505 oz) and US$1,232 in Q1 (US$4,861, US$3,011M on 829,651 oz) → modelled as US$1,000 + 5% of gold price (royalties/NTI scale with price). EBITDA = 3.3M × (0.95P − 1,000): P=3,000 → US$6.11B; 3,500 → 7.67B; 4,160 (spot) → 9.74B; 4,500 → 10.81B; 5,500 → 13.94B; 6,500 → 17.08B; 7,000 → 18.64B (model reproduces Q2 at US$2.72B vs actual US$2.74B). Sensitivity: every US$100/oz = ~US$314M EBITDA; a 10% gold move from spot (US$416) = ~US$1.30B ≈ 13.4% of EBITDA. Silver/by-products (~1.5% of revenue) ignored, so the Ag legs of the column labels are irrelevant. Market check: at spot the stock prices ~9.2× forward EBITDA (US$89.7B EV ÷ US$9.74B), i.e. it discounts spot gold at a below-history multiple. Growth case: 4.8 Moz × (0.95P − 1,100) → US$10.7B at US$3,500, US$13.7B at US$4,160, US$26.6B at US$7,000.

Valuation Anchor

~8.9× trailing EBITDA, ~15.7× earnings, ~4.9% FCF yield — the bottom of Agnico's own 8–10× range over five years, below Hecla (~13×) and level with Pan American (~9×), with a far stronger balance sheet than either. The usual Agnico premium is compressed, not stretched.

The case: gold holds around today's price, Barnat restarts in Q4, Odyssey's shaft starts in Q2 2027 and the Feb 2027 guidance (possibly five-year) shows the 2030–31 step to ~4.5–5 Moz. That is a compounding story worth ~1–1.25× in 3–5 years before the metal, plus ~1% dividend and ~1% buyback a year. The bear case is mark-to-market only: US$3,500 gold at 9× is ~0.8× today.

Bucket: producer / cash flow, the compounder end — the core holding for survivability, not for torque.

Jurisdiction risk

CANADA (~85% of Q2 2026 output). Federal: Boyd (29 Sep 2026) says the new federal government is 'more receptive' but approval delays/infrastructure bottlenecks persist and workforce availability is the biggest constraint. QUÉBEC (LaRonde, Canadian Malartic/Odyssey, Goldex; ~29% of Q2 output): Barnat pit-wall movement 1 Jul 2026 (no injuries, guidance cut); fatal accident at Canadian Malartic Apr 2026 with a 6-day mill stoppage; OR Royalties 3–5% NSR on Malartic/Odyssey, 5% on Barnat and East Gouldie. ONTARIO (Detour Lake, Macassa, Upper Beaver, Hammond Reef; ~34%): fatality at Upper Beaver early May 2026; Detour UG and Upper Beaver advancing on schedule. NUNAVUT (Meliadine, Meadowbank/Amaruq, Hope Bay; ~23%): Inuit-owned land under NTI lease — net-profits payment on Amaruq US$185–195M in 2026; diesel/sealift logistics (~70% of fuel bought ~30% over budget); first RAP progress report: C$346M direct Indigenous contributions 2024–25; Hope Bay (Kitikmeot) sanctioned May 2026 as Agnico's 4th Nunavut mine. FINLAND (Kittila, Ikkari, Fingold; ~7%): Parliament raised the mining royalty on metal ores from 0.6% to 2.5% of contained-metal value effective 1 Jan 2026 (approved Dec 2025) — a direct margin hit for Kittila and the Ikkari economics just acquired. AUSTRALIA — Victoria (Fosterville; ~5%): fatal accident Dec 2025; grade decline, mill upgrade to 3,300 tpd from 2028. MEXICO (Pinos Altos, Chihuahua ~2%; 50% San Nicolás, Zacatecas): special mining duty raised 7.5%→8.5% and extraordinary gold/silver duty 0.5%→1.0% (Congress, Nov 2024), plus the 2023 mining-law reform; yet San Nicolás obtained ETJ and MIA-R permits in Jul 2026 — evidence the Sheinbaum administration will still permit large projects. Net: lowest-risk jurisdictional mix among seniors; the live issues are operating (geotech, safety, Nunavut logistics) rather than political.

Differentiator

(1) Canadian scale nobody else has: ~85% of output from Québec/Ontario/Nunavut; Boyd says Agnico produces more gold in Canada than the next eight companies combined. (2) Two 100%-owned, 20+-year cornerstones each aiming at ~1 Moz/yr — Detour Lake (18.6 Moz reserves) and the Malartic/Odyssey complex (9.1 Moz) — something no other Western-hemisphere producer has. (3) First-half cost position with an A-rated, net-cash balance sheet (AISC US$1,459; Boyd: production costs ~US$300/oz below peer average; US$3.27B net cash). (4) A fully self-funded organic pipeline (+~1.5 Moz from 2030) and the industry's largest exploration budget (US$565–635M in 2026) with a record of adding ounces at ~US$10/oz. (5) Regional-cluster model (11 mines built in 20 years with in-house teams, standardised designs, ~50% lower staff turnover than peers). Counterweight: production is flat at 3.3–3.5 Moz through 2028 and Barnat removes up to ~150 koz/yr in 2027–28; capex is rising (US$2.6–2.8B + Hope Bay peak 2027) while AISC is up ~14–20% YoY; three fatalities in 12 months; short-life tails (Meadowbank, Pinos Altos) need replacing; Finland deal was paid at a 67% premium into a royalty hike; and at 8.9× EBITDA with ~13% EBITDA sensitivity per 10% gold, it offers far less torque than higher-cost peers — you buy it for compounding, not for leverage.

Targets: Detour UG conversion/west extension, East Gouldie lateral extensions, Patch 7 conversion, Macassa Main Break east to >2,000 m, Central Lapland (US$60–100M over 3 yrs). Junior equity portfolio as option book: Radisson (C$57.2M, 10.45%, Aug 2026), Cadillac Mines (Jul 2026), Wallbridge (May 2026), Canada Nickel (8.68%), Vizsla Copper (19.99%→~22%, pending), Cascadia, Maple Gold, Osisko Metals, Prism, Fuerte.

Context & updates
Central Lapland consolidation — Rupert, Aurion, Fingold (announced 20 Apr 2026; closed 22 Apr–16 Jun 2026)

Three deals worth ~C$3.4B: Rupert Resources (Ikkari) for 0.0401 AEM shares + CVRs up to C$3.00/sh (~C$2.87B fully diluted, 67% premium; ~8.5M AEM shares issued, closed 16 Jun), Aurion Resources for C$2.60 cash (~C$481M, 46% premium; closed 15 Jun) and B2Gold's 70% of the Fingold JV for US$325M cash (closed 22 Apr). Adds Ikkari's 3.5 Moz probable reserve 50 km from Kittila and a 2,492 km² land package; Agnico targets a ~500 koz/yr Finnish hub within a decade and up to US$500M synergies. Q2 cash outflow for acquisitions ~US$578M.

Hope Bay construction decision (19 May 2026)

US$2.4B initial capex (2026 US$428M, 2027 US$797M, 2028 US$591M, 2029 US$520M), 435 koz/yr at 6.50 g/t over 11 years (4.5 Moz), AISC ~US$1,200/oz; after-tax NPV5 US$2.7B/IRR 19% at US$3,600 and US$4.3B/26% at US$4,500; first gold 2030, design capacity 2032. 2026 capex guidance raised to US$2.6–2.8B as a result (29 Jul).

Barnat pit-wall movement at Canadian Malartic (1 Jul 2026)

~1 Mt rock-mass movement on the north wall, no injuries; mill fed from low-grade stockpiles; mining to resume Q4 2026 behind 15–25 m berms. Impact −60–80 koz in H2 2026 (2026 now at low end of 3.3–3.5 Moz) and up to −150 koz in each of 2027 and 2028 (~370 koz total); Malartic 2026 TCC guide ~US$1,260/oz. Stock −3.8% pre-market on 2 Jul; 52-wk low set in July.

Q2 2026 results — record FCF and record returns (29 Jul 2026)

855,816 oz at AISC US$1,459; adjusted EBITDA US$2.74B; FCF US$1.335B (record); net cash US$3.27B; US$625M returned (US$400M buyback at US$178.86 + US$0.45 dividend). Small miss vs consensus (adj. EPS US$3.07 vs US$3.10; revenue US$3.80B vs US$3.89B). Fitch upgrade to A- (Apr 2026). San Nicolás received ETJ and MIA-R permits (Jul 2026). Stock then rallied ~55% to US$224 by 25 Aug before fading with gold.

Safety reset after three fatalities (Dec 2025–May 2026)

Fatal accidents at Fosterville (Dec 2025), Canadian Malartic (Apr 2026, 6-day mill shutdown) and the Upper Beaver project (early May 2026). CEO Al-Joundi called three fatalities in a year 'not acceptable' (23 since 1960) and launched a global safety reset (critical-controls acceleration, supervisor training) — an execution/ESG watch-point during the heaviest build period in company history.

Red flags
  • Executive pay governance 2021-23 (24% say-on-pay, merger bonuses opposed by ISS and Glass Lewis).
  • Malartic 370koz loss shows geotechnical risk at the flagship; 2026 now 'lower end' of range.
  • Regulatory friction in Nunavut (Meliadine extension withdrawn; caribou violations).

What the numbers say
  1. Cash rose from US$977M in September 2024 to US$3,464M in June 2026 and debt fell to US$197M, giving net cash of US$3.3B plus an undrawn US$2B facility.
  2. Capex is accelerating: additions to PP&E went from about US$500M a quarter in 2024 to US$801M in Q2 2026, with 2026 guidance of US$2.6–2.8B.
  3. Share count is about 500M; 9M new shares were issued in June 2026 for Rupert Resources, and buybacks reached US$400M in Q2 2026 with the dividend at US$0.45 a quarter.
  4. Revenue rose from US$2,155.6M in Q3 2024 to US$3,802.8M in Q2 2026 on gold price alone; production was flat and AISC drifted up to US$1,459–1,517/oz.
  5. FY2025 operating cash flow was US$6.8B and free cash flow US$4.4B; net income of US$4.46B includes a US$229M impairment reversal and a US$224M derivative gain.

Thesis

Wheaton is the largest pure precious-metals streamer (99% PM revenue): 47 streams/royalties with 38 partners in 19 countries, anchored by Salobo (Vale, Brazil; 75% of Au at US$433/oz; 34% of Q2 2026 revenue, 45% of FY2025), Peñasquito (Newmont, Mexico; 25% of Ag at US$4.62; 21%), Antamina (Peru; 67.5% of the mine's silver after the US$4.3B BHP stream closed 1 Apr 2026; 16%) and Constancia (Hudbay; 5%). It produced 691,670 GEOs in 2025 (beat 600–670k guidance; ~804k at 2026 prices), guides 860–940k GEOs for 2026 (H1 414,755) and ~1.2M by 2030 with no new capital required. Cash costs are mostly contractual — US$568/GEO in Q2 2026 vs a ~US$4,440 realized GEO price (~87% margin) — so H1 2026 revenue was US$1.83B (+88%), net earnings US$1.13B and OCF US$1.42B; annualized EBITDA ~US$3.1B. The Antamina deal turned ~US$1.15B net cash into US$1.87B net debt (~0.6x EBITDA; US$1.5B 2-yr term loan + US$2.5B revolver to 2031) with US$2.6B liquidity and a return to net cash targeted within a year; Canada's 15% global minimum tax now costs real cash (US$109M paid Jun 2026, C$346M due Mar 2027). Dividend US$0.195/qtr (+18%, 0.57% yield), no buyback. New CEO Haytham Hodaly (since 31 Mar 2026; ran corporate development since 2012) with co-founder Randy Smallwood as chair and CFO Vincent Lau (since 2025). At US$136.28 (US$61.9B cap, EV ~US$63.8B) it trades at 23.9x TTM EV/EBITDA and 23.7x forward P/E — the low end of its 22–30x 5-yr range; consensus PT US$166–178 (11 Buy/1 Hold per MarketBeat).

CEO & President Haytham Hodaly since 31 Mar 2026 (announced 5 Feb 2026; joined 2012 as SVP Corporate Development, President 2025; mining engineer, ex-RBC mining analyst; led >US$11B of streaming deals and the US$4.3B BHP Antamina deal; board since May 2026). Randy Smallwood (co-founder 2004, CEO 2011–Mar 2026) became non-executive Chair; George Brack moved from Chair to Lead Independent Director. CFO Vincent Lau (appointed Jan 2025, succeeded Gary Brown). Other execs on the Q2 2026 call: Wes Carson (VP Mining Operations), Neil Burns (VP Corporate Development), Emma Murray (VP IR). Track record: beat 2025 guidance (691,670 GEOs vs 600–670k), five-plus straight record quarters (Edison), dividend +18% for 2026, claimed ~20% 20-yr average IRR and ~20% 2026 ROIC; the Antamina deal (5-yr process) is the biggest capital-allocation test of the new team.

The Gate

Deliver the ~1.2M GEO 2030 profile (+~33% vs the 900k 2026 midpoint) on time while Salobo and Antamina hold up — the multiple (~21–24x EBITDA) already prices in that growth.

At ~21–24× EBITDA the market already pays for the 1.2M GEO profile. Returns from here come from delivering it on time, metal prices and reinvesting ~US$2.5B a year at the ~20% returns Wheaton has historically earned — the Antamina price is the first test of the new CEO.

Sub-gates
  1. The Q4 2026 ramp group hits its dates: Blackwater Phase 1A commissioning (6→8 Mtpa), Platreef and Fenix commercial production, Koné ramp after first gold on 27 Sep 2026 (hard-rock circuit Q2 2027), Kurmuk first gold (Oct 2026).
  2. 2026 lands within 860–940k GEOs (H1 414,755 = 46% of midpoint, so H2 needs ~485k) and the Feb 2027 guidance steps up toward ~1.0–1.1M GEOs (Edison 2027E 1,075k).
  3. Salobo: Q3 2026 grade recovery, CPF start-up H1 2028, no Vale disruption — Salobo goes from ~34% of revenue now to ~27% of production by 2030.
  4. Deleveraging: net debt US$1.87B (Jun 2026) back to net cash within ~12 months (Investor Day) despite the C$346M GMT (Mar 2027) and Spring Valley/Jervois installments, while new deals stay at historical ~20% IRRs rather than Antamina-style low-teens-or-below returns.
  5. Antamina delivers ~12 Moz/yr combined over the first 5 years and the JV advances permits beyond 2036.

Valuation modelColumns use the 2030 volume (~1.2M GEOs) × a 20–25× royalty multiple.Own estimate on 2026 guidance volumes (415 koz Au, 28 Moz Ag, ~20k GEOs other): gold margin = 415k oz x Au – fixed payments ~US$147M (Salobo ~260 koz x US$433, Sudbury x US$400, Constancia x US$429, San Dimas x US$643, Stillwater x US$570) – ~24% of spot on ~88 koz (Blackwater 35%, Hemlo/Koné/Fenix 20%, Kurmuk 15%) → 393.9k x Au – US$147M. Silver margin = 28 Moz x Ag – 20% of spot on ~10 Moz Antamina – 18% on ~0.8 Moz (Blackwater/Mineral Park) – fixed ~US$74M (Peñasquito US$4.62, Constancia US$6.32, Zinkgruvan/Neves-Corvo ~US$4.6, Aljustrel US$0) → 25.86M x Ag – US$74M. Other-metals margin ~+US$75M, cash G&A ~–US$80M (estimate). EBITDA ≈ 393.9k·Au + 25.86M·Ag – US$226M → spot US$4,160/US$60.7 = US$2.98B (EV US$63.8B / 2.98 = 21.4x; implied cash cost ~US$540/GEO vs US$568 actual Q2). Sensitivity: +10% gold = +US$164M (+5.5%); +10% silver = +US$157M (+5.3%); both = +10.8% (Edison: +10% Ag → +6.7% EPS, both → +13.7% EPS). Check: the company's annualized H1 2026 EBITDA was US$3.1B on lower H1 sales volumes at higher prices (Q2 Au US$4,452 / Ag US$73.41). 2030 case: +300k GEOs (60:1), ~70% gold, at a ~78% margin (mostly %-of-spot streams). Ratio = re-rated EV ÷ US$61.9B market cap (subtracting ~US$1.9B net debt lowers each by ~0.03x). Multiples would likely compress at the high price decks, so the top columns are generous.
Valuation Anchor

~23.9× trailing EBITDA (~21× forward at spot), ~30× earnings, ~4–4.6% pre-acquisition cash-flow yield — the low end of Wheaton's own 22–30× range, two to three times the producers on this page. You pay for contractual costs, no capex and growth that is already built.

The case: the Q4 2026 commissioning group (Blackwater 1A, Platreef, Fenix, Kurmuk, Koné) lands on time, 2027 guidance steps toward ~1.0–1.1M GEOs and net cash returns by ~2027. That compounds to ~1.25–1.55× at today's prices by 2030. The risk is the multiple, not solvency: 18–20× at US$3,500 gold is ~0.6–0.8× today.

Read: A widely held, index- and ETF-heavy large cap where management owns very little and insider trading is only routine option monetisation — insider activity tells you nothing about direction. The register is the strength here: Capital Group, Fidelity, First Eagle and VanEck are long-term holders who pay up for quality, and that is why the shares trade at a premium multiple. The risk is the flip side: if the growth story or metal prices disappoint, the same quality-focused holders can de-rate it together, as the ~17% drop from the late-Aug high shows.

Jurisdiction risk

BRAZIL (Salobo, ~34% of Q2 revenue; ~27% of 2026–30E per deck): federal mining regime stable; Vale Base Metals (Vale with Manara/Engine No.1 minority) approved the CPF expansion 12 Aug 2026; general election first round 4 Oct 2026 (constitutional calendar) — no specific mining-tax threat found. PERU (Antamina + Constancia, ~21% of Q2 revenue; 23% of 2026–30E): 7 Jun 2026 runoff won by Keiko Fujimori (pro-investor) by ~35,000 votes over leftist Roberto Sánchez, who had proposed phasing out open-pit mining, higher mining taxes and reviewing tax stability agreements (Mining.com 12 May 2026; Atlantic Council) — tail risk reduced but the country remains divided; local layer: Áncash/Cusco community and corridor blockades (Constancia/Las Bambas corridor) are recurring. MEXICO (Peñasquito, San Dimas, Cozamin, Los Filos; ~25% of Q2 revenue, 13% of 2026–30E): 2023 mining law reform (shorter concessions, open-pit restrictions) affects new projects more than existing streams; local labour risk (Peñasquito 4-month strike in 2023). CANADA (Blackwater BC, Sudbury/Hemlo Ontario, Voisey's Bay NL, Goose Nunavut; ~10%): stable mines; Wheaton is subject to Canada's 15% global minimum tax from 2024 (C$155M paid Jun 2026; C$346M due Mar 2027). EUROPE (Zinkgruvan Sweden, Neves-Corvo/Aljustrel Portugal; ~9%): stable. Development exposure: Côte d'Ivoire (Koné), Ethiopia (Kurmuk, Benishangul-Gumuz), South Africa (Platreef), Chile (Fenix, Santo Domingo), Ecuador (El Domo), USA (Spring Valley NV, Copper World and Mineral Park AZ, Stillwater MT), Australia (Jervois NT), Japan (Cipango royalty).

Differentiator

1) Most silver-levered large streamer — ~50% of revenue from silver (Franco-Nevada and Royal Gold are mostly gold plus energy/base-metal royalties), 99% PM revenue vs 85% (FNV) and 89% (RGLD) per company deck. 2) Fixed, low per-ounce costs on legacy streams (Salobo US$433, Sudbury US$400, Constancia US$429/US$6.32, Peñasquito US$4.62, Zinkgruvan US$4.81, Aljustrel US$0) → ~87% cash margin, no exposure to capex or operating-cost inflation. 3) Tier-1, long-life anchors run by majors — Salobo (40–50-yr life, CPF expansion), Antamina (two-thirds of silver, BHP/Glencore), Peñasquito (Newmont). 4) Organic growth already paid for: ~50% to 1.2M GEOs by 2030, 9 development assets (6 in construction, Koné pouring), management calls it conservative. 5) Very lean (48 staff) with a claimed ~20% 20-yr average portfolio IRR. Counterweight: priced as a compounder (~21–24x EBITDA, 30x TTM P/E); now levered (0.6x) after paying US$4.3B for Antamina at what one third-party model puts at a single-digit IRR below ~US$100 silver; Vale/Salobo concentration; 15% minimum tax is permanent; new GEOs come mostly from %-of-spot streams (20–35% of spot), so incremental margins are below the legacy book; and with 20–25 deals under review plus ~US$250M/month of capacity, there is pressure to keep deploying capital.

Exploration upside

Free optionality on partners' drilling · moves the needle: low. Wheaton has no exploration budget of its own; reserve growth comes from operators' drilling at no cost to Wheaton (e.g., Antamina ~95% reserve replenishment, Salobo 40–50-yr life, Koné higher-grade upside per CEO 29 Sep 2026). Exploration upside works as free optionality on extensions (Salobo CPF/'Salobo IV', Blackwater EP2 + Vista Gold royalty/ROFR, Antamina beyond 2036), not as a share-price driver.

Open Questions
  • What is the exact remaining upfront-commitment schedule (Spring Valley, Jervois, Copper World, Santo Domingo, El Domo, Kurmuk, Toroparu, Cotabambas, Salobo CPF) by year, and does it still allow net cash by ~Q3 2027 at ~US$4,160/US$60 rather than the deck's US$4,350/US$65?
  • What return does the US$4.3B BHP Antamina stream earn at today's ~US$60 silver if mine life stays limited to 2036 by tailings, and when will the JV file permits for an extension?
  • Is the 15% Canadian global minimum tax fully in consensus, and could the June 2025 G7 'side-by-side' arrangement or Canadian policy changes alter Wheaton's GMT exposure?
  • How fast does Salobo's grade recover from Q3 2026, and what attributable output does the CPF expansion (+6 Mtpa, H1 2028) actually add (~15 koz/yr on a 100% basis)?
  • With 20–25 opportunities under review and ~US$250M/month of new capacity, what hurdle rate will the new CEO accept, and will he use buybacks if streaming returns fall?
  • How big is the produced-not-delivered build (H1 production 414,755 vs sales 390,859 GEOs) and when does it turn into revenue?
Context & updates
BHP Antamina silver stream — US$4.3B, largest deal in company history (announced 16 Feb 2026, closed 1 Apr 2026)

33.75% of payable silver until 100 Moz, then 22.5% LOM, at 20% of spot; with the Glencore stream Wheaton now owns 67.5% of Antamina's silver (~12 Moz/yr first 5 yrs). Funded with ~US$1.9B cash + US$1.5B 2-yr term loan + ~US$0.9B revolver; added ~70k GEOs to 2026 and 66 Moz Ag P&P. Antamina went from 10% (FY2025) to 16% (Q2 2026) of revenue and the balance sheet went from net cash to US$1.87B net debt.

CEO succession: Hodaly in, Smallwood to chair (announced 5 Feb 2026, effective 31 Mar 2026)

President Haytham Hodaly (deal architect since 2012) became CEO; co-founder Randy Smallwood moved to non-executive Chair; George Brack became Lead Independent Director. CFO Vincent Lau has been in the role since 2025. Continuity, but the new team owns the Antamina returns.

2025 beat, 2026 guidance and 1.2M GEO 2030 outlook (16 Feb / 12 Mar 2026)

2025: 691,670 GEOs (vs 600–670k), revenue US$2.31B, OCF US$1.90B, cash cost US$514/GEO. 2026: 860–940k GEOs at US$4,800/US$80; 2030 ~1.2M GEOs, flat through 2035. Dividend +18% to US$0.195/qtr.

Record H1 2026, revolver upsized, first minimum-tax payment (6 Aug 2026)

H1 revenue US$1.83B (+88%), net earnings US$1.13B, OCF US$1.42B; Q2 cash cost US$568/GEO. Revolver raised to US$2.5B and extended to Jun 2031 (+US$0.5B accordion) → US$2.6B liquidity; first global minimum tax payment US$109M; guidance unchanged, H2-weighted.

Investor Day, Salobo CPF approval and Koné first gold (12 Aug – 29 Sep 2026)

Vale approved the Salobo CPF expansion (12 Aug; Wheaton US$40M). At Investor Day (16 Sep) and Mining Forum Americas (29 Sep) management reiterated the 1.2M GEO 2030 target as conservative, with 20–25 deals under review and US$2.6B capacity growing ~US$250M/month. Montage poured first gold at Koné 27 Sep, ahead of schedule. Meanwhile the shares fell ~17% from US$163.72 (25 Aug) to US$136.28 (2 Oct) as gold and silver pulled back.

Management review
A★tier 1 — proven at this job, candid, investedTrack record 4/5 · Fit 5/5 · Candour 4/5 · Skin in the game 2/5

Beat guidance three years running and no write-offs; took on US$1.9B of net debt for Antamina in April 2026 (first leverage in years); the CEO changed in March 2026 and the growth plan depends on other operators' builds, so no odds move.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Haytham Hodaly (President & CEO, since CEO 31 March 2026 (President before; SVP Corporate Development from 2012 — date unverified)): Deal-maker behind the 2023-26 stream portfolio; first year as CEO. · Randy Smallwood (Non-Executive Chair, since Chair 31 March 2026; co-founder of Silver Wheaton 2004; CEO 2011-2026): George Brack moved from Chair to Lead Independent Director. · Vincent Lau (SVP & CFO, since January 2025): Succeeded Gary Brown (CFO 2008–2024).
Track record
  • 2025: ~692k GEOs vs 600-670k guidance (beat top end); gold 416koz vs 350-390koz guidesource
  • 2024: exceeded guidance (release headline 'Exceeds 2024 Production Guidance')source
  • 2022: guidance was revised down mid-year and the year closed at 638k GEOs, below the revised 640-680k floor, on Salobo throughput and Stillwater flooding; headlined as 'solid'source
  • 2026 guidance 860-940k GEOs (+11%) with additional Antamina silver stream from 1 Apr 2026; 1.2M GEOs by 2030 (same 2026 outlook release)
  • Capital allocation: serial new streams (Blackwater, Goose, Mineral Park, Fenix, Platreef, Antamina add-on) funded from cash flow, no net debt; record Q2 2026 revenuesource
  • Smallwood's wins span 2011-26; the 2022 miss and the Salobo expansion delays (2020-23) are the main soft spots; no write-offs on the scale of Franco-Nevada's Panama (Wheaton's Cobre Panama stream is small — unverified).

Boards today: Hodaly: Wheaton only (unverified). Smallwood: Wheaton chair; other boards unverified (he chaired the World Gold Council in the past).

Fit to this job
Same job: financing and administering streams on third-party mines, which this team has done for 20 years. New for them: Hodaly's first year as CEO; a growth plan to 1.2M GEOs that depends on development-stage mines run by others (Goose, Blackwater, Platreef, Mineral Park) coming in on time.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake from grants or cheap founder paper; little buying. Smallwood 2025 total pay +6% y/y, ~80% at risk (absolute figure not in the excerpt fetched; prior years ~C$9-10M — unverified). Share counts for Smallwood/Hodaly not fetched. Say-on-pay 2026 vote pending at May 2026 meeting in circular; result unverified. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1323404/000110465926038311/wpm-20260401xex99d2.htm

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • CEO transition in March 2026 — Hodaly is unproven as CEO.
  • Growth outlook relies on other companies' construction schedules; long-term targets have historically slid a year.
  • 2022 guidance was cut and then narrowly missed.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash fell from $2.16B at 31 March 2026 to $100M at 30 June 2026 after the $4.3B Antamina silver stream, funded with $1.97B of new bank debt.
  2. Stream payments were $1.34B in FY2025 and G&A only about $47M a year, around 2% of revenue; there is no exploration spend.
  3. Share count is flat at about 454M with no equity issued; dividends grew from $265M in FY2023 to $296M in FY2025 and the quarterly rate rose to $0.195 a share.
  4. Quarterly sales rose from $308M in Q3 2024 to $929M in Q2 2026; cash operating margin is about 87% of sales and H1 2026 net earnings were $1,125M.
  5. Operating cash flow was $1.90B in FY2025 and $1.42B in H1 2026, enough to repay the term loan within a year; Q2 2026 cash taxes jumped to $109M.

The largest, most diversified gold royalty company — debt-free, ~91% margins, US$4.3B to deploy — with Cobre Panamá as a free option and two top-4 streams stepping down in 2027–28

Gate The ONE thing: grow per-share GEOs through the 2027–28 stream step-downs (Candelaria 68%→40% in 2027, Antapaccay →30% in H2 2028) to the 555–615k 2030 outlook — with a Cobre Panamá agreement that keeps FNV's stream intact as the swing factor. Sub-gates: (1) 2026 delivery: upper half of 510–570k GEOs — needs ≥286k GEOs in H2 after 268,758 in H1; check Q3 results 11 Nov 2026 and FY2026 ~Mar 2027. (2) Panama: GOP opens formal negotiations with First Quantum (commission 30 Sep 2026) and signs an operate-to-closure framework by end-2027 without cutting the stream; stockpile delivers ~23.1k oz Au + 265k oz Ag (1/3 H2 2026); full restart adds 150–175k GEOs/yr. (3) Capital deployment: put ≥US$1B/yr of the US$4.3B to work at returns above FNV's cost of capital without paying peak-gold prices — first markers: Bullabulling FID early 2027, Côté buy-back decision by ~mid-2027 (≥US$262.5M per 25% tranche returning cash). (4) Organic pipeline on time: Eskay Creek Q2 2027, Cascabel 2028, Coroccohuayco decision 2026 → first ore 2028, Magino 20 ktpd early 2028, Detour 1 Moz/yr 2031. (5) No further sovereign hits beyond Karma (Burkina court 'nullification', Jun 2026; already zero book value).

The 'gap' is a deployment gap, not a funding gap — US$4.3B idle capital earning cash rates dilutes returns unless deployed at acceptable IRRs.
Thesis

Franco-Nevada is the largest and most diversified gold royalty/streaming company: 435 assets (119–121 producing) with no asset >12% of 2026 revenue; top H1 2026 contributors Antamina silver stream (11.3% of revenue), Candelaria (11.1%), Guadalupe-Palmarejo (8.0%), Antapaccay (7.8%), Western Limb (3.8%), Tocantinzinho (3.7%), Côté 7.5% GMR (3.3%) and Detour 2% NSR (3.0%), plus ~10.5% from U.S./Canadian energy royalties. 2025: 519,106 GEOs, revenue US$1.82B, adjusted EBITDA US$1.66B (90.9%). 2026 guide 510–570k GEOs (tracking upper half incl. Cobre stockpile ounces); H1 2026 268,758 GEOs, revenue US$1.23B (+67%), adj. EBITDA US$1.12B (91.1%), OCF US$1.0B; cash costs US$344/GEO (~92.5% cash margin). 2030 outlook 555–615k GEOs ex-Cobre, whose restart would add 150–175k GEOs/yr and is carried at nil. Debt-free with US$1.01B cash, US$1.04B investments and US$4.3B available capital; dividend US$0.44/qtr (19 straight annual increases, 0.74% yield); no buyback. Deployed ~US$2.3B in 2025 (Côté US$1.05B, Western Limb US$500M, Porcupine, Arthur) and ~US$0.68B in 2026 YTD (i-80, Orezone/Casa Berardi, Bullabulling ×2). CEO Paul Brink (since 2020; WGC Chair from Sep 2026), CFO Sandip Rana, Chair Tom Albanese (May 2026); 44 employees; 17–18% compound annual returns since the 2007 IPO. At US$239.30 (US$46.2B cap) it trades ~21–22× EBITDA, ~31× TTM P/E, ~3.9% OCF yield; 15 analysts: 8 Strong Buy / 4 Buy / 3 Hold, mean target US$286.97; BMO put P/NAV at ~1.8× in Jan 2026.

Paul Brink — President & CEO since 2020 (President since 2018 per MarketScreener; age 58); appointed Chair of the World Gold Council 28 Sep 2026 while remaining CEO. Sandip Rana — CFO (MarketScreener: since 2010). Eaun Gray — Chief Investment Officer (since 2025). Lloyd Hong — GC & Corporate Secretary; Christian Thatcher — General Counsel; Darrol van Deventer — VP Mining (QP). Board: Tom Albanese (ex-CEO Rio Tinto, Vedanta) became independent non-executive Chair at the 12–13 May 2026 AGM; founder David Harquail (CEO 2007 IPO–2020, then Chair) became Chair Emeritus; co-founder Pierre Lassonde remains a director. Changes 2025–26: CIO appointment (2025), chair succession (announced 26 Jan 2026), director appointment (8 Jan 2025). Track record: 17% compounded annual shareholder return since the 2007 IPO (2026 handbook; ~18% per Sep 2026 presentation summary), GEOs 3× and revenue 12× since 2008, 19 consecutive dividend increases; misses: Cobre Panamá (US$1.17B impairment 2023) and Karma (zero book). Lean: 44 full-time employees.

The Gate

The ONE thing: grow per-share GEOs through the 2027–28 stream step-downs (Candelaria 68%→40% in 2027, Antapaccay →30% in H2 2028) to the 555–615k 2030 outlook — with a Cobre Panamá agreement that keeps FNV's stream intact as the swing factor.

EBITDA moves roughly one-for-one with gold and organic growth to 2030 is only ~8%, so per-share growth depends on deploying US$4.3B well and on Panama. The 30 Sep commission report opened a path to negotiation but frames Cobre as an orderly closure that must end all arbitrations.

Sub-gates
  1. 2026 delivery: upper half of 510–570k GEOs — needs ≥286k GEOs in H2 after 268,758 in H1; check Q3 results 11 Nov 2026 and FY2026 ~Mar 2027.
  2. Panama: GOP opens formal negotiations with First Quantum (commission 30 Sep 2026) and signs an operate-to-closure framework by end-2027 without cutting the stream; stockpile delivers ~23.1k oz Au + 265k oz Ag (1/3 H2 2026); full restart adds 150–175k GEOs/yr.
  3. Capital deployment: put ≥US$1B/yr of the US$4.3B to work at returns above FNV's cost of capital without paying peak-gold prices — first markers: Bullabulling FID early 2027, Côté buy-back decision by ~mid-2027 (≥US$262.5M per 25% tranche returning cash).
  4. Organic pipeline on time: Eskay Creek Q2 2027, Cascabel 2028, Coroccohuayco decision 2026 → first ore 2028, Magino 20 ktpd early 2028, Detour 1 Moz/yr 2031.
  5. No further sovereign hits beyond Karma (Burkina court 'nullification', Jun 2026; already zero book value).

Risk score2/5Permanent loss is limited by a debt-free balance sheet, US$4.3B of available capital, ~91% EBITDA margins with no cost or capex exposure, and 121 cash-flowing assets where the largest is ~11% of revenue — even at US$3,000 gold FNV would still generate ~US$1.3B OCF (~2.8% yield) and never need equity. It is not a 1 because the risk here is valuation, not solvency: at ~22× EBITDA and ~31× earnings the stock already discounts growth and a premium multiple, and two top-4 assets step down in 2027–28. The loss path: gold reverts to ~US$3,000–3,500 while the market compresses royalty multiples toward ~15–18× (as in 2022–23), Cobre talks stall into an arbitration-free closure that excludes the stream, and capital deployed at 2025–26 prices (Côté US$1.05B, i-80, Bullabulling) earns sub-par returns — EBITDA ~US$1.5–1.75B × 15–18× ≈ US$23–31B, i.e. a 35–50% drawdown that would take years to recover but not a wipe-out.

Valuation Anchor

~21.6× trailing EBITDA, ~31× earnings, ~3.7–3.9% pre-acquisition cash-flow yield — the low end of Franco-Nevada's own 21–26× history and of the 20–30× royalty band, two to three times the producers here. You pay for zero debt, 435 assets and no cost or capex exposure.

The case: 2026 lands in the upper half, the US$4.3B is deployed at sensible returns and Panama signs a framework that keeps the stream — Cobre adds ~30% to GEOs. That is ~1.2–1.5× at today's prices. Without Cobre it is a gold-price compounder with ~8% organic growth. The downside is multiple compression, as in 2022–23: 15–18× at US$3,500 gold would be a 35–50% drawdown.

Bucket: royalty & streaming — the defensive core of a gold book.

Jurisdiction risk

Revenue by region Q2 2026: 88% Americas — South America 40%, Canada 25%, U.S. 16%, Central America & Mexico 7%; rest of world ~12% (South Africa, Australia, Burkina Faso). PANAMA (Cobre): Supreme Court struck down the concession law Nov 2023 → P&SM; Law 407 (2023) bars new mining concessions; FNV impaired US$1,169.2M (2023) to nil; FNV ICSID claim under Canada–Panama FTA (~US$5B, filed 27 Jun 2024) suspended 18 Jun 2025; FQM discontinued ICC and suspended FTA arbitration (31 Mar 2025); stockpile processing approved 7 Apr 2026; SGS integral audit 87.7% compliance published 19 Jun 2026; ministerial commission (30 Sep 2026) recommends negotiating a new agreement ending ≥US$27B of claims, with orderly closure and no extension — President Mulino adopted six criteria, no timeline. BURKINA FASO (Karma stream): local court purported to nullify the stream (Riverstone Karma release, 16–18 Jun 2026); FNV contests under Ontario law; zero book value. PERU (Antamina, Antapaccay, Yanacocha, Condestable — largest country exposure): operator-level permitting (Coroccohuayco decision 2026); national political volatility (2026 election cycle — outcome not verified). CHILE (Candelaria, Salares Norte): stable; 2023 copper royalty law applies to operators. MEXICO (Guadalupe-Palmarejo): 2023 mining-law reform tightened concessions/water (background). BRAZIL (Tocantinzinho, Pará). CANADA/USA (Côté, Detour, Hemlo, Porcupine, Valentine, Greenstone, Nevada royalties, energy): top-tier; CRA transfer-pricing disputes settled 11 Sep 2025. SOUTH AFRICA (Western Limb, Sibanye). ECUADOR (Cascabel, Jiangxi Copper-controlled since Mar 2026).

Differentiator

(1) Scale + diversification no peer matches: 435 assets/121 cash-flowing, 88% Americas revenue, no asset >12% — single-asset shocks (Cobre 2023, Karma 2026) dented but did not break the model. (2) ~91% adjusted EBITDA margin with zero operating/capex exposure — cost inflation that squeezes producers barely touches FNV (cash cost/GEO US$344). (3) Fortress balance sheet — zero debt, US$4.3B available capital, 44 employees — lets it write US$1B cheques (Côté) and package streams+equity+debt for juniors (Porcupine, Bullabulling, Orezone). (4) Free options: Cobre Panamá at nil book (+150–175k GEOs/yr if restarted), ~222k GEOs/yr of long-dated optional assets (Conga, Pascua-Lama, New Prosperity, Ring of Fire), and 275 exploration royalties. (5) Energy royalties (~10%) diversify away from pure gold beta. Counterweight: you pay for it — ~22× EBITDA and ~31× earnings for ~9% EBITDA growth per 10% gold move (no operating leverage), the 2027–28 Candelaria/Antapaccay step-downs hollow out two top-4 assets, US$4.3B of idle capital is being deployed near record gold prices (2026 deals skew to development-stage juniors: i-80, Bullabulling, Orezone), and the stock has de-rated from 26 Feb 2026 highs despite record results.

Exploration upside

Operators drill on its ground at no cost · moves the needle: low. FNV spends nothing on exploration itself; upside comes from operators drilling on its ground (275 exploration + 41 advanced assets at 10 Mar 2026). 2026 positives: Hemlo resource increase (Jun 2026) and 130,000 m program; Musselwhite stacked extension zones (mine-life extension); Porcupine (19 rigs; Kidd acquisition could double Timmins output to ~500 koz/yr); Detour underground ramp at 180 m; Valentine Phase 2 FS (4.5 Mtpa); Antapaccay trend extension 1.6 km; Bullabulling resource growth to 4.4 Moz Ind + 1.7 Moz Inf (Jul 2026). ~222k GEOs/yr of 'optional' assets beyond the 5-yr outlook (New Prosperity, Conga, Pascua-Lama, Ring of Fire). Needle is low because no single discovery moves a 550k-GEO portfolio by >2–3%.

Open Questions
  • Does a Panama 'operate-to-orderly-closure' agreement — which must terminate all arbitrations, including FNV's suspended ~US$5B ICSID claim — preserve the stream on existing terms, and over what life (the commission's 25-yr 'illustrative example')? Management said on 12 Aug 2026 there were no negotiations on stream modifications.
  • How much of the 2027 Candelaria (68%→40%) and H2 2028 Antapaccay (→30%) step-downs is offset by Côté, Detour, Porcupine, Valentine, Eskay Creek and Cascabel — i.e. what are 2027–28 GEOs before Cobre?
  • Can US$4.3B be deployed at acceptable returns with gold ~US$4,160 (below FNV's US$4,500 guidance deck) — and does the 2026 tilt toward development-stage juniors (i-80 US$250M, Bullabulling A$420M, Orezone US$100M) signal reaching for growth?
  • Will IAMGOLD/Sumitomo exercise the first Côté buy-back by ~mid-2027 (≥US$262.5M) — trading away part of a US$1.05B, 2025-vintage asset at a modest IRR?
  • Can FNV enforce its Ontario-law Karma stream in Burkina Faso, and does the ruling set a precedent for other streams in Sahel/LatAm jurisdictions?
  • With cash costs/GEO up to US$344 (H1 2026) from US$302 as %-of-spot payments scale, and Q3 realised gold likely ~US$4,100–4,200 vs US$4,418 in Q2, how much does H2 2026 EBITDA fall sequentially?
Context & updates
Côté Gold 7.5% GMR acquired for US$1.05B (27 May 2025)

Largest deal of the cycle, bought from a private party: covers all Côté reserves and 99.9% of resources plus Gosselin; FNV estimated ~US$67M/yr at US$3,200 gold. IAMGOLD/SMM can buy back up to 50% in two 25% tranches (min US$262.5M each; 1st within 2 yrs). Côté contributed US$41.2M (3.3%) in H1 2026 and reached near-full capacity in Jun 2026. Part of ~US$2.3B deployed in 2025 (with Western Limb US$500M, Porcupine US$448.6M, Arthur US$250M).

Record 2025 results, 2026 guidance and 2030 outlook (10 Mar 2026)

2025: 519,106 GEOs, US$1.82B revenue, US$1.66B adj. EBITDA (90.9%), US$1.49B OCF. 2026 guide 510–570k GEOs at US$4,500/75; 2030 outlook 555–615k GEOs ex-Cobre (Cobre restart +150–175k GEOs/yr). Dividend +16% to US$0.44 (26 Jan 2026). Revolver extended to 2031; available capital US$3.1B → US$4.3B by 30 Jun 2026.

Cobre Panamá: stockpile processing approved (7 Apr 2026) → commission recommends negotiation (30 Sep 2026)

Panama authorised processing of ~38 Mt of stockpiles (~70 kt Cu) → ~23,100 oz Au + 265,000 oz Ag to FNV, first concentrate May 2026. SGS audit 87.7% compliance (19 Jun 2026). On 30 Sep 2026 a ministerial commission recommended formal negotiations for a new agreement ending ≥US$27B of arbitration claims, with orderly closure 'at no cost to the Nation and with no possibility of extension' (25-yr life cited as illustrative). FQM fell up to 36%; FNV –4.0% that day. The stream remains at nil book value and outside guidance.

2026 deal flow: Orezone, i-80, Bullabulling ×2, Cascabel buy-back (Jan–Sep 2026)

US$100M Casa Berardi stream to Orezone (6,500 oz/yr fixed for 5 yrs, 20% of spot); US$250M i-80 Nevada royalty (1.5% NSR → 3.0% from 2031); A$220M (Feb) + A$200M (Sep) Bullabulling packages (3.90% gross royalty + equity); Victoria Gold portfolio C$55M; Youanmi A$47M; Comet Vale A$12M. SolGold/Jiangxi bought back 50% of the Cascabel stream (US$138.2M value, US$63.8M gain). H1 acquisitions US$529.7M.

Karma stream 'nullified' by Burkina Faso court (16–18 Jun 2026)

Riverstone Karma announced a local judgement purporting to nullify FNV's Karma stream; FNV calls it invalid and is pursuing remedies under Ontario law. No book value remains (Q2 call), so the financial hit is nil, but it is a second sovereign/counterparty loss after Cobre.

  • 30 SepCobre Panamá UpdateFNV notes the ministerial commission's first recommendation: open formal negotiations with Cobre Panamá/FQM on a new agreement ending the arbitrations, with orderly closure at no cost to the Nation and no extension. Changes the card: moves Cobre from 'stalled' to 'negotiation framework exists' — positive optionality on 150–175k GEOs/yr, but 'closure' framing and mandatory arbitration termination cap the value; FNV fell 4.0% on the day.

Links go to the company's own site · all releases · grey notes are my read of whether a release changes this card.

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 5/5 · Candour 4/5 · Skin in the game 3/5

Proven royalty team that reports plainly and runs no debt; the Cobre Panama concentration was a US$1B misjudgement whose resolution is outside its hands.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Paul Brink (President & CEO, director, since CEO May 2020; joined FNV 2008 (COO before)): Age 58. No other public boards listed. · Tom Albanese (Independent Chair, since May 2026 (Lead Independent Director before)): Age 68; ex-CEO Rio Tinto and Vedanta; also on CoTec Holdings board. Replaced founder David Harquail (now Chair Emeritus). · Eaun Gray (Chief Investment Officer, since 2025): Leads deal origination; CIO appointment 2025 (previously SVP Business Development).
Track record
  • Cobre Panama: FNV's largest stream (~US$1.36B invested 2012-19, roughly a fifth of revenue — figures unverified); mine shut Nov 2023 by Panama's Supreme Court; US$1B impairment taken; arbitration tribunal formed Dec 2024, hearing Oct 2026source
  • 2025: 519,106 GEOs sold, top end of a revised 2025 range (original range not stated in release); record results; debt-free with US$3.1B availablesource
  • 2025 deals: Casa Berardi stream US$100M, i-80 royalty US$250M upfront, Bullabulling royalty A$170M, Victoria Gold royalties; 2026: Youanmi US$32.9M, Victoria Gold portfolio US$40M, small Australian/Canadian royalties (same; https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/franco-nevada-reports-q2-2026-results-302848909.html)
  • 2026 guidance 510-570k GEOs; H1 268,758 GEOs; tracking to upper half with Cobre Panama stockpile deliveries resuming Q3 2026 (same Q2 release)
  • Say-on-pay 97.9% for (2025 AGM); Brink owns 252,655 sharessource
  • Business-model wins span every cycle since the 2007 IPO; the one large loss (Panama) was a 2012-19 cycle bet on a single asset.

Boards today: Brink: Franco-Nevada only. Albanese: Franco-Nevada chair + CoTec Holdings.

Fit to this job
Same job, done for 18 years: buying royalties and streams and sitting on them. The current task is rebuilding growth after losing ~20% of GEOs to Panama; the team has done the deals, and the Panama restart is outside their control.
Skin & pay
3/5 — meaningful stake, mostly founder stock or grants; not selling. Brink holds 252,655 common shares (well above guidelines; at-risk equity incl. RSUs/options ~C$123M per circular) — accumulated mainly via grants; open-market buying not found. 2025 total pay not in the excerpt fetched (unverified). Say-on-pay 97.9%. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1456346/000110465926040281/fnv-20260407xex99d1.htm

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Single-asset concentration (Cobre Panama) cost a US$1B impairment and ~20% of output; outcome still hangs on Panamanian politics and an Oct 2026 arbitration.
  • Founder-chair handover in 2026 (Harquail to Albanese) — first non-founder chair.

  1. Cash fell to a low of $160.3M in June 2025 after $1.35B of royalty purchases, then rebuilt to $1,014.2M by June 2026 from operations; no debt at any quarter end.

The largest primary silver producer on earth at 6× EBITDA and a ~9% free-cash-flow yield with US$1.7B of net cash — priced at a 40–60% discount to peers because 75% belongs to Peñoles, 100% of the mines are in Mexico, and the flagship's grade has halved in a decade

Gate Whether a 6× multiple with a 25% free float can re-rate at all — and whether the ore bodies that pay for it hold up while the pipeline is still seven years out. The discount is structural: Industrias Peñoles owns 74.99%, sells and refines essentially every ounce through its Met-Mex smelter (treatment charges renegotiated with the parent each half), shares services, and once sold Fresnillo a silver stream on its own mine that then failed. Index weight and liquidity are capped by the float; no buyback exists; the dividend is the only channel. Sub-gates: (1) grade — the Fresnillo mine runs 162 g/t against 300+ g/t a decade ago (2026 guide 160–180 g/t), Saucito 198 g/t with ventilation and ground-control constraints flagged to lower 2027–28 output; San Julián has 3.3 years of reserves, Ciénega 4.0; (2) costs — H1 production costs +20.5%: 13.8% inflation of which the peso (12.5% stronger, US$58.5M) is most; wages +7% in pesos (+22% in dollars), diesel +20%, contractors +12%; Fresnillo and Saucito AISC US$29–33/oz AgEq, up 48–71% year-on-year; (3) Mexico as the only country — no new concessions since 2018 (seven titles issued to Fresnillo in July 2026 were reorganisations), duties raised in 2025 (special duty 7.5→8.5%, precious-metals duty 0.5→1.0%), water-law tightening gates Rodeo and Orisyvo, Zacatecas is the most violent state in the country, and Herradura was blockaded for 14 days in May 2026 in a union-representation fight with a renewed threat in July; (4) the pipeline is 2029–2033 — nothing new produces before Rodeo, and the three large projects are PFS-stage; (5) management turnover — the CFO of 18 years steps down Nov 1, the COO has left and is not replaced.

Deposit Reserves (Dec 2025) 362.6 Moz Ag + 7.8 Moz Au · resources 2,058 Moz Ag + 44 Moz Au · 2026 guide 42–46.5 Moz Ag, 500–550 koz Au

Funded to the next catalyst Fully self-funded — every project in the pipeline is paid from cash, no raise, stream or partner needed. 2026–28 capex of US$500–600M/yr against US$2.5B+ of annual operating cash flow at H1 prices; a 50% payout at H2 planning prices still leaves ~US$1B/yr of surplus. The question is not funding; it is allocation — dividend vs Novador/Orisyvo/Rodeo builds from 2027.
Thesis

Six operating mines, all in Mexico: Fresnillo and Saucito (Zacatecas; the two largest primary silver mines in the world), Juanicipio (56%; Pan American holds 44% since buying MAG Silver in Sep 2025; AISC US$15.82/oz), San Julián Veins (Chihuahua), Ciénega (Durango), and Herradura (Sonora; ~340 koz Au/yr open-pit heap leach). 2025: 48.7 Moz Ag, 600 koz Au, EBITDA US$2.8B, net profit US$1.57B, record dividends of US$950M plus a US$308M special. H1 2026: revenue US$3.38B (+75%), EBITDA US$2.35B at a 69.5% margin, net profit US$1.46B (+213%), realised US$78.9 Ag / US$4,667 Au; operating cash flow US$1.49B after US$890M of taxes; capex cut to US$500–550M for the year; net cash US$1.66B against one US$840M 4.25% bond due 2050; interim dividend 43.4¢ (+109%), and management working toward a 50% payout. 2026 guidance 42–46.5 Moz Ag (no more Silverstream — Peñoles' Sabinas mine failed) and 500–550 koz Au; H1 delivered 22.0 Moz and 291 koz. Reserves 362.6 Moz Ag (+9%) and 7.8 Moz Au. Growth is a decade-long pipeline: Novador (Québec; Probe Gold bought for C$780M cash, closed Jan 2026; PFS 2H 2026; 200+ koz/yr from ~2033), Orisyvo (9.6 Moz Au, 2033), Guanajuato (388 Moz Ag, 2033), Rodeo (heap leach 90–110 koz/yr, 2029–30), Tajitos (2030), Noche Buena restart (2027), Valles (Q3 2026). Stock 2,771p, 38% below its January peak of 4,470p; six analysts, consensus Hold, average target 3,490p (JPMorgan 4,700p, Jefferies 2,700p).

The Gate

Whether a 6× multiple with a 25% free float can re-rate at all — and whether the ore bodies that pay for it hold up while the pipeline is still seven years out. The discount is structural: Industrias Peñoles owns 74.99%, sells and refines essentially every ounce through its Met-Mex smelter (treatment charges renegotiated with the parent each half), shares services, and once sold Fresnillo a silver stream on its own mine that then failed. Index weight and liquidity are capped by the float; no buyback exists; the dividend is the only channel.

Sub-gates
  1. Grade — the Fresnillo mine runs 162 g/t against 300+ g/t a decade ago (2026 guide 160–180 g/t), Saucito 198 g/t with ventilation and ground-control constraints flagged to lower 2027–28 output; San Julián has 3.3 years of reserves, Ciénega 4.0.
  2. Costs — H1 production costs +20.5%: 13.8% inflation of which the peso (12.5% stronger, US$58.5M) is most; wages +7% in pesos (+22% in dollars), diesel +20%, contractors +12%; Fresnillo and Saucito AISC US$29–33/oz AgEq, up 48–71% year-on-year.
  3. Mexico as the only country — no new concessions since 2018 (seven titles issued to Fresnillo in July 2026 were reorganisations), duties raised in 2025 (special duty 7.5→8.5%, precious-metals duty 0.5→1.0%), water-law tightening gates Rodeo and Orisyvo, Zacatecas is the most violent state in the country, and Herradura was blockaded for 14 days in May 2026 in a union-representation fight with a renewed threat in July.
  4. The pipeline is 2029–2033 — nothing new produces before Rodeo, and the three large projects are PFS-stage.
  5. Management turnover — the CFO of 18 years steps down Nov 1, the COO has left and is not replaced.

Read the discount as the market's price for the shareholder register, not for the mines. That is why it has persisted through three cycles and why it may persist through this one.

Absolute costs rose ~56% year on year (stronger peso, wages, diesel, falling grade); the position held only because peers inflated too. Watch the two flagships, not the blend.

How to read it: picture every primary silver mine in the world lined up from cheapest to most expensive to run (all-in sustaining cost per ounce, weighted by output). The percentile is the share of world output that costs less; the middle line splits the cheaper half from the costlier half. Lower-half mines keep earning when the metal price falls. Dot = 2026, ring = 2025. Silver curve: estimated from 18 primary silver mines' 2026 guidance and H1 actuals (~116 Moz) on the Silver Institute's by-product basis — gold, zinc, lead and copper revenue subtracted; silver-equivalent figures converted (±US$3–5/oz). Approximate — it ranks the names, it is not decimal-precise.

MetricHeadlineDetail
Risk score2/5Six mines with US$2.5B of cash, one long bond, a 70% EBITDA margin, 362 Moz of silver reserves and 7.8 Moz of gold, a dividend policy that has paid out through every cycle since the 2008 IPO. Not a 1: a single country with rising duties, security and water constraints; a controlling shareholder that is also the customer, refiner and service provider; falling grade at the two flagships; short reserve lives at two of six mines; and a record of silver guidance misses from 2019 to 2023. The loss path is a multiple that never re-rates while grade and the peso erode margins — dead money with a 4% yield, not capital loss.

On every producer metric this is the cheapest name on the page; the question is only whether cheap is the permanent condition.
Valuation Anchor

~6× EBITDA, ~9% FCF yield, 4% dividend yield, net cash — a 40–60% discount to every listed silver peer, and it has been there for fifteen years. The re-rate path exists on paper: a 50% payout at H2's US$55 Ag / US$4,000 Au still funds a ~5% yield; the January peak was 4,470p on the same assets; at 9× peer EBITDA the stock is ~1.4× today's. Whether the market ever pays it is a different question — the float will not change, Peñoles will not sell, and every incremental dollar of value accrues 75% to a shareholder the market cannot trade. So this is a yield-plus-metal holding, not a re-rate trade: the multiples column moves with silver and the dividend follows earnings, and that is the whole case.

The bear case is the one that has already started — H2 silver at US$55 not US$79, the peso at 17.5, wages +22% in dollars, Saucito constrained through 2028 — with the stock 38% off its high before any of it shows in a print.

Bucket: producer / cash flow, the silver-heavy senior: what you pay for the most silver-levered cash flow on the market when it comes with a controlling shareholder attached.

Shareholder structure
Management & board
Negligible direct holdings; control sits with the parent. Chair Alejandro Baillères Gual also chairs Peñoles and Grupo BAL (the Baillères family holding) — the controlling family's representative, not an independent. CEO Octavio Alvídrez (since 2012); CFO Mario Arreguín (since the 2008 IPO) steps down Nov 1, 2026 → Rodrigo Sandoval (ex-CFO Grupo Gigante, ex-Grupo México mining division, Torex audit chair). COO vacant since Q2. Independent directors: Dame Judith Macgregor (SID), Alberto Tiburcio (audit), Arturo Fernández, Luz Adriana Ramírez. Executive equity is not a signal here.
Insider activity (12 mo)
None located. No director dealings found in 2025–26; no buyback programme exists; the only capital return is the dividend. The parent's stake has not moved.
Strategic & prominent
Industrias Peñoles 552.6M shares = 74.99% (Grupo BAL / Baillères). Institutions ~17.6% of the total (~70% of the float): First Eagle 5.0% (36.8M), Van Eck 1.0%, BlackRock ~1.0%, Vanguard 0.7%, Global X 0.7%, Norges 0.6%, Wellington 0.4%. No Sprott, Rule, Giustra or activist; a UK-listed Mexican family company held by index and value funds.
Institutions / retail
Peñoles 75%, institutions ~18%, retail and other ~7%. Free float 25.01%; 736.9M shares, no options or warrants of note. Geography of holders: Mexico 75%, US 10%, UK 4%.

Read: Alignment here is with the Baillères family, not with management: the parent needs the dividend (Peñoles' own balance sheet lives on it), which is why the payout policy has survived three downturns and is now heading to 50%. The cost is everything a minority cannot see — refining charges, shared services, a stream on a parent mine that failed — and a float that caps the multiple. Nobody outside is signalling; nobody inside needs to.

Jurisdiction risk

National: Mexico, the whole company. The 2023 mining-law reform stands (Supreme Court challenge pending); Sheinbaum has kept 'no new concessions' since 2018 while clearing the permit backlog (110 of 176 stalled projects resolved, Fresnillo's Orisyvo among the unlocked pipeline); duties rose in 2025 (special mining duty 8.5%, precious-metals duty 1.0% of revenue) and the 2026 water-law changes add obligations in over-exploited basins — Rodeo's timing is explicitly gated by water. Effective tax rate 23.9% before mining rights; US$890M of taxes and rights paid in H1 alone. Novador in Québec is the first non-Mexican asset and produces nothing before ~2033.

Local: three live layers. Labour — Herradura (Sonora) was blockaded for ~14 days from late April 2026 by ~1,800 FRENTE-union participants disputing profit-sharing and union representation against the incumbent CTM contract; ended by state police; a renewed strike threat was reported in July; the interim report does not mention it. Security — Zacatecas is Mexico's most violent state and Fresnillo city among its most insecure; extortion demands on suppliers are documented in the district; no disclosed material incident at the company's mines, but Vizsla's January 2026 killings in neighbouring Sinaloa set the reference. Community/land — Soledad-Dipolos has been suspended since 2013 over an ejido land dispute; Noche Buena's restart and Valles are inside the existing Herradura footprint. Safety: zero fatalities in H1 2026 after two in 2025.

Same country as GoGold, Vizsla and Avino — but Fresnillo has no other country to point to, and Zacatecas is the state the others are glad not to be in.

Differentiator
  1. The most silver-levered cash flow that exists at scale: ~45 Moz a year of primary silver from the two largest silver mines in the world plus 56% of the lowest-cost one, in a company with US$1.7B of net cash and a 70% EBITDA margin. No other producer on the page earns more than half its revenue from silver at this size (Pan American ~38%, Coeur ~36%).
  2. The cheapest multiple of any listed precious-metals producer — 6× EBITDA against 9–15× for peers, a ~9% FCF yield, a 4% dividend, and a stated move to a 50% payout.
  3. Reserve depth — 362 Moz Ag and 7.8 Moz Au in reserve, 2,058 Moz and 44 Moz in resource, and ~US$260M a year of exploration that replaced depletion for two decades.
  4. A paid-for growth pipeline — Novador, Orisyvo, Guanajuato, Rodeo, Tajitos — funded from cash without a raise, a stream, or a partner.
  5. A controlling shareholder that has never cut the dividend policy — Peñoles needs the cash too, which is the one way the register works in a minority's favour.

Read it honestly: everything on this list has been true since 2010, and the discount has never closed. The differentiator explains the yield, not a re-rate.

Exploration upside

Brownfield-heavy, ~US$260M/yr · moves the needle: medium for life, low for the multiple. 468,879 m in H1 (+30%), 75% brownfield: Juanicipio and Saucito extensions, Guanajuato infill (32,844 m), Novador (37,550 m), Orisyvo, Rodeo, Tajitos. The Sinda stake (5%, adjoining Guanajuato) is a small option on a district discovery. Resources are already 5.7× reserves; the constraint is permits and capital allocation, not ounces.

Watch reserve replacement at Fresnillo and Saucito specifically — the group total hides that the two flagships are the ones thinning.

Next Catalyst

Rodeo PEA (overdue, "almost completed" on 28 Sep) and Novador PFS (2H 2026); Orisyvo permit filings by YE; CFO handover Nov 1, COO appointment; Herradura ball-mill shell replacement (Q4); Q4 report Jan 2027 with 2027–28 guidance and the metal-by-metal update; FY results ~early Mar 2027 with the final dividend (50% payout intent) and Dec 2026 reserves; Met-Mex treatment-charge renegotiation for 2H; Supreme Court ruling on the 2023 mining law; Herradura union vote. Q3 production report (21 Oct) done: 10.3 Moz Ag, guidance kept.

Open Questions
  • Is there any path to a higher float — a Peñoles sell-down, a secondary, a buyback — or is 6× the permanent multiple?
  • How much value leaks to the parent through Met-Mex treatment and refining charges and shared services — what are the related-party totals?
  • What do Saucito's ventilation and ground-control constraints cost in ounces in 2027–28, and when does Fresnillo mine grade stop falling?
  • At US$55 silver and a 17.5 peso, what is the group AISC and the free cash flow — and does the 50% payout survive it?
  • Rodeo's PEA was guided for early Q3 2026 and has not appeared — why, and is water the reason?
  • Why is the COO seat vacant, and what does the CFO change mean for capital allocation after 18 years?
Context & updates
21 Oct 2026 update

Q3 production (21 Oct): silver 10.32 Moz, down 5.5% on the quarter and 11.6% on the year; gold 135.1 koz, down 12.8% on the quarter. Nine-month silver 32.4 Moz and gold 425.9 koz; 2026 guidance of 42–46.5 Moz and 500–550 koz is maintained, so Q4 needs about 9.6 Moz and 74 koz, which the current run-rate covers. Grades fell at Juanicipio, Saucito and San Julián (ground conditions, equipment availability); Herradura lost 18% of its gold to a ball-mill fissure and more sulphide ore, with the mill shell to be replaced in Q4. Nothing on Rodeo or costs. Shares −2.1% to 2,632p. Odds unchanged.

3 Oct 2026 refresh

No announcement since 14 Sep; Q3 production expected ~20–22 Oct. Management said on 28 Sep the overdue Rodeo PEA is 'almost completed' (90–110 koz a year).

H1 2026 results (Aug 4)

Revenue US$3,382.6M (+75%); EBITDA US$2,349.7M (69.5% margin); net profit US$1,463.4M, attributable US$1,290.0M, EPS US$1.75 vs ~US$1.52 consensus. Realised Ag US$78.9/oz (+134%), Au US$4,667 (+47%). Production costs +20.5% (peso US$58.5M). Capex guidance cut US$200M to US$500–550M. Interim dividend 43.4¢ (US$319.8M, +109%), paid Sep 18. Net cash US$1,663M after US$797M final dividend, US$548M for Probe and US$890M of taxes.

Q2 2026 production (Jul 22)

Ag 10.93 Moz (−9.3% y/y), Au 154.8 koz (+13.8% q/q); H1 22.05 Moz Ag, 290.9 koz Au. Guidance maintained. Fresnillo mine 162 g/t; Saucito hauling temporarily by road at US$151/t until the Jarillas shaft sections connect in Q3. COO Iturriaga departed; Central Region under an interim head.

M&A and pipeline (Nov 2025 – Jul 2026)

Probe Gold (Novador, Val-d'Or) bought for C$3.65/share ≈ C$780M cash, completed Jan 22, 2026 — first asset outside Mexico; PFS 2H 2026. Sinda 5% stake (US$95.3M at the US$12 IPO price) Jul 27. MAG Silver stake sold May 2025 after Pan American's bid; Pan American is now the 44% Juanicipio partner. Silverstream (Peñoles' Sabinas) terminated 2025: US$132M non-cash loss.

Herradura labour dispute (Apr–Jul 2026)

FRENTE union strike notice Apr 27 over profit-sharing and contract ownership vs CTM; ~1,800 participants blockaded ~14 days; ended by Sonora state police; company: illegal, no material impact. Renewed strike threat reported Jul 7 (BNamericas). Not mentioned in the interim report.

Aside

Peñoles holds 74.99% — precisely on the old FCA 25% free-float floor. Trailing dividends 151.5¢ on a ~US$36 ADR ≈ 4.2%; 2025 paid US$1.26B including the special. Mexico's seven July 2026 mining titles to Minera Fresnillo were reorganisations of existing rights, not new concessions — the first titles of any kind under Sheinbaum.

Track record
  • Largest primary silver producer globally, 100+ year Mexican operator; CEO 14 years in seatsource

  • H1 2026: net profit tripled, US$2.5B cash, interim dividend doubled; capex guidance raised to US$500-550Msource

Fit to this job
Exact fit: same mines, same district, same mining methods, same people for decades. Nothing new except declining grades at Saucito, Ciénega and Fresnillo and narrower veins — a geological problem, not an experience gap.
Skin & pay
1/5 — under ~0.5%, options only, or net sellers while promoting. Alvídrez: 0 ordinary shares (AR 2024); single total remuneration US$2.04M (2024), ~US$2.06M (2025) — low for a US$15B+ company, mostly salary (bonus US$458k, no LTI shown). Baillères family controls 74.99%. Say-on-pay 2024 AGM 98.7% (94.1% of independent holders). Insider trading: no open-market buys/sells found. Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Funded to the next catalyst Fully funded for everything in the plan, including the US$1.9B Skarn build over 2026–31 from internal cash flow. No financing question exists here.
Thesis

Eleven producing mines across seven countries plus 44% of Juanicipio (Fresnillo-operated, acquired with MAG Silver in Sep 2025 for ~US$2.1B), which runs at a negative AISC. 2026 guidance 25–27 Moz Ag and 700–750 koz Au; H1 2026 attributable revenue US$2.6B, net earnings US$761M, attributable free cash flow US$832M. Net cash US$777M, US$3.2B liquidity, 417M shares after buying back 7.3M YTD at ~US$49, a US$0.184 quarterly dividend, and a framework returning up to US$1B in 2026 (35–40% of FCF). Silver reserves 511 Moz P&P (+13% y/y with Juanicipio), gold 6.3 Moz.

Two dormant giants: Escobal (Guatemala, 264 Moz reserve, idle since 2017 under an open-ended ILO 169 consultation) and La Colorada Skarn (Mexico, revised PEA Mar 2026: NPV5% US$2.6B at US$45 Ag, US$1.9B capex, first production 2032, 19 Moz/yr at peak; US$265M decline approved May 2026).

The Gate

Gold-cost discipline, because gold is where the earnings are. Management says silver is ~38% of revenue and gold ~60%; the Q2 miss (adj. EPS US$0.73 vs ~US$0.86–0.92 consensus, stock −10%) came from the gold segment: AISC US$1,984/oz against US$1,700–1,850 guided, Jacobina and El Peñon each ~10 koz short, gold guidance now "low end", cash-tax guidance raised to US$585–635M. The silver segment's AISC jump (US$6.63 → US$17.80 in one quarter on royalties, FX and inventory) shows how much of the "low-cost silver" story is Juanicipio's arithmetic.

Sub-gates
  1. Escobal — 264 Moz sitting idle at US$16–18M/yr holding cost, Xinka Parliament formally rejected restart (May 2025) and alleges interference; no timeline.
  2. La Colorada Skarn — US$1.9B, six-year build, PEA-level, already re-scoped once.
  3. H2-weighted delivery across Bolivia blockades, Chilean/Argentine El Niño access disruptions and Jacobina seismicity.

For a name this size the gate is not survival — it is whether the multiple expands from 9× or stays a gold-miner multiple with a silver label.

Figure used: Gold segment (~60% of revenue): US$1,850/oz, the top of guidance, where management says it will land (Q2 actual US$1,984 → ~68th). Silver segment: guidance midpoint US$17.0/oz Ag → ~61st (Q2 US$17.80 → ~62nd).

Juanicipio (44% owned) is first-quartile (~16th), as the company says — but averaged with costlier mines it does not make Pan American a low-cost producer: both segments sit just above the middle.

Flat on position since 2025; no visible gold-cost fix for 2026 (Jacobina and El Peñón shortfalls).

How to read it: picture every primary gold (or silver) mine in the world lined up from cheapest to most expensive to run (all-in sustaining cost per ounce, weighted by output). The percentile is the share of world output that costs less; the middle line splits the cheaper half from the costlier half. Lower-half mines keep earning when the metal price falls. Dot = 2026, ring = 2025. Gold curve: Metals Focus / World Gold Council, Q1 2026 (average US$1,785/oz; the quartile lines are estimates). Silver curve: estimated from 18 primary silver mines' 2026 guidance and H1 actuals (~116 Moz) on the Silver Institute's by-product basis — gold, zinc, lead and copper revenue subtracted; silver-equivalent figures converted (±US$3–5/oz). Approximate — it ranks the names, it is not decimal-precise.

Valuation Anchor

~9× EBITDA, ~8% FCF yield, net cash — a gold-miner multiple on a silver-branded balance sheet. The arithmetic case for a re-rate is that 511 Moz of reserves and the Skarn (309 Moz Indicated) make it the largest silver optionality on the market, and silver-pure peers (Aya ~14×) trade five turns higher; the arithmetic case against is that 60% of revenue is gold at ~US$1,980 AISC, which is a mid-tier gold-miner profile and deserves a mid-tier gold multiple. Both are true.

In this file it is a benchmark row: what the market pays for scale, diversification and capital return — not a multi-bagger candidate. Escobal is a free option with a ten-year fuse; the Skarn is a paid-for option with a six-year one.
