Shareholder structure
Management & board
~0.09% — CEO Michael Steinmann ~107,600 shares (~US$5M) plus RSUs/PSUs; directors hold DSUs and small share blocks (de Gelder ~C$5M total). Ross Beaty (founder) retired as Chair in 2021 and is not on the board; his residual personal stake is undisclosed. Ownership guideline 3× retainer by May 2028.
Insider activity (12 mo)
Sales only, RSU-sized. Steinmann 27.9k @ ≤US$51.13 (Dec 2025, ~US$1.4M); Busby, McAleer, Lemon, Wafforn each ~US$0.9–1.4M. ~US$4.5M net selling, zero open-market buys. Routine for a US$20B senior; not a signal either way.
Strategic & prominent
None above 5% except Van Eck 5.1% (21.4M at Mar 2026; trimmed to 19.1M in Q2). Global X ~3.7%, Vanguard ~2.7%, BlackRock ~2.1% (new US$376M position Q2 2026), Norges 1.4%, Capital Research 1.5%. Ex-MAG Silver holders received ~60M shares (~14%) in Sep 2025 and have dispersed. Fresnillo is the Juanicipio JV partner, not a shareholder.
Institutions / retail
Institutions ~56%, insiders <0.1%, retail/other ~44%. 417.1M shares at Jun 30 → ~414.6M after post-quarter buybacks; dilutives ~1.1M units (negligible). NCIB for 21.1M (5%) to Mar 2027; 7.3M bought YTD at ~US$49, US$358M.

Read: Insider ownership is irrelevant at this size — nobody expects the CEO of a US$20B company to own 5%. What matters is the buyback: US$358M repurchased YTD at ~US$49 against a ~US$65 consensus target is management voting with the company's cash. The register is an index register; the stock moves with GDX and silver, and no single holder can change that.

Jurisdiction risk

National: seven countries, three with live problems. Guatemala (Escobal: ILO 169 consultation open-ended, Xinka rejection); Bolivia (~4%: nationwide blockades May–Jun 2026, dollar peg abandoned, IMF talks); Mexico (~22% + Juanicipio: 2023 mining-law limits, La Colorada royalties scaling with prices); Peru (~17%: Fujimori inaugurated Jul 2026, pragmatic); Argentina (~13%: export duties cut to 0% Aug 2025 — positive; Navidad still blocked by Chubut's open-pit ban); Chile (~19%: El Niño access disruptions); Brazil (~15%: Jacobina seismicity — operational); Canada (~10%: clean).

Local: the diversification is the mitigation — no single licence decision is material to the group except Escobal, which is already carried at zero.

This is the mirror image of Aya: many small jurisdiction risks that net out, versus one large one that doesn't.

Differentiator
  1. Juanicipio and the reserve base. A 44% stake in the lowest-cost primary silver mine in the world (AISC negative, 2026 guide US$2.25–4.25/oz) and 511 Moz of P&P silver — no other company owns that much defined silver.
  2. Balance sheet and capital return — net cash US$777M, a doubled US$1.5B undrawn revolver, US$1B/yr framework, buybacks at ~US$49 that are accretive below the analyst range.
  3. Two latent tier-one silver mines (Escobal 264 Moz, Skarn 309 Moz) that cost nothing to hold at today's price.
  4. Scale — index weight, liquidity, and the ability to buy a MAG Silver for US$2.1B without a raise.

Read it honestly: the differentiator (Juanicipio's negative AISC) is also why the silver-segment AISC swung from US$6.63 to US$17.80 in one quarter — the segment number is one asset's arithmetic. And the gold that pays the bills is cost-inflating.

Exploration upside

Conversion and brownfield · moves the needle: low. US$132–135M exploration budget replaces depletion and grew silver reserves 13% (mostly Juanicipio inclusion) while gold reserves stayed flat. The Skarn's 309 Moz Indicated is the growth; it does not need more drilling, it needs US$1.9B and six years.

At 511 Moz of reserves, exploration is maintenance.

Next Catalyst

Q3 results (Nov) — gold-cost recovery and whether Q3 gold lands 3–6 koz below the quarterly range as warned; Skarn shaft/material-handling engineering to the Board H2 2026; Escobal consultation (Government–Xinka meeting Jul 7, 2026; no date); Timmins PEA H1 2027; continued buyback (~US$700M planned for 2026).

Open Questions
  • What is the true consolidated silver share once Juanicipio is counted on an attributable basis — and does the company ever publish revenue by metal?
  • Does gold AISC return inside US$1,700–1,850, or is US$1,980 the new base for Jacobina/El Peñon/Timmins/Minera Florida?
  • Is Escobal worth anything inside a 3–5 year horizon, or should it be carried at zero indefinitely?
  • Does the Skarn survive a feasibility study at US$1.9B, and who else could fund it?
  • At 9× EBITDA with net cash, why does the market not pay a silver multiple — and what would change that?

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 5/5 · Candour 4/5 · Skin in the game 1/5

Candid operator that delivers roughly to guidance and returns cash; its three biggest deals (Tahoe, Yamana, MAG) were bought at or near the top and Escobal is seven years idle.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Michael Steinmann (President & CEO, since Jan 1, 2016 (with company since 2004)): Age 59, geologist. Board: Lumina Gold. Say-on-pay fell to 69% in 2024. · Gillian Winckler (Independent Chair, since Chair since 2021 (director since ~2016)): Succeeded founder Ross Beaty, who retired as Chair in 2021. · Steven Busby (COO, since unverified (long-tenured)): Sold ~25k shares Jan 2026.
Track record
  • Tahoe Resources bought Feb 2019 (~US$1.07B, unverified) mainly for Escobal; Escobal has been shut since 2017 and the ILO 169 consultation still has 'no timeline' in Aug 2026 — 7 years of dead capitalsource
  • Yamana bought Mar 2023 (~US$4.8B with Agnico taking the Canadian assets, unverified); non-core assets since sold (La Arena, MARA stake, Morococha — unverified prices); Jacobina and El Peñón kept and both had 2026 guidance trimmed
  • MAG Silver bought Sep 4, 2025 (~US$2.1B, unverified) for 44% of Juanicipio at a cycle highsource
  • Guidance: 2023 silver cut mid-year and missed original (unverified figures); 2024 21.1 Moz at low end of 21-23; 2025 met (unverified); 2026 silver reiterated 25-27 Moz, gold guided to low end after Jacobina/El Peñón cuts (Q2 2026 release)
  • Capital returns: record US$300M in Q2 2026, framework 35-40% of FCF, 'up to US$1B' in 2026; Q2 FCF US$344Msource
  • La Colorada Skarn: US$265M decline project approved, first cut Aug 2026 — long-dated growth; Navidad (Argentina) still blocked by Chubut law since 2010 (unverified status)

Boards today: Steinmann: 2 (Pan American + Lumina Gold).

Fit to this job
Exact fit: 30-year Americas silver/gold operator, same regions (Mexico, Peru, Bolivia, Argentina, Brazil, Chile). What the team has not managed to do: reopen Escobal or unlock Navidad — the two biggest silver assets it owns are both idle after 7 and 16 years.
Skin & pay
1/5 — under ~0.5%, options only, or net sellers while promoting. Steinmann: 145,408 shares (Mar 2025, ~CA$5.4M) + 310k PSUs + 85k RSUs; ~0.03% of company; holdings from grants, CEO sold 21% of direct shares Dec 2025 (~US$1.4M); insiders net sellers US$4.5M/12 months. CEO total comp 2025 ~US$10.79M (11% salary). Say-on-pay 2024: 69.2% (2023: 88%). Sources: https://panamericansilver.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/2025-InfoCirc-Final-2025-03-17.pdf ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/materials/nyse-paas/pan-american-silver/management

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Two idle flagship silver assets (Escobal, Navidad) with no path, after US$1B+ spent on Escobal
  • CEO pay US$10.8M (2025, 89% variable) with 0.026% ownership; sold stock Dec 2025; 69% say-on-pay in 2024
  • MAG Silver bought at the top of the silver cycle for ~US$2.1B
  • Gold segment guidance trimmed at two mines in 2026

What the numbers say
  1. Cash grew from US$439M in September 2024 to US$1,566M in June 2026 while borrowings stayed flat at about US$710–720M, giving net cash of about US$850M.
  2. Capex is US$60–105M a quarter, absorbing only 20–30% of operating cash flow; 2026 guidance is US$320–360M sustaining plus US$195–255M project spend.
  3. The MAG Silver acquisition in September 2025 cost US$500M cash plus 60.2M shares, lifting the count from 362M to 422M; US$249M of buybacks cut it to 417.1M by June 2026.
  4. Revenue rose from US$716M in Q3 2024 to US$1,124M in Q2 2026 on silver at US$71–89/oz; mine operating margin went from about 25% to 41–53%.
  5. H1 2026 free cash flow was US$832M and dividends plus buybacks US$401M; FY2024 had a US$137.4M gain on the La Arena sale and a 74% effective tax rate.

Funded to the next catalyst Fully funded. All growth is ramp and sustaining capital from cash flow; no note matures before Feb 2029. The question is delivery, not funding.
Thesis

Coeur tripled its share count to ~1.03B to buy SilverCrest (Las Chispas, Feb 2025, ~US$1.7B) and New Gold (Rainy River + New Afton, closed Mar 20, 2026, ~US$6.9B in shares), turning a Nevada-Mexico silver-gold mid-cap into a seven-mine, three-country senior: Rainy River (ON), New Afton (BC, gold-copper cave), Kensington (AK), Wharf (SD), Rochester (NV, post-expansion), Palmarejo and Las Chispas (Mexico).

Q2 2026 was a record on the top line — 163.5 koz Au, 4.4 Moz Ag, 11.4 Mlb Cu, revenue US$1.09B, adjusted EBITDA US$478M, free cash flow US$388M, net cash ~US$347M — and a miss on the bottom line (adj. EPS US$0.12 vs US$0.22–0.32 consensus, stock −8.5%) as US$264M of purchase-price inventory step-up flowed through costs. Gold is 64% of revenue, silver 30%, copper 6%. A US$750M buyback (US$121M done by end-July), the first dividend in ~30 years (US$0.02 semi-annual), a US$1B undrawn revolver, and a stated "path to investment grade" (S&P B+ → reportedly BB).

The Gate

H2 delivery on a guidance that has already been cut once. August's update trimmed gold to 630–750 koz (from 680–815), copper to 40–50 Mlb (from 50–65), raised capex to US$520–605M (from US$437–526M) and cut the 2026 EBITDA/FCF targets to ~US$2.3B / ~US$1.5B from ~US$3.0B / ~US$2.0B at the deal announcement — five months after closing. Three ramps have to land at once: Rainy River underground from 2,300 tpd (Q2) to 5,000 tpd by year-end with the Phase 4 pit ending late 2026; New Afton C-Zone cave ~3 months late, 12k → 16k tpd by early Q4; Rochester, which delivered ~26 koz Au / 2.6 Moz Ag in H1 against a 70–90 koz / 6.4–7.8 Moz full-year guide — H2 must carry ~70% of the year, after 2025 guidance was also cut.

Sub-gates
  1. Kensington grades and CAS (US$2,323 vs US$1,750–1,950 guided); Palmarejo silver CAS above guide and the Franco-Nevada stream taking 40–51% of its gold at US$800/oz; integration of a company that doubled its size on paper before it had run the assets through a full quarter.

Two misses in a row (Q1 on PPA, Q2 on everything) plus a Rochester that has missed three years running is a pattern, not noise. Q3 (Nov) is the test.

How to read it: picture every primary gold mine in the world lined up from cheapest to most expensive to run (all-in sustaining cost per ounce, weighted by output). The percentile is the share of world output that costs less; the middle line splits the cheaper half from the costlier half. Lower-half mines keep earning when the metal price falls. Dot = 2026, ring = 2025. Gold curve: Metals Focus / World Gold Council, Q1 2026 (average US$1,785/oz; the quartile lines are estimates). Approximate — it ranks the names, it is not decimal-precise.

Risk score3/5Seven producing mines in tier-one jurisdictions, net cash, record FCF: permanent loss is remote. But this is a 3 rather than a 2 because the last four quarters contain three misses, a mid-year guidance cut, three simultaneous ramps, and a share count that tripled — the loss path is a further de-rating if H2 disappoints, on a name already ~45% off its 52-week high.
Market cap15 Oct 2026: ~US$15.9B (US$15.41 on 1,027.9M shares; 52-wk US$13.55–27.77, ~45% off the high). EV ~US$15.5B (net cash ~US$0.35B); EV/EBITDA ~9.5× TTM; P/E ~14× trailing / ~9.4× forward; yield ~0.3%; short interest ~4.8% (Sep). Earlier: ~US$18.2B on 2 Oct (US$17.66), ~US$19.4B on 24 Sep (US$18.90) — the 11.7× TTM / 11.5× forward figures quoted then were struck on US$19.1B EV. Consensus Buy/Moderate Buy, avg target ~US$24–25.5 (range 18–35); BMO cut to US$26. S&P MidCap 400 since Jun 2026. Zacks #5 post-Q2.
Capex / IRR2026 capex US$520–605M (sustaining US$360–405M, development US$160–200M; raised ~15% in Aug), exploration US$147–169M, cash taxes US$350–450M, price deck cut to US$4,000 Au / US$60 Ag / US$6 Cu. No growth-project IRR — growth is ramps, not builds: Rochester Stage 6 pad US$96–110M; Rainy River UG; New Afton C-Zone; Silvertip PFS early 2027.
NPVNo project NPV; the company is valued on EBITDA and FCF.Management's own 2026 FCF target US$1.5B → ~9.4% yield on US$15.9B (15 Oct) if delivered; H1 actual US$654M (43% of it). Wharf technical report LOM FCF US$1.1B.
DepositLegacy P&P (Dec 2025, US$2,200 / US$26): 4.4 Moz Au, 274.4 Moz AgRochester 1.33 Moz / 182 Moz, Wharf 1.25 Moz (+65%, ~12-yr life), Palmarejo 0.93 Moz / 64 Moz (+36/40%), Kensington 0.55 Moz (5-yr life), Las Chispas 0.30 Moz / 28 Moz. Plus New Gold: Rainy River 2.2 Moz Au (to 2035), New Afton 0.78 Moz Au + 591 Mlb Cu (+ K-Zone 0.72 Moz / 606 Mlb). Silvertip M&I 57.6 Moz Ag + 1.23 Blb Zn. Q2 CAS by mine: Las Chispas US$841/oz Au, Palmarejo US$1,016, Wharf US$1,267, New Afton US$1,766, Rochester US$1,832, Kensington US$2,323, Rainy River US$3,788 (PPA-inflated).
NPV : capexn/a — no build.Producer screen: FCF yield ~9.4% on target, ~8.2% on H1 run-rate (US$15.9B cap, 15 Oct); EV/EBITDA ~9.5× TTM but ~6.7× on the US$2.3B target — cheaper than Aya, dearer than Pan American; EV/oz P&P gold ~US$2,100 (US$15.5B ÷ 7.4 Moz), before crediting silver and copper.
Valuation Anchor

~6.7× 2026 target EBITDA, ~9.4% target FCF yield, ~9.4× forward P/E (15 Oct, US$15.41) — a turnaround multiple, not a quality one. If H2 delivers the US$2.3B and the ramps hold into 2027 (consensus 2027 EPS US$2.04 → ~7.6× at today's price), the discount to Pan American closes and the stock is the cheapest senior in North America. If Rochester misses a fourth year and Rainy River's underground stalls, the market keeps treating it as the company that paid US$8.6B in shares for assets it cannot yet run.

Of the four producers this is the cheapest on forward numbers and the least proven on delivery — which is what the multiple says. Gold-led: silver is a 30% by-line, so the gold decks apply.

Shareholder structure
Management & board
~0.9% post-New Gold (D&Os ~1.5% of 642M shares pre-deal, diluted). Chair/CEO Mitchell Krebs ~2.15M shares / 0.21% (~US$45M) — built over 15 years overwhelmingly from RSUs/PSUs, minimal cash purchases. Directors each <0.03%.
Insider activity (12 mo)
Sales, one token buy. Krebs sold ~125k (Sep 2025); Watkinson 39k @ US$18.60 (Jun 2026); director Thompson 25k, CFO Whelan 6k, GC Nault 20k (Aug–Sep 2026). Only cash purchase: EVP Exploration Aoife McGrath, 635 shares @ US$16.95 (Jun 2026). ~US$1.8M sold vs US$11k bought. The August–September sales came after the Q2 miss, at US$18–21.
Strategic & prominent
None. BlackRock 11.7% (120.8M, Jun 2026 — largest; inflated by ex-New Gold index shares), Van Eck 6.5% (67.0M), Vanguard ~6% via sub-entities, Arrowstreet 4.4%, Global X 2.8%, CalSTRS 2.6%, State Street 2.3%, Sprott 7.5M (trimmed 19%). Ex-New Gold holders (~38% at close) have dispersed into index funds. No Sprott/Lassonde/Lundin block.
Institutions / retail
Institutions ~58–63%, insiders ~0.6–0.9%, retail ~37–41%. ~1,028M shares (Aug 3, 2026); US$750M buyback (5.98M bought in Q2 for US$110M; ~US$629M remaining); US$0.02 semi-annual dividend.

Read: Same read as Pan American — insider ownership is not the lever at this size — but with a worse detail: officers and a director sold into the post-miss bounce in August and September, while the company was buying back stock. That is not a vote of confidence in the H2 delivery the multiple depends on. BlackRock's 11.7% is passive index weight, not a view.

Jurisdiction risk

National: the cleanest set of the four. Canada (~40% of Q2 revenue), USA (~28%), Mexico (~32%). No permit, royalty or community disputes found in 2025–26. Mexico exposure is two operating underground mines with existing concessions (Palmarejo, Las Chispas) — the 2023 mining-law reform bites on new concessions and open pits, neither of which Coeur needs. The only structural Mexican drag is contractual: the Franco-Nevada stream on Palmarejo.

Local: low everywhere; Wharf (South Dakota) and Rochester (Nevada) are decades-old operations.

Jurisdiction is not why the stock is cheap. Execution is.

Differentiator
  1. All-North-American senior scale with a copper by-product — the only one at this size.
  2. Las Chispas — US$841/oz gold CAS and US$13.27/oz silver CAS, the lowest-cost asset in the file after Juanicipio, with 2025 discoveries (Augusta, La Promesa) already in reserves.
  3. The balance sheet turn — debt cut 42% in 2025 to US$341M before New Gold, net cash after it, revolver undrawn, a US$750M buyback and a dividend, ratings up three notches in eighteen months.
  4. Rochester's expansion is built — 6.8 Mt crushed in Q2, 97% through all three stages — so the fix is operating, not capital.

Read it honestly: the differentiator (a bought-in senior portfolio) and the gate (running it) are the same fact. Coeur has never operated Rainy River or New Afton through a full year.

Exploration upside

Brownfield conversion · moves the needle: low–medium. US$147–169M budget; Palmarejo drilling >70% outside the Franco-Nevada stream area (the one exploration program that changes economics, not just ounces); New Afton K-Zone maiden resource (715 koz Au / 606 Mlb Cu); Silvertip PFS early 2027 (57.6 Moz Ag, 1.23 Blb Zn) is the only new-mine option.

Reserve life is the quiet issue: Kensington 5 years, Rainy River to 2035.

Next Catalyst

Q3 results (early Nov) — Rochester's H2 silver "spike", Rainy River UG tonnage, New Afton C-Zone, the last ~US$38M of PPA step-up; year-end ramp targets (5,000 tpd RR; 16k tpd NA); combined-company reserve statement in Feb 2027; Silvertip PFS early 2027; buyback pace (US$629M of the US$750M remaining).

Open Questions
  • Does Rochester finally deliver a guided year — and if H2 needs 70% of annual silver, what is the realistic 2026 outcome?
  • What do Rainy River and New Afton cost to run once PPA noise clears — is Rainy River really a US$2,700–3,000 CAS mine?
  • How much of the US$2.3B 2026 EBITDA target is price (deck US$4,000 / US$60) versus volume?
  • Does Kensington's 5-year reserve life get extended, or is it a wind-down?
  • At ~6.7× target EBITDA with net cash, is the discount to Pan American execution risk or dilution memory?

The 29 Sep deck shows US$221M of buybacks since May, an H2 weighted to Q4 (Q3 the peak capex quarter), and the 2026 targets struck at US$4,400 gold / US$66 silver — above today's spot.

Q2 2026 (Aug 5)

Record production and FCF; adj. EPS US$0.12 miss on US$264M PPA inventory uplift; guidance cut (Au 630–750 koz, Cu 40–50 Mlb), capex raised to US$520–605M, EBITDA/FCF targets to ~US$2.3B / ~US$1.5B; deck cut to US$4,000 / US$60 / US$6. Stock −8.5%.

New Gold (closed Mar 20, 2026)

0.4959 CDE per NGD share; 392.7M shares issued at US$17.67 (~US$6.9B). Brought Rainy River (2.2 Moz Au P&P) and New Afton (0.78 Moz Au, 591 Mlb Cu). New Gold's US$400M 6.875% 2032 notes exchanged into Coeur paper (96.45% tendered). Revolver replaced with US$1.0B facility.

Rochester history

2025 guidance cut in Q3 2025 (Ag 7.0–8.3 → 6.0–6.7 Moz); FY2025 actual 60.2 koz / 6.1 Moz. H1 2026 ~26 koz / 2.6 Moz against 70–90 koz / 6.4–7.8 Moz. Wharf crusher fire (Nov 2025) halved Q1 output; new crusher commissioned Q2, US$20M insurance received.

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 4/5 · Candour 4/5 · Skin in the game 2/5

Hits annual guidance and reports bad news plainly; Rochester came in 72% over budget, Silvertip was written off, and the New Gold block cave is new ground.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Mitchell J. Krebs (Chairman, President & CEO, since CEO since July 2011; joined Coeur 1995; chairman later (date unverified)): Ex-CFO of Coeur; has run the company through the Silvertip write-off, the Rochester build and the SilverCrest and New Gold deals. · Michael (Mick) Routledge (SVP & COO, since 2020 (unverified)): Ran Rochester commissioning and ramp-up; 2025 pay US$3.07M. · Thomas S. Whelan (SVP & CFO, since 2019 (unverified)): 2025 pay US$2.81M.
Track record
  • Silvertip (BC): bought 2017 for up to US$250M, suspended Feb 2020 with a US$251M impairment, i.e. a full write-off within ~2.5 yearssource
  • Rochester expansion: original estimate ~US$425M and completion early 2023; final cost US$730M (+72%), commercial production 31 Mar 2024; Krebs: 'Once you push Go on a project like this, you can't push Pause'source
  • SilverCrest / Las Chispas: closed 14 Feb 2025; Las Chispas generated US$286M FCF for Coeur by end-2025; debt cut 42% to US$341M, cash US$554M at end-2025source
  • 2025 production inside guidance at all five mines: 419koz Au vs ~415koz guide, 17.9Moz Ag vs ~17.6Moz guide (same source)
  • New Gold: ~US$7B all-stock acquisition announced Nov 2025 (stock fell on announcement), closed March 2026; two New Gold directors joined the board (https://www.mining.com/coeur-mining-buys-new-gold-in-7b-all-stock-merger/ ; https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CDE/pre-14a-coeur-mining-inc-preliminary-proxy-statement-2cf5c2c926fe.html)
  • Wins (Las Chispas FCF, Rochester ramp, deleveraging) came in the 2024-26 gold/silver bull cycle; misses (Silvertip, Rochester overrun) came in 2019-23.

Boards today: Krebs: Coeur (chair+CEO) only known public role (other boards unverified).

Fit to this job
Long-time multi-mine open-pit/heap-leach and underground operator in US and Mexico; same job for 15 years. New for them: New Afton block-cave and Rainy River open pit in Canada (Coeur has never run a block cave) and integrating a company of similar size; capital-project record (Rochester) shows weak cost control on builds.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake from grants or cheap founder paper; little buying. Krebs 2025 total pay US$6.6M (salary US$850k; stock awards US$4.2M; cash bonus US$1.4M), +51% y/y; say-on-pay 97%; annual incentive paid 133% of target, 2023-25 LTIP 166%. Insider ownership % and open-market buying not found in sources fetched (unverified). Sources: https://gloom.sh/stocks/cde/proxy/2026 ; https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/CDE/pre-14a-coeur-mining-inc-preliminary-proxy-statement-2cf5c2c926fe.html

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Rochester capex +72% vs the 2020 estimate and ~1 year late.
  • Silvertip: full write-off of a US$250M acquisition within 2.5 years.
  • Two large stock-funded acquisitions in 13 months (SilverCrest ~US$1.7B, New Gold ~US$7B) at the top of the cycle; integration risk.

Thesis

Equinox has changed shape three times since mid-2025: Calibre (Jun 2025) brought Valentine and Nicaragua; Brazil (three mines) was sold to CMOC for US$900M + US$115M contingent (Jan 2026) and the proceeds retired nearly US$1B of debt; Orla Mining (Jul 31, 2026) brought Musselwhite, Camino Rojo and South Railroad for 378M shares. The result: seven mines, 22.7 Moz of reserves, 2026 guidance 870–920 koz (pro forma ~1.1 Moz/yr), a 15-year Canadian core (Greenstone 5.3 Moz + Valentine 2.75 Moz, guided to average 543 koz/yr for a decade), US$1.2B of liquidity and net cash US$214M ex-converts, a dividend raised 50% to US$0.0225/qtr, and a 5% buyback. H1 2026: revenue US$1.63B, adjusted EBITDA US$885M, mine-site FCF US$633M, realised gold US$4,440. Then the cost side: Q2 AISC US$2,175/oz, 2026 AISC guidance raised from US$1,775–1,875 to US$1,900–2,000, Valentine's from US$1,200–1,300 to US$2,000–2,200; Greenstone's recovery stuck near 80% on arsenopyrite; Valentine's Phase 2 (US$436M, 5 Mtpa, late 2028) approved anyway. Leadership: Greg Smith out (Jul 2025), Darren Hall (ex-Calibre) CEO until Oct 31, 2026, then Jason Simpson (ex-Orla); Ross Beaty now Chair Emeritus; Chuck Jeannes Chair. Consensus Buy, avg target C$24.50 vs ~C$17.50.

The Gate

Making Greenstone and Valentine run at design — the two mines the whole re-rate rests on, and the two that have missed every year since they opened. Greenstone: guidance cut in Oct 2024 and Jun 2025; recovery ~80% vs. design on higher arsenopyrite; mill now at nameplate 27,000 tpd on 69% of days but grade ~1.0 g/t against a 1.16 g/t ten-year plan. Valentine: capex C$508M → C$653M under Calibre; Q1 2026 grade reconciliation miss; now at 113% of nameplate but AISC guided US$2,000–2,200 — and Phase 2 doubles it before Phase 1 has delivered a clean year.

Sub-gates
  1. Cost position — a US$2,000+ AISC producer earns well at US$4,300 gold and is the first to bleed at US$3,000; fuel assumed +50% in the revised guide.
  2. Nicaragua — ~25% of guided ounces under a US executive order that authorises sanctions on anyone "operating in the gold sector"; Treasury sanctioned seven Nicaraguan gold companies in April 2026 (not Equinox), and Q2 output there fell from 81k to 59k oz without explanation.
  3. Integration and churn — three mergers, a share count from 630M to 1,168M, two CEOs in fifteen months and a third arriving in November.
  4. Los Filos — restarting under 20-year community agreements after a two-year shutdown, still excluded from guidance.

Every cost number in the 2026 guide went the wrong way in August. The market pays up for this name when the Canadian mines finally print a quarter at plan — that quarter has not happened yet.

Valuation Anchor

~8.8× trailing EBITDA on a pre-merger base, ~4× on a pro forma that assumes the ramps work — the widest gap between 'trailing' and 'promised' of any producer in the file. If Greenstone reaches 87% recovery and 1.16 g/t, Valentine prints a US$1,600 AISC year, and Musselwhite and Camino Rojo contribute as guided, this is a 1.1 Moz, US$1,800 AISC senior at 4–5× EBITDA with net cash — and the C$24–27 targets are conservative. If the Canadian mines keep missing, it is a US$2,100 AISC producer whose earnings halve at US$3,500 gold, at a beta of 3. The stock's 38% fall from the Orla-announcement high while gold held US$4,000+ is the market moving from the first reading toward the second. Reserve life (22.7 Moz) and jurisdiction (majority Canadian) are the floor; costs and execution are the ceiling.

Read: A senior-style register — index funds, Fidelity, Van Eck — with two named votes that arrived through a deal rather than a cheque: Fairfax and Lassonde came from Orla and did not choose Equinox at today's price. Beaty's stake is real and founder-earned but is now under 3% and he has stepped back. Nobody inside has sold meaningfully; nobody has bought meaningfully either. Ownership is neither a warning nor an endorsement here — the numbers in the Numbers tab are.

Jurisdiction risk

National: majority tier-one, with one live sanctions exposure. Canada (Greenstone, Valentine, Musselwhite — ~55% of guided ounces, First Nations agreements in place at all three, Valentine Phase 2 permitting underway); USA (Mesquite, Castle Mountain in FAST-41, South Railroad ROD received); Mexico (Camino Rojo operating; Los Filos restarting under 20-year agreements with all three communities after a two-year blockade); Nicaragua ~25% — US EO 13851 authorises sanctions on the gold sector and import bans; Treasury designated seven Nicaraguan gold entities on Apr 16, 2026; the 2022 BHMB expropriation is precedent; Equinox is not named and books no risk premium. Brazil exited Jan 2026 (US$115M contingent receivable Jan 2027).

Local: the Los Filos precedent — an ejido refused to renew and the mine stopped for two years — is the template for what local licence risk looks like in this portfolio; now resolved on paper.

Diversified enough that no single licence matters — except Nicaragua, where the risk is a Treasury press release, not a community.

Differentiator
  1. The largest Canadian-weighted reserve base among mid-tier and senior gold producers, freshly net-cash. 8.1 Moz of Canadian reserves at Greenstone and Valentine guided to 543 koz/yr for a decade, plus Musselwhite — a long-life core in the safest jurisdiction, which is exactly what the generalist gold investor pays for.
  2. The balance sheet turn — >US$1.1B of debt retired in twelve months, from net debt US$1.2B to net cash, revolver undrawn, converts converting, a dividend and a buyback where a year ago there was a Sprott loan and a gold prepay.
  3. A pipeline with permits — Valentine Phase 2 approved, South Railroad with its federal ROD, Castle Mountain in FAST-41, Los Filos back on paper: ~600 koz/yr of growth by 2029 without a new acquisition.
  4. Camino Rojo — the lowest-cost asset (AISC ~US$865) with a large sulphide deposit underneath it, and Pierre Lassonde and Fairfax on the register from Orla.

Read it honestly: the differentiator (a big Canadian reserve base) is why the stock trades at a senior's EV/oz, and the gate (those same Canadian mines missing plan) is why it trades at a junior's EV/EBITDA. Same fact, two sides — and the same story as Coeur, one year behind.

Exploration upside

Brownfield, large budget · moves the needle: low–medium. US$110–120M of growth exploration: Greenstone underground (1.63 Moz M&I @ 2.36 g/t below the pit), Valentine depth, Camino Rojo sulphides (portal and decline in 2026), Musselwhite life extension (the shortest reserve life in the group at ~6 years). With 22.7 Moz of reserves, exploration is about reserve life at the short-life assets, not the investment case.

Musselwhite's six-year life is the quiet number in a 22.7 Moz reserve base.

Next Catalyst

Q3 results (early Nov) — Greenstone recovery and grade, Valentine unit costs, first Orla contribution, Nicaragua explanation; CEO transition Nov 1 (Jason Simpson); convert redemption Oct 20; Castle Mountain federal permits (Dec 2026); Los Filos restart in 2027 guidance (Feb 2027); Brazil contingent US$115M (Jan 2027); Valentine Phase 2 and South Railroad construction milestones through 2028.

Open Questions
  • Does Greenstone ever reach 87% recovery on arsenopyrite-bearing ore — and if not, what is the honest ten-year AISC?
  • Why was Valentine's 2026 AISC guide raised US$850/oz in one revision, and how much of Phase 2's US$436M is fixing Phase 1?
  • What happened to Nicaraguan production in Q2 (81k → 59k oz), and what is the plan if Treasury widens the gold-sector sanctions?
  • What does Jason Simpson keep, sell or fix — Mesquite (US$2,500 AISC), Nicaragua, Los Filos?
  • At a 2.4–3.4 beta and US$2,000+ AISC, what is the earnings profile at US$3,500 gold — and does the dividend survive it?
  • Is 4× pro forma EBITDA a bargain or a warning that the market does not believe the pro forma?

Effect on the odds: chance it works 35% → 32%, odds of a 3× 7% → 7%.

People
Jason Simpson (CEO (from Nov 1, 2026), since Nov 1, 2026): Ex-CEO Orla Mining (2019-2026, unverified dates); came with the Orla merger closed Jul 31, 2026. Third CEO in 15 months. Holding: Orla-derived shares, size unknown. · Darren Hall (CEO (retiring Oct 31, 2026), since Jul 22, 2025): Age 61. Ex-CEO Calibre Mining 2021-25, ex-COO Kirkland Lake and Newmarket Gold, ~30 years Newmont. Took over when Greg Smith stepped down after the Greenstone miss. · Chuck Jeannes (Chair, since Jul 31, 2026 (Orla close)): Ex-CEO Goldcorp. · Ross Beaty (Chair Emeritus / Special Advisor, founder, since Chair Dec 2017 – Jul 2026; Chair Emeritus since the Orla close): Age 74. Founder of Pan American Silver, Lumina group, Alterra. Largest individual holder (~27M shares, ~2.3% post-Orla).
Track record
  • Beaty: founded Pan American Silver (1994) and the Lumina Copper group (projects sold to several buyers for >US$1.5B combined, 2000s-2010s) — multiple hits across cycles (unverified amounts; https://www.equinoxgold.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/2026-Management-Information-Circular.pdf for current role)
  • Equinox under Greg Smith (CEO 2019-Jul 2025): grew to ~900 koz via acquisitions (Leagold, Premier, Calibre) but missed original production guidance in 2022 and 2024 and cut Greenstone's 2025 guidance 300-350 -> 220-260 koz in Jun 2025; Smith left six weeks later (https://magazine.cim.org/en/news/2025/equinox-gold-sees-a-slow-start-at-greenstone-mine-en/ ; https://www.equinoxgold.com/news/equinox-gold-announces-senior-leadership-transition/)
  • Greenstone: commercial production Nov 2024, nameplate 27,000 tpd first held over 30 days in Dec 2025, 13 months latersource
  • Capital allocation: Calibre merger C$2.6B (Jun 2025), Orla merger (Jul 2026), Brazil sold for up to US$1.015B, Nevada US$115M, >US$1.1B debt reduced, first dividend 2026 (Q4 2025 release; https://www.equinoxgold.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/20260805-EQX-Q2-Financial-Results-News-Release-final.pdf)
  • Los Filos (Mexico) suspended indefinitely Apr 2025 after community agreement failed; restart only 'gradual' (Q2 2026 release)
  • 2025 actual 922.8 koz vs 750-915 koz revised guidance (beat); 2026 guidance 870-920 koz post-Orla (Q2 2026 release)

Boards today: Hall: 1 (Equinox). Beaty: Equinox chair; other public boards not listed in the circular (he also holds Pan American/Lumina-related roles historically, unverified today).

Fit to this job
Hall is a genuine operator (Newmont, Kirkland Lake, Calibre) and is the right fit for a multi-mine Americas producer — but he leaves in four weeks. Simpson built and ran Orla's Camino Rojo heap leach (Mexico) and Musselwhite acquisition; he has not run a 27,000 tpd hard-rock open-pit mill like Greenstone at this scale (unverified). Greenstone's ramp-up is the piece the company has not done before and it took a year longer than guided.
Skin & pay
4/5 — meaningful stake with real market buying. Beaty holds ~25.05M shares (plus 143k DSUs, 119k RSUs) — founder capital, worth several hundred million US$; strongest insider alignment in the batch. Hall holds 1.71M shares + 0.79M options (largely from Calibre rollover). Hall 2025 total comp not extracted (circular p.41+); Smith severance not extracted. Say-on-pay 2025 not extracted. Insider trading pattern not checked. Source: https://www.equinoxgold.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/2026-Management-Information-Circular.pdf

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Three CEOs in 15 months (Smith -> Hall -> Simpson)
  • Original annual guidance missed in 2022, 2024 and 2025 (Greenstone); met only on revised ranges
  • Two large stock mergers in 13 months (Calibre, Orla) — serial dilution to grow, though assets sold for cash
  • Los Filos indefinite suspension

What the numbers say
  1. Debt was cut from $1.78B in June 2025 to $583M by June 2026 using $845M of Brazil sale proceeds; net debt is $265M with $560M undrawn on the revolver.
  2. Capex stays heavy at $692M in FY25 and $390M in H1 2026, about 60% growth spend; G&A is about $105M a year, roughly 5% of revenue.
  3. Shares rose from 318M in December 2023 to about 1,167M after the July 2026 Orla merger, following the Greenstone raise and Calibre deal; a quarterly dividend started in 2026.
  4. Revenue scaled from $1.09B in FY23 to $1.63B in H1 2026 alone on gold price, but AISC rose to $2,175/oz in Q2 2026, so margin gains are price-driven.
  5. Operating cash flow was $818M in FY25 and $440M in H1 2026; free cash flow after capex and interest was about zero in FY25 and about $19M in H1 2026.

Gate Côté Gold has to sustain nameplate and then step up — turning a 20.3 Moz resource into reserves at lower unit cost — while Essakane keeps sending cash out of Burkina Faso. Thesis

Three mines: Côté Gold (Ontario; 70% with Sumitomo 30% — IAMGOLD let its stake dilute to 60.3% in 2022–23 and bought the 9.7% back for US$377M in Dec 2024; nameplate 36,000 tpd first reached Jun 2025; 2026 guide 270–310 koz attributable at AISC US$1,775–1,925 incl. the 7.5% Franco-Nevada gross-margin royalty; reserves 7.04 Moz, 16–18 years; Côté+Gosselin M&I 20.3 Moz), Essakane (Burkina Faso; 85% after the state lifted itself to 15% by decree in Jun 2025; 340–380 koz at AISC US$2,000–2,150; sliding royalty 8%+ now 12%; reserves 1.68 Moz, ~4 years, extension to 2034–35 under study; US$680.7M repatriated in H1 2026) and Westwood (Québec; 110–130 koz at AISC US$1,950–2,100; 6.67 g/t reserves; bulk-mining study for ~200 koz by 2030).

2025: 765.9 koz attributable at AISC US$1,900. 2026 guide 720–820 koz, H2-weighted. H1 2026: 371.7 koz, revenue US$1,887M, adj. EBITDA US$1,174M (62% margin), mine-site FCF US$894M at US$4,631 realised; AISC US$2,195 incl. royalties — above the top of the guide. Balance sheet: net debt US$813M (Sep 2025) → net cash US$52M (Jun 2026) while buying back 27.9M shares for US$510M (avg US$18.28); only the US$450M 5.75% notes (Oct 2028) remain; prepays gone; liquidity US$1.35B. Reserves 9.9 Moz (7.5 attributable) fell 7% in 2025; the Nelligan district in Québec (Northern Superior, ~US$329M, Dec 2025) adds 4.3 Moz Indicated + 7.5 Moz Inferred, PEA mid-2027.

CEO Renaud Adams since Apr 2023 (ex-New Gold): delivered the Côté ramp, the Sumitomo buy-back and the deleveraging; stated strategy is optimisation, capital returns (dividend flagged for early 2027) and 'no M&A — more likely a target'. Thirteen analysts, consensus Buy, average US$24.33. At US$18.44 the stock is ~26% off its Feb–Mar high, ~4.7× TTM EBITDA, ~9× P/E.

The Gate

Côté Gold has to sustain nameplate and then step up — turning a 20.3 Moz resource into reserves at lower unit cost — while Essakane keeps sending cash out of Burkina Faso.

The market pays ~5–6× EBITDA for a company with net cash and 80% of its NAV in Ontario and Québec because ~47% of the ounces and most of the repatriable cash come from a junta with a 12% sliding royalty, and because the cost base sits at the third/fourth-quartile boundary (~74th percentile on guidance, ~82nd on Q2). The gate is whether the Canadian half grows into the valuation before the Burkina half becomes the story.

Sub-gates
  1. H2 delivery: ~350–450 koz attributable in H2 (H1 was 371.7 koz, 48% of the mid-point) with Côté ≥ 150–190 koz — ~13 Mt at ≥ 1.1 g/t.
  2. Costs: AISC inside US$2,000–2,150 incl. royalties by Q4 2026; royalties alone ran ~US$380/oz in H1.
  3. Côté technical report (Q4 2026): reserves materially above 7.04 Moz, a 36k→~40k tpd plan with AISC going down, and a reserve gold price near the US$2,100 management mentioned.
  4. Essakane: ~US$400M repatriated in 2026 as in 2025 (US$680.7M); H1 2027 report extends mine life to 2034–35; no escalation beyond convoy attacks.
  5. Capital returns without re-levering: NCIB renewal, dividend from early 2027, and a decision on the Franco-Nevada 25% royalty tranche (floor US$262.5M) by ~Apr 2027.

Figure used: 2026 guidance midpoint, US$2,075/oz including royalties (US$2,000–2,150, royalties modelled at US$4,000 gold). Q2 actual US$2,271 → ~82nd; at the curve's ~US$4,860 gold, royalties add ~US$100–150 (~79th).

At the 3rd/4th-quartile boundary: high third quartile on guidance, fourth on Q2. The driver is Burkina Faso's sliding royalty at Essakane (12% at Q2 prices) — structural. The fix is Côté at nameplate, then ~40k tpd; the Q4 2026 Côté technical report should show whether AISC can fall.

How to read it: picture every primary gold mine in the world lined up from cheapest to most expensive to run (all-in sustaining cost per ounce, weighted by output). The percentile is the share of world output that costs less; the middle line splits the cheaper half from the costlier half. Lower-half mines keep earning when the metal price falls. Dot = 2026, ring = 2025. Gold curve: Metals Focus / World Gold Council, Q1 2026 (average US$1,785/oz; the quartile lines are estimates). Approximate — it ranks the names, it is not decimal-precise.

Valuation Anchor

~4.7× trailing EBITDA, ~5.6× at spot, ~US$1,400 per attributable reserve ounce, ~9× earnings — a 30–40% discount to senior gold producers on multiples, and the discount is for two things the balance sheet no longer explains: Burkina Faso and a US$2,200 cost base. Net cash, no streams and ~80% of NAV in Canada are not priced.

The case: the Q4 Côté report converts a large part of 20 Moz into reserves with a 40k tpd, sub-US$1,800 AISC plan, Essakane is extended to 2035 and the dividend starts — a ~US$2.0B EBITDA business re-rating from ~5.6× to 7–8× is ~US$14–17B of EV, ~1.3–1.6× today before any help from gold, which is where the sell-side average of US$24 sits. The bear case: Côté stalls at 36k tpd with grades drifting toward the 0.75 g/t resource average, Essakane's extension is uneconomic under a 12%+ royalty, and gold at US$3,000 cuts EBITDA in half — the multiple then stays at 5–6× on a shrinking number.

Honest read on the register: the company bought 27.9M shares at ~US$18 while the COO, CFO and directors sold ~C$9M at C$31–33 in Feb–Mar. The buyback is the alignment; the insiders are not.

Bucket: producer / cash flow, the turnaround-to-compounder end of it — a B2Gold-shaped discount (a jurisdiction and a cost line) with a cleaner balance sheet and a dated Canadian catalyst.

Shareholder structure
Management & board
Well under 1%. Positions built from RSU and option vesting rather than open-market buying: COO Bruno Lemelin and CFO Maarten Theunissen are the largest known; director David Smith held 20,000 shares after his Feb 2026 sale. Catherine McLeod-Seltzer joined the board 1 Sep 2026. No precise percentage disclosed in the sources fetched.
Insider activity (12 mo)
Net selling, clustered at the top. COO Lemelin ~156k shares 25–26 Feb 2026 (~C$4.95M at C$31–32) + ~22k on 4 Mar; CFO Theunissen ~61k on 26 Feb (~C$2.0M); director Smith 31,000 on 27 Feb (C$1.02M, SEC Form 4); director Toutant ~13.7k on 20 Feb; SVP Quinn ~44.7k on 9 Mar. Buys: Lemelin ~9.9k at C$20.35 (13 Nov 2025); reported May 2026 buys by director Racine and officer Shah come from a source with corrupted price fields — unverified. The company bought 27.9M shares for US$510M (avg US$18.28) over the same period.
Strategic & prominent
No strategic equity holder. Sumitomo Metal Mining owns 30% of Côté at the asset level (a future buy-out counterparty either way); the Government of Burkina Faso 15% of Essakane; Franco-Nevada holds the Côté royalty (bought for US$1.05B in May 2025).
Institutions / retail
Widely held — GDX/GDXJ and Canadian/US institutions dominate; 13 covering analysts. ~571M shares; NCIB authorised for up to 57M (9.9% of float) to ~Dec 2026, 27.9M used by 5 Aug. Top-holder percentages not verified.

Read: Management's realised behaviour was to sell meaningfully at C$31–33 in February and March, right at the high, while the company bought at US$18–20. That is the honest read: the register is being de-risked by the corporate buyback, not accumulated by the people running it. No activist, no strategic overhang, and Sumitomo's 30% at Côté is the obvious strategic conversation if the stock stays at 5× — Adams himself says 'more likely a target than an acquirer'.

Jurisdiction risk

Burkina Faso is the layer that prices the stock — ~47% of ounces and most of the repatriable cash. Military junta under Capt. Traoré since Sep 2022, out of ECOWAS since Jan 2025, Russia-aligned; a 2024 mining-code revision; an Apr 2025 royalty decree (8% minimum above US$3,000 gold, +1% per US$500 — 12% at Q2 2026 prices, ~30% of cash costs); a Jun 2025 decree that lifted the state's Essakane stake from 10% to 15%. Jihadist attacks on supply convoys in 2024–25 (convoys suspended, one injured); Q1 2026 had no significant incidents, Q2's MD&A says they are 'still occurring' and pressuring supply chains. Repatriation has worked: US$680.7M out in H1 2026; a further ~US$500M declared for 2026 at the Essakane level (~US$425M attributable at 85%). Essakane sits in Oudalan near the Niger and Mali borders, with a 4-year reserve and diesel exposure (oil US$25–30/bbl over budget ≈ US$35/oz).

Ontario (Côté): tier-1; agreements with Mattagami and Flying Post First Nations; grid-power access and provincial mining tax are the live items; any expansion beyond debottlenecking needs new permitting with baseline work from 2027. Québec (Westwood, Nelligan): tier-1, Plan Nord-friendly; Nelligan in the Chibougamau area under Cree and Québec consultation. Senegal exposure ended with the Bambadji sale (Aug 2026). Local: no material community dispute reported at any of the three mines in 2025–26.

A three-mine portfolio where one mine carries half the ounces, most of the free cash and all of the discount — the same shape as B2Gold, with the Canadian half larger and longer-lived.

Differentiator

The only mid-tier with a brand-new, 18-year, tier-1 bulk mine whose resource has doubled to 20 Moz since it was sanctioned. Most peers' growth is brownfield or in riskier countries; Côté's is in Ontario, already built, and the next step (40k tpd) is debottlenecking rather than a new build.

  1. The balance-sheet inflection just happened — a US$865M net-debt swing in nine months to net cash, with US$1.35B of liquidity and no streams, prepays or converts.
  2. A return engine already running — US$510M of buybacks in eight months (~45% of mine-site FCF) with a dividend flagged for early 2027.
  3. ~40 Moz of Canadian resources (Côté/Gosselin + the Nelligan district) with ~80% of NAV in Canada — a scarce, low-royalty Canadian growth pipeline.
  4. Embedded options — 50% of the Franco-Nevada royalty can be bought back at terms struck in a lower-gold world; Essakane underground; Westwood bulk mining.
  5. Management that says no — no M&A, Bambadji sold, cheap Québec ground bought, dividend only after net cash.

Counterweight: a cost base at the third/fourth-quartile boundary (AISC US$2,195–2,271 incl. royalties — thin margins at US$3,000); ~47% of ounces and most near-term cash from Burkina Faso with a 4-year reserve; reserves −7% in 2025; and insiders who sold ~C$9M at the highs. The Côté story is real; the stock price is still a Burkina price.

Exploration upside

Reserve conversion at Côté, with a long-dated Québec district · moves the needle: medium. 2026 budget US$54M (mostly expensed): 30,000 m at Côté/Gosselin (infill + extension, incl. the new Saddle zone between the pits) feeding the Q4 2026 reserve; ~US$24M at the Nelligan complex (4.3 Moz Indicated + 7.5 Moz Inferred) feeding the mid-2027 PEA; Essakane drilling for the H1 2027 extension. The lever is conversion, not discovery: the Jun 2026 update took Côté+Gosselin M&I to 20.34 Moz (+2.2 Moz) and Inferred to 3.48 Moz (+61%). Nelligan is 2033–35 production at best — optionality the market carries at roughly nothing.

Next Catalyst

5 Nov 2026: Q3 results (Côté 64.4 koz attributable pre-released 21 Oct; AISC vs the guide); Q4 2026: Côté mine plan and reserve, technical report shortly after — 36k→~40k tpd plan, reserve gold price; ~Dec: NCIB renewal; Feb 2027: FY results, 2027 guidance, dividend initiation; early 2027: third Vertimill at Côté; ~Apr/May 2027: Franco-Nevada royalty tranche-1 decision (≥US$262.5M); H1 2027: Essakane extension report; mid-2027: Nelligan PEA; H2 2027: Westwood report; Oct 2028: notes maturity.

Open Questions
  • Does H2 Côté deliver ≥150–190 koz attributable (13 Mt at ≥1.1 g/t) to hit 720–820 koz, and does AISC come back inside US$2,000–2,150?
  • What reserve, throughput and AISC profile does the Q4 Côté report show — and at what gold price?
  • Does IAMGOLD exercise the Franco-Nevada 25% buy-back (floor US$262.5M) by ~Apr 2027, and does Sumitomo fund its 30%?
  • Can Essakane be extended to 2034–35 economically under a 12%+ sliding royalty — and does the junta leave 85/15 and repatriation alone?
  • What is the 2027 dividend framework — fixed base or a share of FCF — and does it come out of the NCIB?
  • Why did the COO, CFO and directors sell ~C$9M at C$31–33 while the company bought at US$18–20?
Context & updates
21 Oct 2026 update

Côté pre-release (21 Oct): Q3 64.4 koz attributable, Q2 67.3 koz; 2026 attributable production guided to the lower end of 270–310 koz after an extended August shutdown and a Vertimill outage. September ran a record 37,100 tpd (103% of nameplate) with no contractor crushing; a third Vertimill is due early 2027 and the updated mine plan and reserve in Q4 2026 with a technical report shortly after, targeting ~40,000 tpd. Odds unchanged.

3 Oct 2026 refresh

No release since 9 Sep. The company frames Q4 as the Côté mine plan and reserve, with the NI 43-101 report 'shortly thereafter'. Burkina Faso opened a state gold refinery on 28 Sep and President Traoré wants all metals refined at home — no rule for industrial mines yet, but a watch item for Essakane doré.

Q2 2026 and the September de-rating (Aug–Sep 2026)

Q2: 188.1 koz, adj. EBITDA US$507M, mine-site FCF US$369M; H1 AISC US$2,195 incl. royalties vs the US$2,000–2,150 guide — royalties ~US$380/oz and diesel. Bambadji (Senegal) sold for ~US$70M (10 Aug). Jefferies initiated at Buy/US$24 (21 Aug). At Mining Forum Americas (28 Sep) Adams ruled out M&A and framed Côté 40k tpd, Essakane to 2035 and Westwood 200 koz as the plan. Shares to ~US$18.4 as gold hit ~US$4,150.

Resource growth: Nelligan and Côté+Gosselin 20.3 Moz (Dec 2025 – Jun 2026)

Northern Superior (~US$329M) and Orbec (~US$14M) acquired Dec 2025 to form the Nelligan Mining Complex (4.3 Moz Ind. / 7.5 Moz Inf., 17 Feb 2026). YE2025 reserves 9.9 Moz (−7%) but M&I 31.0 Moz (+16%). 1 Jun 2026: unified Côté+Gosselin model 20.34 Moz M&I (+12%), 3.48 Moz Inferred (+61%) at US$2,500 gold; technical report Q4 2026.

Net debt to net cash, US$510M of buybacks (Sep 2025 – Aug 2026)

Net debt US$813M (Sep 2025) → US$344M (YE2025) → net cash US$52M (Jun 2026); revolver repaid and upsized to US$850M to 2030; prepay deliveries finished H1 2025. NCIB from Dec 2025 for up to 57M shares; 27.9M bought for US$510M (avg US$18.28) by 5 Aug. Dividend flagged for early 2027.

Burkina Faso tightens Essakane's terms (Apr–Jun 2025)

Royalty decree: 8% minimum above US$3,000 gold, +1% per US$500 (12% in Q2 2026); a June decree lifted the state's stake from 10% to 15% (IAMGOLD 90% → 85%). Essakane still paid a ~US$855M 2025 dividend (US$680.7M to IAMGOLD, fully repatriated by Jun 2026) and declared ~US$500M for 2026 (Essakane level; ~US$425M attributable at 85%).

Côté at nameplate; 70% restored (Dec 2024 – Jun 2025)

The 9.7% diluted interest bought back from Sumitomo for US$377M (closed Dec 2024). Côté first averaged 36,000 tpd in Jun 2025; Q4 2025 a record 2.9 Mt milled; Q1 2026 held back by a conveyor failure (replaced May); June 2026 >1.0 Mt at nameplate, 1.12 g/t, 93% recovery. Franco-Nevada bought the 7.5% royalty for US$1.05B in May 2025.

Simplified from the original filings (last 8 quarters and 3 fiscal years, US$ millions, fiscal year ends 31 Dec). Every column links to the statements it came from.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash rose from US$224M in June 2025 to US$501M in June 2026 while debt fell from US$1,062M to US$449M; only the US$450M 2028 senior notes remain.
  2. Sustaining capex runs US$90–100M a quarter and expansion capex US$12–22M; exploration is about US$8M a quarter and G&A US$15–22M, about 2% of revenue.
  3. A buyback launched in December 2025 bought 24.5M shares for US$458M, taking the share count from 591.1M to 574.3M after the February 2024 US$300M bought deal added 85M.
  4. Quarterly revenue went from US$477M in Q1 2025 to US$857–1,030M in H1 2026 with gross margin of 48–55%; AISC rose to US$2,271/oz in Q2 2026 on higher royalties.
  5. Operating cash flow was US$1,143M in FY2025 and US$570M in Q1 2026; Q3 2024 earnings of US$603M were mostly a US$462M Côté impairment reversal.

The largest US silver producer, now debt-free and nearly pure silver after selling Casa Berardi — and priced as the quality name at ~13× EBITDA, with the growth gated by a Yukon permit

Gate Keno Hill has to become a permitted, reliable 440 tpd operation — it is the only large organic silver growth lever (53 Moz of reserves, 13 years) and the reason the silver-linked dividend was scrapped. Sub-gates: (1) Quartz Mining Licence and Water Licence amendments filed and granted under the post-Eagle Yukon regime (no public filing date; mine-waste guidelines being rewritten for spring 2027); (2) 2026 delivered at ≥2.4 Moz (mid of the cut 2.2–2.6 guide) with no repeat of Q1's cold-weather power outage; (3) the water-treatment upgrade and Phase 2W tailings built inside the US$61–65M 2026 growth capex; (4) Keno Hill moved to commercial-production accounting so its AISC becomes visible — expect it well above the US$6–13 consolidated figure; (5) in parallel, the Greens Creek pyrite circuit sanctioned in 2027 for a Q4 2027–H1 2028 start to bridge 15 → 20 Moz.

Deposit P&P 231 Moz Ag at US$25 (Dec 2025; 12–15 yrs by mine) · M&I +161 Moz · 2026 guide 15.1–16.1 Moz Ag + 51–55 koz Au

Funding & next catalyst
Cash
US$483.5M cash + US$152.5M investments (incl. ~65.8M Orezone shares) at 30 Jun 2026; US$500M undrawn revolver to 2030 signed 16 Sep 2026 (+US$100M accordion) → liquidity ~US$1B
Debt
Essentially none — US$12.7M of finance leases at 30 Jun 2026 (10-Q). The US$263M 7.25% notes due 2028 were redeemed at par on 9 Apr 2026. No converts, no streams. The new revolver restricts dividend/capital-stock payments
Burn · runway
Strongly cash-generative: H1 FCF US$279M after ~US$80M capex; 2026 capex US$208–223M + US$55M exploration (record) covered by operating cash flow at silver above ~US$35. Dividend a token US$0.015/yr; no buyback — CEO: returns 'sometime after' cash nears US$1B
Next catalyst
Lucky Friday cooling completion Sep 2026 → Q3 results ~5 Nov → Greens Creek tailings Phase 4 decision Q4 → 2027 guidance Dec/Jan → YE reserves Feb 2027 (re-priced from US$25?) → Yukon guidelines spring 2027 → Keno Hill licence amendments 2027 (undated) → pyrite circuit first production Q4 2027–H1 2028
Funded to the next catalyst Everything in guidance is funded from cash flow. Undefined rather than unfunded: Keno Hill capital beyond 2026, the pyrite circuit, a Midas restart and tailings reprocessing — none has a public capex number, but ~US$1B of liquidity covers any plausible combination. The gap is permits, not money.
Thesis

Three underground mines: Greens Creek (Admiralty Island, Alaska; ~49% of silver, all the gold; 2026 guide 8.0–8.3 Moz Ag + 51–55 koz Au; Q2 AISC −US$10.71/oz after gold/zinc/lead credits; 12-year reserves; record Q2 FCF US$130M), Lucky Friday (Idaho; record 1.53 Moz in Q2, guide 4.9–5.2 Moz; Q2 AISC US$17.08, guide US$24.50–26.00; 15-year reserves; surface cooling project finishing Sep 2026; strike 2017–20, fire 2023) and Keno Hill (Yukon; 2.2–2.6 Moz after two cuts; running ~300–330 tpd against a 440 tpd permit while licence amendments and infrastructure catch up; still 'pre-commercial', so no AISC disclosed; 13-year reserves). Casa Berardi (Québec gold) was sold to Orezone on 25 Mar 2026 for US$160M cash + ~65.8M shares and a royalty (US$130M) + up to US$321M contingent, carried at US$4.2M; gold fell from ~30% to ~14% of revenue. Nevada (Midas, Hollister, Aurora) is exploration with a permitted 1,200 tpd mill.

2025: 17.0 Moz Ag. 2026 guide 15.1–16.1 Moz Ag + 51–55 koz Au at consolidated silver AISC US$12.50–13.50 (lowered from US$15–16.25). H1 2026: revenue US$745M, adj. EBITDA US$464M (62% margin), FCF US$279M; Q2 AISC US$6.07/oz. Q2 realised silver was US$63.06 against a US$73.44 London average and payable sales ran 0.8 Moz below production — a timing question for Q3. Balance sheet: notes redeemed in April, net cash ~US$0.5–0.6B, a new US$500M revolver. Reserves 231 Moz Ag at US$25 silver — a very conservative deck with a Feb 2027 reset coming.

CEO Rob Krcmarov since Nov 2024 (ex-Barrick EVP exploration): sold Casa Berardi, redeemed the debt, slowed Keno Hill to permit properly, removed the silver-linked dividend (Feb 2025), and is explicitly organic-growth-first toward 20+ Moz with shareholder returns deferred until cash nears US$1B. Ten analysts, consensus Buy, target ~US$23. At US$17.03 the stock is ~50% off its US$34.17 high and lost ~15% in September; ~12–13× TTM EBITDA, ~21× P/E.

The Gate

Keno Hill has to become a permitted, reliable 440 tpd operation — it is the only large organic silver growth lever (53 Moz of reserves, 13 years) and the reason the silver-linked dividend was scrapped.

The stock pays ~13× EBITDA and ~21× earnings for the cleanest US-listed silver beta with a fortress balance sheet. That multiple needs EBITDA growth to justify it, and the growth is permits: Keno Hill's guidance has been cut twice in 2026 while Yukon rewrites its rules after the Eagle heap-leach failure.

Sub-gates
  1. Yukon permits: QML and Water Licence amendments for 440 tpd under a regime that has implemented 23 of 56 post-Eagle recommendations and is rewriting mine-waste guidelines (spring 2027). No filing date.
  2. 2026 delivery: ≥ 2.4 Moz at Keno Hill after two cuts (2.9–3.2 → 2.2–2.6); Greens Creek 8.0–8.3 Moz and Lucky Friday 4.9–5.2 Moz as guided.
  3. Infrastructure inside budget: water treatment and Phase 2W tailings within US$61–65M growth capex.
  4. Transparency: commercial-production accounting at Keno Hill — the by-product-flattered consolidated AISC will rise when it is included.
  5. The bridge: Greens Creek pyrite circuit (+1.0–1.2 Moz Ag, 10–15 koz Au) sanctioned 2027, first production Q4 2027–H1 2028; Midas restart decision later.

Cost-curve position

Figure used: 2026 guidance midpoint, US$13.00/oz Ag after gold, zinc and lead credits (US$12.50–13.50, lowered mid-year) — already on the curve's basis. Q2 actual US$6.07 → ~29th.

Mine by mine: Greens Creek (~−US$4) ~6th percentile — consistent with Hecla's "best 15th percentile" claim; Lucky Friday (~US$25) ~77th. Keno Hill is left out until commercial production and will raise the consolidated figure when it is included.

The risk to this position is by-product prices (gold, zinc, lead), not cost inflation. Hecla's "lower end of the silver cost curve" slide holds for Greens Creek; for the company as a whole it is lower half, not bottom quartile.

How to read it: picture every primary silver mine in the world lined up from cheapest to most expensive to run (all-in sustaining cost per ounce, weighted by output). The percentile is the share of world output that costs less; the middle line splits the cheaper half from the costlier half. Lower-half mines keep earning when the metal price falls. Dot = 2026, ring = 2025. Silver curve: estimated from 18 primary silver mines' 2026 guidance and H1 actuals (~116 Moz) on the Silver Institute's by-product basis — gold, zinc, lead and copper revenue subtracted; silver-equivalent figures converted (±US$3–5/oz). Approximate — it ranks the names, it is not decimal-precise.

Detail
MetricHeadlineDetail
Risk score2/5Zero debt, ~US$0.5B of cash plus a US$0.5B revolver, 12–15-year reserves at US$25 silver, and two Tier-1 US mines that generate free cash flow even at US$30 silver because by-products cover most of the cost. Not a 1 because the equity trades at ~13× EBITDA on by-product-flattered costs — a 30% silver pullback compresses both EBITDA and the multiple — and because Lucky Friday has twice lost years of production (the 2017–20 strike, the 2023 fire). The loss path is operational, not financial: a Keno Hill permit refusal or tailings incident under the post-Eagle Yukon regime, a Lucky Friday shaft or seismic event, or a zinc/lead/gold slump that turns 'negative AISC' into US$20+ real costs while the market de-rates the premium.

Valuation Anchor

~12–13× trailing EBITDA, ~21× earnings, ~US$47 per reserve ounce of silver (EV / 231 Moz) at a US$25 reserve price — the most expensive producer in this file on multiples and the cheapest on balance-sheet risk. Pan American trades at ~9×, Fresnillo ~6×, First Majestic ~8–9×; the premium is for Alaska and Idaho, zero debt, 12–15-year reserves and a 70% silver revenue mix. It is the quality name, and the price says so.

What the multiple needs: EBITDA growth, because there is no multiple expansion left to harvest. The 20 Moz plan (Keno Hill ~5 Moz at 440 tpd + pyrite circuit 1.1 Moz + Midas) adds ~US$0.45–0.55B of EBITDA at US$85 silver — ~US$4.5B of EV at 9×, ~40% on top of whatever silver does. The bear case is simpler: silver gives back a third, by-product prices follow, the 'negative AISC' becomes US$20 real costs, and the market pays 8× instead of 13× — a −35–50% move with the balance sheet untouched.

Also on the shelf: a Feb 2027 reserve re-pricing from US$25 silver, the Orezone shares (~65.8M) and up to US$321M of Casa Berardi contingent payments carried at US$4.2M.

Bucket: producer / cash flow, the compounder end — the name to own for survivability, not for torque. The one thing it does not pay you to wait is a dividend.

Shareholder structure
Management & board
~0.1%. CEO Rob Krcmarov held 786,708 shares and units at 24 Jun 2026 (181,241 direct + ~600k performance units and unvested RSUs); his only open-market buy was 6,570 shares at US$5.29 in Feb 2025. CFO Russell Lawlar and the VPs hold RSU grants with tax withholding. Board and management combined well under 1%.
Insider activity (12 mo)
Net sellers, no open-market buys. VP Sustainability Patrick Malone sold 23,994 shares at ~US$20.8 on 20 Aug 2026 (~US$498k, not under a plan); the CEO's June grants came with 79,437 shares withheld for tax at US$15.98; directors show trust allocations. GuruFocus counts ~US$9.7M of insider sales and zero buys over twelve months. The September slide came with no insider buying.
Strategic & prominent
None. Hecla itself holds ~65.8M Orezone shares from the Casa Berardi sale. No corporate or financier holder; no activist.
Institutions / retail
BlackRock 9.5%, VanEck 5.7% (GDX/SIL), State Street 4.9% (Sep 2026 deck); retail ~22%. 671.8M shares; Series B preferred (US$0.875/quarter) outstanding. 10 covering analysts.

Read: A passive-held large-cap silver name: index funds own it because it is the biggest US silver producer, retail trades it as silver beta, and management owns a token amount acquired through RSUs. The only insider signals in a year are tax withholding and one non-plan VP sale at ~US$21 — a mild negative, not a red flag. Nobody with skin in the game is buying the −50% from the high, and nobody is being paid to hold it either: the dividend is 0.09% and buybacks are explicitly deferred.

Jurisdiction risk

USA ~85% of output — the cleanest jurisdiction mix of any silver producer here. Alaska (Greens Creek, on Admiralty Island National Monument under a federal USFS lease; stable long-running permits; tailings expansions go through USFS EIS cycles). Idaho (Lucky Friday in the Silver Valley; Superfund-adjacent; union workforce — the 2017–20 strike cost three years; the 2023 fire another; state permitting straightforward).

Yukon ~15% — the layer that gates the growth. Keno Hill sits on Na-Cho Nyäk Dun territory with business agreements in place; the mine carries prior Waters Act/QMA charges and a C$100k fine (2024) from the Alexco/early-Hecla period and inspector warnings on its water licence 2023–25. After Victoria Gold's Eagle heap-leach failure (Jun 2024) the territory has implemented 23 of 56 Independent Review Board recommendations (Apr 2026), is rewriting mine-waste guidelines (spring 2027), reviewing quartz licences, expanding inspections and created a Major Mines branch (Mar 2026) to make permitting 'more predictable'. Net effect for Keno Hill: more scrutiny on tailings and water from a government that publicly wants investor confidence back. Québec exposure ended with the Casa Berardi sale; Nevada is exploration with a permitted mill.

Differentiator

The only large-cap pure-play silver producer in Tier-1 US jurisdictions — 70% silver revenue from Alaska and Idaho; the cleanest US-listed silver beta at scale.

  1. Negative-to-single-digit consolidated AISC on Greens Creek's gold, zinc and lead credits — at spot by-product prices the silver is 'free'.
  2. A fortress balance sheet — zero debt, ~US$0.5B cash, a US$0.5B revolver, in a sector of leveraged mid-caps.
  3. 12–15-year reserves at US$25 silver — the longest of the silver peers, with the reserve-price reset still to come.
  4. Brownfield growth that needs no new mine permit — the Greens Creek pyrite circuit, the permitted Midas mill, Lucky Friday tailings to 2044.

Counterweight: already priced as the quality name (~13× EBITDA, ~21× P/E); growth is slow and permit-gated (Keno Hill cut twice in 2026); by-product credits reverse if zinc, lead or gold fall; Lucky Friday is a single-shaft deep mine with a record of multi-year outages; the dividend is negligible and buybacks deferred; insiders have only sold. The strengths are what you pay 13× for; the weaknesses are what you get for it.

Exploration upside

Record budget, three mines already replacing · moves the needle: medium. US$55M for exploration and pre-development in 2026 (~2× 2025), US$16M of it in Nevada (3×). Q2 highlights (29 Jul): Keno Hill Bermingham Deep footwall vein 62.7 oz/t Ag over 10.2 ft and the high-grade trend extended to >800 ft toward historic Hector-Calumet; Greens Creek East Zone 169.5 oz/t Ag + 0.55 oz/t Au + 5.8% Zn over 8.4 ft; Lucky Friday 30 Vein 12.6 oz/t Ag + 11.4% Zn + 11.4% Pb over 10.5 ft; Midas new veins in the Sinter–Pogo gap. Hollister drilling resumed Jul 2026, Aurora in Aug. With 12–15 years of reserves the drilling is for Keno Hill's reserve step-up at the Feb 2027 update and for a Midas restart case — the two things that would move the valuation; Greens Creek and Lucky Friday are replacement.

Next Catalyst

Sep 2026: Lucky Friday surface cooling completion (88% at Q2; enables deeper, hotter mining); ~22 Oct: Q3 call notice; ~5 Nov: Q3 results — does Q2's realised-price and sales lag reverse; Q4 2026: Greens Creek tailings Phase 4 pilot decision; Dec/Jan: 2027 guidance; Feb 2027: YE reserves — first at a higher price deck? — and FY results; spring 2027: Yukon mine-waste guidelines; 2027: Keno Hill QML/Water Licence amendments (undated); Q4 2027–H1 2028: pyrite circuit first production.

Open Questions
  • What is Keno Hill's AISC today, and when does Hecla declare commercial production and stop excluding it from consolidated costs?
  • When are the 440 tpd QML and Water Licence amendments filed and decided — and does the post-Eagle review of quartz licences add conditions to the existing one?
  • Why was Q2 realised silver US$63.06 against a US$73.44 London average with payable sales 0.8 Moz below production — timing, or a structural concentrate lag?
  • Will the Feb 2027 reserves be re-priced from US$25 Ag / US$2,100 Au, and how much does life extend if so?
  • What capex and returns sit behind the pyrite circuit, Midas and tailings reprocessing — none has a public number despite carrying the 20 Moz target?
  • What does the new revolver's restriction on dividends and capital-stock payments mean for the promised post-US$1B returns?

CEO at Mining Forum Americas: 'organic by design', returns deferred (28 Sep 2026)

Path to 20+ Moz via Keno Hill, Midas and the pyrite circuit; cash to approach US$1B; shareholder returns 'sometime after' if nothing material to invest in; M&A only if it meets criteria. Shares −6.5% that day to US$17.01.

4.2 Moz Ag, adj. EBITDA US$199M, FCF US$136M, AISC US$6.07/oz. 2026 silver guide 15.1–16.1 Moz — Greens Creek raised, Keno Hill cut to 2.2–2.6 Moz from 2.9–3.2; AISC guide lowered to US$12.50–13.50. Realised silver US$63.06 vs a US$73.44 London average; payable sales 3.39 Moz vs 4.2 Moz produced.

US$263M 7.25% notes due 2028 redeemed at par from Casa Berardi proceeds and cash; net leverage from 1.6× (YE2024) to net cash ~US$0.5–0.6B by June.

US$160M cash + ~65.8M Orezone shares + royalty (valued US$130M) + up to US$321M contingent, gold-price linked (carried at US$4.2M); non-cash write-down US$192M; H1 discontinued-ops loss US$183.7M. Gold falls from ~30% to ~14% of revenue; the Québec open-pit transition is now Orezone's problem.

Policy revised to a fixed US$0.015/yr base to prioritise Keno Hill and deleveraging — so the record 2026 silver price produced no dividend uplift.

Thesis

Four Mexican mines — Los Gatos (70%, Dowa 30%; Chihuahua; Q2 AISC US$16.82, record 4,078 tpd in June, ~10-year LOM, all the zinc/lead), San Dimas (Durango; 2026 guide 4.6–4.9 Moz Ag + 52–56 koz Au; Wheaton stream; the 13-year SAT tax dispute), Santa Elena (Sonora; Ermitaño plus the Navidad/Santo Niño discoveries, 90.7 Moz AgEq, portals permitted Jun 2026, mill 3,100→3,500 tpd) and La Encantada (Coahuila; nearly pure silver, AISC guide US$31–32, the highest-cost unit) — plus Jerritt Canyon in Nevada, suspended Mar 2023, restart plan Apr 2026 (US$75M in 2026, PFS Q4, first gold H2 2027, 7.8 Moz Au resource, a permitted roaster).

2025: 31.1 Moz AgEq (15.4 Moz Ag + 147 koz Au) at AISC US$21.17. 2026 guide raised in July to 14.6–15.5 Moz Ag + 128–135 koz Au — but AISC to US$27.69–28.77 and capex to US$318–344M. H1 2026: revenue US$892M, adj. EBITDA US$578M (65% margin), FCF US$418M at ~US$64 silver. Balance sheet: US$1.25B treasury against ~US$405M of near-zero-coupon converts; net cash ~US$690M. Returns: dividend 2% of net revenue (~0.35% yield), NCIB. Portfolio pruned — San Martin (US$90M) and Del Toro (up to US$60M) sold in 2026. First Mint sells 10–15% of output at a 15–20% retail premium.

Founder-CEO Keith Neumeyer since 2002 (~0.9%, a net seller in 2026), President Mani Alkhafaji, CFO Neil Beaumont, new COO Dave Howe (ex-Pan American, May 2026). Nine analysts, mean target US$23.83. Stock −45% from the Feb 2026 peak, −13% in September; ~8–9× TTM EBITDA, ~25× trailing P/E, beta 2.2.

The Gate

Mexican operating margin has to hold while costs inflate: AISC went US$21.17 (FY25) → US$29.76 (Q1) → US$25.68 (Q2) with the guide at US$27.69–28.77 — at US$54 silver the margin halves.

Silver guidance rose 10% in July while AISC guidance rose 4% — price-linked duties, a stronger peso and sustaining capex are eating the price. The stock pays ~8–9× EBITDA for the purest large silver beta on the NYSE; it will keep paying that only if the margin survives a silver pullback.

Sub-gates
  1. Costs: Q3 (~9 Oct production, ~5 Nov financials) and Q4 AISC ≤ US$28.8 with silver 14.6–15.5 Moz on the year.
  2. Los Gatos: ≥ 4,000 tpd sustained in H2 2026 (June averaged 4,078) at ≤ US$21 AISC — the one first-half-curve asset.
  3. Jerritt Canyon PFS (Q4 2026): owner-operated plan, AISC meaningfully below US$2,000/oz, total capex that stays near the US$75M 2026 budget; first gold H2 2027. It was bought in 2021 and shut in 2023.
  4. Mexico: no new fiscal or water step; the Primero/San Dimas APA dispute lost at the Supreme Court in Nov 2025 — quantum still undisclosed.
  5. Capital allocation: NCIB and the 2%-of-revenue dividend rather than M&A — the CEO flagged 'flexibility for M&A' on 28 Sep.

Figure used: 2026 guidance of US$27.69–28.77/oz silver-equivalent for the three silver mines, converted at First Majestic's own price deck to ~US$16.7/oz Ag after credits, including corporate costs. Price-sensitive: at spot ~53rd, at US$66 silver ~44th — it straddles the line. Q2 actual → ~37th.

Borderline watchIt has crossed the middle of the curve (~49th → ~60th) as silver-equivalent costs rose ~33% (FY2025 US$21.17). Los Gatos (≤US$21 at ≥4,000 tpd) is the cost anchor; the rest is peso, price-linked duties and sustaining capex. Watch Q3 and Q4 against the US$28.77 top of guidance.

How to read it: picture every primary silver mine in the world lined up from cheapest to most expensive to run (all-in sustaining cost per ounce, weighted by output). The percentile is the share of world output that costs less; the middle line splits the cheaper half from the costlier half. Lower-half mines keep earning when the metal price falls. Dot = 2026, ring = 2025. Silver curve: estimated from 18 primary silver mines' 2026 guidance and H1 actuals (~116 Moz) on the Silver Institute's by-product basis — gold, zinc, lead and copper revenue subtracted; silver-equivalent figures converted (±US$3–5/oz). Approximate — it ranks the names, it is not decimal-precise.

Valuation Anchor

~8–9× trailing EBITDA, ~7× on the run-rate, ~US$47 per reserve AgEq ounce (EV / 184.8 Moz) and ~US$13/oz across M&I — a modest discount to Pan American and Fresnillo on multiples, a premium per reserve ounce because the reserves are short. The market pays for liquidity (US$200–250M a day; ~100% monthly float turnover) and for the purest silver beta at scale, not for cost position or reserve life.

The case: silver at US$69+ holds, Los Gatos runs at 4,000 tpd, Santo Niño and Navidad enter the mine plan and Jerritt adds 100–150 koz of Nevada gold from 2028 — EBITDA ~US$1.5B at 9.5× is ~1.5–1.7× today, before the metal. The bear case: AISC stays near US$28–30 while silver gives back a third, EBITDA halves, and the multiple compresses toward the 52-week low. Both are mostly silver; the company-specific swing is Jerritt and the cost line.

Bucket: producer / cash flow, the silver-beta end of it. Hold it for torque, not for compounding.
