Shareholder structure
Management & board
~0.9–1.1%. Keith Neumeyer (founder, CEO since 2002) ~4.26M shares (~0.9%) + 1.29M options + ~0.8M RSU/PSUs at Mar 2025, built from options, awards and early purchases; directors hold small positions (Polman 125k, Muñiz 69k). No 10%+ holder — Sprott's 11.3% from the 2021 Jerritt deal has been diluted and sold down.
Insider activity (12 mo)
Net selling, all Neumeyer. 52,500 at C$35.00 on 13 Feb 2026 (the top), then five August sales at C$25.87–30.00 and one on 27 Aug — ~176k shares, ~C$4.6M in calendar 2026 (~C$14M over the 12 months to Aug 2026 including late-2025 sales; SEDI via third-party summaries). No insider purchases found in 2026. Consistent with his pattern over the years rather than a new signal.
Strategic & prominent
None at the equity level. Dowa Metals & Mining (Japan) owns 30% of the Los Gatos JV with a zinc offtake; Wheaton streams San Dimas gold-equivalent; First Majestic itself owns 24.8% of Sierra Madre (62.4M shares) from the Del Toro sale.
Institutions / retail
Institutions ~27–48% depending on the source; an unusually retail-heavy register (the CEO cites ~100% monthly float turnover, US$200–250M daily volume). 492.7M shares; converts could add ~3.3M (2027) + 15.7M (2031, if ever in the money). Short interest 22.4M shares (4.5%).

Read: A founder-led but widely held silver proxy with thin management ownership (<1%) and a CEO who sold into both 2026 rallies. That is not alignment on capital allocation, which is exactly the open question with US$1.25B in the treasury and 'flexibility for M&A' on the record. The retail-heavy register explains the 2.2 beta and the −13% September on a modest silver pullback; nobody with size is defending the price.

Jurisdiction risk

Mexico is ~100% of current output and all of the discount. National: the 2023 Mining Law (30-year concessions + one renewal, mandatory water concessions, prior consultation, 5% of profit to communities) was upheld by the Supreme Court in 2025; secondary regulations still unpublished; a de facto moratorium on new concessions under Sheinbaum; the Dec 2025 National Waters Law ends private transfer of water concessions and lets volumes be cut for human consumption; a General Environmental Law bill (hearings 28–29 Sep 2026) would lift EIA costs from MXN 0.5M to MXN 40–50M. Fiscal: 30% corporate tax + 7.5% special mining duty on EBITDA + 0.5% on precious-metal sales; H1 2026 current tax ran ~US$175M. Tax disputes: the 13-year SAT dispute over Primero's 2012 APA at San Dimas went against the subsidiary at the Supreme Court in Nov 2025 (stock −15% that week); the quantum has not been disclosed. A separate forward-silver dispute settled for US$10.1M in Q2 2026.

Local: a Q2 haulage delay at San Dimas from labour negotiations (resolved); cartel security in Durango, Sonora and Chihuahua is a standing cost with no 2026 incident disclosed; a strong peso lifted the AISC guide. Nevada (Jerritt Canyon, from 2027) is the only diversification — fully permitted, a roaster already built, a Tier-1 regime that is shortening permitting times. Until then this is a single-country cash flow under a regime that is hardening on water, fees and tax.

Differentiator

The purest large-cap silver exposure on the NYSE — ~60–66% of revenue is silver, the float turns over monthly, and it is the default vehicle for silver beta. That is what the multiple is for.

  1. A US$1.25B treasury at near-zero coupons — can self-fund Jerritt, Santa Elena and buybacks through a downturn; no bank debt.
  2. Los Gatos — a 10-year, sub-US$21 AISC, by-product-rich anchor with 103,000 ha largely unexplored, now running above the old 3,500 tpd nameplate.
  3. A permitted Nevada roaster — Jerritt Canyon is scarce US gold optionality (7.8 Moz Au resource) if the restart works this time.
  4. First Mint — 10–15% of silver sold at a 15–20% premium; a marketing edge more than an earnings driver.

Counterweight: the highest AISC among the larger silver producers (guide US$27.7–28.8 vs Pan American, Fresnillo, Aya well below); ~95% of EBITDA in one hardening jurisdiction; ~6 years of reserves; a Jerritt that already failed once under this management (bought 2021, shut 2023); and a share count that has roughly doubled since 2020. Every strength is financial; every weakness is operational.

Exploration upside

Replacement drilling, with two district options · moves the needle: medium. 2026 budget US$41–45M, ~308,000 m (+16%): 117 km at San Dimas (89 km done by 9 Sep — El Cristo 1.30 m @ 6,994 g/t AgEq, Sinaloa-Elia 0.88 m @ 5,835 g/t, a new Convención vein), 62 km to define Navidad/Santo Niño for the LOM plan, Los Gatos south-east/west extensions, 42 km for the Jerritt PFS. Bonanza grades over narrow widths are the San Dimas norm — they replace depletion rather than grow it. What could move the valuation is the Santa Elena district (90.7 Moz AgEq, 300–450 m from infrastructure) and Jerritt; watch the Mar 2027 MRMR for whether ~6 years becomes 7–8.

Next Catalyst

5 Nov 2026: Q3 financials and dividend (AISC vs the US$27.69–28.77 guide; San Dimas 12-day strike impact after the 8 Oct production release: 3.44 Moz Ag, −9% q/q); Q4 2026: Jerritt Canyon PFS (Stantec) — capex, AISC, annual ounces; Q4: San Martin closing (Mexican antitrust), Santo Niño/Navidad portals collared; mid-Jan 2027: 2027 guidance; Jan 2027: the ~US$55M 2027 converts mature in the money; Feb/Mar 2027: FY results and MRMR; H2 2027: Jerritt first gold.

Open Questions
  • What are the total Jerritt Canyon restart capex and steady-state AISC/ounces in the Q4 PFS — and who carries execution risk after the 2023 contractor failure?
  • What is the quantum and timing of the Primero/San Dimas APA tax dispute after the Nov 2025 Supreme Court ruling, and is any ICSID/USMCA claim alive?
  • Why does AISC guidance rise 4% while silver guidance rises 10% — how much is price-linked (duties, AgEq by-product mechanics) and how much is real inflation?
  • How do the Dec 2025 water law and the proposed EIA fee affect the Santa Elena expansion, the new portals and Los Gatos at 4,000 tpd?
  • What does management do with US$1.25B — faster NCIB, a special dividend, or the M&A it keeps mentioning?
  • Can reserves (~6 years) be rebuilt at San Dimas and La Encantada, or does holding 30 Moz AgEq past 2028 depend on Navidad and Jerritt?
Context & updates
13 Oct 2026 update

Mexico and First Majestic agreed a framework to settle the old Primero tax dispute over San Dimas; the NAFTA arbitration is paused to 31 Dec 2026. This could remove a long-running overhang, but no amount is public and nothing is signed, so odds and risk stay as they are until a settlement is announced. Separately, the San Dimas strike continues with no talks reported.

9 Oct 2026 update

The San Dimas dispute is now a formal strike (declared 8 Oct by Sindicato Minero sections 21 and 22; reported by El Siglo de Durango and La Jornada). Mining there has been stopped since 18 Sep, so Q4 silver will be well below Q3 unless it ends soon, and full-year silver guidance (72% of the midpoint reached after Q3) is now at risk. No negotiation date reported. Odds stay 9% for now: the 3-5 year case rests on Jerritt Canyon and the silver price, not one quarter; a strike lasting into 2027 or a guidance cut would change that.

8 Oct 2026 update

Q3 2026 production: silver 3.44 Moz (−11% y/y, −9% q/q), gold 29.6 koz (−17% y/y). A 12-day labour dispute at San Dimas, the core mine, cut its silver 41% y/y; management says it is working to resolve it, so it was still open on 8 Oct. Year to date silver is 72% of the revised guidance midpoint (75% would be on pace); guidance was not changed. Jerritt Canyon first gold still H2 2027. Buyback renewed for up to 10M shares (~2%) from 14 Oct. Q3 financials and AISC on 5 Nov. Watch: a longer San Dimas stoppage would put silver guidance at risk and push AISC up.

3 Oct 2026 refresh

No release since 9 Sep; Q3 production ~9 Oct. On 28 Sep management hedged the Jerritt Canyon PFS to 'end of this year, early next year'. If it formally moves into 2027, the chance the plan works should come down.

Guidance raised, costs up, portfolio pruned (Jun–Jul 2026)

Del Toro to Sierra Madre (up to US$60M, 22 Jun); San Martin sale agreed (US$90M, 7 Jul); Santa Elena portals permitted (25 Jun). 8 Jul: guidance to 14.6–15.5 Moz Ag / 128–135 koz Au but AISC to US$27.69–28.77 and capex to US$318–344M. Q2 (30 Jul): revenue US$415.5M, adj. EBITDA US$257M, FCF US$195M, treasury US$1.25B, 1.2M shares bought back.

Jerritt Canyon restart plan (2 Apr 2026)

US$75M 2026 programme, PFS Q4 2026, first gold H2 2027, owner-operated; M&I 4.1 Moz + Inferred 3.7 Moz Au after a +116% resource (at US$3,400 gold). Reverses the Mar 2023 suspension; new managing director Alex Thompson.

US$350M 2031 converts and a doubled dividend (Dec 2025 – Jan 2026)

0.125% notes at a US$22.36 conversion (42.5% premium); US$174.7M of the 2027 notes repurchased for US$214.7M; dividend policy to 2% of net revenue from 1 Jan 2026. FY2025: revenue US$1.26B, adj. EBITDA US$679M, FCF US$471M.

Supreme Court upholds SAT on the Primero APA (Nov 2025)

The 13-year San Dimas tax dispute lost at the top court; stock −15% in the week despite a record 3.9 Moz silver quarter. Neumeyer: 'no change'. Quantum undisclosed; a separate forward-silver dispute settled for US$10.1M in Q2 2026.

Gatos Silver acquired (16 Jan 2025)

2.55 First Majestic shares per Gatos share (~US$970M) for 70% of Cerro Los Gatos — the lowest-cost mine in the portfolio and all of the zinc/lead. Share count ~300M → ~485M; 2025 output +~45% to 31.1 Moz AgEq.

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 4/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 2/5

Twenty-year Mexican silver operator, guidance met since 2023, Gatos deal good; offset by the Jerritt Canyon failure, the SAT tax fight and a CEO who sells while promoting.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Keith Neumeyer (President & CEO, founder, since 2002 (CEO since Nov 2001 per circular)): Also Chair of First Mining Gold (TSX: FF) since 2015. Co-founder/first president of First Quantum Minerals in 1996 (unverified detail, widely reported). Vocal silver-price promoter. · Neil Beaumont (CFO, since Jul 2026): Replaced David Soares. · Dave Howe (COO, since May 2026): Ex-Pan American Silver; runs the Mexican operations.
Track record
  • Built First Majestic from a shell into a 3-4 mine Mexican silver producer over 20+ years; main hit is longevity and the Gatos dealsource
  • Jerritt Canyon (Nevada) bought Mar 2021 for ~US$470M in stock; mining suspended Mar 2023 for costs; restart now targeted H2 2027 — a capital-allocation miss (https://www.miningweekly.com/article/first-majestic-buys-jerritt-canyon-from-sprott-2021-03-12 ; https://www.mining.com/first-majestic-stock-plunges-as-it-shuts-down-jerritt-canyon-mine-to-reduce-costs/)
  • Gatos Silver (70% of Los Gatos) acquired Jan 2025 for ~US$970M stock; mine performing, 2026 guidance raised 5% mid-pointsource
  • Primero/San Dimas acquisition (2018) brought a Mexican SAT transfer-pricing dispute; NAFTA/ICSID arbitration filed 2021, still listed as pending (https://www.firstmajestic.com/investors/news-releases/first-majestic-provides-sat-tax-dispute-update ; https://www.iareporter.com/arbitration-cases/first-majestic-silver-v-mexico/)
  • First Mining Gold (Neumeyer chair since 2015) has not built a mine; Springpole still at permitting (unverified status)
  • 2026 guidance raised twice in two years: silver 13.0-14.4 -> 14.6-15.5 Moz, but AISC also raised 4%source

Boards today: Neumeyer: CEO First Majestic + Chair First Mining Gold = 2 public roles (circular 2026).

Fit to this job
Same job: Mexican underground silver-gold operator for 20+ years, same region, same method. New for them: Nevada refractory gold (Jerritt Canyon) was a failure and is still not restarted; Los Gatos is their first JV-operated asset with a partner (Dowa 30%).
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake from grants or cheap founder paper; little buying. Neumeyer holds 4.73M shares (~0.95%, ~CA$120M) plus 0.7M options, 0.38M RSUs, 0.30M PSUs (circular Apr 2026); shares mostly from grants/options over 20 years, recent pattern is option exercise then sale (net seller ~CA$14M over the 12 months to Aug 2026, of which ~CA$4.6M in calendar 2026 — the card quotes the calendar-2026 figure). CEO total comp 2025 ~US$7.43M (17% salary). Say-on-pay 2025 'strong' (percentage not extracted). Sources: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1308648/000119312526191171/d102132dex9931.pdf ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsx-ag/first-majestic-silver-shares/management

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Jerritt Canyon: ~US$470M acquisition idled after 2 years; capital-allocation miss not acknowledged as such
  • CEO net seller of stock in 2025-26 while promoting silver
  • Long-running Mexican tax dispute (SAT/ICSID) unresolved
  • CEO pay US$7.4M (2025) at the high end for a ~US$5-10B producer; 83% variable

  5. Debt is US$302.8M after a US$350M convertible note replaced the 2027 note in December 2025; FY25 current tax was US$273M and cash taxes lag earnings.

Thesis

Four mines: Fekola (Mali, ~47% of 2026 output; open pit in a Phase-8 strip, underground stoping since Jul 2025, Fekola Regional permit finally granted Aug 7, 2026 after an 18-month slip), Goose (Nunavut; first gold Jun 2025; a crushing-circuit fire in April 2026 cut Q2 to 12,890 oz at US$6,390 AISC; mobile crusher running >3,000 tpd since mid-August, fixed-plant upgrade mid-October, 4,000 tpd design not before H2 2027), Masbate (Philippines; 180–200 koz, AISC US$1,430–1,580, the reliable one) and Otjikoto (Namibia; open pit finished, underground and stockpiles, 80–100 koz until Antelope in 2029). 2025: 979,604 oz at AISC US$1,584; 2026 guidance cut in August to 820–920 koz at AISC US$2,370–2,550 (guidance modelled at US$5,000 gold, which inflates price-linked royalties). H1 2026: 441 koz, revenue US$1.95B, adjusted net income US$301M, free cash flow US$104M after the last gold-prepay deliveries (done June) and collar losses (end December). Balance sheet: cash US$287M, US$800M revolver (US$95M drawn post-quarter), US$460M 2.75% converts due 2030 convertible at US$3.17 — deep in the money, ~145M shares of dilution; Fingold sold to Agnico for US$325M cash in April. Returns: US$0.02 quarterly dividend (~1.5%) and a buyback that took 35M shares for US$172M in H1. Reserves 8.99 Moz (Goose 2.38 Moz at 6.79 g/t; Gramalote FS Jul 2025: US$740M capex, NPV5% US$941M at US$2,500 — deferred). Founder-CEO Clive Johnson retired in June; CFO Mike Cinnamond is CEO, Kelvin Dushnisky (ex-AngloGold, ex-Barrick) executive chair. Thirteen analysts, consensus Buy, average target US$6.45.

The Gate

Whether Goose becomes the 300 koz/yr mine that justifies C$1.54B — and whether Mali lets Fekola pay for the wait. Goose has missed every number attached to it: 2025 guidance 120–150k → 80–110k → 53k delivered; 2026 '~250k' → 170–230k → 170–200k; capex C$1.25B → C$1.54B; then the fire. Steady state is now guided for H2 2027, with a ten-week fixed-plant shutdown in H1 2027 for the Phase-2 crusher, on a site fed by one winter ice road and one sealift window.

Sub-gates
  1. Mali — a junta at war with JNIM (fuel blockade since Sep 2025; the Defence Minister killed in April 2026 attacks), a 2023 code that takes 35% and 30% CIT on all new ground, and a permit that arrived 18 months late; Barrick's US$430M settlement is the precedent for how disputes end.
  2. Cost — consolidated AISC has gone US$1,584 → US$1,964 → US$2,356 in three prints and the guide is US$2,370–2,550; some is price-linked royalties, more is Fekola stripping and Goose remediation; at US$3,000 gold the margin is thin.
  3. The converts — US$460M convertible at US$3.17 means ~145M shares arrive whatever the buyback does.
  4. Namibia and the Philippines — Otjikoto has 90 koz of reserves and a hole until Antelope (2029); Masbate has 7–8 years at 0.72 g/t.
  5. A new CEO and CFO in their first year running two remediation programmes.

The market is not paying 3.5× because it missed something. It is paying 3.5× because it has watched Goose for two years.

Valuation Anchor

~3.5× EBITDA, ~US$800 per reserve ounce, 0.8–0.9× a spot NAV — the widest peer discount of any producer here, wider than Fresnillo's, and for reasons that are operational rather than structural. That is the case: Fresnillo's discount cannot close because the float cannot change; B2Gold's can, because Goose can work. If Goose reaches 4,000 tpd in H2 2027 and Fekola Regional adds 150 koz from 2028, this is a ~1.1 Moz producer with AISC back under US$2,000, and 5× EBITDA on that is roughly 2× today's price before any help from gold. The collars expire in December, so 2027 is the first fully-spot year.

The bear case is that 2027 looks like 2026: Goose stuck at 3,200 tpd through the shutdown, Fekola in a strip, AISC US$2,400, and a Mali headline — in which case 3.5× is fair, the converts arrive, and the stock is dead money at a 1.5% yield.

Bucket: producer / cash flow, the turnaround end of it — a re-rate that depends on one Arctic crusher and one Sahelian government.

Read: A widely held, founder-less senior where the only alignment signal is the company's own buyback — and where the insiders who could sell into the August rally did. Van Eck's weight makes this a GDX flow stock as much as a Mali stock. Nothing here says the people closest to Goose expect a re-rate soon; nothing says they expect disaster either.

Jurisdiction risk

Mali is the layer that prices the stock. Fekola Complex is ~47% of 2026 ounces. The Sep 2024 framework keeps the Fekola mine under the 2012 code to 2040 (80/20 with a priority dividend to the state, effective tax ~40%) and puts all regional ground under the 2023 code (65/35, 30% CIT); disputes since 2016 settled, fuel-tax exemptions surrendered. Since then: JNIM's fuel blockade from Sep 2025, national rationing in Jan 2026, coordinated attacks in April 2026 that killed the Defence Minister, a new mining ministry, and a permit that was 'Q1 2026', then 'June', then Aug 7. B2Gold says 2026 fuel is secured and ~36% hedged, 3,300 staff are 98% Malian, and processes are now 'harmonised'. Barrick's Loulo-Gounkoto settlement (US$430M, Nov 2025) is the template for what a dispute costs. Nunavut is the opposite problem — a supportive jurisdiction with brutal logistics: one winter ice road from the marine laydown, one sealift, ten-week shutdown windows, a knowledge-sharing pact with Agnico. Philippines (Masbate) and Namibia (Otjikoto, 90%) are stable and small. Colombia (Gramalote) is resettlement and an EIA modification away from a decision the company keeps deferring. Local: no material community dispute reported at any of the four mines in 2025–26; the Goose fire was an accident, not a licence event.

A four-country portfolio where one country carries half the ounces and all of the discount.

Differentiator
  1. The cheapest senior gold multiple on the market with a real path to fixing the reason: Goose is a 6.8 g/t reserve with 3.8 Moz Indicated and a district (Llama, Nuvuyak, Tattuk, George) that keeps growing — the mine is right; the crusher was wrong.
  2. Fekola Regional is permitted — the 18-month wait is over, tolling has started, and the complex can run ~500 koz/yr into the late 2030s.
  3. Capital returns while repairing — US$224M to shareholders in H1 (buyback + dividend), Fingold monetised for US$325M cash, gold prepay and collars rolling off by December.
  4. Gramalote is optional growth on the shelf — a feasibility-stage 227 koz/yr mine at US$985 AISC that nobody is paying for.
  5. A board built for the fix — Dushnisky (ran AngloGold and Barrick's operations) as executive chair over a first-year CEO.

Read it honestly: every differentiator is a repair of a self-inflicted problem. The upside is real because the execution was bad; that cuts both ways.

Exploration upside

Back River is the one that matters · moves the needle: high for Goose life, low for the multiple. US$46M and >35,000 m in 2026 (27,500 m done by August): Llama 21.2 m @ 19.1 g/t and 4.7 m @ 44.6; new Tattuk zone 150 m down-plunge of Nuvuyak, 10 m @ 10.9 g/t; George 9.4 m @ 26.5. Goose reserves are only 2.38 Moz against 3.79 Moz Indicated and 2.28 Inferred — conversion is the lever. Mali exploration is US$5M (Dandoko exploitation application 2027 for 2028). Otjikoto US$14M underground on Wolfshag/Antelope.

If Goose is a 300 koz mine for fifteen years, Back River drilling is what proves it. Watch the Dec 2026 reserve update.

Next Catalyst

Mid-Oct 2026: Goose Phase-1 crusher complete (3,200 tpd); Q3 results ~early Nov (Goose ~43 koz, Fekola Regional pre-strip, revolver balance); Dec: collars expire, first Regional ounces possible, R&R update (Goose additions, Antelope); Jan/Feb 2027: 2027 guidance — management says 'every chance' 2027 > 2026, earlier talk of ~980 koz; H1 2027: Goose Phase 2 to 4,000 tpd with a ten-week shutdown; Gramalote EIA and resettlement; Dandoko application; NCIB pace; Mali.

Open Questions
  • What does Goose actually produce in Q3 and Q4 2026 — and does the Phase-2 shutdown in H1 2027 come with enough stockpile to avoid a third missed year?
  • What is consolidated AISC at US$3,500 gold once price-linked royalties normalise — is US$2,000 reachable in 2027?
  • What is the real cost of Mali: fuel, security, the 35% state share on Regional, and repatriation — and what did the 2024 settlement cost in cash?
  • Buyback or converts: US$172M repurchased in H1 against ~145M shares coming at US$3.17 — what is the net share count in 2030?
  • When does Gramalote get a decision, and is it a build or a sale?
  • What changes under Cinnamond and Dushnisky — capital allocation, guidance discipline, Mali posture?

Aside

Founder retired; a career CFO is CEO. Goose capex went C$800M → C$1.54B and guidance was cut twice, with the misses buried under neutral headlines.

Effect on the odds: chance it works 35% → 32%, odds of a 3× 10% → 9%.

People
Mike Cinnamond (President & CEO, since Jun 4, 2026): CFO 2014-2026, joined 2013; accountant/finance background, first CEO role. Boards: Onyx Gold, Contango Silver & Gold. · Clive Johnson (Chair Emeritus (retired CEO), since founder 2007; retired Jun 2026): Founded Bema Gold (sold to Kinross 2007, ~US$3B — unverified) and B2Gold; built Otjikoto, Fekola, Goose. · Kelvin Dushnisky (Executive Chair, since Feb 23, 2026 (chair earlier)): Ex-Barrick president, ex-AngloGold Ashanti CEO (left 2020). · Michael McDonald (CFO, since Jun 4, 2026): Succeeded Cinnamond.
Track record
  • Johnson's record: Bema Gold built and sold to Kinross (2007); B2Gold built Otjikoto (2014) and Fekola (2017) on time and budget — wins in two cycles (unverified amounts)
  • Goose (Nunavut): bought via Sabina (Apr 2023, ~C$1.1B); capex guided ~C$800M (Sep 2023) -> C$1.05B (Jan 2024, +30%) -> C$1.54B (Sep 2024), with first gold moved Q1 -> Q2 2025 (https://www.miningnewsnorth.com/story/2024/01/26/news/goose-gold-mine-costs-now-at-1-billion/8367.html ; https://www.miningweekly.com/article/b2gold-reaffirms-c154bn-development-estimate-for-goose-gold-project-eyes-mill-expansion-2025-03-28)
  • Goose first gold Jun 30, 2025 (last day of Q2); 2025 Goose guidance cut 120-150 -> 80-110 koz (Sep 2025, crushing constraints); 2026 outlook 'roughly 250 koz' (Sep 2025) became 170-200 koz after an April 2026 crusher fire (https://www.miningweekly.com/article/b2gold-trims-goose-output-guidance-but-reaffirms-2025-group-forecast-2025-09-15 ; https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/commodities/articles/b2gold-corp-btg-q2-2026-230115309.html)
  • Mali: 2024 guidance lowered mid-year (Fekola), 804.8 koz 'within the revised range'; Menankoto/Fekola Regional permit finally granted mid-2026 after years of delaysource
  • Consolidated guidance met on revised ranges in 2024 and 2025; 2026 narrowed to 820-920 koz with AISC $2,370-2,550 (Q2 2026)
  • Q2 2026: US$71M realised loss on gold collars, free cash flow -US$258M on cash taxes and gold prepays; cash US$287Msource

Boards today: Cinnamond: B2Gold + Onyx Gold + Contango Silver & Gold = 3 public roles (circular 2026). Johnson: chair emeritus only (no nominee listing).

Fit to this job
Company has built and operated open-pit gold mines in Namibia, Mali and the Philippines — same job. Arctic Nunavut (Goose, sealift logistics, winter ice road, crushing in cold) was new and is where the misses came. New CEO is a career CFO, not an operator; the executive chair is a lawyer/administrator by background.
Skin & pay
1/5 — under ~0.5%, options only, or net sellers while promoting. Cinnamond: 137,501 shares (~0.024%, ~US$1.7M), meets 3x salary requirement; sold ~77k shares Apr 1, 2026 (~US$356k, 20% of holdings). Johnson sold ~73k shares Mar 2026. Insiders net sellers ~US$10M/12 months. Cinnamond 2025 total comp as CFO ~US$2.46M; Johnson's 2025 CEO comp not extracted. Say-on-pay 2025: 93.2%. Sources: https://s204.q4cdn.com/324791784/files/doc_downloads/2026/04/B2Gold-MIC-FYE-December-31-2025.pdf ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/materials/nysemkt-btg/b2gold/management

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Goose capex ~2x B2Gold's own first estimate and ~2.5x Sabina's feasibility (C$610M, unverified); two production guidance cuts in its first year
  • Press-release headlines consistently lead with good news and bury cuts ('Remains On Track', 'Strong Operating Performance')
  • New CEO sold 20% of his holdings (Apr 2026) two months before taking the job; insiders net sellers US$10M over 12 months
  • Gold collar/prepay losses and negative free cash flow in a record gold price environment
  • Mali political/fiscal risk; Fekola is the biggest mine

What the numbers say
  1. Cash fell from US$480M in March 2026 to US$287M in June 2026 despite US$325M from selling the Finland properties; Q2 26 operating cash flow was negative US$79M.
  2. FY25 operating cash flow of US$896M barely covered US$812M capex and US$51M exploration, and FY24 cash flow was flattered by a US$500M gold prepay.
  3. Dividends were cut from US$0.16 to US$0.08 a share, but US$172M of buybacks in H1 26 took the share count from 1,340.6M to 1,321.1M.
  4. Revenue hit a record US$3.06bn in FY25, but Q2 26 revenue fell to US$789M after the April 2026 Goose crusher fire; AISC jumped to US$2,356/oz and guidance was cut.
  5. Debt is US$456M of 2030 convertible notes plus a US$257M gold-stream obligation; FY24 carried a US$876M impairment and gold-collar losses were US$267M in FY25.

The purest listed silver producer — one high-grade Moroccan mine at a US$17 cash cost — now priced as if Boumadine, a gold-led PEA, is already built

Gate Growing into a ~US$4.1B valuation that already discounts Boumadine. At ~14× annualised EBITDA and ~24× forward earnings, Zgounder alone — 73 Moz of reserves, 11-year life, ~6 Moz/yr — does not carry the price; the market is paying for a US$3.5B PEA whose resource is 4.3 of 5.4 Moz AuEq Inferred, with a 22.6:1 strip, a roaster/payability chain untested at scale, and an FS that has already slipped from H1 to H2 2027. Sub-gates: (1) Zgounder grade — 2025 missed guidance (4.83 vs 5.0–5.3 Moz) on head grade of 145 g/t against 170–200 g/t guided; the reserve grade (145) sits below M&I (165) and the mill runs at ~140; H2 2026 strip ratio rises from ~10:1 to ~16:1, lifting cash cost toward the US$21.50 guide; (2) single-asset, single-country — Morocco is drafting a new mining law (May 2026) and is structurally drought-prone; Boumadine needs an ESIA; (3) beta — the stock is ~3× in twelve months with a ~3.3 beta; a silver pullback compresses the multiple before it touches the mine.

Thesis

Zgounder, in Morocco's Anti-Atlas, is a ~3,900 tpd underground-plus-open-pit silver mine producing at a US$16.82/AgEq oz cash cost with 141 g/t feed and 91% recovery after a 2024 plant expansion. 2026 guidance 6.2–6.8 Moz AgEq (Zgounder 5.2–5.8 Moz Ag); H1 delivered 3.17 Moz AgEq, revenue US$214M, net income US$83.6M, operating cash flow US$118.6M.

Cash US$182.8M against ~US$80–85M of EBRD debt (being repaid early); no equity issued since the C$144M bought deal of Jun 2025. Silver is 93% of revenue — the cleanest silver beta on a major exchange (Nasdaq-listed May 2026, added to GDX).

The second leg is Boumadine: an updated PEA (Sep 9, 2026) shows after-tax NPV5% US$3.5B and 93% IRR at US$3,500 Au / US$50 Ag on US$463M initial capex, 8,000 tpd, 14 years, ~271 koz AuEq/yr — but it is gold-led by value (~58%), 80% Inferred, and a feasibility study is not due until H2 2027. 14 rigs turning; 145,000 m drilled YTD.

The Gate

Growing into a ~US$4.1B valuation that already discounts Boumadine. At ~14× annualised EBITDA and ~24× forward earnings, Zgounder alone — 73 Moz of reserves, 11-year life, ~6 Moz/yr — does not carry the price; the market is paying for a US$3.5B PEA whose resource is 4.3 of 5.4 Moz AuEq Inferred, with a 22.6:1 strip, a roaster/payability chain untested at scale, and an FS that has already slipped from H1 to H2 2027.

Sub-gates
  1. Zgounder grade — 2025 missed guidance (4.83 vs 5.0–5.3 Moz) on head grade of 145 g/t against 170–200 g/t guided; the reserve grade (145) sits below M&I (165) and the mill runs at ~140; H2 2026 strip ratio rises from ~10:1 to ~16:1, lifting cash cost toward the US$21.50 guide.
  2. Single-asset, single-country — Morocco is drafting a new mining law (May 2026) and is structurally drought-prone; Boumadine needs an ESIA.
  3. Beta — the stock is ~3× in twelve months with a ~3.3 beta; a silver pullback compresses the multiple before it touches the mine.

Read the September sell-off (−7% on Sep 23) as what happens to a 14× silver name when the metal wobbles — not as news about Zgounder.

Cost-curve position

Upper half~64th percentile of primary silver mines · 3rd quartile — ~64% of the world's primary silver output costs less to produce. In 2025: ~86th.

Figure used: Zgounder AISC ~US$19/oz (management, 29 Sep — no AISC is published; Q2 cash cost US$16.82). On the cash-cost guide (~US$24.5 estimated AISC) it would be ~72nd — upper half either way.

Why mid-curve if it is cheap? Per silver-equivalent ounce Aya is the cheapest of the five silver names here (Fresnillo's silver mines ~US$26.6, First Majestic ~US$28.2, Avino ~US$38.75). But the industry curve subtracts gold, zinc and lead revenue, and a pure-silver mine has none to subtract — so mines with big by-products sit below it.

Improving: ~86th in 2025 → ~64th as cash costs fell (US$20.41 → US$16.82) while peers' rose. H2's higher strip ratio (10:1 → 16:1) pushes costs back toward guidance.

How to read it: picture every primary silver mine in the world lined up from cheapest to most expensive to run (all-in sustaining cost per ounce, weighted by output). The percentile is the share of world output that costs less; the middle line splits the cheaper half from the costlier half. Lower-half mines keep earning when the metal price falls. Dot = 2026, ring = 2025. Silver curve: estimated from 18 primary silver mines' 2026 guidance and H1 actuals (~116 Moz) on the Silver Institute's by-product basis — gold, zinc, lead and copper revenue subtracted; silver-equivalent figures converted (±US$3–5/oz). Approximate — it ranks the names, it is not decimal-precise.

Valuation Anchor

~14× annualised Q2 EBITDA, ~24× forward P/E, ~US$55/oz on silver reserves. Zgounder at 6.5 Moz and a US$50/oz margin (which needs ~US$71.5 silver) earns ~US$325M a year; at 10× that is ~US$3.3B — roughly today's EV. At ~US$61 silver (1 Oct) the margin is ~US$37–39/oz, ~US$240–250M a year, ~US$2.4–2.5B at 10× — so Boumadine is carrying ~US$1.6B of the price. So Boumadine is in the price at a Boumadine-in-2030 discount rate, not a PEA discount rate.

The bull case is the spot NPV (US$5.5B) plus Zgounder; the bear case is silver at US$50 and an FS that trims the NPV to something a 22.6:1 strip and a roaster deserve.

Of the four producers this is the one whose valuation is most a call on a study rather than on cash flow — closer to NGEx in the copper file than to Pan American.

Shareholder structure
Management & board
~1–2% after the January 2026 block sale (stale aggregators still show ~10%). CEO Benoit La Salle: 158,930 common shares + 1.8M options + 217k RSUs + 26k PSUs (C$6.9M total) — almost entirely granted; the cash-bought block is small. No La Salle family, Windiga or founder block exists. Director guideline 3× retainer. John Burzynski is the one director with genuine open-market buys (20k shares in 2025).
Insider activity (12 mo)
Large selling at the top. Jan 14–21, 2026: Chair Robert Taub sold 7.0M shares (~C$150M) and Lead Director Hambrecht ~0.5M in a secondary at C$21.47; both left the board at the June AGM. Management sold ~1.1M securities (~12% of holdings) alongside — La Salle 235k shares (~C$5M) [one source says 35k], Beaudoin, Landry-Tolszczuk, Ball, Burzynski. La Salle also sold 64k in mid-2025. No purchases by the CEO in 2025–26. The stock has since doubled from the sale price — the sellers were early, not wrong about the risk.
Strategic & prominent
Van Eck ~7.1% (10.2M shares, Aug 2026; was ~10% in 2024) — the largest holder, and GDX inclusion (Jun 2026) makes it a structural buyer. Global X (SIL) ~3.7%. Robert Taub's residual stake after the sale is undisclosed. No Sprott, Lundin, La Mancha or other strategic block.
Institutions / retail
2024 baseline: retail 57%, institutions 32%, insiders ~11%; post-Jan 2026 insiders ~1–2% and institutional share rising with the Nasdaq listing (US 13F coverage still thin; Canadian holders — Ninepoint, Mackenzie, RBC — not captured). 143.3M shares (Apr 2026), ~146M basic now. No buyback.

Read: This is the weakest ownership picture in the file for a US$4B company: the founding chair took C$150M off the table in January, the CEO's exposure is options, and nobody with a name has bought. The counter-argument is real — the stock doubled after they sold, and index flows (GDX, Nasdaq) now dominate — but insiders do not own the Boumadine story they are asking the market to pay 14× for.

Jurisdiction risk

National: better than its reputation, but concentrated. Morocco: Law 33-13, no mandatory state equity outside phosphates; Aya bought out ONHYM's 15% in 2022 (3% royalty remains); EBRD as lender; tax incentives keep 2025 government payments to ~C$2.3M. A new draft mining law (May 2026: safety, penalties, registry, permit reassignment) is not yet adopted and has no announced royalty change — watch it.

Local: low — no community disputes reported; water reservoirs full after a wet season, but the Anti-Atlas is structurally drought-prone and Boumadine's ESIA is still to come.

Single-asset, single-country is the real jurisdiction risk: there is no second mine to carry a bad year.

Differentiator
  1. Silver purity plus the lowest cost of the silver names per silver-equivalent ounce. 93% of revenue from silver at a US$17 cash cost with 141 g/t feed (on the industry's by-product curve it is mid-pack, ~64th percentile, because a pure-silver mine has no by-products to subtract — corrected 3 Oct from "first-quartile") — no other producer of this size offers that combination; Pan American and Coeur are gold companies with silver brands.
  2. Net cash and self-funded growth — H1 OCF US$119M, no equity since 2025, EBRD debt being retired early.
  3. Boumadine's scale — a 5.4 km mineralised trend with 14 rigs on it, 271 koz AuEq/yr in the PEA, a second company inside the first.
  4. Nasdaq listing and GDX inclusion (2026) — index flows that small silver names never get.

Read it honestly: the differentiator is silver purity, and Boumadine — the growth leg the price depends on — is a gold project by value. If it gets built, Aya becomes a balanced Au/Ag producer and the purity premium goes away. Same fact, two sides.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, district-scale · moves the needle: high. Boumadine: 145,719 m YTD, 14 rigs, 360,000 m infill plus 40,000 m step-out through 2027 — the FS depends on converting Inferred, so this is conversion drilling that is the thesis. Zgounder near-mine (16,217 m YTD; 4,770 g/t / 2.4 m) targets life extension beyond 2036 and the west-of-fault block from Q4 2026.

More Boumadine ounces matter less than Indicated Boumadine ounces.

A price-led plan for a producer: 30% at C$30, 30% at C$25, 40% on a green Boumadine feasibility study, with two dated reads that decide whether the price levels still apply.

How the position is builtThree buys: 30% · 30% · 40%
at or below C$30, on a silver-driven fall · at or below C$25 · on a green Boumadine feasibility study (H2 2027), at any price
What the rankings sayChance of a 3× in 3–5 years ~10% · chance it works ~38% · risk 3 of 5 · management C
Market temperature · can the plan buy now?Yes. Aya is a producer, so the junior-miner dials do not apply; only the book-level rule does: keep ≥ 25% cash.
What has to go right

Zgounder has to keep its costs at the higher strip ratio (Q3 results, 12 Nov: cash cost ≤ US$21.50/oz, grade ≥ 140 g/t, guidance kept) after two years of missed guidance under record headlines. Then the Boumadine feasibility study (H2 2027) has to turn a PEA whose resource is 80% Inferred into reserves, a capex and a funding sentence without equity.

Why the stock is priced where it is

At the plan price (~US$3.8B) the market pays about 10× for Zgounder's cash flow and about US$1.6B for Boumadine on a PEA, on a stock with a beta of ~3.3 that moves 20% on a silver wobble. A different kind of plan from the developers': no raise coming, no placement to buy at, no study that creates a first NAV. The rankings give ~10% odds of a 3×, at the luck line; the multibagger case needs silver near US$100.

What the plan does about it

Lets the price come to it. Standing limits at C$30 (about 12× Zgounder's cash flow) and C$25 (pay for Zgounder, get Boumadine free), filled only on silver-driven falls, cancelled on company news; a third of the position reserved for the study, bought at any price if it reads green. This is for owning the best silver cash-flow name on the exchange at a fair price, not for a multibagger.

What to watchPrice C$30 (€19.0) and C$25 (€15.8)Q3 results, 12 Nov 2026Boumadine feasibility study, H2 2027Silver below US$50Any release: "mining law", "guidance", "equity"

Sizing: every amount is a share of the position you decide to hold in this company, whatever that is (100% = the full position). At €4 an order the fee is small; keep each tranche at €200 or more (fee ≤ 2%), and if a tranche would come out smaller, merge it with the next one. Not advice; my read written down in advance so that on the day I compare numbers against thresholds I set beforehand, not against the price move.

Step 1first tranche: 30% at C$30 (€19.0 / US$21.4) or below — the first ordinary pull-back

Nothing at today's ~14× annualised EBITDA. Place a standing limit at C$30 = €19.0, about 20% below the 21 Oct close: a C$4.3B cap, roughly 12× Zgounder's cash flow at ~US$60 silver with Boumadine carried at ~US$1B instead of US$1.6B. A stock with this beta has visited −20% several times in the past year (−7% on 23 Sep alone) without any news about the mine. Limit order only.

  1. Hit on a silver-only move (silver down, Zgounder news unchanged) → fill it. That is the entry the ladder is built for.
  2. Hit on company news (a guidance cut, a Boumadine slip, a Moroccan law change) → cancel the order and go to Step 2 or Step 5 first; a lower price on worse facts is not a discount.
  3. Never hit? Then the plan buys nothing before the FS, and that is fine: at today's price the position would be a bet on silver, which can be made more cheaply elsewhere.

Three or four green → the levels stand. Two or more red → lower every level by 15% (Step 1 to C$25.5 / €16.2, Step 3 to C$21 / €13.3) and cancel any open order; management is already a C for two years of missed guidance under record headlines, and a third miss is a pattern the price has not yet discounted. Step 3second tranche: 30% at C$25 (€15.8 / US$17.8) or below — pay for Zgounder, get Boumadine free

At C$25 the cap is ~C$3.6B, the EV ~US$2.5B — about 10× what Zgounder earns at ~US$60 silver, with nothing in the price for Boumadine. Standing limit at €15.8. It takes a −33% move from the 21 Oct close, which on this stock means a silver drawdown of 15–20% or a cost miss; both have happened in the last twelve months.

  1. Hit with Step 2 green → fill it and bring 15% of the position forward from Step 4; this is the price the plan hopes for.
  2. Hit with Step 2 red → the lowered level applies (C$21 / €13.3); do not fill at C$25.
  3. Silver below US$45 at the time → fill half; at that price the Zgounder margin is ~US$25/oz and 10× is no longer cheap. Hold the rest for Step 4.
Step 4third tranche: 40% — the Boumadine feasibility study (H2 2027): read five numbers before buying at any price
WhatGreenRed
NPVafter-tax NPV8% ≥ US$2.0B at ≤ US$3,000 gold / ≤ US$40 silver< US$1.2B at those decks, or only quoted at 5%

  1. Four or five green → buy 40% within two weeks at the market, whatever the price. A reserve-backed Boumadine funded without equity is the point at which the PEA premium becomes earned; the ladder no longer applies.
  2. Three green → 20% at the market, 20% only at the Step 3 level.
  3. Two or more red → nothing. If NPV and capex are both red, see Step 6: the valuation was carrying US$1.6B for a project that just got smaller.
Step 5overrides — events that change the plan whatever step it is at
  1. Buy at the ladder regardless of the calendar: a silver drawdown of 25%+ with Zgounder guidance intact and costs on guide — the metal, not the mine; fill every open level.
  2. Stop adding and cancel the orders: a Moroccan mining-law draft that changes royalties, tenure or foreign ownership (Morocco is one asset, one country); a Zgounder grade below 130 g/t for two quarters; the FS slipping a second time (H2 2027 → 2028); an equity raise for Boumadine.
  3. Sell half on a takeover bid: producers rarely multibag after a bid; take the premium on half and let the rest see whether a second bidder appears.
  4. Sell everything: January 2027 guidance for 2027 is missed or cut within the year for a third time — the management pattern becomes the thesis.
Step 6once in: sell-or-hold triggers
  1. Sell if the FS lands red on NPV and capex and silver is below US$50 — Zgounder alone at a 10× multiple is then roughly the price, with no reason for a re-rate.
  2. Sell half if the stock doubles from the average entry before the FS; on a producer that is the metal, and the metal gives it back.
  3. Otherwise hold through the Boumadine build (2028–29). The thesis is the lowest-cost pure silver producer adding a second mine from its own cash flow; first production at Boumadine, not the study, is where that is proven.
PracticalWhere to buy, currency, and the most likely outcome

Main liquidity is the TSX (AYA) in CAD; since May 2026 it also trades on Nasdaq (AYA) in USD, the simplest line for a USD account. German venues quote it in EUR with tight spreads for a C$5B name — a EUR limit set from the Toronto close converted at the day's ECB rate will be close to the venue's quote, so this is one of the few names in the file where buying in EUR costs almost nothing extra. The levels above are in CAD because the stock is valued in CAD; the EUR equivalents move with the exchange rate and should be recomputed on the day. Most likely outcome (my read, not a forecast): Q3 costs come in a little above guide and the stock gives up 15–20% into early 2027 on the strip-ratio story and a silver pause — Step 1 fills, Step 3 does not — then the FS lands in late 2027 with a smaller NPV at 8% and a bigger capex than the PEA, still funded without equity: "three green", 20% more. Average entry around C$29 (€18.4) with 50–70% of the planned position bought, no multibagger but a producer bought at ~11× with a second mine coming. If silver runs instead and the stock never pulls back, the plan buys nothing, which is the correct result: at 14× plus a PEA premium, this is a silver trade with extra steps.

Next Catalyst

Q3 results 11 Nov — first costs at ~16:1 strip; 138 koz Ag cement unsmelted at quarter-end and the ore stockpile +16% q/q (inventory build, not catch-up sales) after the record 2.03 Moz AgEq quarter (14 Oct); Boumadine infill results through 2027 and an updated MRE; Boumadine FS H2 2027 (slipped once) with ESIA; infrastructure ground-breaking "end of 2026"; tertiary crusher early 2027 (3,850 tpd steady state); Moroccan mining-law adoption.

  • Can Aya fund a US$463M+ build from cash flow, or does Boumadine bring back the equity market?

  • At what silver price does the market stop paying 14× — and how much of the stock's 3× move was the metal?

Management review
Creal weaknesses: slipped dates, thin fit or thin candourTrack record 3/5 · Fit 4/5 · Candour 2/5 · Skin in the game 1/5

Built Zgounder on budget and 2026 is running to plan, but two straight years of production guidance missed under 'record' headlines plus a failed 2025 pay vote are a pattern, not a yellow flag — the same facts that make B2Gold a C. Odds cut at half weight (producer). Back to B if 2026 guidance is met and said plainly in January.

Fit to this job

New for the team: Boumadine is a polymetallic (Au-Ag-Zn-Pb) project with a much larger build than Zgounder, feasibility now guided H2 2027 (slipped from H1-2027); the Sept 2026 Cu-Ag portfolio acquisition adds a new commodity.

1/5 — under ~0.5%, options only, or net sellers while promoting. Simplified from the original filings (last 8 quarters and 3 fiscal years, US$ millions, fiscal year ends 31 Dec). Every column links to the statements it came from.

What the numbers say
  1. The Zgounder expansion changed the company: revenue US$39M (FY24, with a US$27M impairment and a loss) → US$202M (FY25) → US$214M in H1 2026 alone; gross margin 69% vs 14% in FY24; cash cost down to US$16.8/oz AgEq.
  2. Cash US$49.8M (end 2023) → low of US$18.3M (Mar 2025) → US$182.8M (Jun 2026). The June 2025 C$144M bought deal bridged the gap; since then operations fund everything (H1 2026 operating cash flow US$119M, ~US$80M free cash flow).
  3. Money now goes into the ground at Boumadine (US$42M in FY25, US$25M in H1 2026) while mill capex fell to ~US$15M in H1 2026; EBRD debt is being repaid (US$112M → US$84M).
  4. Shares 122M (end 2023) → 144M (+18%) through two bought deals; no dividends or buybacks. G&A jumped to US$7.9M in Q2 2026 and share-based pay is heavy (US$13.9M in FY25).
  5. Watch: no AISC is disclosed (only cash cost per ounce), Moroccan tax takes ~37% of pre-tax profit, and the 2024 cash-flow comparatives were restated.

Terronera FS (effective 9 Sep 2021, amended May 2023): ~4 Moz Ag + 38 koz Au/yr over 10 years at 2,000 tpd; capex rose from US$230M (construction decision Apr 2023) to US$271M (Jan 2024); the FS NPV/IRR and the final spend were not retrievable (unverified). Pitarrilla: no economic study yet — FS budgeted US$15M for 2026, management's preliminary capex US$500–600M, 3,500–4,000 tpd.

Mid-tier silver producer (Terronera + Guanaceví in Mexico, Kolpa in Peru; ~14.5 Moz AgEq/yr) at US$2.44B, carrying a US$350M convertible and a US$500–600M Pitarrilla build still without a study.

Gate Costs down and Terronera at plan — before Pitarrilla can be financed The 2026 plan said consolidated cash costs of US$12–13/oz silver and AISC of US$27–28; the first half came in at US$23.03 and US$36.96, and management reaffirmed the AISC guidance in July while calling actual costs 'much higher'. On 8 October the company said 2026 production will land 'at or slightly below the low end' of guidance and that production and cost guidance are being recalculated (update 9 November). Terronera is milling 126–152 g/t silver against a 200 g/t reserve grade and produced 7,157 oz gold in Q3 against a 35–36 koz annual guide; Guanaceví is on roughly two years of reserves with a third of its feed bought from third parties; and two blockades (February and 12–24 August 2026) stopped Terronera. Until the unit costs fall into the low-30s or better and Terronera holds plan grades, the cash flow to fund a US$500–600M Pitarrilla is not there without more debt or equity.

Deposit P&P (31 Dec 2025, excl. sold Bolañitos) 7.49 Mt @ 208 g/t Ag, 2.14 g/t Au = 50.0 Moz Ag + 516 koz Au (90.9 Moz AgEq), of which Terronera 7.08 Mt / 45.5 Moz Ag + 505 koz Au; Guanaceví only 0.41 Mt P&P (~1 year of mill feed). Pitarrilla Indicated 158.7 Mt / 491.6 Moz Ag (+ Pb, Zn), Inferred 35.4 Mt / 99.4 Moz Ag. Kolpa has no current NI 43-101 estimate on the company's reserves page (historical M&I 6.2 Mt @ 107 g/t Ag, 3.5% Pb, 3.4% Zn = 21.4 Moz Ag).

Funding & next catalyst
Cash
US$236.6M cash and US$214.4M working capital at 30 Jun 2026 (Q2 2026 results, 29 Jul 2026). A ~US$70M Mexican VAT refund was expected in Q3 2026 (CEO on the Q2 call; receipt not yet confirmed).
Debt
US$350M 0.25% unsecured convertible senior notes due 2031, conversion price US$12.455 (carrying value US$241.2M at 30 Jun 2026); Versamet copper-stream liability US$45.4M carrying (US$59.2M undiscounted); loans payable US$5.6M; gold forward swap liabilities US$65.8M (mostly due within a year; hedges run to June 2027); contingent Kolpa payment US$9.4M. The US$135M Terronera bank facility (ING/SocGen) was fully repaid by June 2026. Net debt on principal basis ≈ US$350M + 45M + 6M − 237M ≈ US$164M (my arithmetic), before the hedge liability.
Burn · runway
Cash-generative at the mine level: Q2 2026 operating cash flow US$39.8M after working capital (US$44.9M before), PP&E spend US$27.8M → free cash flow ~US$12M (my calculation; the company does not define FCF). 2026 capital programme raised to US$181.4M (from US$157.8M) incl. US$48M Pitarrilla capital and a US$15M feasibility study.
Next catalyst
9 Nov 2026 Q3 results with recalculated 2026 production and cost guidance; Pitarrilla feasibility study (management said 'by the end of September 2026' on the Q2 call; not published as of 18 Oct); Kolpa resource update by year-end 2026; January 2027 guidance.
Partly funded to the next catalyst The three mines and the 2026 capital programme are funded from cash and operating cash flow. Pitarrilla is not: management's own preliminary capex range is US$500–600M against ~US$240M of cash (plus the VAT refund) and ~US$190M/yr of AISC margin at US$57 silver. A build decision (targeted around 2027–28 for production ~2030) would need project debt, a stream and/or equity; an ATM with US$35.3M capacity remained at 30 June 2026.
Thesis

Endeavour has just finished its transformation from a two-mine, high-cost Mexican producer into a three-mine, ~14–15 Moz AgEq/yr company: Terronera (built 2022–25, commercial production 1 Oct 2025, 10-year reserve life) and Kolpa (bought May 2025 for US$134M, expanded to 2,500 tpd in Q1 2026) replaced the sold Bolañitos mine. The next step is Pitarrilla in Durango, one of the largest undeveloped silver deposits anywhere (Indicated 492 Moz Ag, Inferred 99 Moz), where management talks about a US$500–600M build, a 3,500–4,000 tpd mill and production around 2030. At US$57 silver the current mines generate roughly US$270–280M of EBITDA a year, so the share price (EV ~US$2.6B) already pays ~9–10× for the existing mines plus an undated option on Pitarrilla.

The Gate

Costs down and Terronera at plan — before Pitarrilla can be financed The 2026 plan said consolidated cash costs of US$12–13/oz silver and AISC of US$27–28; the first half came in at US$23.03 and US$36.96, and management reaffirmed the AISC guidance in July while calling actual costs 'much higher'. On 8 October the company said 2026 production will land 'at or slightly below the low end' of guidance and that production and cost guidance are being recalculated (update 9 November). Terronera is milling 126–152 g/t silver against a 200 g/t reserve grade and produced 7,157 oz gold in Q3 against a 35–36 koz annual guide; Guanaceví is on roughly two years of reserves with a third of its feed bought from third parties; and two blockades (February and 12–24 August 2026) stopped Terronera. Until the unit costs fall into the low-30s or better and Terronera holds plan grades, the cash flow to fund a US$500–600M Pitarrilla is not there without more debt or equity.

Detail
MetricHeadlineDetail
Risk score3/5Three producing mines in two countries, US$237M cash, positive free cash flow and a 10-year reserve at Terronera make permanent loss unlikely — not a 4. Not a 2 because: AISC ~35% above guidance with the guide only now being 'recalculated', two blockades at the flagship in eight months, Guanaceví on ~2 years of reserves, US$350M of convertible debt plus a US$66M hedge liability, insiders selling, and a share price that already fell 46% from its high while silver stayed above US$55. The loss path is a de-rating to a high-cost-producer multiple, not insolvency.
Market cap16 Oct 2026: ~US$2,440M (US$8.24 · ~US$2.44B (NYSE close × 296.14M shares; TSX C$ figure not computed) on ~296.1M shares). US$2.44B at US$8.24 (16 Oct 2026; 296.14M shares), down from a 52-week high of US$15.15 (low US$6.60); EV ~US$2.6B. Shares rose from ~255M (early 2025) through the Kolpa share consideration (US$48–65M at US$4.618), a US$40–50M bought deal at US$3.88 (Apr 2025) and ATM sales; the US$350M convertible (Dec 2025, US$12.455) adds 28.1M shares if converted. (a) Trailing: Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA US$90.0M × 4 = US$360M at US$70 silver → 7.2×; stockanalysis shows 8.7× on reported LTM. (b) At 16 Oct prices: ~8.5 Moz Ag/yr × (57.3 − 35 AISC) = US$190M AISC margin + ~US$90M sustaining capex = EBITDA ~US$280M → EV/EBITDA ≈ 9.3× (9.7× on the 2026 run-rate of ~8.0 Moz). Not cheap for a top-decile-cost producer; the premium is Pitarrilla.

Pitarrilla: no economic study yet — FS budgeted US$15M for 2026, management's preliminary capex US$500–600M, 3,500–4,000 tpd.

La Luz; Parral 32.9 Moz) + Pitarrilla 99.4 Moz Ag + Guanaceví Ag-Pb-Zn 3.9 Moz. · No current NI 43-101 estimate on the company's reserves page; the April 2025 acquisition release cited historical M&I 6.2 Mt @ 3.43 oz/t Ag, 3.47% Pb, 3.41% Zn, 0.28% Cu (21.4 Moz Ag) and Inferred 5.0 Mt (14.6 Moz Ag) and said Endeavour was not relying on them. A resource update is promised by year-end 2026. · Terronera: 10 years (FS; ~7.1 Mt at ~730 kt/yr). AIF: operating mines with current estimates have expected lives of two to ten years.Terronera (Jalisco): 24 concessions / ~17,970 ha, Probable reserve 7.08 Mt @ 200 g/t Ag + 2.22 g/t Au (45.5 Moz Ag, 505 koz Au) plus Inferred 1.03 Mt incl. the high-grade La Luz vein (61 kt @ 150 g/t Ag, 11.4 g/t Au). Guanaceví (Durango): a 20-year-old narrow-vein operation, P&P 0.41 Mt @ 339 g/t Ag, M&I 0.53 Mt @ 360 g/t, Inferred 0.5 Mt @ 436 g/t; the mill also buys third-party ore. Kolpa (Huancavelica, Peru): 143 concessions / 25,177 ha, ~10% worked, 2,500 tpd after the 2026 expansion, 20,100 m of drilling in 2026, resource update due year-end. Pitarrilla (Durango): Indicated 491.6 Moz Ag + Inferred 99.4 Moz (Pb, Zn credits) — one of the world's largest undeveloped silver resources, bought from SSR Mining in 2022; underground sulphide (24.8 Mt @ 146 g/t Ag, 1.0% Pb, 2.1% Zn) is the first-phase target; mill and underground works permitted, dry-stack tailings permit outstanding. Parral: 36.7 Moz Ag Indicated+Inferred, idle.
DividendNone paid.
Valuation Anchor

The market pays ~9–10× EBITDA at today's silver (7× on the Q2 print at US$70 silver) for three mines whose consolidated AISC (US$37/oz) is among the highest in the primary-silver peer set, plus an undated Pitarrilla option. Aya (US$17 cash cost, ~14–15× EBITDA) and Avino (US$39 AISC, ~US$0.9B, no debt) bracket it: Endeavour trades at a lower multiple than Aya but carries net debt and a cost base closer to Avino's. A 3× (US$24.7/share, EV ~US$8B) needs ~US$800M of EBITDA at 10× — silver above ~US$110 on today's asset base, or Pitarrilla built.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~0.5% or less (CEO Dickson 0.097%, ~US$2.9M; simplywall.st, Sep 2026; circular not fetched — unverified); no strategic holder; the register is institutional/retail (Van Eck/GDXJ-type index funds typical for the group, not verified here). Insiders were net sellers: Castro Valdez sold ~77k shares at ~US$13.74 on 28 Jan 2026 (40% of his holding); Dickson sold ~50k at ~US$11.01 on 11 May 2026 and ~250k (US$968k) on 15 Apr 2025. No open-market buys found. Convertible holders (US$350M) are a latent 9.5% dilution above US$12.455.

Read: Nobody inside owns a meaningful stake and the recent direction is selling into strength; the register gives no anchor.

Jurisdiction risk

National: Mexico (two mines, Pitarrilla) — the 2023 mining-law reform (shorter concessions, water permits, no new concessions) and the 7.5% special mining duty; a new dry-stack tailings permit is still needed at Pitarrilla. Peru (Kolpa) — illegal miners on the concessions cited in the AIF; a 2025 Lima state of emergency; Kolpa has operated for decades. Local: Terronera's ejido blockaded the mine twice in 2026 — a security/blockade pause ending 25 Feb 2026 and a 12–24 Aug 2026 blockade over roads, medical services, water access and 'increased financial assistance'; the company called it illegal and threatened legal remedies while 'continuing to work with the Ejido'. Guanaceví depends on third-party ore purchases from local miners.

Two stoppages at the flagship in eight months is the single biggest operating risk; community terms at Terronera are evidently not settled.

Differentiator

Pitarrilla's 492 Moz Ag Indicated is the only resource in this peer group large enough to double the company — and it has no study, no capex and no financing. Terronera is a real new mine with a 10-year reserve at reserve grades well above what is being milled today, so there is grade upside if the sills deliver; Kolpa adds Peru diversification and 25,000 ha barely explored.

The edge is scale of resource; the weakness is that converting it needs US$500–600M the balance sheet does not have.

Exploration upside

Pitarrilla FS + Kolpa resource + Terronera grade · moves the needle: high 2026 budget US$25.9M / 52,500 m: Kolpa 20,100 m (resource update by year-end), Terronera 10,300 m (La Luz and extensions), Guanaceví 8,550 m (reserve replacement on ~2 years of life), Pitarrilla 8,550 m (13 holes / 4,524 m in Q2) plus greenfield in Chile and the USA. The item that matters is not drilling but the Pitarrilla FS and permits.

Next Catalyst

9 Nov 2026: Q3 financials and recalculated 2026 production and cost guidance — the first honest read on where unit costs settle with LNG running and Terronera sills open. Then the Pitarrilla FS (promised 'by the end of September 2026', not yet out) and the Kolpa resource by year-end.

Open Questions
  • Where does consolidated AISC settle in 2027 with LNG, Terronera at 150–200 g/t and Kolpa stabilised — low-30s (the bull case) or high-30s (H1 2026)?
  • What does the Pitarrilla FS show (capex, throughput, AISC, NPV at what deck) and how will US$500–600M be funded without heavy dilution below the US$12.455 conversion price?
  • Is the Terronera ejido relationship settled, or will blockades recur each time demands escalate at higher silver prices?
  • Can Guanaceví keep replacing a one-to-two-year reserve while its grade has fallen from 362 to 235 g/t?
  • Will the Kolpa NI 43-101 resource (year-end 2026) support a 2,500 tpd life beyond a few years?

Management review
Creal weaknesses: slipped dates, thin fit or thin candourTrack record 3/5 · Fit 4/5 · Candour 2/5 · Skin in the game 1/5

Delivered a new mine and a sensible acquisition, but late and over budget, and in 2026 the team reaffirmed a cost guide it was missing by a third, let a study date pass silently and sold stock near the top. Real weaknesses, not a pattern of failing shareholders yet; back to B if the 9 Nov reset is plain and 2027 guidance is met.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Dan Dickson (CEO and director, since CEO since May 2021; previously CFO (c. 2010s)): CPA, CA, ex-KPMG assurance. Led the Terronera build, the Kolpa purchase, the Bolañitos sale and the US$350M convertible. Owns ~0.1%; sold ~250k shares Apr 2025 and ~50k May 2026. · Elizabeth Senez (CFO, since January 2024): Former Group Treasurer, First Quantum Minerals. Said on 29 Jul 2026: 'no plans to do any further metal hedging'. · Luis R. Castro Valdez (COO, since 2026 (with Endeavour since 2004; VP Exploration from 2012)): 33 years in exploration; a geologist now running three mines. Sold ~77k shares (40% of holding) at ~US$13.74 on 28 Jan 2026. · Rex McLennan (Chair, since not stated): Former CFO of Viterra and Placer Dome. · George Paspalas (Independent director, since not stated (post-2025)): Former CEO of MAG Silver (2013–2025), Kinross director — the most relevant operating experience on the board. · Gord Bussieres (VP Projects, since not stated): Two decades at JDS Energy & Mining; the Pitarrilla build would run through him.
Track record
  • Built Terronera: FS (effective Sep 2021) planned plant commissioning end-Q3 2023; commercial production declared 1 Oct 2025 — about two years late; capex US$230M at the Apr 2023 construction decision, US$271M by Jan 2024 (AIF 2025); the mine now runs at nameplate but at 126–152 g/t Ag vs a 200 g/t reserve grade (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1277866/000106299323012527/exhibit99-1.htm; https://edrsilver.com/news-media/news/endeavour-silver-announces-commercial-production-a-11543/; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1277866/000106299326001662/exhibit99-1.htm)
  • Bought Kolpa (Peru) for US$134.3M, closed 1 May 2025, funded by a US$35M copper stream, a US$40M bought deal at US$3.88 and US$48.4M of shares at US$4.618; expanded the plant to 2,500 tpd by end-Q1 2026 as promised; 2026 budget there raised by US$18M (https://edrsilver.com/news-media/news/endeavour-silver-announces-expansion-into-peru-wit-10017/; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001277866/000106299326003913/exhibit99-2.htm)
  • Sold Bolañitos to Guanajuato Silver (US$30M cash + US$10M shares + up to US$10M contingent), closed 15 Jan 2026 — a clean exit from a declining minesource
  • Refinanced: US$350M 0.25% convertible due 2031 at US$12.455 (Dec 2025) repaid the US$135M Terronera bank facility and funds Pitarrilla; cheap money, but the 2025 hedges attached to the bank debt cost US$126M of derivative losses in 2025source
  • 2025 production: Guanaceví 5.01 Moz AgEq inside its 4.8–5.5 guide; Bolañitos 1.83 Moz vs 2.2–2.4 (miss); Guanaceví + Bolañitos silver 4.48 Moz vs 4.5–5.2 guided (just under) (https://edrsilver.com/news-media/news/endeavour-silver-provides-2025-guidance-for-guanac-9874/; https://edrsilver.com/news-media/news/endeavour-silver-announces-q4-2025-financial-resul-13419/)
  • Shareholder outcome: shares rose from ~US$4 (Apr 2025 bought deal at US$3.88) to US$15.15 (52-week high) and back to US$8.24 — the stock doubled with silver, then gave half back on costs and blockades while silver stayed above US$55source

Boards today: Dickson: Endeavour only (as far as found). Paspalas: Kinross Gold director. Johnson: executive at Faraday Copper. No executive runs a second listed company.

Fit to this job
Twenty years of underground narrow-vein silver mining in Mexico; Terronera was the first mine the team built from scratch and it came in late and over budget but works. Pitarrilla — a US$500–600M, 3,500–4,000 tpd project — is a step up in scale and would be the largest build in the company's history; the project VP (Bussieres, ex-JDS) is the relevant hire. Peru is new ground since 2025.
Skin & pay
1/5 — tiny stake from grants, net selling by CEO and COO into the January–May strength, pay rising while the stock fell. Dickson 0.097% (~US$2.9M at US$8.24, mostly grants); sold ~250k shares (US$968k) 15 Apr 2025 and ~50k (US$551k) 11 May 2026; no officer buys found in the last 12 months; insiders net sellers by ~US$2.6M. 2025 CEO pay ~US$1.56M (29% salary / 71% bonus and equity; salary US$447k, +11%) at a ~US$2.4B company. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/materials/nyse-exk/endeavour-silver/management (management information circular not fetched — unverified).

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Cost guidance missed by ~35% in H1 2026 and reaffirmed on the call anyway; the reset comes only with Q3 results in November.
  • Pitarrilla FS date (end-Sep 2026) passed without comment.
  • CEO and COO are net sellers (COO sold 40% of his holding at the January high); the CEO owns ~0.1% while his 2025 pay rose to ~US$1.56M (+~50% y/y per simplywall.st; circular not fetched) in a year the stock later halved.
  • Two Terronera stoppages in 2026 — the community relationship at the flagship is unresolved.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash rose from US$35.3M in December 2023 to US$236.6M in June 2026 while the company spent US$117.8M (FY23), US$195.4M (FY24), US$169.2M (FY25) and US$67.0M (H1 26) on mines and equipment (Terronera build, Kolpa, Pitarrilla); this was funded by US$262M of net equity over FY23-FY25 (shares 217.2M to 296.1M, +36%), the US$120M Terronera bank facility, a US$35M Versamet copper-stream prepayment and, in December 2025, US$339.1M net from a US$350M 0.25% convertible note due 2031.
  2. Debt (loans + convertible + copper stream) went from US$8.5M in December 2023 to a peak of about US$196M in September 2025 and US$292.2M in June 2026, but its shape changed: the bank facility (US$131.9M) and Kolpa loans were repaid from the convertible in December 2025 (US$6.3M early-repayment penalties), so at June 2026 there is no bank debt, only US$5.6M of equipment loans, the convertible (US$350M face, US$241.2M carried) and the US$45.4M copper-stream liability.
  3. Revenue grew from US$205.5M (FY23) and US$217.6M (FY24) to US$467.5M (FY25) and US$421.8M in H1 2026 alone as Terronera (commercial production 1 Oct 2025) and Kolpa (acquired 1 May 2025 for US$134.3M) came in; the mine operating margin (revenue minus cost of sales) rose from 18-19% in FY23-FY25 to 45% in Q1 26 and 35% in Q2 26.
  4. The bottom line was dominated by hedges: 68,000 oz of gold forwards at US$2,311/oz taken for the Terronera loan produced derivative losses of US$30.5M (FY24) and US$126.2M (FY25) and net losses of US$31.5M and US$119.1M; in H1 2026 US$66.3M of cash went to settle these contracts (inside operating cash flow), 33,461 oz remain to be delivered through July 2027 (liability US$63.4M), and H1 net earnings of US$131.4M include a US$36.5M gain on the Bolanitos sale.
  5. Operating cash flow was US$60.6M in H1 2026 against US$67.0M of capex, so free cash flow was slightly negative before the US$27.5M Bolanitos proceeds; AISC rose from US$23.88/oz (FY24) to US$31.52/oz (FY25) and US$36.89/oz in Q2 26 against 2026 guidance of US$27-28/oz, and Q3 26 production (3.6M AgEq oz) was hit by a Terronera blockade and a Guanacevi mill repair, with guidance under review. G&A is about 5% of revenue.

Thesis

Diablillos, on the Salta–Catamarca border at ~4,000 m, is a large oxide silver-gold system (Oculto, JAC and satellites) that AbraSilver has grown from a modest historical resource to M&I 248 Moz Ag + 2.54 Moz Au (Apr 2026) at a discovery cost of ~US$0.10/oz AgEq. The DFS (Jun 2026, Worley): 9,000 tpd open pit and tank leach, 25-year life, years 1–5 averaging 13.9 Moz Ag + 89 koz Au (20.3 Moz AgEq) at AISC US$19.69, initial capex US$721.5M (15.5% contingency), after-tax NPV5% US$3.0B and IRR 41.9% at US$50 Ag / US$3,650 Au; US$4.8B / 56.5% at spot; US$1.9B / 31.4% at the US$40 / US$2,920 downside. Reserves 183.5 Moz Ag + 1.76 Moz Au. Everything that can be de-risked on paper has been: both provincial environmental approvals (Salta Apr 27, Catamarca Jun 24, 2026), RIGI adhesion (Resolution 562/2026 — 25% income tax, 0% export duties, 30-year stability, FX freedom), a Kolla community public hearing without opposition, and a Worley bridging-engineering contract. What is not done: the money. FID has slipped from Q4 2026 → Q2 2027 → "H2 2027"; no debt, stream or partner is announced.

Cash ~C$70M net after a C$50M raise at C$14.70 in July. Kinross (4%) has participation rights and a ROFO on new Argentine projects; Eric Sprott ~8%. Central Puerto sold its entire 9.9% on Sep 16 for C$228M (a US$138M gain) and the stock fell 22% in a week. CEO John Miniotis; Executive Chair Marie Inkster (ex-Lundin Mining CEO). Five analysts, all Buy, avg target C$21.20; company NAVPS C$26 base / C$42 spot.

Valuation Anchor

~0.5× NAV at the DFS deck (~0.3× at spot) on a permitted, RIGI-approved, reserve-backed 25-year mine — the largest defined discount in the file that is actually computable. The re-rate path is textbook: financing package (H1 2027) → FID (H2 2027) → construction → producer multiple; developers at this stage in tier-one Latin American provinces have historically moved from ~0.5× to ~0.8–1.0× NAV through that sequence, which is 1.6–2× on progress alone and 2.5–3.5× if silver holds US$69+.

The bear case is not the mine — it is the terms: a US$720M package at US$40 silver built from a stream on the gold, a project loan with hedging, and equity at a lower price than July's C$14.70, leaving shareholders with less of a bigger pie.

Bucket: scale & financing — the Solaris archetype from the copper file: fully permitted, technically done, one big cheque away.

Read: Two real votes and one loud exit. Sprott has bought twice and held through dilution; Kinross has bought at every price up to C$14.70 — that is a major saying the asset is real at four times the entry price. Against that, Central Puerto took US$163M off the table in a single day and management sold ~C$6.6M within weeks of publishing the DFS. The register is telling you the asset is good and the next twelve months are hard; both are true.

Jurisdiction risk

National: the best Argentina has offered a miner in thirty years. Milei's coalition won the Oct 2025 midterms; RIGI is law and Diablillos is approved under it (US$482M investment, 25% tax, 0% export duties, 30-year stability, FX freedom phasing to 100% by year 4); export duties on all mining already 0% since Aug 2025; the Apr 2026 glacier-law reform handed periglacial oversight to provinces — helpful at 4,000 m, and being litigated. Mining exports +74% in H1 2026. The risk is reversal: RIGI is a Milei policy, and a Sep 2026 political row over Central Puerto's RIGI-linked gain shows the opposition's line of attack.

Provincial / local: strong. Salta is the Fraser Institute's top Latin American jurisdiction; both Salta and Catamarca issued DIAs within two months of each other and ratified an inter-provincial cooperation agreement; the Kolla community of Santa Rosa de los Pastos Grandes attended the public hearing without recorded opposition. Physical constraints are the local issue: 4,000 m, water (60 L/s), solar-diesel power, contract mining, a 2.5-year build in the Puna.

Same national tailwind as Argenta, one valley over; a far more advanced project, and therefore far more exposed if the tailwind reverses.

Differentiator
  1. Everything except the money is done — permits, RIGI, DFS, reserves, engineering partner, land, community. No other developer in this file has both environmental approvals, a fiscal-stability regime and a definitive feasibility study in hand simultaneously.
  2. Scale and life — 25 years, 20 Moz AgEq/yr in the first five, 366 Moz AgEq of reserves, with a 130 Mt heap-leach resource (PEA Q4 2026) and Oculto West / Cerro Viejo drilling outside the pit as free options.
  3. A team that has sold companies and run a major — Miniotis (AuRico → Centerra), Inkster (Lundin Mining CEO), Weyland (Lundin/Kinross), a project director from Lydian and AngloGold; plus Kinross on the register with participation rights.
  4. The cleanest multiple in the file — 0.5× NAV, no warrants, no debt, five Buy ratings, a C$50M raise done at C$14.70 with no discount to the market.

Read it honestly: the differentiator (a de-risked, buildable, US$720M project) and the gate (financing US$720M) are the same fact. And the two things that happened after the DFS — insiders selling and the anchor exiting — are the market's own read of how hard the next step is.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, expanding beyond the pit · moves the needle: medium. Phase VI (15,000 m, fully funded, three rigs) is finding ounces outside the DFS pit: Oculto East DDH-26-061 228 m @ 1.79 g/t Au in oxides incl. 66 m @ 4.04 g/t (21 Oct 2026, ~50 m below the pit floor, outside the resource — the best gold hole on the project), Oculto West 109 m @ 221 g/t Ag / 0.72 g/t Au, Condoryacu 72 m @ 18.7 g/t Au + 2.1% Cu from surface, Cerro Viejo (new gold target 4 km north). With 454 Moz AgEq M&I already, more ounces extend life and support a second phase (water permitting); a high-grade gold core under the pit could also lift the Phase 1 plan when the MRE is redone in Q2 2027. They do not change the financing question. La Coipita (Cu-Au, Teck earn-in to 80%) is a free option.

The next MRE (early 2027) and heap-leach PEA (Q4 2026) matter for the expansion case, not the FID.

Next Catalyst

Financing package — debt / stream / partner (undated; the whole re-rate); heap-leach PEA ("in the coming weeks", 21 Oct release); early works and long-lead procurement (funded from July raise); Phase VI results through Q4 (drilling ends by year-end) and an updated MRE (Q2 2027, now with the Oculto East gold core to add); FID Q2 2027 per the 21 Oct release, H2 2027 in the September deck (slipped twice before); Central Puerto's exit fully absorbed; any Argentine political move against RIGI.

Open Questions
  • What does the financing package look like — how much stream, how much debt, at what silver price, and how much equity at what price?
  • Who buys Central Puerto's 9.9%, and does Kinross step up from 4% or stay a passenger?
  • What does the DFS look like at reserve prices (US$29.50 / US$2,800) — does the IRR still clear 25%?
  • Why did the FID slip from Q4 2026 to H2 2027 within nine months, and is H2 2027 real?
  • Does the water plan (60 L/s) survive a 25-year, 9,000 tpd operation in the Puna — and what does an expansion cost in water rights?
  • Can this team build a US$720M mine at 4,000 m on schedule, having never built one?
Context & updates
21 Oct 2026 update

Best gold hole yet at Oculto East (DDH-26-061: 228 m at 1.79 g/t Au in oxides, incl. 66 m at 4.04 g/t), a high-grade core about 50 m under the DFS pit floor and outside the current resource; shares +12.5% to C$12.70. Timing from the release: Phase VI drilling finishes by year-end, heap-leach PEA in the coming weeks, updated resource Q2 2027, FID on schedule for Q2 2027 (the September deck said H2 2027). The financing gate is unchanged.

3 Oct 2026 refresh

No release since 9 Sep. The heap-leach PEA is still Q4 and there is no financing package. Company sources conflict on FID timing: the Chair's September letter says H1 2027, the September deck H2 2027.

Central Puerto exit (Sep 16, 2026)

Sold its entire 9.9% (~16.4M shares) for C$228.4M / US$163.1M — a US$137.6M gain on a US$25.5M cost — paid out as an extraordinary dividend Sep 25; "no longer strategic." Buyer undisclosed. Stock −22% in the following week. Argentine opposition deputy alleged a RIGI-linked windfall; no legal action.

DFS (Jun 22, 2026)

NPV5% US$3.0B / IRR 41.9% / payback 1.7 yr at US$50 / US$3,650; capex US$721.5M; 25-yr LOM; 20.3 Moz AgEq/yr years 1–5 at AISC US$19.69. Technical report filed Jul 21. FID guided Q2 2027 in the release, H2 2027 in the Sep deck.

Permits and RIGI (2026)

RIGI approved Feb 27, resolution published May 11 (US$481.7M approved investment, US$352M minimum in two years to Nov 2027). Salta DIA Apr 27; Catamarca DIA Jun 24 — "final major permitting milestone." Worley bridging engineering Aug 27; project director hired Aug 17.

Financings

Jan/Feb 2025 C$48.4M @ C$2.55; Oct 2025 C$46.2M LIFE @ C$7.10 (Sprott participated); Jul 2026 C$50M bought deal @ C$14.70 + Kinross C$2M (NBF / Beacon / Raymond James), no warrants. Cash C$23.5M at Jun 30 → ~C$70M net post-raise. H1 2026 spend C$23.8M exploration; net loss C$30.1M.

Aside

TSX30 #1-tier performer (+904% over three years to Jun 2026). The AgEq figures use US$34.50 / US$3,200 (MRE) and US$50 / US$3,650 (DFS) — different ratios; strip back to Ag and Au before comparing to Vizsla. No Central Asia Metals involvement (a confusion with Central Puerto).
