Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 4/5 · Skin in the game 1/5

Delivered explorer-to-DFS-and-permits on the dates promised; the build is new for this team, capex doubled across studies and insiders sold into the DFS.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
John Miniotis (President, CEO & Director, since CEO Dec 2019; joined board July 2026): Corporate-development/capital-markets background: Barrick corp dev, BMO and Wellington West equity research, Lundin Mining corp dev/IR, VP Corp Dev AuRico Metals (sold to Centerra ~C$310M, 2018), CEO Aethon Minerals (merged into AbraSilver 2019). · Marie Inkster (Executive Chair, since Board Sept 2025; Executive Chair July 2026): CPA; President & CEO of Lundin Mining Oct 2018–Dec 2022 (operator of multiple base-metal mines); stepped down citing personal reasons. · Jeremy Weyland, P.Eng. (COO (leads Diablillos execution), since COO July 2026; previously SVP Projects & Development): Lundin Mining Director of Project Studies / acting VP Technical Services (2017+); 10 yrs Kinross projects/strategy; led feasibility studies in Chile/Brazil and due diligence on Josemaria, Caserones. Study and DD background, not a construction-director track record. · Carlos Pinglo (CFO, since unverified): Sold C$2.5M of stock June 2026 (62% of direct holdings).
Track record
  • Miniotis: AuRico Metals (VP Corp Dev) acquired by Centerra for ~C$310M in Jan 2018 — a win in the 2016-18 upcycle; Aethon Minerals merged into AbraSilver 2019source
  • Miniotis has run AbraSilver since Dec 2019: from a ~C$20M explorer to a C$2.1B developer with DFS and environmental approval — explorer-to-developer job done once, heresource
  • Inkster: CEO of Lundin Mining 2018-2022 (ran Candelaria, Chapada, Neves-Corvo, Eagle, Zinkgruvan; acquired Chapada US$800M 2019); left at end-2022, said decision was personal, not board dissatisfactionsource
  • Diablillos study capex rose at every step: US$374M (PFS Mar 2024) → US$544M (updated PFS Dec 2024, +45%) → US$722M (DFS June 2026, +33%); NPV rose alongside on higher prices and tax changes (https://www.mining.com/abrasilver-update-at-diablillos-raises-npv-and-costs-by-about-half/ ; https://thedeepdive.ca/abrasilver-pegs-diablillos-npv-at-4-8-billion-in-definitive-feasibility-study/)
  • DFS promised 'first half of 2026' in Dec 2024 — delivered 23 June 2026, on time (https://www.mining.com/abrasilver-update-at-diablillos-raises-npv-and-costs-by-about-half/ ; https://thedeepdive.ca/abrasilver-pegs-diablillos-npv-at-4-8-billion-in-definitive-feasibility-study/)
  • No prior mine built by Miniotis or Weyland; Inkster is the only executive who has run operating minessource

Boards today: Miniotis: AbraSilver only verified. Inkster: AbraSilver executive chair; other current boards unverified (previously Lundin Mining board). Weyland: none found.

Fit to this job
Same stage done once (explorer→DFS) by this CEO at this company. Same region: Argentine Puna, Catamarca/Salta — team has handled Argentine permitting (RIGI, EIA) successfully. What is NEW: building a US$722M open-pit, agitated-leach silver-gold mine. Neither CEO nor COO has been the construction executive on a mine build; Weyland's experience is studies and due diligence at a major. Inkster adds operator credibility but as chair, not builder. Expect an owner's-team/EPCM hire (Worley led DFS) to carry construction.
Skin & pay
1/5 — under ~0.5%, options only, or net sellers while promoting. CEO Miniotis holds ~0.86% (~C$18M) — mostly via grants/options, not verified as market purchases. Insider selling: ~C$6.6M of named SEDI sales in the weeks after the Jun 2026 DFS (the card's figure); SimplyWall.st puts 12-month net selling at ~C$11M, a vendor aggregate that also counts option-exercise sales (CFO Pinglo sold C$2.5M June 2026; chief geologist O'Connor exercised options C$1.9M). CEO total comp C$1.62M (22% salary, 78% bonus/equity) — about 0.08% of C$2.1B market cap, proportionate. Group D&O ownership % from 2026 circular not retrieved (wrong document returned).source

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Capex nearly doubled across three studies in 27 months (US$374M → US$722M) while headlines always led with NPV.
  • Insiders net sellers: ~C$6.6M of named SEDI sales right after the DFS (card), ~C$11M over 12 months per SimplyWall.st (vendor aggregate); CFO sold 62% of his direct holdings June 2026, days after the DFS.
  • Project financing (Q4 2026 target) and FID (Q2 2027) not yet done — the biggest promises are still open.
  • No mine-building executive on staff yet.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash plus term deposits were C$23.5M at 30 June 2026, and a July 2026 C$50M bought deal lifts liquidity to about C$70M, roughly 12 months of runway.

  4. Shares outstanding rose from 113.3M in December 2023 to 165.5M in August 2026, up 46%, after about C$190M of equity raised, all at rising prices.
  5. No debt remains after the final US$6.85M Diablillos payment in April 2025; the 2024 going-concern note was dropped in 2025, and key management pay was C$3.3M in H1 2026.

Thesis

Panuco, in the Sierra Madre 40 km from Mazatlán, is a high-grade epithermal vein district consolidated by Vizsla since 2019 — 413,000 m drilled, 1,100 holes. The feasibility study (Nov 2025) is the strongest set of numbers in this file: initial capex US$239M, after-tax NPV5% US$1.80B and IRR 111% at US$35.50 Ag / US$3,100 Au, payback 7 months, AISC US$10.61/oz AgEq, 17.4 Moz AgEq/yr over 9.4 years from reserves of 102.7 Moz Ag + 829 koz Au at 416 g/t AgEq. It is fully funded: US$406.5M cash (Jul 31, 2026) after a US$115M equity raise (Jun 2025) and US$300M of 5% convertible notes (Nov 2025, conversion US$5.84), plus an undrawn FIFOMI working-capital line. Engineering and procurement are underway — M3 (EPCM), Mining Plus/Byrnecut (mine design), FLSmidth (eight equipment packages) — targeting a construction decision in H2 2026 and first silver in H2 2027. Then January 2026: ten Mexican employees were abducted at gunpoint from the Concordia compound; nine are confirmed dead, one missing; the Sinaloa Cartel's Chapitos faction mistook them for rivals. The site has been suspended since Jan 23 — no drilling, no underground development, no bulk-sample results — and the environmental permit (MIA, filed Q1 2025, guided "mid-2026") has not arrived. CEO Michael Konnert and Chair Craig Parry (Inventa Capital); new Mexico president and government-relations VP hired 2026. Analysts: NBF and CIBC downgraded in Feb–Mar; no coverage updates in 90 days.

The Gate

Reopening the site and receiving the MIA — two things outside the company's control, in the state that hosts Mexico's most violent cartel war. Every economic number is excellent and every operational number since January is zero. The construction decision was guided for H2 2026 "on permit receipt"; the permit is overdue, SEMARNAT granted three environmental approvals in all of 2025, the 2023 mining-law regulation is still unpublished, and the Sheinbaum government has opened a labour-conditions probe into the company after the abductions.

Sub-gates
  1. The bulk sample — the 10,000 t reconciliation test that was to validate grade and ground conditions before construction was never completed.
  2. The accusation — ex-workers told CBC that local management coordinated with armed groups; the company categorically denies it, but the FGR is investigating.
  3. The timeline — H2 2027 first silver assumes a 2026 restart that has not happened; each quarter of suspension pushes production and burns ~US$20M.
  4. The royalty — a 2–3.5% NSR now sits with Elemental (no buyback), after Vizsla Royalties was sold for C$327M in September.

The FS is not the gate. The FS is done. The question is whether a mine can be built and staffed in Concordia municipality in 2027.

Valuation Anchor

~0.7× NAV at a stale deck, ~0.4× at spot, on a fully-funded, feasibility-stage, 111%-IRR project — the cheapest defined ounces in the file, and the market is not wrong to price them that way. The discount is not Mexico in the abstract; it is Concordia, Sinaloa, specifically — a site the company itself has not reopened in nine months.

The bull case: MIA arrives, site restarts under new security arrangements, construction decision in H1 2027, first silver 2028, and the stock re-rates toward 0.8–1.0× a spot NAV of US$3B+ — a 2–3× from here on progress alone.

The bear case: a permanent 40–50% security discount, a permit that arrives late or with conditions, and a workforce that will not come back — in which case US$406M of cash is the floor and the equity trades on it. Bucket: cheap defined ounces — reserves, FS, funded; the discount is one variable (site/permit), legible and binary.

Buys: director Pokrandt 170k (Nov–Dec 2025, ~C$1.2M); director Cobbold 89k (Jun 2026). Twelve months to Jan 2026: insiders bought C$1.3M, sold C$7.0M.
Strategic & prominent
No 10%+ holder. Eric Sprott put C$10M in the 2020 placement (last filing Apr 2022: 5.2M shares + 5.3M warrants, 3.5%); no disclosure since — current stake unknown. Institutions ~52% of the register (158 filers): Sprott Inc 4.9%, Tidal/SILJ 3.9% and adding (Sep 2026), Franklin 3.8%, Global X 3.7%, Van Eck 3.7%, Jupiter 2.8%, Vanguard 2.7%, Waratah, Fourth Sail, Ninepoint, Mackenzie. Macquarie's mining vice-chair sits on the board (Macquarie held a US$220M project-finance mandate in 2025, since superseded by the converts). No Rule, Gentile, Palisades or Crescat found.
Institutions / retail
Institutions ~52%, insiders ~5%, retail ~43%. 355.0M shares; FD ~379M; US$300M converts → 51.4M shares at US$5.84 (capped call to US$10.51). Inventa Capital (Parry/Konnert) incubated Vizsla Silver, Vizsla Copper and Vizsla Royalties; no fees paid to Inventa by VZLA.

Read: A founder-led, institution-owned register where the founders have been quietly selling into strength for two years and sold C$6.3M two weeks before the worst event in the company's history. Nobody with a name has bought the drawdown; the buyers are silver ETFs. Read the ownership as 'index money on a project the insiders were already trimming' — not as a vote against the asset, but not as a vote for it either.

Jurisdiction risk

National: the hardest permitting regime in the file, in a country with no new concessions. Sheinbaum has reiterated no new mining concessions; Camimex counts three environmental permits granted in 2025 and ~US$11B of projects waiting; the 2023 mining-law reform (30-year concessions, water prerequisite, community benefit-sharing) has been upheld by the Supreme Court but its regulation is still unpublished; an open-pit ban bill is pending (Panuco is underground). Panuco's MIA is caught in exactly this queue.

Local: the worst security layer in either file, by an order of magnitude. The Chapitos–Mayos war since the Sep 2024 Zambada rendition has made Culiacán and Concordia municipality a battlefield: mass displacement, up to 15,000 troops, US FTO designation, and in April 2026 US indictments of ten Sinaloa politicians including the sitting governor. Vizsla's ten workers were killed in that war. The five ejido agreements (30 years) are intact and there is no community opposition — the community is the victim. Water is from underground dewatering; the TSF is conventional slurry, not dry-stack.

Same country as Avino and Coeur's Mexican mines; not the same risk. Durango and Chihuahua are not Concordia.

Differentiator
  1. Economics nobody else in the file can match — and cash to build them. A 111% IRR, 7-month payback, US$10.61 AISC, 416 g/t AgEq reserves, and US$406M in the bank against US$239M of capex: the only developer here that needs no financing, no partner and no stream to reach production.
  2. Execution is procured — EPCM (M3), mine contractor (Byrnecut), equipment (FLSmidth) all under contract or mandate; this is a project waiting for permission, not for engineering.
  3. District scale behind the reserve — 128.8 Moz Ag + 1.04 Moz Au M&I plus 74 Moz Inferred, 413,000 m of drilling, a new discovery (Animas) and the Fresnillo ground added in December.
  4. Balanced metal — ~60% silver / 40% gold means it is silver torque with a gold floor, and the only silver developer here with reserves in the Measured category.

Read it honestly: the differentiator is a built-and-funded project in a district the cartel controls; the FS numbers are why the stock is US$1.4B and the site closure is why it isn't US$3B. Same fact, two sides.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, district-scale · moves the needle: medium — but paused. 2026 was to be a 60,000 m year with 13,000 m of underground infill from the 480 level; effectively nothing has been drilled since January. Animas (897 g/t AgEq / 5.8 m) and the San Dimas corridor land package are the upside; Copala at depth and Napoleon are the reserve-conversion targets. With 129 Moz M&I already, exploration adds mine life, not the investment case.

The resource is not the constraint. Access is.

What has to go right

The numbers are finished (feasibility study: NPV US$1.80B, IRR 111% at US$35.50 silver; US$406M cash against US$239M capex; contractors signed). What is missing is a site anyone has worked on since the January abductions, guided to reopen by end-2026 under an army-backed camp, and the environmental permit (MIA), guided for Q4 2026–Q1 2027 after slipping from mid-2026. Then a construction decision funded without equity.

Why the stock is priced where it is

At US$3.09 the enterprise value is ~US$990M, 0.55× the FS NPV at a silver price now 35% below spot. The cheapest set of defined, funded ounces in the file, and the market is not wrong: it is pricing the chance that Concordia cannot be mined by this company in 2027. The realistic re-rate if both facts arrive by mid-2027 (~45% odds) is ~1.1–2×; a 3× needs silver near US$90.

What the plan does about it

Lets the money follow the two events that answer the question, and only a small starter follow the price, at a level under February's low where cash covers 42% of the share. The restart tranche has a cap (US$4.50) because paying 45% more for an open site is the point; the permit tranche has none, because a permitted, funded, procured build is the asset the study described.

Step 1optional starter: 20% at US$2.75 (€2.46 / C$3.85) or below — a silver-driven or no-news fall only

Nothing at today's price. Place a standing limit at US$2.75 = €2.46, 11% below the 23 Oct close and under the US$2.88 low of February: a new twelve-month low reached on silver alone, which this stock — down 28% in a month on a 12% silver fall and no company news — is capable of. At US$2.75 the cap is ~US$976M and the EV ~US$870M: 0.48× the FS NPV, ~0.28× the +50% case, and cash of US$1.14 a share covers 42% of the price (US$0.30 a share after the US$300M of notes). The starter is small because nothing it buys is resolved — the site is still closed at any price — and because the two later tranches are tied to events that will be announced with the price already up. It exists because a restart release could gap the stock 30% on a Tuesday and a 0% position has nothing to add to.

  1. Hit on silver or on silence (silver down, no company release) → fill it.
  2. Hit on company news — a restart date slipping past Q1 2027, an FGR charge against an officer, a second incident, an equity or stream announcement — → cancel the order; see Step 5. A lower price on worse facts is not a discount here, because the facts are the whole discount.
  3. Never hit? Then the plan buys nothing before the restart, which is fine: the thesis is the events, not the level.

  3. Sell half on a takeover bid: a bid from a producer is the most likely way this re-rates fast; take the premium on half and let the rest see whether a second bidder appears.

Step 6once in: sell-or-hold triggers
  1. Sell if no construction decision has been taken by 31 Dec 2027: two years of guidance will then have failed, and the cash will have fallen toward the capex it was meant to exceed.
  2. Sell half if the stock doubles from the average entry before first silver; on a developer that is the re-rate arriving early, and the metal can take it back.
  3. Otherwise hold through the build to first silver (company: H2 2027; realistically 2028). The thesis is a funded 111%-IRR mine reaching production; first doré, not the permit, is where it is proven.
PracticalWhere to buy, currency, and the most likely outcome

Two main lines: NYSE American (VZLA) in USD, about 5M shares a day, and the TSX (VZLA) in CAD. German venues quote it in EUR; for a US$1.1B name the spread is modest, but set any EUR limit from the New York close converted at the day's ECB rate and use limit orders only. The levels above are in US dollars because the card, the US line and the company's own reporting are in US dollars; the EUR equivalents move with the exchange rate and should be recomputed on the day. Most likely outcome (my read, not a forecast): the return to site slips into Q1 2027 but happens, under an army-backed camp; the MIA arrives in Q2 2027 with standard conditions; the construction decision follows mid-2027 and first silver moves to 2028. Along the way silver keeps the stock drifting — Step 1 fills around US$2.75 if silver gives up another 10%, Step 3 fills at US$3.50–4.00 on the restart, Step 4 at US$4.50–5.50 on the decision: 60–100% of the planned position at an average near US$4, for a stock that trades toward ~0.8× a US$3B spot NAV (US$6–7) by first pour. That is a 1.5–2×, not the 3× the rankings give 8% odds to; the 3× needs silver above ~US$90 or a bid. If the site does not reopen by mid-2027, the plan owns at most the 20% starter and sells it, which is the correct result for a project whose only problem is also its only variable.

Next Catalyst

Return to site (guided by end-2026, temporary camp with army barracks); MIA + change of land use (guided Q4 2026–Q1 2027 on 29 Sep; was mid-2026); construction decision after the permits, realistically H1 2027 (was H2 2026); mining-contract award; Byrnecut NTP; bulk-sample / reconciliation results; Q2 FY27 results (Dec) — cash burn and any suspension update; FGR investigation outcome; new coverage after two downgrades.

  • When does the site reopen, under what security arrangements, and who staffs it — the same Concordia workforce, or contractors flown in?
  • Does the MIA arrive in 2026, and with what conditions, in a regime that granted three in 2025?
  • Is there anything to the ex-workers' allegation that local management coordinated with an armed group — and what does the FGR conclude?
  • What did the 10,000 t bulk sample show, or was it never processed?
  • At what point does US$20M/quarter of burn with no site activity start to erode the 'fully funded' claim?
  • Why did the CEO and COO sell ~C$6.3M of stock two weeks before the abduction — and has any insider bought since?
Context & updates
3 Oct 2026 refresh

Site still closed. On 29 Sep the CEO said the aim is to be back on site by end-2026 with a temporary camp that houses an army barracks, and re-guided the environmental permit (MIA) and land-use change to Q4 2026–Q1 2027 (was mid-2026). No construction decision yet; the company still targets first silver H2 2027 / first pour mid-2028.

Abduction (Jan 23, 2026) and aftermath

Ten employees taken from the Concordia compound; bodies recovered from a clandestine grave near El Verde; 9 confirmed dead by Apr 6, 1 missing. Chapitos regional boss arrested Jun 2; two more Sep 9. Site suspended since; engineering continues remotely. Stock −41% in two weeks. Nationwide miner protests Feb 14; FGR probe of labour conditions; company denies extortion, ransom or coordination.

Q1 FY27 (Jul 31, 2026; MD&A Sep 4)

Cash US$406.5M (−US$20.8M in the quarter); net loss US$19.8M; no drilling, no UG development; convertible notes US$300M face. "Construction decision subject to completion of permitting." Chief Geologist resigned Aug 27.

Procurement (Apr–Jun 2026)

M3 Engineering EPCM (~US$170M scope); Mining Plus / Byrnecut mine design (US$50M development capex + US$40M ore development pre-production); FLSmidth eight equipment packages sized for 3,300/4,000 tpd. FIFOMI MXN 173M (~US$10M) working-capital line, undrawn.

Royalty (Sep 15, 2026)

Elemental Royalty completed the C$327M acquisition of Vizsla Royalties — a 2.0–3.5% NSR on Panuco with no buyback — so the royalty is now held by a third party. Vizsla no longer holds VROY.

Aside

The FS deck (US$35.50 Ag) is now about half of spot; every published multiple is on stale prices. Insider sales by the CEO (310k @ C$7.78–8.22) and COO (500k @ C$7.79) on Jan 9–12 preceded the incident by two weeks.

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 2/5

Real builders hired and fully funded; the founders are financiers with several roles who sold stock in the drawdown, and permit dates have drifted via conference remarks.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Michael Konnert (President, CEO & Founder, since Sept 2017 (founded Vizsla; Panuco optioned 2019)): Deal-maker/financier: co-founder and managing partner of Inventa Capital (raised >C$800M); co-founded CobaltOne Energy (2017, acquired by Blackstone Minerals — small). Also executive chairman of Vizsla Royalties, director of Vizsla Copper and Summa Silver. · Craig Parry (Chairman (founder), since Dec 2018): Geologist; Rio Tinto 2000-08; co-founder NexGen Energy (Arrow discovery) and IsoEnergy (Hurricane); lead director Skeena Resources; executive chairman & CEO Vizsla Copper. Serial founder with several concurrent roles. · Simon Cmrlec (COO & Director, since Director since formation; COO appointed 2024/25 (date unverified)): 30+ yrs; former COO of Ausenco (EPCM builder of many plants); Olympic Dam (WMC), Goro Nickel project manager (Inco). The genuine mine-builder on the team. · Dave D'Antonio, P.Eng. (SVP Technical Services, since unverified (2025)): Ex head of mine technical services at K92 Kainantu; OceanaGold Didipio — underground operations experience. · Luis Lázaro (President, Mexico, since unverified): Mexican industrial CEO (Citrofrut, CEMEX ops) — not a miner.
Track record
  • Konnert: built Vizsla from an option deal (2019) to a C$1.9B company with a feasibility study (Nov 2025) and US$450M cash — explorer-to-FS job done once, heresource
  • Konnert's prior company CobaltOne Energy was acquired by Blackstone Minerals (small, outcome value not verified)source
  • Parry: NexGen (Arrow) and IsoEnergy (Hurricane) are major uranium discoveries from the 2013-2022 cycle; neither has been built or sold yet; Tigers Realm Coal (ASX) went nowhere for shareholderssource
  • Cmrlec: COO of Ausenco — a contractor that has delivered multiple precious-metal process plants; his personal project record at Vizsla is untestedsource
  • Spin-outs: Vizsla Copper (2021) and Vizsla Royalties (2024) — Konnert/Parry hold executive roles at both; value creation for VZLA shareholders from these not quantifiedsource

Boards today: Konnert: Vizsla Silver (CEO), Vizsla Royalties (exec chair), Vizsla Copper (director), Summa Silver (director) = 4. Parry: Vizsla Silver (chair), Vizsla Copper (exec chair & CEO), Skeena (lead director), plus Surge Copper/Gold Bull/Outback Goldfields per 2023 circular = 5-6. Both are stretched across several companies while Panuco heads into construction.

Fit to this job
Same stage done once by this team (explorer→FS, here). Mexico: Konnert/Parry had no prior Mexican operating history; they hired for it (Lázaro, Hernandez, Gómez Olmos ex-FIFOMI). Underground narrow-vein silver-gold at ~4,000 tpd is new for the executives; Cmrlec (plant builder) and D'Antonio (underground technical) cover the gap on paper. What is NEW and unproven: running a mine site in cartel-contested Sinaloa after 10 workers were abducted and 9 killed in Jan 2026 — this is now a security-management job none of them has done.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake from grants or cheap founder paper; little buying. CEO Konnert ~0.77% (~C$14.8M), chairman Parry holdings not quantified; both net sellers over the last 12 months — SimplyWall.st aggregate: Konnert -C$3.8M, Parry -C$2.0M (217k sh at C$5.14, June 2026); the card's SEDI-based figures are Konnert ~C$2.4M (310,000 sh at C$7.78–8.22, 9 & 12 Jan 2026) and COO Cmrlec C$3.9M (500,000 sh at C$7.79, 9 Jan 2026), two weeks before the abduction — the two sources count different windows and transactions. Only notable insider buy: director Harry Pokrandt C$1.0M at C$7.09 (Dec 2025). CFO exercised 225k options at C$2.31 (June 2026). CEO total comp US$2.07M, 15% salary / 85% bonus-equity (SimplyWall.st, latest year) — ~0.15% of a C$1.9B market cap. 2023 circular shows 208M shares then; current D&O group % not retrieved.source

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Insiders net sellers of ~C$11M in 12 months (SimplyWall.st aggregate: CEO Konnert -C$3.8M, chairman Parry -C$2.0M incl. 217k sh at C$5.14 June 2026, during the post-abduction drawdown); on SEDI the card shows Konnert ~C$2.4M and COO Cmrlec C$3.9M sold on 9–12 Jan 2026, two weeks before the abduction.
  • Timeline drift communicated in conference remarks rather than a plain revised-guidance release; H2-2027 first silver and mid-2028 first pour coexist.
  • CEO and chairman each hold 4-6 public roles including sister companies (Vizsla Copper, Vizsla Royalties).
  • Site inaccessible since late Jan 2026; the security problem is structural (Sinaloa cartel conflict), not a one-off.
  • CEO comp US$2.07M (85% equity/bonus) at a pre-construction developer.
  • AGM 8 Oct 2026 (6-K): 34% of votes withheld from chairman Craig Parry and 41% from director David Cobbold, against 96–99.8% support for the others — a protest vote after the January abductions and the governance questions since.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash was US$406.5M at 31 July 2026 after a US$300M 5% convertible note and US$126.7M of equity in FY26; that covers years until Panuco construction starts.
  2. Overhead is large and growing: FY26 cash G&A was US$16.2M plus US$10.9M of share-based pay, against US$32.8M of capitalised exploration, about a third of spend.
  3. In Q1 FY27 overhead exceeded in-ground spending as capitalised exploration dropped to US$3.1M while spend shifts to engineering and holding costs.
  4. Shares outstanding rose from 232.6M in April 2024 to 355.0M in July 2026, up 53%; the notes could add 51.4M shares on conversion at US$5.84.
  5. Quarterly net income is dominated by fair-value swings on the notes' conversion feature, a US$49.5M derivative at FY26 year-end; the first US$9.6M coupon was paid in July 2026.

Thesis

Los Ricos South, in the Hostotipaquillo district of Jalisco, is a high-grade silver-gold underground project (with a late-life open pit) that GoGold has advanced since 2019 alongside Parral, a Chihuahua tailings-reprocessing operation that has thrown off cash since 2014 (FY2025: 2.15 Moz AgEq, US$72.5M revenue, US$25.7M operating cash flow). The FS (Jan 2025): initial capex US$227M, after-tax NPV5% US$355M and IRR 28% at US$26.80 Ag / US$2,330 Au — a deck now less than half of spot; 7.3 Moz AgEq/yr in years 1–5 at AISC US$11.19; 15-year life; reserves 47.8 Moz Ag + 457 koz Au at 145 g/t / 1.39 g/t; 2,000 tpd long-hole with paste fill. After a permit wait that ran from "mid-2024" to Jun 8, 2026 (SEMARNAT approvals granted; board approved construction the same day), the build began Aug 25, 2026: M3 as EPCM, >150 contractors on site, plant design 90%, all long-lead orders placed (SAG mill May 2027 is the critical path), Cominvi mobilising underground in Q4, powerline Nov 2026, portal and paste plant Jan 2027, first pour Q2 2028. Funding: US$284M cash and no debt, stream, royalty or offtake — from two bought deals (C$86M at C$1.82, Apr 2025; C$144M at C$2.65, Nov 2025) plus Parral cash flow; the company models cash never falling below US$130M through the build. Los Ricos North (PEA 2023: NPV US$413M, 110 Moz AgEq) is the sequel, to be permitted around first pour. CEO Brad Langille built Ocampo and El Cubo (Gammon Gold) and Parral in 18 months. Three analysts, all Buy at C$5.50; stock C$3.85 (15 Oct 2026).

The Gate

Building a 2,000 tpd underground mine on time and on a US$227M budget struck in January 2025 — in Jalisco, during a cartel succession war. The FS capex has not been formally revised for 2025–26 inflation or peso strength, but on 29 Sep 2026 the CEO guided the build at ~US$260–265M (+15–17%). Execution risk is concentrated in two places management itself names: bulk sub-level stoping in and around the historic Cinco Minas workings (ground conditions), and the SAG mill delivery (54-week lead, May 2027).

Sub-gates
  1. The permit's fine print — the June release says "all permits and approvals required from SEMARNAT"; it does not itemise land-use change, SEDENA explosives or CONAGUA water, and Mexico's MIA processing still runs 12–15 months with the 2023 mining-law regulation unpublished.
  2. Jalisco — CJNG's leader was killed at Tapalpa in February 2026, triggering statewide roadblocks and a succession fight; TD Cowen named Los Ricos as Jalisco-exposed; no incident at site, but Endeavour's Terronera — the nearest analogue — was shut for eleven days by an ejido blockade in August.
  3. Parral is the bridge and it is ageing — Q3 FY26 AISC US$40.78/oz (from US$23.72 in FY25) with four to five years of tailings left.
  4. The price — at C$1.89B the market has moved from 0.4× to something near 1× a spot NAV; the re-rate for permit + funding + construction start has largely happened.

This is the file's first genuinely de-risked developer — and the first where the question is 'what is left to earn?' rather than 'what could go wrong?'

Producer-style screens for the transition: EV ÷ years-1–5 AgEq (7.3 Moz × ~US$52 margin at spot) ≈ 2.8× annual pre-tax margin — cheap on cash flow if the mine is built to plan; P/NAV ~0.7–0.9× at spot (my range) — the highest in the developer set.
Valuation Anchor

~0.7–0.9× a spot NAV, ~3× the FS-deck NAV — priced as a mine under construction, not as a developer waiting for something. That is the correct price for what it is: permitted, funded, building, with a producer's cash flow already inside it. The remaining upside is (a) the gap to ~1.0× NAV as construction milestones land (powerline, portal, mill delivery, commissioning), (b) Los Ricos North being permitted and added to the plan around first pour, and (c) silver — years 1–5 of production at 7.3 Moz AgEq are 60% silver, so a US$85 tape adds ~US$150M of annual margin.

The bear case is not a lost project; it is a US$260–280M capex, a six-month slip, and a stock that trades sideways for eighteen months while the market waits for first pour.

Bucket: quality / jurisdiction premium — with the caveat that the premium is for execution position (permit, cash, contractors), not for Jalisco; this is the Osisko Metals archetype from the copper file, and the first developer in this file the market pays up for.

Insider activity (12 mo)
Quiet — grants, not trades. Option grants Dec 2025 (Langille, Hatfield, Nehme, Turner); Langille received 85k RSU/DSU shares (Dec 26); director Cooper exercised and sold ~140k in Aug 2026. No open-market buying and no meaningful selling by the CEO through a 2× move. Governance note: directors Turner and Cooper drew 21–27% withhold votes at the March 2026 AGM; Chair Turner's law firm (Fasken) is company counsel; Aguirre resigned Jun 2026.
Strategic & prominent
No 10%+ holder; no strategic miner; no named financier. Institutions ~30%: Global X (SIL) 3.7%, Franklin Templeton 3.3%, Van Eck (GDXJ) 3.1%, Konwave 2.8%, ASA 2.2%, Sprott Gold Equity Fund ~2%, Amplify (SILJ), Goehring & Rozencwajg. Eric Sprott: no disclosed position. Rick Rule interviews Langille at his symposium but holds nothing disclosed. Palisades, Crescat: none.
Institutions / retail
Institutions ~30%, insiders ~6%, retail ~64%. 433.5M shares; FD 475.1M (27.1M in-the-money warrants @ C$3.50 = ~US$67M if exercised). Halifax HQ; ~225 Mexican employees.

Read: A founder-CEO with a real, long-held stake who has neither bought nor sold through a doubling; no famous names, no strategic, an ETF-and-fund register. Nobody outside is signalling anything; the insider signal is simply that the man who has built three Mexican mines still owns 3.7% of the fourth. The weak spot is board governance (withhold votes, counsel as chair), not alignment.

Jurisdiction risk

National: Mexico's permitting freeze — survived, at a cost of two years. The 2023 mining-law reform stands (upheld by the Supreme Court, Jun 2025), Sheinbaum has confirmed no new concessions, the implementing regulation is still unpublished, and SEMARNAT's backlog (176 MIAs inherited in 2024) is being cleared at 12–15 months per file — GoGold's June 2026 approval is part of that clearance. It was underground-first by design, to sidestep the open-pit controversy.

Local: manageable but not benign. Hostotipaquillo is in Jalisco, CJNG's home state; the February 2026 killing of "El Mencho" at Tapalpa set off roadblocks across the state and a succession fight; no incident at Los Ricos is reported. Surface rights via Ejido Cinco Minas (2020 agreement, 12+12 years, escalating payments to US$100k/yr in production) and private landholders for the mill site; US$20M of local purchasing in 2025. The August 2026 eleven-day ejido blockade at Endeavour's Terronera, also in Jalisco, is the template for what local friction looks like here. Water via a CONAGUA concession "available at a cost"; power from CFE's La Yesca hydro over a 36 km line.

Jalisco is not Sinaloa — but it is the state where the cartel's leadership war is being fought this year.

Differentiator
  1. Every gate the other silver developers still face is behind it: permit received, capex funded from cash, no debt, no stream, no royalty, construction started, contractors on site.
  2. A producer inside a developer — Parral has funded the company for a decade and still generates ~US$25M+ a year, so the build carries no financing risk and the equity has already absorbed its dilution.
  3. Grade — 145 g/t Ag and 1.39 g/t Au in reserve, with a 3,034 g/t AgEq geotech hit below the stopes; AISC US$11–12/oz AgEq puts it in the lowest-cost decile.
  4. A team that has done this three times in Mexico — Langille built Ocampo and El Cubo at Gammon Gold and Parral in 18 months; the COO ran Ocampo's construction.
  5. A second permitted-in-waiting project, Los Ricos North, larger than the first.

Read it honestly: everything that makes it safe is why it trades at 3× the FS-deck NAV. The market has paid for the permit and the money; it has not yet paid for the mine.

Exploration upside

Near-mine, high impact on sequencing · moves the needle: medium. The Eagle zone (21 m @ 3,034 g/t AgEq, 250 m below the FS stopes) could pull very high grades into the early years; the FS resource is otherwise well defined. Los Ricos North's 110 Moz AgEq PEA is the real expansion — a permit application is planned around first pour, with a revised PEA/PFS that was promised for 2025 and has not appeared. Exploration is not the thesis; construction is.

The promised Los Ricos North study update is a year late — a small tell about bandwidth during the build.

Next Catalyst

Construction milestones: powerline (Nov 2026), portal / ramp / paste plant (Jan 2027), SAG mill delivery (May 2027), commissioning (Jan 2028), first pour Q2 2028; quarterly Parral production and FY results (Dec); Los Ricos North permit application (~Q1 2027) and study update; any capex re-statement; Jalisco security.

Open Questions
  • What is the real capex in 2026 dollars — US$227M, or the ~US$260M that circulates — and when does the company say so?
  • Which permits exactly are in hand: MIA, land-use change, explosives, water — and are any conditional?
  • How does the underground plan handle the old Cinco Minas workings, and what is the contingency if ground conditions differ?
  • Does Parral's AISC keep rising toward US$40+, and does it matter once construction cash is committed?
  • What is the security plan for a 150–500-person site in Hostotipaquillo through a cartel succession?
  • At ~0.8× spot NAV, what is left to earn before first pour — and is Los Ricos North the answer?

Boards today: Langille: 1 public board (GoGold). Turner: 2 (GoGold chair, Arcadium Lithium) plus full-time law practice.

Fit to this job
Closest fit in this batch: Langille and COO Nehme built and ran Ocampo and El Cubo in Mexico, and the same team built Parral and has operated it since 2014. Los Ricos South is an underground silver-gold mine in Jalisco — same country, same team, same contractors culture. New for them: an underground mine of this scale (first pour targeted June 2028) and scaling from a small tailings reprocessor to a mid-tier producer; Ocampo's ramp-up history is the cautionary precedent.
Skin & pay
3/5 — meaningful stake, mostly founder stock or grants; not selling. Langille controls ~16.0M shares directly/indirectly (incl. 10.9M via Grupo Pan American and 4.5M by spouse) — ~3.7% of ~430M shares, worth ~US$46M; D&O group 6.4% per Mar 2024 circular. Mix of founder/early shares and awards; no recent open-market buying found (not verified either way). CEO total comp US$1.48M FY2023 (salary US$134k, bonus US$497k, share/option awards US$564k, consulting fees ~US$280k via controlled company); Simply Wall St shows ~US$1.2M latest year. Reasonable at today's ~US$1.2B market cap, high relative to the C$384M cap it was paid at. Thesis

A 20-year-old Durango producer (Avino mine: ~2.5 Moz AgEq/yr from a 736 kt/yr mill) using record silver prices to fund the La Preciosa transformation without debt or equity: 100% ownership consolidated in 2025 (royalties and contingent payments bought out), inaugural consolidated reserve Apr 2026 (Avino mine + La Preciosa + Oxide Tailings) of 27 Mt @ 145 g/t AgEq for 127 Moz AgEq, M&I 301 Moz AgEq — of which La Preciosa alone is P&P 11 Mt / 72 Moz Ag + 128 koz Au and M&I 33.2 Mt / 158 Moz Ag + 287 koz Au.

Development ore is already being milled through both Avino circuits (100.7 koz AgEq in Q2, +59% q/q); long-hole sub-level-caving stopes on Level 3 are nearly ready, targeting 500 tpd in H2 2026.

Q2 2026: revenue US$26.8M, EBITDA US$12.6M, net income US$10.9M, operating cash flow US$13.3M on US$68.90 realised silver; cash US$144.2M, working capital US$140.8M, no debt; a 5% buyback running. Stated ambition: a Mexico-focused mid-tier primary silver producer. CEO David Wolfin. Four analyst Buys, consensus target ~US$10.8.

The Gate

Getting La Preciosa's economics onto paper — and then delivering them. There is a reserve and, since the 15 Oct 2026 production release, a decision — trade-off studies are complete and preparation for a stand-alone La Preciosa plant has begun — but still no economic study, no capex, no permits and no timeline to steady state (management's spoken plan, 29 Sep: PFS mid-2027, FS mid-2028, production ~2030). Until those are on paper, the mid-tier story has no NPV and no firm date.

Sub-gates
  1. Costs — Q2 AISC US$38.75/AgEq oz against 2026 guidance of US$25–27 (cash cost US$28.62 vs US$19–21), driven by silver recovery falling to 69% (from 85% a year earlier; partly oxidised ore from lower-grade Avino areas), near-waste La Preciosa development rock put through the mill at high metal prices, less copper (fewer AgEq ounces) and a strong peso — reported silver and gold feed grades actually rose 22% and 30% y/y; gold recovery 72%. Q3 (15 Oct): 582,836 AgEq oz, silver recovery still 70%, long-hole stoping not yet started; YTD 1.69 Moz against 2.4–2.7 Moz AgEq guidance, so Q4 would need a record 0.71–1.0 Moz (best quarter so far 672k, Q4 2025) — 2026 guidance at risk; the 4 Nov results (AISC and any revision) are the test.
  2. Mexico — the 2023 mining-law reform (shorter concessions, water permits, no new concessions) matters less for a brownfield with existing concessions, but a standalone La Preciosa plant would need new permits under the Sheinbaum regime.
  3. Silver beta — at ~54% silver revenue and realised prices that doubled y/y, the earnings base is a silver-price call first and an operating story second.

The Q2 print shows the transition cost: EBITDA +69% y/y on price while cost per ounce rose ~50% on poor recovery, near-waste development feed and less copper. That inversion has to resolve when long-hole grades arrive.

How to read it: picture every primary silver mine in the world lined up from cheapest to most expensive to run (all-in sustaining cost per ounce, weighted by output). The percentile is the share of world output that costs less; the middle line splits the cheaper half from the costlier half. Lower-half mines keep earning when the metal price falls. Dot = 2026, ring = 2025. Silver curve: estimated from 18 primary silver mines' 2026 guidance and H1 actuals (~116 Moz) on the Silver Institute's by-product basis — gold, zinc, lead and copper revenue subtracted; silver-equivalent figures converted (±US$3–5/oz). Approximate — it ranks the names, it is not decimal-precise.

Valuation Anchor

Valued on cash flow and silver, not on ounces. ~17× annualised Q2 EBITDA, ~10–12× at guided costs; ~US$2.9/oz company-wide M&I AgEq.

The re-rate case is arithmetic on volume, not multiple: La Preciosa at 500 tpd of 145 g/t adds ~0.7 Moz AgEq a year (~0.85 Moz contained) — and that is already what the 2026 guide of 2.4–2.7 Moz needs; doubling output needs the undecided standalone mill (~1,500–2,000 tpd), which has no study, capex or date (corrected 2 Oct); if it lands at guided costs and silver holds, EBITDA could double or triple, which is what the analyst targets (~US$10.8) are pricing.

The bear case is the same arithmetic in reverse: silver mean-reverts before the ramp, and you own a US$1B company earning US$50M.

Bucket call: producer / cash flow — the fifth bucket, added for this name; the four developer archetypes don't fit a company with revenue.

Shareholder structure
Management & board
~6.4% insiders in aggregate. CEO David Wolfin ~5.17M shares / 3.0% (~US$30M) — a founder-family holding built over three decades (director since 1995), part legacy, part exercised options. COO Carlos Rodriguez ~2.66M / 1.6%. Other directors small, mostly options/RSUs.
Insider activity (12 mo)
Selling, no cash buying. Wolfin sold ~527k shares Oct 2025–Jan 2026 (~C$4.5M, up to C$15.59). Rodriguez sold ~325k Feb–May 2026 (C$9.55–12.40); CFO Nathan Harte 50k @ C$10.83 (Apr); director Michael Clark ~82k; others smaller. The only purchase (Peter Latta, 50k @ C$12.63, Jan 2026) may be an exercise. Net: insiders monetised the 2025 run before the stock halved.
Strategic & prominent
None. No 10%+ holder, no strategic miner, no named financier. The largest holders are silver ETFs: SILJ (Amplify) ~5.2%, SIL (Global X) ~3.6%, Van Eck ~3%, Mackenzie ~3.5%. Sprott a token 0.26M.
Institutions / retail
Institutions ~25–32% (101 filers), insiders ~6.4%, retail ~62–69%. ~170M shares; NCIB for 8.4M (5%) approved Apr 2026 — 508k bought in Q2.

Read: The tell here is the direction, not the level: 6% is respectable, but every insider transaction in the last year was a sale, clustered at the top, and the CEO sold ~10% of his stake at C$15 before the stock went to C$8. The buyback is the company buying what its officers sold. The ETF-dominated register means the stock trades with the silver-miner basket regardless of La Preciosa.

Jurisdiction risk

National: the weakest in this file, but brownfield-mitigated. Mexico's 2023 mining-law reform (shorter concession terms, tighter water permits, no new concessions under Sheinbaum, stricter open-pit scrutiny) is the same regime that discounts Oroco in the copper file — but Avino is underground, operating for two decades on existing concessions, and La Preciosa's concessions are held. The exposure is a new standalone mill permit and water, if that route is chosen. Peso strength is a live cost headwind (management cites a 12–15% premium).

Local: low. Durango is an established mining state; La Preciosa was permitted and largely built by Coeur before Avino bought it; no organised opposition known; safety record improving (LTIFR 3.55 in 2025).

Mexico is why a debt-free producer trades at a discount to Canadian peers on EV/oz — and why the discount won't fully close.

Differentiator
  1. A reserve-backed path to doubling — though the step that doubles output (a standalone mill) has no study or capex yet. 127 Moz AgEq of consolidated P&P (La Preciosa's share: 11 Mt / 72 Moz Ag + 128 koz Au, ~83 Moz AgEq) on a company producing ~2.5 Moz AgEq/yr, with US$144M cash, no debt and positive free cash flow — the growth needs no financing, no partner, no stream.
  2. The mill already exists — La Preciosa ore is being processed today through the Avino circuits 15 km away, so the ramp is a mining-rate and grade question, not a construction project (unless the standalone option wins).
  3. 100% ownership, royalties bought out (2025) — every incremental ounce is unencumbered.
  4. Silver leverage with a producer's floor — 54% silver revenue, realised price doubled y/y, and the buyback signals management thinks the equity is cheap.

Read it honestly: the differentiator (an existing mill absorbing La Preciosa ore) is also the source of the Q2 cost blow-out — near-waste development tonnes and oxidised Avino ore pushed silver recovery down to 69% and cost per ounce up, even though reported feed grades rose. Same fact, two sides.

Exploration upside

Conversion done; step-outs starting · moves the needle: medium. The 2026 programme (15,000 m at each site) shifted from infill to exploration and step-outs mid-year (6,591 m at La Preciosa by end-Q2), targeting outside the current resource model. With 301 Moz AgEq of consolidated M&I already on the books (La Preciosa 158 Moz Ag), more ounces don't change the thesis — grade delivered to the mill does.

The exploration that matters is at the Avino mine itself: sustaining feed grade there while La Preciosa ramps.

What the rankings sayChance of a 3× in 3–5 years ~8% · chance it works ~20% · risk 3 of 5 · management B · cost curve: 83rd percentile, sell-trigger watch

What has to go right

The costs have to come back. Q2 AISC was US$38.75 an ounce against a US$25–27 guide, because the mill was fed near-waste development rock and oxidised ore; the fix is long-hole stoping at La Preciosa, which had not started on 15 Oct. The 4 Nov results are the first print after the bad quarter. Then the La Preciosa pre-feasibility study (mid-2027) has to put a capex, a cost and a date on the doubling that is so far only spoken.

Why the stock is priced where it is

At US$4.60 the market pays ~12.6× the cash flow of the bad quarter (EV ~US$637M on ~US$50M annualised EBITDA) but only ~9× what the mine earns at guided costs and today's silver (~US$70M). The stock fell 40% in two months while silver fell 12%: a cost problem the company has not yet explained, insiders who sold at the top, and a register of silver ETFs that trade it as a basket. No raise coming, no study yet to create a NAV. The rankings give ~8% odds of a 3×; the win case is costs back on guide plus a funded mill, a 1.7–2.5×.

What the plan does about it

Buys nothing before the results. Standing limits at US$4.00 (~7.6× guided-cost cash flow, cash a fifth of the price) and US$3.40 (~6×, La Preciosa free), filled only on silver-driven falls and cancelled if the 4 Nov print is red; a red print lowers both levels 15%. 40% is kept for the study, bought at any price up to US$7.00 if it reads green. The stop is the card's own sell trigger: AISC above US$34 for a second quarter means the cost-curve migration is the company, not the quarter.

What to watchPrice US$4.00 (€3.58) and US$3.40 (€3.04)Q3 financials, 4 Nov 2026Long-hole stoping start dateLa Preciosa PFS, mid-2027Silver below US$45Any release: "guidance", "equity", "permit"

Sizing: every amount is a share of the position you decide to hold in this company, whatever that is (100% = the full position). At €4 an order the fee is small; keep each tranche at €200 or more (fee ≤ 2%), and if a tranche would come out smaller, merge it with the next one. Not advice; my read written down in advance so that on the day I compare numbers against thresholds I set beforehand, not against the price move.

Step 1first tranche: 30% at US$4.00 (€3.58 / C$5.61) or below — a silver-driven fall only, not a results-driven one

Nothing at today's ~12.6× annualised Q2 EBITDA (EV ~US$637M on US$50M), because the quarter it is built on is the bad one and the next print is nine days away. Place a standing limit at US$4.00 = €3.58, 13% below the 26 Oct close and just under the US$4.05 twelve-month low: a US$679M cap, an EV of ~US$535M, cash 21% of the price, and ~7.6× the EBITDA this mine earns at its guided costs and today's silver (2.5 Moz × (US$54 − US$26) ≈ US$70M). A stock that fell 40% in two months with silver −12% is capable of the last 13% on the metal alone.

  1. Hit on silver, or on a sector sell-off with no company news → fill it.
  2. Hit on the 4 Nov results (a red Step 2) → cancel the order and use the lowered levels; a cheaper price on confirmed higher costs is not the discount the plan wants.
  3. Never hit? The plan buys nothing before the study, which is the right result at 12–13× a quarter whose costs the company has not yet explained.
Step 2Q3 financials (4 Nov 2026): the first cost print after the US$38.75 quarter — read five numbers before keeping the levels
WhatGreenRed
AISC per AgEq oz≤ US$31 — the Q2 figure was mostly fewer ounces sold, and it is unwinding≥ US$34 — the cost base, not the shipment timing, is the problem
Ounces sold vs producedsold ≥ 90% of the 582,836 AgEq oz produced; the Q2 backlog (produced 534,945, sold 387,142) clearedsold under 80% of produced for a second quarter — concentrate is not moving, or payability is
Guidanceproduction guide (2.4–2.7 Moz) kept; the cost guide revised with a reason and a dateproduction guide cut, or the cost guide dropped without a new one
Long-hole stoping at La Preciosastarted, or dated inside Q4 2026 — real ore replacing development rock is the fixno date, or pushed into 2027
Cash≥ US$140M after the US$8.75M royalty payment and the buyback< US$130M with no acquisition to show for it

Four or five green → the levels stand. Two or more red → lower every level by 15% (Step 1 to US$3.40 / €3.04, Step 3 to US$2.90 / €2.59) and cancel any open order: the card's sell-trigger — a producer migrating from the lower half of the cost curve to the upper half in a year — would then be confirmed rather than suspected. Red on AISC and on stoping → see Step 5.

Step 3second tranche: 30% at US$3.40 (€3.04 / C$4.77) or below — pay 6× guided-cost cash flow, get the La Preciosa plan free

At US$3.40 the cap is ~US$577M and the EV ~US$433M: ~6× the EBITDA at guided costs and today's silver, cash a quarter of the share price. The entire US$1B of La Preciosa ambition (standalone mill, ~6.5 Moz AgEq a year by ~2030) would be in for nothing. Standing limit at €3.04. It takes −26% from the 26 Oct close, which on this stock is one more silver leg down, or a red 4 Nov.

  1. Hit with Step 2 green → fill it and bring 10% of Step 4 forward; this is the price the plan hopes for.
  2. Hit with Step 2 red → the lowered level applies (US$2.90); do not fill at US$3.40.
  3. Silver below US$45 at the time → fill half; at that price the guided-cost margin is US$19/oz and 6× is no longer cheap. Hold the rest.
Step 4third tranche: 40% — the La Preciosa pre-feasibility study (management: mid-2027): read five numbers before buying at any price up to US$7.00 (€6.26 / C$9.82)
WhatGreenRed
Scalea standalone 2,500–3,000 tpd plant, consolidated output ≥ 5.5 Moz AgEq a yearunder 2,000 tpd, or La Preciosa still fed through the Avino mill
Capex≤ US$200M initial, inside management's US$100–200M range, funded "from cash and cash flow" — no equity, no stream> US$250M, or an equity or stream component
Costslife-of-mine AISC ≤ US$22/AgEq oz — the lower half of the curve, where this company sat in 2025> US$26/oz — the expansion would only reproduce today's cost problem at twice the size
Economicsafter-tax NPV5% ≥ US$600M at ≤ US$35 silver; IRR ≥ 30%NPV only quoted at spot, or IRR under 20% at ≤ US$35
Dates and permitsFS mid-2028 and production ≤ 2030 held; the permits for a standalone plant named with a filing dateproduction past 2031, or permits "to be determined" under the Sheinbaum regime
  1. Four or five green → buy 40% within two weeks at the market, up to US$7.00 (a US$1.19B cap). A costed, funded doubling at lower-half costs is the asset the ~US$10.8 analyst targets are pricing; the ladder no longer applies below the cap.
  2. Three green → 20% up to US$7.00, 20% only at or below the Step 3 level.
  3. Two or more red → nothing. If costs and capex are both red, see Step 6: the transformation would then be a bigger version of the problem.
Step 5overrides — events that change the plan whatever step it is at
  1. Buy at the ladder regardless of the calendar: a silver drawdown of 25%+ with Q3/Q4 AISC on or under US$31 and the production guide intact — the metal, not the mine; fill every open level.
  2. Stop adding and cancel the orders: AISC above US$34 for a second consecutive quarter (Q4 results, ~March 2027) — the cost-curve migration is then the company, not the quarter; an equity raise or stream for a company with US$144M of cash; a Mexican permit refusal or a water-concession problem for the standalone plant; the La Preciosa PFS slipping past end-2027; the standalone plan quietly dropped for "optimising the existing mill".
  3. Sell half on a takeover bid: a debt-free Durango silver producer with 300 Moz of M&I is a plausible target for a mid-tier; take the premium on half, keep half for a second bidder.
  4. Sell everything: 2026 production guidance missed and 2027 guidance set below 2.4 Moz — two years of shrinking at a company whose case is doubling.
Step 6once in: sell-or-hold triggers
  1. Sell if the PFS lands red on costs and capex: the thesis is a bigger mine at lower-half costs; a bigger mine at today's costs is a silver trade with construction risk.
  2. Sell half if the stock doubles from the average entry before the PFS — on a producer that is silver, and silver gives it back.
  3. Otherwise hold through the FS (mid-2028) toward first production from the standalone plant (~2030). The rankings' win case — costs back on guide and the mill funded and built — is a ~1.7–2.5× from here, not a multibagger; the 3× needs silver near US$90 or the mill built early.
PracticalWhere to buy, currency, and the most likely outcome

Main liquidity is the NYSE American (ASM) in USD, the simplest line for a USD account and the one the levels are set on; the TSX (ASM) in CAD is the home listing. German venues quote it in EUR with modest spreads for a US$780M name; a EUR limit set from the New York close converted at the day's ECB rate will be close to the venue's quote. The EUR equivalents move with the exchange rate and should be recomputed on the day. Most likely outcome (my read, not a forecast): 4 Nov prints an AISC around US$29–32 with the cost guide revised and the production guide kept — "three or four green" — and the stock drifts with silver into year-end; Step 1 fills in Q4 on a silver leg down, Step 3 does not; the PFS lands mid-2027 at ~2,500 tpd with capex near the top of the range, "three green", 20% more. Average entry around US$3.90 (€3.49) with 50–70% of the planned position bought: a debt-free producer at ~7× guided-cost cash flow with a costed doubling ahead of it — a 1.5–2× if silver holds and the mill is funded, and a US$780M company earning US$50M if silver mean-reverts first, which is the bear case the card already carries.

Next Catalyst

Q3 2026 financials (4 Nov) — whether AISC turns back toward $25–27 and whether 2026 guidance (2.4–2.7 Moz AgEq) is revised: after Q3 production (15 Oct: 582,836 AgEq oz, YTD 1.69 Moz) Q4 would need a record 0.71–1.0 Moz; long-hole stoping start (not started at 15 Oct); the stand-alone La Preciosa plant — decision made (15 Oct release), economic study, capex and permits still to come; buyback execution; silver price.

Open Questions
  • What do long-hole stopes actually grade at the mill versus the La Preciosa reserve grade (~206 g/t Ag; 145 g/t AgEq is the consolidated figure), and when does AISC re-converge with guidance?
  • Build, now decided (15 Oct): what capex, what permits, and does the US$144M cover it without a raise?
  • Does 2026 guidance (2.4–2.7 Moz AgEq) survive an H1 of ~1.1 Moz?
  • What is the sensitivity of EBITDA to silver at US$50 versus US$70 — i.e. how much of Q2 was price?
  • Does the oxide-tailings project (PFS 2024) ever get a decision, or is it quietly shelved?
  • Why did the stock halve from US$11.99 while silver stayed high — is that a cost story, a silver-momentum unwind, or both?
Context & updates
5 Oct 2026 update

Management candour (review of what was said and when). Flagged early: the Feb 2026 guidance warned costs would be 'higher than recent years', and the Q1 release tied a 16% cash-cost rise to La Preciosa development ore. Played down: Q2 AISC came in ~45–50% above the US$25–27 guide, yet guidance was kept and defended on cost per tonne (where it looks fine) rather than per ounce; the Q2 results release itself gave no explanation for the cost jump and nothing on guidance; the production release led with higher feed grades while silver recovery fell from 85% to 69%. Timelines moved: '500 t/day in H2 2026' became 'nearly complete', then 'we need a bit more time', then a different, bigger and later plan (standalone 2,500–3,000 t/day mill, ~2030) announced on stage on 29 Sep, not in a release. Long-time insiders (~6%) are net sellers. Verdict: not dishonest, but promotional — a yellow flag on the promotional-management sell trigger. Test: do the Q3 reports (Oct/Nov) explain the numbers in the release and revise guidance honestly if H2 falls short, and does the mill plan get a formal announcement?

3 Oct 2026 refresh

Spoken at a 29 Sep conference, not yet in a release: La Preciosa is going to a standalone 2,500–3,000 tpd mill — PFS mid-2027, FS mid-2028, ~16-month build, production ~2030, capex US$100–200M (management estimate), potential 7–8 Moz AgEq a year from La Preciosa. The near-term long-hole start (the old '500 tpd in H2 2026') has slipped to 'Q4, any day now'. Q3 production is due in October.

Q2 2026 (Aug 12)

Revenue US$26.8M (+23%), EBITDA US$12.6M (+69%), net income US$10.9M, OCF US$13.3M; realised silver US$68.90 (+104% y/y); provisional-pricing hit ~US$5M. Cash cost US$28.62 and AISC US$38.75 per AgEq oz vs US$15.11 / US$20.93 a year earlier. Cash US$144.2M, working capital US$140.8M.

Q2 2026 production (Jul 22)

534,945 AgEq oz (−17% y/y): 267 koz Ag, 2,178 oz Au, 730 klb Cu on 184 kt milled. La Preciosa 100,658 AgEq oz (+59% q/q); Circuit 2 now on La Preciosa ore; Level 3 stope preparation nearly complete. 508k shares bought back.

2026 outlook (Jan)

2.4–2.7 Moz AgEq; AISC US$25–27; capex US$20–26M; La Preciosa 500 tpd in H2 via long-hole sub-level caving. Production weighted to H2.

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 4/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 2/5

Met production guidance three years running and runs no debt; the Q2 2026 cost miss sat in a table rather than the headline and insiders are net sellers. Yellow flag, not a pattern yet.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
David Wolfin (President & CEO, director, since CEO since June 2010 (with the company since 1990s; son of founder Louis Wolfin)): Age 58. Also President & CEO of Silver Wolf Exploration. · Nathan Harte (CFO, since ~2018): Handles cost explanations on calls; net seller of stock in last 12 months. · Carlos Rodriguez (COO, since ~2012): Runs the Durango operations; net seller of stock Feb–May 2026.
Track record
  • Restarted the Avino mine (Durango) in 2012 and has operated it since; family-controlled management for 30+ yearssource
  • Sold Bralorne (BC gold) to Talisker Resources in 2019 — small exit, non-coresource
  • Bought La Preciosa from Coeur in 2022 and bought out the remaining royalties/contingent payments in 2025; permits Jan 2025, first blast Apr 2025, development ore in the mill from Q4-2025source
  • 2025 production 2.6Moz AgEq inside 2.5-2.8Moz guidance; debt-free; cash ~US$144M mid-2026 (same source; https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/19/avino-silver-gold-mines-asm-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/)
  • Q2 2026 AISC US$38.75/oz AgEq (cash cost US$28.62) vs 2026 guidance US$25-27 (cash cost US$19-21)source
  • Wins came in the 2024-26 silver bull cycle; the company diluted through ATMs in the 2015-22 period (unverified detail).

Boards today: Wolfin: Avino (CEO/director) and Silver Wolf Exploration (CEO/director) — 2 public executive roles.

Fit to this job
Exactly the same job: small-scale underground/open-pit silver-gold-copper mining and flotation milling in Durango, which they have done for 13 years. La Preciosa is a second mine 20 km away feeding the same mill — new in scale, not in kind. They have not built a standalone new plant.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake from grants or cheap founder paper; little buying. Wolfin owns ~3.0% (long-held family position; recent activity is selling, not buying). 2025 total pay ~US$1.43M (20% salary, 80% bonus/equity), +20% y/y, at a ~US$1B company. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/materials/nysemkt-asm/avino-silver-gold-mines/management (circular not fetched).

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Cost blow-out vs guidance (+45% AISC) was left out of the release headline and CEO quote and only explained on the call under questioning.
  • CEO, CFO and COO were all net sellers in the past 12 months (CEO ~US$3.2M, incl. ~210k shares at ~US$8.40 on 23 Jan 2026).
  • CEO also runs a second listed company (Silver Wolf) with properties adjacent to Avino's.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash rose from US$2.7M in December 2023 to US$144.8M in June 2026, mostly from US$98.9M of ATM equity; no bank debt, only US$6–9M of equipment leases.
  2. Capex was US$26.3M in FY25, including a US$13.25M royalty buyback, with a further US$8.75M royalty payment due in Q3 2026; G&A is about 8–9% of revenue.
  3. Shares outstanding rose from 128.7M in December 2023 to 169.9M in June 2026, up 32%; a 5% buyback started in Q2 2026 with US$3.0M repurchased.
  4. Revenue grew from US$43.9M in FY23 to US$92.2M in FY25 and US$66.2M in H1 2026 alone; mine operating margin rose from 18% to 55% as silver doubled.
  5. AISC jumped from US$23.75/oz in FY25 to US$38.75/oz in Q2 26 on fewer payable ounces and a stronger peso; free cash flow was US$20.4M in H1 26.

Newfoundland's high-grade Queensway discovery, now a funded Phase 1 build feeding its own Pine Cove mill, with Hammerdown already in commercial production since Aug 2026.

Gate Delivering Phase 1 ore at the modelled grade, on the Q4 2027 date, through an EPR that was not in the plan. The revised PEA (22 Oct 2026, effective 19 Oct) resets the plan: Phase 1 mills 700 tpd of Keats and Iceberg open-pit material at the company's own Pine Cove plant (gravity-CIL) from Q4 2027 to 2030 at a 13.41 g/t head grade, 97% of it Measured and Indicated, for C$149.8M of initial capital (C$154.8M in 2025). The higher grade means more selective mining in a nuggety system, so grade control is the test. The NL Minister required an Environmental Preview Report (3 Jul 2026; guidelines 2 Sep 2026; submission targeted Q4 2026, then a 35-day public review and a 45-day decision); the surface and mining lease is targeted for mid-2027, contractor mobilisation Q1 2027, mining Q3 2027. Phase 2 (a new 4,900 tpd Queensway mill from 2031, C$646M in 2028–29) is unfunded and is where the share count moves next. Sub-gates: Hammerdown's ~US$2,500/oz AISC leaving thin cash flow; EdgePoint's first lien and a going-concern note in the Q2 statements.

Funded to the next catalyst The company says Phase 1 is fully funded: C$167M cash + C$35M undrawn vs C$155M PEA initial capex (2025 estimate) plus the Pine Cove conversion (cost not disclosed) plus C$44M/yr exploration and overhead. That is enough for Phase 1 if the updated capex stays near the PEA and Hammerdown covers its own costs; Phase 2 (C$442M growth capital in the PEA) is not funded and will need debt, cash flow or equity around 2028.
Thesis

New Found Gold is no longer a drill story: it bought Maritime Resources (Nov 2025) for the permitted Pine Cove mill and the Hammerdown mine, raised C$115M equity plus a C$105M EdgePoint facility (Apr 2026), declared commercial production at Hammerdown on schedule (19 Aug 2026) and targets first Queensway Phase 1 ore to Pine Cove in Q4 2027. The PEA (Jul 2025, US$2,500 gold) gives Queensway an after-tax NPV5 of C$743M and 56% IRR on C$155M initial capex, rising to C$1.45B at US$3,300; at today's ~US$4,180 the NAV is a multiple of the ~C$855M market cap, but the plan rests on Inferred-heavy resources, a 9.64 g/t selective Phase 1 head grade and a Phase 2 plant that still needs C$440M. The owner's question is whether a US$600M company can still triple: it needs Phase 1 to produce at the modelled grade and a Phase 2 decision inside the window.

The Gate

Delivering Phase 1 ore at the modelled grade, on the Q4 2027 date, through an EPR that was not in the plan The July 2025 PEA assumed 1.15 Mt at 9.64 g/t Au trucked to a toll mill and first gold in Q3 2027. Since then the toll mill became the company's own Pine Cove (conversion to 1,400 tpd gravity-CIL due Q4 2027), the NL Minister required an Environmental Preview Report (3 Jul 2026; guidelines issued 2 Sep 2026; 35-day public review plus a 45-day decision after submission), and first material slipped to Q4 2027 with commercial production in H2 2028. The updated Technical Report and MRE, promised for Q1 2026, then Q2, then H2 2026, is the document that will reset capex and grade; until it lands, the C$155M capex and the 9.64 g/t are 2025 numbers. Sub-gates: nuggety high-grade continuity under selective mining and ore sorting; Hammerdown's US$2,500/oz AISC leaving thin cash flow; EdgePoint's first lien and a going-concern note in the Q2 statements.

Valuation Anchor

~C$855M for 2.0 Moz of Queensway resource (~US$300/oz) plus a producing 20–25 koz/yr mine and a permitted mill. On the company's own PEA decks (Queensway US$2,500, Hammerdown US$3,475 long-term) the combined after-tax NPV5 is ~C$940M plus ~C$97M net cash, so the market pays ~0.8× study-deck NAV; at spot gold (~US$4,180) the extrapolated NAV is ~C$2.5B and the stock trades ~0.35× — the discount prices the Inferred-heavy plan, the EPR and the unbuilt Phase 2. Peers: funded Canadian developers near construction tend to trade 0.5–0.8× NAV; small producers at ~1×.

Shareholder structure

Eric Sprott ~19% (46.4M direct + 25.7M via Sprott Mining; a TSXV 'control person' since Aug 2025; bought 6.75M sh in the Apr 2026 deal). Palisades Goldcorp (Collin Kettell's vehicle) ~6.9% — a seller of ~3.1M sh in Oct 2025. ASA Gold 4.2%, Merk 4.2%, Dundee 3.2% (sold 24.5M sh Dec 2025), Sprott Inc. 2.7%, VanEck 2.1%, EdgePoint 2.1% plus the C$105M loan. Institutions ~21%, retail ~50%. Officers' own stakes are small: Boyle bought 100k sh at ~C$1.63 (Jun 2025) and 67,560 in the Apr 2026 deal; Assabgui 33,780 (Apr 2026); director Williams 100k sh on market Mar–May 2026 at C$2.44–2.69; Huet 18k at ~C$1.97 (Apr 2026). No officer selling found.

Read: Sprott is the anchor and the swing vote; management conviction is real but small in dollars; the founder's vehicle has been selling.

Jurisdiction risk

National: low — Canada, with Hammerdown operating and Pine Cove permitted. Local: medium — the NL Minister required an Environmental Preview Report for Queensway Phase 1 (3 Jul 2026) rather than releasing it from assessment, adding a 35-day public review and 45-day decision after submission; hydro transmission lines crossing the project must be rerouted; Good Neighbour Agreements are 'being advanced'; >88% of the Queensway workforce is local. Former Premier Andrew Furey joined the board in Sep 2025.

A top-tier jurisdiction where the permit clock, not politics, is the risk.

Differentiator

The only Newfoundland junior that owns both a district-scale high-grade discovery and the mill to process it. Buying Maritime gave it a permitted 700 tpd mill 180 km from Queensway, a producing mine, and an operating team, so Phase 1 does not depend on a third party. Grade: Phase 1 is modelled at 9.64 g/t, and 2026 channel sampling at Lotto (15.88 m @ 23.66 g/t) keeps returning the kind of numbers that built the 2020–21 story.

Infrastructure and grade are the edge; the resource category and the share count are the weakness.

Exploration upside

District-scale, >110 km strike, open below 1,000 m · moves the needle: medium The 2026 programme puts 45% of 90,000 m into discovery (Dropkick, Greenwood 4.7 × 2.0 km footprint, Gazeebow South, Pauls Pond) and 55% into conversion and grade control. New ounces matter more for Phase 2 and 3 than for the share price in the next two years, when the market will watch the build and the EPR.

Next Catalyst

Updated Queensway Technical Report with a new MRE and Phase 1–3 costs in H2 2026 (already slipped twice), then EPR submission and EA release; Q3 financials on 11 Nov 2026 give the first clean look at Hammerdown's cash cost.

Open Questions
  • Does the H2 2026 Technical Report hold the C$155M Phase 1 capex and the 9.64 g/t head grade once Pine Cove conversion costs and 2026 prices are in?
  • How long does the EPR add — can early works and construction permits still support first ore in Q4 2027?
  • Does Hammerdown make money at US$2,500 AISC with a 12:1 strip, or does it consume cash meant for Queensway?
  • How will the C$442M Phase 2 plant be funded, and at what share count?

Fit to this job
Stage: construction of a small high-grade open-pit feeding an existing mill, with a 20 koz/yr mine already running — fits Huet (Klondex) and Assabgui (Vale, Hudbay mill restart) well; Boyle's Reunion record is a study-and-sale, not a build. Deposit: nuggety orogenic gold under selective mining — Klondex is the right analogue. Region: Newfoundland — Assabgui and the ex-Maritime operations team are on the ground; Furey brings the province. New for them: running two sites 180 km apart on one balance sheet while a 90,000 m programme continues.

Officers' stakes are small in % terms (individual insiders 12.2% per simplywall.st, but ~46M of the 47M shares are Sprott's). Pay: Boyle's 2025 package not found (former CEO Kettell was C$518k in 2024 on a C$500M+ cap). Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • The updated Technical Report slipped from Q1 2026 to 22 Oct 2026 without ever being called a slip; the delivery release does not mention the earlier dates.
  • Going-concern 'material uncertainties' note in the Q2 2026 statements despite C$194M cash, because of negative operating cash flow during ramp-up and reliance on financing.
  • Chairman holds a concurrent CEO job (Americas Gold and Silver).
  • Founder vehicle Palisades (6.9%) sold ~3.1M shares in Oct 2025; Dundee exited 24.5M shares in Dec 2025 — two long-time holders leaving.
  • Hammerdown AISC guided at ~US$2,500/oz with a 12:1 strip: profitable only at today's gold.
  • Eric Sprott is a TSXV control person (~19%) and a lead order in every raise — the register depends on one man.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash went from C$22.3M at Dec 2024 to C$193.8M at 30 Jun 2026 and C$167M at 30 Sep 2026 (15 Oct 2026 production release), after a C$115.1M bought deal (Apr 2026, 38.9M sh @ C$2.96) and the C$70M EdgePoint Tranche 1 (May 2026, 8.75%, matures May 2029). Q3 2026 burn was ~C$27M; at C$25-30M a quarter the cash covers 5-6 quarters, plus the optional C$35M Tranche 2 until 15 May 2027 — but Queensway Phase 1 capex (first ore Q4 2027) is not yet funded from this and is the next raise/draw driver.
  2. Exploration remains the main use of cash: C$27.4M expensed in H1 2026 (Queensway 94%, 90,000 m / C$44M 2026 programme), C$41.4M in FY25, C$52.6M in FY24, C$94.0M in FY23. Hammerdown capex kicked in in 2026: PP&E purchases C$20.0M in H1 2026 (crusher/sorter, Gravity-CIL conversion) vs C$1.8M in all of FY25.
  3. Overhead is rising with producer status: G&A C$7.7M in H1 2026 (Q1 C$5.1M was the high point) vs C$5.5M in H1 2025 and C$6.9M for all of FY24; SBC C$3.5M in H1 2026 and C$6.3M in FY25 (replacement awards for Maritime). Overhead ran ~10-15% of cash spend in 2024-25 and roughly a fifth in H1 2026 once the C$4.8M Maritime transaction costs (Q4 2025) are counted.
  4. Share count grew from 186.9M (Dec 2023) to 200.5M (Dec 2024), 342.3M (Dec 2025, of which 94.3M for Maritime and 2.8M for Exploits claims) and 384.4M at 30 Jun 2026 (385.2M at 11 Aug 2026; 408.5M fully diluted). Cash equity raised: C$75.6M FY23, C$27.5M FY24, C$82.5M FY25, C$112.5M H1 2026 net.
  5. Hammerdown/Pine Cove: revenue C$5.8M (Q4 2025 stub), C$9.9M Q1 2026, C$15.7M Q2 2026 with thin mine-operating income (C$1.4M and C$1.9M) during ramp-up; Q3 2026 sold 6,035 oz at US$4,310/oz (production 4,863 oz, strip 12.4). Unusual items: going-concern paragraph in every audit (incl. Q2 2026 note), C$124.5M goodwill and C$83.2M deferred tax liability from the Maritime purchase (PPA provisional until 13 Nov 2026), flow-through premium recoveries flattering reported losses (C$7.6M FY25, C$5.6M H1 2026; C$10.8M qualifying CEE still to spend by 31 Dec 2026), and C$5.1M deferred revenue (prepaid gold sales) at 30 Jun 2026.

A 6.7 Moz brownfield open pit in Québec at ~0.25× NAV — because the NAV needs US$3,600 gold, the capex is US$1.43B, the permits are Q1 2027 and only US$850M of a US$1.1B debt package is committed (28 Sep)

Gate Turning the US$850M debt commitment (28 Sep) into a signed US$1.1B facility with EDC's US$250M, and US$3,600 gold into a lender's base case — before the permits, the Cree agreement and the equity gap catch up. The Sep 2026 study tripled the headline NPV entirely through the price deck: at US$2,000 gold the same mine plan is worth US$384M (IRR 7.4%); capex rose 33%, reserve grade fell 0.49 → 0.44 g/t, gold recovery fell 92.7% → 86.7%, AISC rose US$1,109 → US$1,340. Lenders will not underwrite at US$3,600; the debt sizing will be done at a deck where this is a 12–17% IRR project, which is why the mandate was upsized twice before the 28 Sep commitment came in at US$850M, below the US$1.2B mandate. Sub-gates: (1) the stack — the target structure is 55–65% senior debt, 25–35% stream/sub-debt (US$360–500M, none announced) and ~10% equity (US$140M+, against ~C$140M of cash and C$70M/yr burn); (2) permits — federal IAAC and provincial COMEX both in the information-request phase, decisions slipped from "year-end 2026" to Q1 2027; (3) the Cree IBA — a 2018 pre-development agreement exists; the impacts-and-benefits agreement that a Québec mine cannot open without is still unsigned; (4) slippage record — financial close "before end 2025" → Q4 2026; construction decision 2026 → construction start 2027; and the CFO hired in March ran Victoria Gold's finances through the Eagle build.

Partly funded to the next catalyst Sep 28 update: a credit-approved US$850M senior-debt commitment letter (SocGen / KfW IPEX / EDC) — the first binding-grade piece of the stack. It is US$350M short of the US$1.2B mandate, which is the lenders' answer on the gold deck: against US$1,428M of capex, ~US$580M of stream, sub-debt and equity is still to be found — ~US$330M if EDC's US$250M closes (my arithmetic), on a ~US$0.9B company. Funded to the permits; expect the stream and an equity raise to follow definitive documentation, before construction in 2027.
Thesis

Troilus is the former Inmet mine (1996–2010) north of Chibougamau: a 50 MW substation, 60 km of high-voltage line, a permitted tailings facility and an all-weather road already exist. The company (ex-Troilus Gold, renamed Dec 2025) has grown the deposit to P&P 478 Mt @ 0.44 g/t Au = 6.69 Moz Au + 568 Mlb Cu and M&I 10.2 Moz Au. The updated technical report (Sep 8, 2026), on 95,000 hours of basic engineering by BBA: 50,000 tpd open pit, 26-year life, ~251 koz Au + 20 Mlb Cu per year, initial capex US$1,428M (Class 3, +15/−10%), after-tax NPV5% US$3.2B and IRR 22% at US$3,600 Au; AISC US$1,340/oz; construction 2027, first ore Sep 2029, commercial production Mar 2030. Financing is a wall of paper: ECA letters of intent totalling US$1.3B (Euler Hermes US$500M, Finnvera US$300M + US$132M for Metso equipment, EKN US$200M, EDC US$300M), a US$1.2B senior-debt mandate to Société Générale / KfW IPEX / EDC (upsized twice, now a credit-approved US$850M commitment from KfW IPEX and Société Générale, 28 Sep, toward a US$1.1B package with EDC's US$250M pending), offtake MoUs with Aurubis and Boliden, Québec's Filon fast-track selection and a 70 MW Hydro-Québec block granted Jun 2026 — and, until 28 Sep, nothing binding. ESIA filed Jun 2025 to Québec (COMEX) and Canada (IAAC); decisions now guided Q1 2027; the Cree Nation of Mistissini impacts-and-benefits agreement is not yet signed.

Cash ~C$140M (Apr 30), no debt, burn ~C$70M/yr; 554.8M shares after a C$172.5M bought deal at C$1.29 (Nov 2025). CEO Justin Reid (founder; ex-Sulliden). Eight analysts, consensus target ~C$3.80–4.30; stock C$1.61 (14 Oct 2026); added to GDXJ Sep 18.

The Gate

Turning the US$850M debt commitment (28 Sep) into a signed US$1.1B facility with EDC's US$250M, and US$3,600 gold into a lender's base case — before the permits, the Cree agreement and the equity gap catch up. The Sep 2026 study tripled the headline NPV entirely through the price deck: at US$2,000 gold the same mine plan is worth US$384M (IRR 7.4%); capex rose 33%, reserve grade fell 0.49 → 0.44 g/t, gold recovery fell 92.7% → 86.7%, AISC rose US$1,109 → US$1,340. Lenders will not underwrite at US$3,600; the debt sizing will be done at a deck where this is a 12–17% IRR project, which is why the mandate was upsized twice before the 28 Sep commitment came in at US$850M, below the US$1.2B mandate.

Sub-gates
  1. The stack — the target structure is 55–65% senior debt, 25–35% stream/sub-debt (US$360–500M, none announced) and ~10% equity (US$140M+, against ~C$140M of cash and C$70M/yr burn).
  2. Permits — federal IAAC and provincial COMEX both in the information-request phase, decisions slipped from "year-end 2026" to Q1 2027.
  3. The Cree IBA — a 2018 pre-development agreement exists; the impacts-and-benefits agreement that a Québec mine cannot open without is still unsigned.
  4. Slippage record — financial close "before end 2025" → Q4 2026; construction decision 2026 → construction start 2027; and the CFO hired in March ran Victoria Gold's finances through the Eagle build.

The 70 MW power block is real and rare. Everything else that matters is a letter, a mandate or a memorandum.
