The honest read: this is a gold-price call with a 26-year mine attached, and the study says so in its own sensitivity table. Market cap ÷ capex ~0.6× — the thinnest coverage of any funded-in-principle developer here; hence the ~10% equity slice in the target structure.
Valuation Anchor

~0.25× NAV at the US$3,600 deck; ~0.35× at US$3,000; ~2× NAV at US$2,000 — the widest P/NAV range in the file, because the NAV itself swings 10× across plausible gold prices. The re-rate path is the Solaris path: debt close (Q4 2026 guided) → permits (Q1 2027) → IBA → stream and equity → construction 2027 → producer multiple 2030. Developers that complete that sequence in Québec have re-rated from ~0.3× toward 0.7–0.8× NAV — 2.5–3× on progress alone at today's gold, and 4–5× if the market adopts US$4,500+.

The bear case is the sensitivity table: at US$3,000 gold this is a 17% IRR, US$1.4B project that lenders size at half the mandate, and the equity slice becomes US$300–400M on a US$0.8B company.

Bucket: scale & financing — the Solaris archetype: tier-one jurisdiction, huge reserve, technically done, one very large cheque away, and the cheque's size depends on the metal.

Mixed and small. Reid bought 32,000 @ C$1.87 (Feb 9, 2026); the same week Denis Rivard sold 95,000 @ C$1.82, Jacqueline Leroux 20,000 @ C$2.07, Julien Roufast 7,500. Net: officers trimmed into the post-financing rally; the CEO added modestly. Nothing since the September study.
Strategic & prominent
No confirmed 10%+ holder. Franklin Templeton ~7.4% (40.9M), Van Eck ~5.0% (27.7M — bought 16.5M at C$0.35 in a Feb 2025 private placement, since GDXJ inclusion adds passive weight), CDPQ ~1.9%, Konwave ~2.1%, Tidal ~2.6%. One aggregator shows Equinox Partners 12.9% (68M) — unverified, no early-warning filing found. Investissement Québec (C$11.5M at C$1.10, 2021) and the Fonds FTQ are on the register (current % undisclosed) — provincial capital, which matters for Filon and power. No Eric Sprott, Ruffer or strategic miner.
Institutions / retail
Company: institutions ~64% (~12% Québec-based), retail ~28%, insiders ~8%. Filings-based: institutions ~27%, insiders ~3.4%, public ~69%. 554.8M shares; FD 600.4M; +45% share count in 19 months.

Read: A Québec-institutional register — Franklin, Van Eck, the Caisse, Investissement Québec, the Fonds — which is exactly the shareholder base a US$1.4B Québec build needs and the one that tolerates dilution longest. Management alignment is RSU-based and modest; the CEO's February purchase was small and sincere, the officers' sales small and telling. The unverified 12.9% Equinox Partners line is the one thing to nail down: a committed 13% holder changes the equity-gap arithmetic.

Jurisdiction risk

Provincial / national: as supportive as it gets, with the permits still pending. Québec allocated the full 70 MW Hydro-Québec block in Jun 2026 (two ministers came to site — a real signal in a province where blocks are scarce); Troilus was among the first three projects selected for Filon, the province's strategic-mine fast-track (Jul 2026); Bill 63 (2024) tightened claims and consultation but not for a brownfield with a permitted TSF; federally, Troilus was on the Carney critical-minerals mission to Germany (Aug 2025). ESIA filed Jun 2025 to both levels; COMEX (under the James Bay agreement) and IAAC are in information requests; decisions Q1 2027. Québec's 5 Oct 2026 election returned a Parti Québécois government (St-Pierre Plamondon premier-designate); no change to the project's provincial fast-track status has been reported — a continuity question, not a threat.

Local: the Cree relationship is the open item. The Cree Nation of Mistissini signed a pre-development agreement in 2018 and has a joint federal-assessment committee role; the impacts-and-benefits agreement is unsigned. No organised opposition found; Cree members attended the power announcement; the company co-funded cabin rebuilding after the 2023 James Bay fires.

Same province as Osisko Metals; a bigger, longer, more price-geared project — and the IBA is the one licence this file cannot yet check off.

Differentiator
  1. Brownfield scale in Québec: 6.7 Moz of reserves, 26 years, a substation, a transmission line, a permitted TSF and a road — with 70 MW of hydro power already allocated. No other developer in either file has power secured before permits.
  2. The deepest bench of institutional support of any pre-FID name here — four ECAs, three mandated lead arrangers, two European smelters, Investissement Québec and the Fonds FTQ on the register, eight analysts, GDXJ inclusion.
  3. Gold torque with a long fuse — the sensitivity table is the bull case: US$5,000 gold makes this a US$5.5B NPV project against a US$0.8B EV.
  4. A takeout profile — a permitted-in-2027, power-allocated, 250 koz/yr Québec asset is exactly what a mid-tier producer buys (Red Cloud's view), and Agnico's June consolidation of Finland shows what happens to de-risked developers in tier-one belts.

Read it honestly: the differentiator (a huge, long, low-grade, tier-one reserve) is why the capex is US$1.43B and why the IRR is single digits below US$2,500 gold. Scale is the asset and the liability.

Exploration upside

Brownfield, in-pit and underground · moves the needle: low–medium. ~40,000 m in 2026 (24,000 m Z87 pit optimisation, 15,000 m Z87 underground) — 129 m @ 0.95 g/t AuEq incl. 22 m @ 3.38 g/t from an Inferred block inside the reserve pit (Sep 17). Converts Inferred, improves early-year grade, may add an underground phase; does not change the financing arithmetic. At 10.2 Moz M&I the file needs a signed loan, not more ounces.

The Z87 underground work is the one exploration line that could move economics — higher grade into the first decade.

Next Catalyst

Debt financing close (US$850M credit-approved 28 Sep; EDC's US$250M pending; close follows the permits); permits — IAAC and COMEX decisions Q1 2027; Cree IBA (undated); stream / sub-debt and equity package; binding offtakes (Aurubis, Boliden); construction start 2027; first ore Sep 2029. Watch the CFO's first financial-close deadline.

Open Questions
  • At what gold price will Société Générale / KfW / EDC actually size the US$1.2B — and how much of the mandate survives at US$3,000?
  • What does the stream cost: US$360–500M of gold or copper stream on a US$3.2B NPV is a large slice — who provides it and on what deck?
  • When is the Mistissini IBA signed, and what does it cost?
  • Why did like-for-like NPV fall ~55% between the 2024 FS and the 2026 report — is the recovery drop (92.7% → 86.7%) final?
  • How much equity at what price — US$140M is the target; US$300M+ is the scenario if debt is sized conservatively?
  • Is this a mine Troilus builds, or a mine someone buys from Troilus once the permits land?

Fit to this job
This is a US$1.07B open-pit redevelopment of a past-producing mine in Quebec — the largest build in this batch. Reid is a capital-markets geologist who has financed developers and sold one (Sulliden) but has never built or operated a mine; the operating bench was only assembled in 2025–26 (Rivard, Rendall, process manager). Jurisdiction fit is good (Quebec, Cree agreements, ECA/EDC backing). New for them: everything about execution — construction, a 50ktpd mill, and servicing US$1.1B of debt. The financing achievement is real but it is the team's first mine.

Thesis

AurMac sits 40 km from Mayo on the Silver Trail highway, with a 138 kV line crossing the property and a 69 kV substation on site, next door to Hecla's Keno Hill and the failed Eagle mine. From nothing in 2017 Banyan has drilled >180,000 m and built the May 2026 MRE: Indicated 167.3 Mt @ 0.68 g/t = 3.64 Moz; Inferred 267.2 Mt @ 0.58 g/t = 4.98 Moz — 8.62 Moz, Indicated ounces +60% year-on-year, largely within 200 m of surface and open in every direction. A higher-grade core (0.55 g/t cut-off) holds 2.45 Moz Indicated @ 1.00 g/t. Metallurgy decided the mine type: cyanide leach recovers 90–93% but heap-leach columns only 64–72%, so this will be a mill — CEO Tara Christie talks about 30–40,000 tpd, >250 koz/yr and a 30–40 year life. The maiden PEA (Q4 2026) will be the first capex, strip ratio and NPV anyone has seen; it uses the May resource and excludes all 2026 drilling. The company is drilling 70,000 m in 2026 (up to six rigs; 13.03 g/t over 14.2 m and 5.58 g/t over 21.7 m in new Powerline zones; 1.05 g/t over 52.8 m) and plans 70–100,000 m in 2027. Funding: C$57M cash at Jun 30 plus a C$58M raise at C$2.00 closing ~Sep 29 — Franco-Nevada took C$20M of it, having already bought the 6% NSR over the deposits from Victoria Gold's receiver (C$55M portfolio); Banyan can buy that royalty down to 1% for a one-time C$10M. Alpayana (the Peruvian Gubbins family, owners of Sierra Metals) holds ~8%; Franklin ~7%. Five analysts, targets C$2.50–3.00; stock C$1.98 after +118% YTD and GDXJ inclusion on Sep 21.

The Gate

The maiden PEA has to show that 0.62 g/t at 30–50,000 tpd works at a capex the market has already, implicitly, assumed. At US$71 per total ounce and US$168 per Indicated ounce, on a mill project with no strip ratio, no capex and no throughput disclosed, the stock is priced for a good study. By analogy — Snowline's Valley at 25,000 tpd and 1.2 g/t needed C$1.7B — AurMac's mill plausibly lands at C$1.5–2.5B (my inference, not company guidance) against a C$883M market cap, and the low grade makes every dollar of cost a large share of margin.

Sub-gates
  1. The Na-Cho Nyäk Dun relationship — no exploration cooperation or consent agreement is disclosed; in September 2025 Chief Dawna Hope called the AurMac acquisition "concerning" and cited "the lack of transparency and communication Banyan Gold has demonstrated to date", and the First Nation opposes new claims in its territory pending land-use planning — a licence gap that the Snowline MOU (Jan 2026, FPIC before construction) shows can be closed but has not been here.
  2. The post-Eagle regime — Yukon is implementing all 56 review-board recommendations and rewriting the mine-waste guidelines (spring 2027); a mill means a tailings facility licensed under rules not yet finished, in the district where the failure happened.
  3. The 6% NSR — Franco-Nevada's royalty takes 6% of revenue until Banyan pays C$10M to cut it to 1%; that decision is undated and pre-PEA cash has other calls on it.
  4. Power — a 69 kV substation does not run a 40,000 tpd mill; grid expansion is 3–5 years away and outside the company's control.
  5. Slippage — the PEA was on a "strict timeline" for 2025 under the earn-in, then H2 2026, then Q4, now "Q3–Q4 2026".

The PEA is the gate. Everything before it has been delivered on time; everything that matters comes after it.

The Rule tests cannot be run until Q4; what can be said is that the market cap is already ~35–60% of the plausible capex range, which is a developer-with-a-study price on an explorer without one.
Valuation Anchor

US$71 per total ounce, US$168 per Indicated ounce, no study — the market has moved this from a discovery multiple to a pre-PEA developer multiple in eighteen months. The bull case is Snowline: a Yukon bulk-tonnage deposit re-rated 3–4× per ounce once a PEA showed a 25% IRR, and Banyan trades at roughly a quarter of Snowline per ounce today. But Snowline has twice the grade and a PEA in hand; AurMac's 0.62 g/t means its PEA will show a larger mill, a bigger tailings facility and a thinner margin, and a 6% royalty on top until C$10M buys it down.

The re-rate path is PEA (Q4) → royalty buy-down → NND agreement → PFS 2027–28 → a major's cheque; Christie has said openly that 5 Moz+ deposits attract Barrick and Newmont, and Franco-Nevada's equity-plus-royalty position is the kind of endorsement that precedes one.

The bear case is the PEA itself: C$2B of capex, a 15% IRR at US$3,000, and a stock at US$71/oz that has nowhere to go but down until gold does the work.

Bucket: scale & financing, the explorer end of it — the Troilus problem (a huge low-grade reserve whose value is set by the metal price) before the study that would tell us how big the problem is.

Shareholder structure
Management & board
~4–5%. Company deck: insiders ~4%, CEO Tara Christie 1.4%; MarketScreener shows Christie at 15.1M shares / 3.5% — unreconciled, likely options included in one figure. Holdings built from a decade of placements and option exercises since 2013; Christie reportedly subscribed ~C$500k in the Sep 2026 raise at C$2.00. 31.5M options at WAEP C$0.46 (6.2M granted FY26 at ~C$1.01); no warrants anywhere in the structure.
Insider activity (12 mo)
Net sellers. Director David Reid sold 5,000,000 @ C$0.80 (C$4.0M) Nov 3, 2025 and exercised/sold 300k options Feb 2026; director Burleton sold 375k @ C$1.38–1.47 (Feb–Mar 2026); CFO Rutt sold 180k @ C$1.43–1.70 (Aug 2026); Christie exercised and sold 500k options (C$120k, Feb 2026). Buys: chair Blythe 20k (~C$25k, Jan 2026); Christie's C$500k financing subscription. Reid's sale is the largest by an order of magnitude and came at 40% of today's price.
Strategic & prominent
Alpayana S.A.C. ~8% (Gubbins family, Peru; acquired Sierra Metals in 2025) — bought essentially the whole Oct 2025 placement; an operating strategic, not a fund. Franco-Nevada ~2.1% plus the 6% NSR — royalty-and-equity is the strongest external endorsement in the structure. Franklin Gold & Precious Metals ~7%. Osisko Development ~2% (Christie sits on Osisko Metals' board). Ixios ~1.3%. Van Eck via GDXJ (passive) from Sep 21. No Sprott, McEwen, Rule, Crescat, Palisades or Giustra positions found; no Hecla, Kinross or Agnico stake despite Hecla's adjacency.
Institutions / retail
Company deck: institutions/HNW ~48% (institutions 29%, HNW 19%), Alpayana 8%, insiders ~4%, retail ~29%. Filings-based aggregators: institutions ~10%, insiders ~5% (much of the HNW/foreign holding is unfiled). 446M shares → ~479M pro forma; +27% in 15 months, all at or above market.

Read: A register that outside money likes — a royalty major, a Peruvian operating family, Franklin — and insiders who own little and have been selling into the rise. The Reid sale (C$4M at C$0.80) is the fact I would put to the company; the CEO's C$500k subscription at C$2.00 is the right answer to it, if confirmed. Alignment is thinner than the story.

Jurisdiction risk

Provincial / national: Canada, Yukon — a mining territory rewriting its rulebook. Since the Eagle heap-leach failure (Jun 2024, 20 km away) the Yukon government has committed to all 56 Independent Review Board recommendations, is reviewing every existing quartz mining licence, and is revising the mine-waste-facility guidelines (23 of 56 done by Apr 2026; the rest targeted spring 2027). The IRB concluded heap leaching can proceed with enhanced oversight; Banyan has sidestepped the question by going to a mill — which means a tailings facility, licensed under rules not yet written, in the district where the failure happened. YESAB not yet entered; multi-year once it is. Infrastructure is the genuine asset: all-weather highway, 138 kV line and a 69 kV substation on the property, hydro 40 km away, cell and fibre — though a large mill would need grid expansion the territory has not scheduled.

Local: the weak layer. The First Nation of Na-Cho Nyäk Dun (NND) has no disclosed agreement with Banyan. In August 2025 NND opposed new claims in its territory pending land-use planning (Banyan agreed to stake none); in September 2025 the Chief called the AurMac transfer "concerning" and criticised Banyan's "lack of transparency and communication". The company points to a 50% Yukoner workforce (30% from Mayo), NND Development Corporation contractors, C$3.3M of education funding since 2012 and baseline work since 2021, and has hired an ex-Kaminak sustainability lead and an ex-Alexco environmental manager. NND's MOU with Snowline (Jan 2026; free, prior and informed consent before construction) shows the First Nation is not anti-mining and shows what Banyan does not yet have.

Same territory as Triumph's Freegold — but AurMac has the road, the power line and the resource; what it lacks is the agreement.

Differentiator
  1. Scale with infrastructure: 8.6 Moz — 3.6 Moz Indicated — within 200 m of surface, beside an all-weather highway and under a 138 kV line, 40 km from a hydro dam. No other pre-study name in this file has both the ounces and the access.
  2. A treasury that removes the financing question for two years — ~C$100M pro forma, no debt, no warrants, every raise since 2025 at or above market, drilling expanded 40,000 → 70,000 m rather than cut.
  3. The register — Franco-Nevada holds the royalty and now equity; Alpayana, a Peruvian operating family, took an entire placement; Franklin ~7%; GDXJ inclusion.
  4. A Yukon-native team — Christie founded YESAB's board and ran a placer mine in the territory for a decade; the chair sold Nevsun to Zijin; the corporate-development hire just sold Probe to Fresnillo; John Robins (Kaminak, Great Bear) advises.
  5. Discovery is still running — 13 g/t over 14 m in a new zone, ten undrilled targets, a 720 km² district that is <2% explored.

Read it honestly: the differentiator is quantity and location. The thing that decides the stock — grade against capex — is the one the differentiator says nothing about.

Exploration upside

Very high · moves the needle: high for ounces, low for the PEA. 70,000 m in 2026 with ~25,000 m of assays still to come; 2027 guided at 70–100,000 m at AurMac plus 20–30,000 m regional, following up the first Gap-zone holes between Powerline and Airstrip (6 Oct 2026: 1.88 g/t over 17.9 m) from January. New high-grade zones at Powerline North (13.03 g/t / 14.2 m; 5.58 g/t / 21.7 m; 149 g/t / 0.4 m) could lift the higher-grade core that a mill would mine first. Keno-style silver (10,734 g/t Ag / 1.7 m) and Nitra (5.70 g/t Au + 544 g/t Ag) are district optionality, not thesis. None of this is in the Q4 PEA.

Watch the higher-grade core (0.55 g/t cut-off) more than the headline ounces — a mill's first decade is built from it.

Next Catalyst

Maiden PEA — Q4 2026 (capex, strip, throughput, NPV: the whole re-rate, up or down); C$58M raise closing ~Sep 29; remaining 2026 assays through Dec; royalty buy-down decision (C$10M, undated); 2027 drill start Jan (Gap-zone follow-up); a resource update on the 2026 drilling (not yet guided); any NND agreement; revised Yukon waste-facility guidelines spring 2027.

Open Questions
  • What capex and strip ratio does the PEA show, and at what throughput — and what is the IRR at US$3,000, not US$3,500?
  • Is the higher-grade core (2.45 Moz @ 1.0 g/t) enough to front-load the mine plan, or does the economics rest on 0.58 g/t Inferred?
  • When is the C$10M royalty buy-down exercised, and why not before the PEA is published?
  • What does an agreement with Na-Cho Nyäk Dun look like, and what has the company done since the Chief's September 2025 statement?
  • How does a 30–40,000 tpd mill get powered — grid expansion timing, LNG bridge cost?
  • Why were directors and the CFO net sellers (Reid C$4.0M) through a year in which the company raised C$135M from outsiders?
Context & updates
3 Oct 2026 refresh

The C$54.3M financing closed 29 Sep (27.16M shares at C$2.00; ~473M shares out, ~505M fully diluted). The company now says proceeds advance AurMac and Nitra 'through 2028'. Maiden PEA still Q4 2026.

C$58M financing and Franco-Nevada (Sep 20–24, 2026)

C$50M brokered LIFE (25M sh @ C$2.00, Canaccord) + C$8M non-brokered (8M @ C$2.00), no warrants, closing ~Sep 29; Franco-Nevada subscribed for 10M shares (C$20M, ~2.1%) on top of the 6% NSR it bought in April. Stock −7.6% on the announcement. Pro forma treasury ~C$100M; funds 2027 drilling and the PEA/PFS programme.

MRE (May 19, 2026) and PEA consultants (Jul 7)

Indicated 3.64 Moz @ 0.68 g/t (+60%), Inferred 4.98 Moz @ 0.58; 0.30 g/t cut-off, US$3,500 shell; technical report filed Jun 26. AMC (mining), Lycopodium (process), BGC (geotech) engaged for the PEA, guided Q4 2026.

Royalty (Apr 16, 2026)

Franco-Nevada closed the purchase of Victoria Gold's royalty portfolio from the receiver for C$55.0M, including the 6% NSR over the 510 claims covering Powerline and Airstrip and 1% on Banyan's Hyland. Banyan retains the right to buy the 6% down to 1% for a one-time C$10M.

Earn-in and ownership (Sep 2025)

100% of Aurex/McQuesten acquired from Victoria Gold's receiver (C$2.0M + C$1.6M) after Eagle's failure ended Victoria's option; the "strict" 2025 PEA deadline fell away with it. Victoria's 8.6% stake fully sold by the receiver; Alpayana bought essentially all of the Oct 2025 C$31.4M placement at C$0.70 / C$0.97 (FT).

Aside

Five raises in 18 months, all without warrants and each at a higher price (C$0.70 → C$0.97 → C$1.40 → C$1.918 → C$2.00) — an unusually clean dilution record for a Venture explorer. Flow-through spend obligations: C$6.6M by Dec 2026, C$29.7M by Dec 2027 — cash that must go into the ground, not the royalty or the study.

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 2/5

Clean Yukon explorer team that grew a big resource and discloses its slips; the CEO has no exit or build behind him.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Tara Christie (President & CEO, director, since Aug 2016): M.Sc., P.Eng; President of Gimlex Gold Mines (family placer operation, Yukon) 2006–2016; past president Klondike Placer Miners' Association; director Osisko Metals · Kai Woloshyn (VP Project Development, since unverified): Ex-Environmental Manager Alexco (Keno Hill, Yukon) 10+ yrs — permitting lead · Patrick Langlois (VP Strategy & Corporate Development, since 2026): Ex-CFO/VP CorpDev Probe Gold, sold to Fresnillo for ~C$780M in 2026 · Marc Blythe (Director (independent), since unverified): Ex-VP CorpDev Nevsun (sold to Zijin US$1.9B 2018); led two feasibility studies that became mines
Track record
  • Christie: no prior public-company CEO role; Gimlex was a private placer miner — AurMac is her first hard-rock development and first public exit attemptsource
  • Banyan under Christie: AurMac optioned from Victoria Gold 2017, resource grown from zero to 8.62Moz (May 2026), 100% earn-in completed Sep 2025 from Victoria Gold's receiver (https://www.miningnewsnorth.com/story/2026/05/22/northern-neighbors/banyan-lifts-aurmac-to-nearly-9m-oz-gold/9685.html; https://banyangold.com/site/assets/files/5404/2025--09-18_banyan_-_closing_option_acceleration_final.pdf)
  • Christie's board history: Western Copper and Gold (to Jun 2025), Constantine Metal Resources (to 2021; sold to American Pacific 2021), Klondike Gold (to 2021), Osisko Metals (since Dec 2024)source
  • C$54.3M financing closed Sep 2026; National Bank target C$3.00source
  • Board: Burleton (ex-CEO GT Gold 2018–19, which was sold to Newmont 2021 after his exit), Blythe (Nevsun exit), Reid (Far West Mining sold to Capstone C$1.1B 2011) — the exits belong to directors, not to the CEOsource

Boards today: Christie: 2 (Banyan CEO, Osisko Metals director). Burleton is also interim CEO of Angus Gold.

Fit to this job
Stage match is good: AurMac is a large low-grade Yukon oxide/sulphide deposit heading to a maiden PEA, and the team is Yukon-native (Christie grew up in Klondike placer mining; Woloshyn permitted at Keno Hill). Nobody on the executive has taken a hard-rock project through feasibility, permitting (YESAB) and construction; the directors with that experience (Blythe, Halsall-Whitney) are non-executive. New for them: economic studies, Yukon permitting, and the 2024 Victoria Gold/Eagle heap-leach failure makes a Yukon heap-leach PEA a harder sell.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake from grants or cheap founder paper; little buying. Christie holds ~14.2M shares, 2.6–3.5% depending on source (worth ~C$20M), accumulated via early placements and option exercises (e.g., 500k options at C$0.24 exercised Feb 2025); insiders collectively net sellers of ~C$350k over the trailing year. CEO total comp ~C$627k (53% salary) — in line for a ~C$840M market cap. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsxv-byn/banyan-gold-shares/management; https://www.marketscreener.com/insider/TARA-CHRISTIE-A0EUR0/. Current circular not fetched.

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash was C$57.4M at 30 June 2026 and about C$110M after a C$54.3M placement in September 2026; peak-season burn is C$15.6M a quarter, so about 7 quarters of runway.
  2. Capitalised exploration was C$19.9M in the first nine months of FY26 against C$4.1M of cash G&A, so overhead is about 15% of spend but more than doubled year on year.
  3. Shares outstanding grew from 284.9M in September 2023 to 445.9M in June 2026, up 57%, and about 473M after the September 2026 placement; no debt, streams or royalties sold.
  4. Reported net losses look small only because of non-cash flow-through premium recoveries; the flow-through premium liability was C$16.0M at 30 June 2026.
  5. Every set of statements carries a going-concern note, the auditor changed in August 2025, and C$3.6M was paid to Victoria Gold's receiver to complete 100% of AurMac.

A fully funded, permitted silver-gold heap-leach build in Sonora, trading ~0.5× its open-pit NAV at spot after a 43% capex rise and a C$100M equity raise.

Gate Build the Stockwork pit on the new US$124M budget and pour gold in December 2027 — on a 0.40 g/t heap leach there is little room for a second cost miss The company has the money (pro-forma ~C$185M against ~C$150M remaining capex) and the permits, so the gate is execution: earthworks were 30% and detailed engineering 65% complete at 14 Sep 2026, with ~66% of capex contractually committed. The first budget already failed (US$86.8M in the Jan 2026 PFS → ~US$124M in Sep 2026, driven by doubled blasting volumes and equipment prices above study assumptions); the excess cash is only ~C$35M, so a further 20% overrun would send the company back to the market or to the debt lenders it stopped mentioning. Sub-gates: (1) ramp-up — years 1–3 run at 7,500 tpd, half the 15,000 tpd that drives the 4.8 Moz AgEq average, so early cash flow will be thinner than the headline; (2) metallurgy on a 15 g/t Ag / 0.40 g/t Au stockwork at heap-leach recoveries (PFS assumptions not re-checked here); (3) Mexico — concessions, water and the open-pit politics are a background risk even with approvals in hand.

Thesis

Silver Tiger has taken El Tigre from a 2020 exploration story to a permitted (SEMARNAT, Nov 2025), board-approved (Mar 2026) open-pit heap leach under construction with Kappes Cassiday as EPCM and first pour guided for December 2027. The Stockwork Zone PFS (Jan 2026, US$3,200 gold / US$38 silver) shows an after-tax NPV5% of US$456M and 65.7% IRR on ~4.8 Moz AgEq/yr for 10 years; a second, standalone underground PEA on the high-grade veins adds US$304M. At today's prices the open pit alone is worth roughly US$690M on my extrapolation of the company's sensitivity table (after the US$37M capex increase), against a US$355M market cap — the market is paying ~0.5× NAV for a funded build. The bear case: a low-grade (0.40 g/t Au, 15 g/t Ag) heap leach whose capex has already risen 43%, in Mexico, run by a Halifax capital-markets team that has not built a mine before, with 659M shares and 50M warrants overhead.

The Gate

Build the Stockwork pit on the new US$124M budget and pour gold in December 2027 — on a 0.40 g/t heap leach there is little room for a second cost miss The company has the money (pro-forma ~C$185M against ~C$150M remaining capex) and the permits, so the gate is execution: earthworks were 30% and detailed engineering 65% complete at 14 Sep 2026, with ~66% of capex contractually committed. The first budget already failed (US$86.8M in the Jan 2026 PFS → ~US$124M in Sep 2026, driven by doubled blasting volumes and equipment prices above study assumptions); the excess cash is only ~C$35M, so a further 20% overrun would send the company back to the market or to the debt lenders it stopped mentioning. Sub-gates: (1) ramp-up — years 1–3 run at 7,500 tpd, half the 15,000 tpd that drives the 4.8 Moz AgEq average, so early cash flow will be thinner than the headline; (2) metallurgy on a 15 g/t Ag / 0.40 g/t Au stockwork at heap-leach recoveries (PFS assumptions not re-checked here); (3) Mexico — concessions, water and the open-pit politics are a background risk even with approvals in hand.

UG PEA: 304 ÷ 83.5 = 3.6×. Both clear a 1× screen comfortably — the issue is not the ratio but the low head grade that makes the margin sensitive to recoveries and costs.
Valuation Anchor

At today's prices the open pit alone is worth ~US$690M after tax (extrapolated), so the market pays ~0.5× NAV for a funded, permitted build 14 months from first pour, with the underground (~US$640M at today's prices on the same method) and a 37,000 ha district on top at roughly nothing. Funded single-asset developers in good jurisdictions commonly trade 0.6–0.9× NAV into first pour and ~1× as producers; the Mexico/low-grade/execution discount is the reason for the gap. Per AgEq ounce: US$355M ÷ 235.5 Moz M&I AgEq ≈ US$1.5/oz AgEq.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~2.6% pre-raise (14.5M shares; Simply Wall St, 15 Oct 2026) — CEO Glenn Jessome 8.47M (1.52%, ~1.3% post-raise), Chair Richard Gordon 2.7M (0.48%), VP Exploration David Duncan 1.6M (0.29%). Institutions ~24%: Franklin Templeton 8.43% (47.1M), ASA Gold & Precious Metals 3.94%, Mirae Asset 3.66%, Konwave 2.74%, VanEck 2.54% (GDXJ inclusion effective 18 Sep 2026), ALPS 1.92%. Eric Sprott participated in the 2020 and Apr 2025 raises (KE Report, Apr 2025) — current stake not disclosed and not on the visible top-holder list. No strategic/major mining holder. Post-raise percentages are ~15% lower than the above. Insider trades (12 mo): Jessome exercised 593k options at ~C$0.17 (Dec 2025); Gordon sold 55k shares at C$0.80–0.82 (May–Jun 2026); Duncan sold 20k at C$0.94 (Aug 2026); no open-market buys found.

Read: An institutional, retail-heavy register with no strategic anchor and a management stake that is small for a founder team — the names that matter here are the bought-deal syndicate and the index funds, and both can leave.

Jurisdiction risk

National: Mexico. The 2023 mining-law reform shortened new concessions to 30 years and tightened water rules; no new concessions have been granted since 2018 and President Sheinbaum has said none will be; AMLO's Feb 2024 proposal to ban open-pit mining by constitutional amendment lacked the two-thirds majority at the time (mining.com, Apr 2024) — its 2026 status was not re-verified. El Tigre holds existing concessions and received 'all required approvals and permits' from SEMARNAT to construct the Stockwork open pit on 7 Nov 2025; the historic underground is described by the company as permitted. CFE has granted grid access. Mexico levies a 7.5% special mining duty on EBITDA plus 0.5% on precious-metal revenue (standard; not re-checked). Local: the district is a historic mining area (El Tigre mine 1903–1938) near Colonia Morelos, Sonora; a 250-person Mexican construction team is on site, the 46 km access road is being rebuilt, and no community opposition was found in the company's releases or the search. Sonora has a security (cartel) profile that the company does not discuss.

Permits are in hand and construction is visibly under way — jurisdiction here is a discount on the multiple, not a gate; the open-pit-ban politics are the tail risk.

Differentiator

**Funded and permitted, with a specialist builder.** Few sub-US$400M developers have cash in the bank that exceeds their remaining capex, SEMARNAT approvals, an EPCM contract with Kappes Cassiday (the firm behind many Mexican heap leaches; VP Operations Francisco Albelais spent 2005–12 at KCA and built/ran Argonaut's Mexican mines) and earthworks 30% done. The second differentiator is the district: a 37,000 ha historic silver camp with a separate high-grade vein system (UG PEA 251 g/t Ag, 0.91 g/t Au; new Northern Veins hits to 29.6 kg/t AgEq) that could be a second mine fed by the pit's cash flow.

The honest flip side: the pit itself is a low-grade, cost-sensitive heap leach whose first budget already missed by 43%.

Exploration upside

Northern Veins high-grade hits, 700 m from the plant · moves the needle: medium 2026 drilling (holes ET-26-637 to -650) on the Caleigh and Protectora veins north of the historic mine returned 2.10 m @ 7,715 g/t AgEq (incl. 0.53 m @ 29,620 g/t) and 93 m @ 70 g/t AgEq; the veins are faulted extensions of the Southern Veins in the UG PEA and sit ~700 m north of the heap leach. Lluvia de Oro drilling is planned for 2027. Infill of the northern resource is planned without a date.

Next Catalyst

Construction updates (quarterly releases: engineering, earthworks, camp, crusher delivery) on the path to commissioning and first pour in December 2027; Northern Veins assays through Q4 2026; an underground development decision and any restated economics on the new capex (neither dated).

Open Questions
  • What do the PFS economics look like on the US$124M capex and 2026 operating costs — the company has not restated NPV/IRR/AISC since the increase?
  • What is production in years 1–3 at 7,500 tpd, and what recoveries did the PFS assume for the 15 g/t Ag / 0.40 g/t Au stockwork?
  • Why did the debt package that was 'nearing completion' in March 2026 not close, and what did lenders see?
  • Does the '314 Moz AgEq' resource headline reconcile with the 235.5 Moz in the resource table?
  • When does the underground get a development decision, and will it be funded from cash flow or another raise?
  • Who holds the remaining ~74% of the register, and has Eric Sprott kept his position?
Context & updates
20 Oct 2026 update

First construction update since the C$100M raise: the company puts cash at ~US$120M against ~US$100M still to spend of the US$124M budget (US$24M spent, US$72M committed), so the build is funded with roughly US$20M of headroom, thinner than the ~C$35M the card assumed. Engineering is 70% done (65% at 14 Sep), the road is finished and the long-lead equipment is ordered; first pour stays December 2027. Nothing here changes the odds (16%) or risk (3); the two open promises, restated economics for the US$124M build and the December 2027 pour, are unchanged.

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 2/5 · Skin in the game 2/5

Delivered the big milestones (PFS, permit, construction decision, funding) and hired real builders, but a PEA slipped seven months by silent re-dating, a debt package vanished without comment, and the first capex estimate missed by 43% after a construction decision that preceded the geotech. Solid financiers, unproven builders, thin skin.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

  • Institutional endorsement: Franklin Templeton 8.4%, ASA, Mirae, Konwave, VanEck; Stifel/BMO/Canaccord/Desjardins syndicates on every raise; Eric Sprott in the 2020 and Apr 2025 raises (https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsx-slvr/silver-tiger-metals-shares/ownership; https://kereport.podbean.com/e/silver-tiger-metals%E2%80%93-eric-sprott-and-asyndicateof-long-only-institutional-funds-participatein-recently-closed15-millionbought-deal-financing)

Boards today: Jessome: CEO and director of Silver Tiger only (no other public boards found). Abriel: CFO and director — a CFO on his own board is a governance weakness. Gordon: chair, ex-CEO, founding shareholder — 'independent' in name. Two of five directors are Mexican and independent.

Fit to this job
Stage: funded construction of a heap leach in Mexico. The CEO is a capital-markets lawyer whose demonstrated skill is exactly what the last 18 months needed — raising ~C$241M in bought deals — and not what the next 14 months need, which is building. The build fit comes from Albelais (25 years building Mexican heap leaches, incl. at KCA) and the KCA EPCM contract. Region: yes — the team has worked Sonora/Mexico since 2020 and GoGold before that. New for them: operating a mine as a company.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small founder stake (~1.5% CEO, ~2.6% all insiders pre-raise), options, small insider sales in 2026 and no open-market buying. Jessome 8.47M shares (1.52% pre-raise, ~1.3% post; ~C$6.5M at C$0.77) — founder stock plus 593k options exercised at ~C$0.17 in Dec 2025; CEO total pay ~C$1.2M (Simply Wall St, year not stated), paid partly through his own corporation (C$93,750 consulting in Q2 2026) — ~0.24% of market cap, modest. Gordon 2.7M shares, sold 55k (C$44k) May–Jun 2026; Duncan 1.6M, sold 20k (C$19k) Aug 2026. Insiders collectively ~2.6% pre-raise; no open-market purchases in the last 12 months found. Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • CFO sits on the board; chair is the founding ex-CEO — three of five directors are founders/executives.
  • Debt financing talked up for 18 months (Jan 2025 'lenders', Mar 2026 'nearing completion') and then silently replaced by equity.
  • Construction decision (Mar 2026) taken before the geotechnical drilling that later doubled blasting volumes and added US$25M — sequencing error disclosed six months later.
  • Insiders ~2% after the raise; chair and VP Exploration were small sellers in 2026 while the company was raising; no open-market buys found.
  • Headline '314 Moz AgEq' resource does not reconcile with the release's table.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash was C$108.6M at 30 June 2026 (down from C$117.1M at 31 March 2026). The quarter's net outflow of C$8.4M was almost all construction spending (C$8.3M); the operating cash burn was only C$0.1M because C$0.6M of interest income covered most of the C$0.9M cash G&A. The company said it had about C$90M of cash on 10 September 2026 and closed a C$100.05M bought deal (100.05M units at C$1.00, 5% commission) on 13 October 2026, giving roughly C$185M pro forma against a remaining El Tigre capex of about C$150M (total capex revised to about US$124M from US$87M; first pour targeted December 2027).
  2. Shares outstanding went from 365.0M (unchanged from March 2024 to March 2025) to 558.6M at 30 June 2026 through four bought deals in FY26 raising C$141.3M gross (C$131.3M net including option exercises); after the October 2026 deal the count is about 658.7M plus 50.0M warrants at C$1.35, the first warrants in the structure.
  3. Everything spent on El Tigre is capitalised, so the income statement shows only overhead: capitalised project spending was C$19.1M in FY24 (the big 2023-24 drill program), C$3.2M in FY25 (net of C$4.4M of Mexican VAT refunds; C$7.9M gross incurred), C$13.5M in FY26 and C$8.3M in the June 2026 quarter as construction started.
  4. Cash G&A was C$2.1M in FY24, C$3.8M in FY25 and C$4.4M in FY26 (about 25% of total cash spending in FY26, down from 10% in FY24 when drilling dominated); shareholder communication (C$1.4M) and consulting fees to the CEO's and CFO's companies (C$1.1M incl. bonuses) are the largest items. Stock-based compensation was C$1.7M in FY26 and C$1.1M in the June 2026 quarter alone after the RSU/option grants of early 2026.
  5. There is no debt, lease or stream; working capital was C$103.7M at 30 June 2026. Net losses are small (C$5.2M in FY26) because the project is capitalised, but the audited resource-property balance (C$103.0M) relies on no impairment indicators, which the auditor flagged as the key audit matter.

Caveats (8)FY24 (year to 31 Mar 2024) line items come from the comparative column of the FY25 audited statements, not from the FY24 PDF itself (link recorded). Q4 FY26 and Q4 FY25 are derived as audited year less 9M YTD; Q3 and Q2 figures are derived from 9M less 6M and 6M less 3M year-to-date statements.Sum of the four FY26 quarters: ni -5.2 = FY -5.2; cfo -3.9 = FY -3.9; fin 131.3 = FY 131.3. FY25: only Q2-Q4 collected (Q1 FY25 to June 2024, from comparatives: ni -0.6, cfo -0.3, exp_cap -3.2, fin 0.0); sum of four quarters ni -4.2 = FY -4.2, cfo -2.9 vs FY -2.8 (rounding), fin 0.0 = FY 0.0.Some quarterly 'is' line items do not sum to 'ni' by 0.1 because of rounding of individual lines (Q4 FY26 -1.1-0.8+0.4 = -1.5 vs reported -1.6; Q4 FY25, Q3 FY25, FY26, FY25 and FY24 differ by 0.1 the same way); the 'ni' values are the reported figures.Resource-property cash outflows are reported 'net of VAT collections'; gross project spending per quarter is not disclosed, so 'ground' in Q2 FY25 (net inflow) and Q3 FY25 understates the gross amount spent. Audited gross costs incurred: C$17.9M FY24, C$7.9M FY25, C$14.0M FY26.The classification of the June 2026 quarter's C$8.3M as 'capex' (construction) rather than 'exp_cap' follows the MD&A wording ('reflecting Stockwork Zone construction'); the statements use a single line for all project spending.Post-period: the C$100.05M bought deal (100.05M units at C$1.00, one-half warrant per unit, whole warrant at C$1.35 for 24 months, 5% commission) closed 13 Oct 2026 per the company's release carried by Cantech Letter; pro forma share count ~658.7M and net proceeds ~C$95M are estimates (other issue costs not disclosed). The 'about C$90M cash at 10 Sep 2026' figure is from the 21 Sep 2026 news release, not a financial statement.The weighted-average share count in the June 2026 quarter (566.4M) is higher than the shares outstanding at both 31 Mar 2026 (558.4M) and 30 Jun 2026 (558.6M); not explained in the statements (possibly includes vested DSUs). Shares outstanding figures are the statement/MD&A values.Calendar dates are estimates from the TSX 45/90-day rules and the company's own filing pattern; the company publishes no results calendar and no notice for the Q2 FY27 release was found. The treatment of Silver Tiger as a non-venture issuer from the September 2026 quarter follows its TSX listing on 21 May 2026 and has not been confirmed by a company statement.

Fiscal year ends 31 March, so 'Q1 FY27' = the quarter to 30 June 2026 and 'FY26' = the year to 31 March 2026. Statements are presented in whole Canadian dollars (not thousands); all figures here are C$ millions. The company has a single asset (El Tigre, Sonora, Mexico) and capitalises ALL project spending into 'resource properties', so 'exp' (expensed exploration) is null everywhere; 'ee' = resource properties (capitalised exploration, land payments, studies and, from the March 2026 construction decision, construction), 'ppe' = property and equipment (an office building, ~C$0.5M). 'ga' = consulting fees (CEO and CFO are paid through their companies) + dues + insurance + office + professional fees + shareholder communication + travel + wages; 'sbc' = stock-based compensation; 'fin' = interest income; 'other' = foreign exchange gain/(loss) and depreciation. Cash-flow line 'expenditures on resource properties, net of VAT collections' is shown as 'exp_cap' up to Q4 FY26 and as 'capex' from Q1 FY27 (the MD&A describes it as Stockwork Zone construction). Quarterly cash flows are derived from year-to-date statements. No debt, leases, streams or warrants at any balance-sheet date shown; 50.0M warrants at C$1.35 were created by the October 2026 unit financing.

A small, unhedged Argentine gold producer (~60 koz/yr, 54% AISC margin) trading at ~2× EBITDA because its defined mine life is about two years and its balance sheet is stretched.

Gate Turn two years of defined mine life into five, while paying down the Sprott notes MDN has no reserves and its last resource is from April 2024 (M&I 13.44 Mt @ 1.13 g/t = 490 koz Au; Inferred 121 koz); the August 2024 PEA gave a five-year life to about 2028. Everything hangs on the new resource estimate and PEA due late Q1 2027 (drilling at Falcon/Calandrias II to finish before year-end; the new 12 Mt leach pad is also late Q1 2027). Meanwhile heap-leach gold recovery has fallen to 33% (Q3) from 47% a year earlier, Q2 AISC jumped to US$1,933 from US$1,348 in Q1, and the company owes Sprott US$8M (due 6 Oct 2026, payment not yet confirmed in a release) and US$12M (due 4 Jan 2027) for the stream buy-back, on top of a US$29M loan and a US$39M working-capital deficit. If the PEA shows 5+ years at ~60 koz and gold holds, the 2× EBITDA multiple is too low; if it shows two or three years, the market is right.

Partly funded to the next catalyst Funded month to month from mine cash flow at US$4,000 gold, but the C$10M Sprott placement at C$2.50 (Sep 2026) while running a buyback says the company needed equity to bridge the stream buy-back and expansion capex. US$20M of Sprott notes fall due Oct 2026–Jan 2027 against ~US$17–25M of cash; a gold price fall or another cost spike would bring another raise or asset sale. Mont Sorcier (US$574M capex, 2029 start) is unfunded and far beyond the company's means alone.
Thesis

Cerrado owns Minera Don Nicolás (MDN) in Santa Cruz, Argentina, bought in 2020 and rebuilt as a heap-leach plus small CIL operation: Q3 2026 output 16,685 GEO (+21% y/y), 2026 guidance 50–60k GEO heading to the top end, Q2 AISC US$1,933/oz against a US$4,184 realised price. The market pays about 2× annualised EBITDA for it because there are no reserves, the M&I resource (490 koz Au, April 2024) supports heap leaching only 'until at least 2028', free cash flow was negative in H1 2026 on expansion capex, and the MD&A carries going-concern language with a US$39M working-capital deficit. The other two assets are not gold: an 80% stake in the stalled Lagoa Salgada copper-zinc project in Portugal and the Mont Sorcier iron-vanadium project in Québec (2022 PEA NPV8 US$1.6B, US$574M capex, BFS now H1 2027). Monte do Carmo in Brazil is no longer Cerrado's: it was sold to Hochschild for US$60M (completed 7 Nov 2024).

The Gate

Turn two years of defined mine life into five, while paying down the Sprott notes MDN has no reserves and its last resource is from April 2024 (M&I 13.44 Mt @ 1.13 g/t = 490 koz Au; Inferred 121 koz); the August 2024 PEA gave a five-year life to about 2028. Everything hangs on the new resource estimate and PEA due late Q1 2027 (drilling at Falcon/Calandrias II to finish before year-end; the new 12 Mt leach pad is also late Q1 2027). Meanwhile heap-leach gold recovery has fallen to 33% (Q3) from 47% a year earlier, Q2 AISC jumped to US$1,933 from US$1,348 in Q1, and the company owes Sprott US$8M (due 6 Oct 2026, payment not yet confirmed in a release) and US$12M (due 4 Jan 2027) for the stream buy-back, on top of a US$29M loan and a US$39M working-capital deficit. If the PEA shows 5+ years at ~60 koz and gold holds, the 2× EBITDA multiple is too low; if it shows two or three years, the market is right.

Risk score4/5A producing mine with a US$2,250/oz margin limits permanent loss, which keeps it from a 5. Not a 3 because: no reserves and a defined life of roughly two years; AISC up 43% in one quarter and heap-leach recovery at 33%; negative free cash flow in H1 2026; a US$39M working-capital deficit, going-concern language and US$20M of secured notes due Oct 2026–Jan 2027; Argentine FX controls on the only cash-generating asset; and a Portuguese concession in court. The loss path is a resource update that disappoints while costs stay high and gold slips.

Lagoa Salgada FS Jul 2023 (Ascendant): post-tax NPV8 US$147M, IRR 39%. MDN: no initial capex (PEA Aug 2024); 2026 growth capex running ~US$20M a quarter (H1 US$40.1M) for the crusher, a 12 Mt leach pad (late Q1 2027), tailings and fleet. Mont Sorcier: US$574M initial capex (2022 PEA; now being re-scoped to 8 Mtpa in two phases, BFS H1 2027, ESIA Q2 2027, permits ~end-2028, construction ~end Q1 2029). Lagoa Salgada: 2023 FS IRR 39%, capex not re-verified. MDN PEA (Aug 2024) NPV5 US$111M at US$2,100 gold, avg EBITDA US$49.2M/yr — stale; at US$4,000 gold the same ounces would carry roughly 2.5–3× that NPV, but the plan only runs to ~2028. Mont Sorcier after-tax NPV8 US$1.61B (2022 deck: US$100/t 62% Fe + US$20/t premium). Lagoa Salgada post-tax NPV8 US$147M (Jul 2023), 80% attributable.
ReservesNone declared at any asset. MDN M&I 490 koz Au + 6.59 Moz Ag, Inferred 121 koz Au (effective 1 Apr 2024); roughly 120–130 koz Au has been mined since, so the undepleted M&I is nearer 360 koz. 2024 PEA life five years to ~2028; the Q1 2027 MRE/PEA is meant to extend it. Mont Sorcier: 2022 PEA on a magnetite resource, 21-year life, 17,890 m infill drilled in 2025. Lagoa Salgada: 2023 FS (Ascendant) on a VMS deposit, numbers not re-verified here.MDN (100%): M&I 13.44 Mt @ 1.13 g/t Au for 490 koz Au and 6.59 Moz Ag; Inferred 3.60 Mt @ 1.05 g/t for 121 koz Au (effective 1 Apr 2024; M&I grew more than tenfold from 2021). Four mining areas: Calandrias Norte/Sur (heap leach, ~0.86–0.89 g/t feed, 33–35% recovery), Martinetas stockpiles, and underground high-grade feed to the 1,100 tpd CIL plant (Q3 head grade 2.29 g/t, 90% recovery). Falcon and Calandrias II properties acquired 2026, drilling to year-end; owner-operated rigs on a large Deseado Massif land package. Tailings dam has ~5 years of capacity.
DividendNone paid.
Valuation Anchor

Valued like a short-life mine: EV ~US$280M against ~US$130M of annualised EBITDA at US$4,000 gold, i.e. ~2–2.5× — the market is paying for about two years of cash flow and nothing for Lagoa Salgada (legal limbo) or Mont Sorcier (iron, US$574M capex). Peers with 10-year reserve lives trade at 5–8× EBITDA. The re-rate requires the Q1 2027 PEA to show a life long enough that a multiple applies; the de-rate requires only that costs stay at Q2 levels or gold falls.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~6.8% (Simply Wall St, Oct 2026): CEO/Chairman Mark Brennan 4.97M shares / 3.5% (~C$11M; bought 12,500 shares at up to C$1.98 on 28 Jan 2026 — the only insider trade found, no sales listed); director Kurt Menchen 2.19M / 1.5%; COO Casper Groenewald 1.02M; director Robert Campbell 0.92M; CFO Jason Brooks 0.29M. Eric Sprott (strategic) ~7.0M shares / ~4.9% from the Jul 2026 stream buy-back (3.0M) and the Sep 2026 placement (4.0M) plus 2.0M warrants at C$3.35; exact total not disclosed. Institutions tiny: CQS (UK) 1.4%, Orrell Capital 0.2%, BlackRock 0.015%; ~1.7% in total. Retail ~90%.

Read: A retail-held TSXV stock with one meaningful insider (Brennan 3.5%, a small 2026 buy) and Sprott as a new anchor; almost no institutions, so the Q1 2027 PEA has no sell-side audience to lift it unless Sprott or a fund follows.

Jurisdiction risk

National (Argentina): improving but still restrictive. Gold has paid no export duty since the 8% retention lapsed in Dec 2023; Aug 2025 decree set mining export duties to 0% on 231 tariff lines (silver and lithium still 4.5%). RIGI (large-investment incentive regime) exists but MDN is too small and already built to use it. FX controls remain: doré export proceeds must be converted to pesos and Central Bank consent is needed for dividends out of Argentina (Q1/Q2 2026 MD&A); the economy is treated as hyperinflationary and local costs in pesos have inflated faster than the peso has devalued. Current tax liability US$12.8M. Local: Santa Cruz is a mining province (Cerro Negro, Cerro Vanguardia, Cerro Moro); MDN's Argentine CEO chairs the provincial mining chamber; water shortages hit heap-leach irrigation in late 2025. Portugal: the Environment Agency gave an unfavourable EIA opinion on Lagoa Salgada (23 Jan 2026); a court injunction (Feb/Jun 2026, final Jul 2026) suspends it while the main case runs — the concession is at risk if the EIA fails. Québec: low risk; Mont Sorcier ESIA Q2 2027, permits ~end-2028.

One producing asset in a country where you cannot freely move the cash out; the two 'safer' jurisdictions hold the two assets that are not producing.

Differentiator

A real, unhedged 60 koz/yr gold mine at a 54% AISC margin for ~2× EBITDA — cheap because the defined life is short, not because the mine is bad. The hedge book ended Jan 2026, so every dollar of gold flows through; the Sprott stream is gone (bought back Jul 2026), so the mine is unencumbered except for a US$29M loan. And two option tickets the market values at zero: Mont Sorcier (NPV8 US$1.6B on a 2022 deck, a BFS in H1 2027) and 80% of Lagoa Salgada (NPV8 US$147M, permit in court).

Cheapness that depends on a resource update is a bet on geology at a mine whose heap-leach recovery just fell to 33%.

Exploration upside

Life-extension drilling at an operating mine · moves the needle: high The entire re-rate case is exploration: Falcon and Calandrias II (acquired 2026) are being drilled to year-end 2026 with owner-operated rigs, plus a new underground rig (Jul 2026) chasing high-grade CIL feed; results feed the Q1 2027 MRE and PEA, which also sizes the new 12 Mt leach pad. Mont Sorcier drilled 17,890 m infill in 2025 and a further programme in late Q3 2026 to convert Inferred tonnes east of the pit.

Next Catalyst

Q3 2026 financials before 23 Nov 2026 — the Q3 AISC (after US$1,933 in Q2), the cash balance after the 6 Oct US$8M Sprott payment, and any 2026 cost comment. Then drill results in Q4, the US$12M Sprott note on 4 Jan 2027, and the MRE + PEA in late Q1 2027.

Open Questions
  • Was the US$8M Sprott note paid on 6 Oct 2026, and from what cash? The Q3 financials will show it.
  • Why did AISC jump from US$1,348 (Q1) to US$1,933 (Q2) and how much of it is heap-leach recovery falling to 33%?
  • How many ounces does the Q1 2027 MRE add, and does the PEA show a life beyond 2028 at 60 koz/yr?
  • What is Mont Sorcier to Cerrado — a core build (impossible alone at US$574M+), a partner deal, or a sale? The company has not said.
  • Does Lagoa Salgada's main court case restore the EIA, or does the concession lapse — and what is the 80% stake carried at?
  • Key management compensation of US$5.25M in H1 2026 (MD&A) against a US$226M market cap — how much is cash?

Management review
Creal weaknesses: slipped dates, thin fit or thin candourTrack record 3/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 2/5 · Skin in the game 3/5

A financier-founder with one clear win (Desert Sun) and several builds that diluted or stalled; at Cerrado the mine was turned round, but three of three development dates slipped or ended in a sale, the 2025 guidance was raised then missed without saying so, and the 'strong cash flow' message sits beside negative FCF, going-concern language and an equity raise. Candour 2 makes the grade; the operating team is competent.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Mark Brennan (CEO & Chairman, founding partner, since 2020 (Cerrado founded 2020; CEO ~4.3 yrs per Simply Wall St)): Serial founder: Desert Sun Mining (Jacobina, Brazil), Largo Resources (Maracás vanadium, Brazil; president & CEO), Sierra Metals (president & CEO from Apr 2015), Ascendant Resources (executive chairman from Apr 2017; merged into Cerrado May 2025), Voyager Metals (founder; merged into Cerrado), James Bay Resources, Brasoil, Morumbi Oil & Gas, Admiral Bay. Also directs multiple related entities. · Cliff Hale-Sanders (President, founding partner, since 2020): Ex-sell-side base-metals analyst (RBC, TD, CIBC, Cormark); Ascendant founder; CEO of Voyager Metals (Mont Sorcier). · Jason Brooks (CFO, since ~2022 (3.9 yrs)): Ex-VP Finance Caldas Gold; Golden Star, New Gold, Barrick. · Casper Groenewald (COO, since ~2022 (3.8 yrs)): Metallurgist; led commissioning of Largo's Maracás plant; ex-DRA, Minopex. · Andrew Croal (Chief Technical Officer, since 2025/26 (<1 yr)): Mine builder: Rosebel, Detour, Buzwagi. · Veronica Nohara (CEO Minera Don Nicolás, since n/a (ran MDN before Cerrado bought it)): President of the Santa Cruz mining chamber. · Ed Guimaraes (Executive Vice President, since n/a): CFO of Sierra Metals 2014–2023; Aur Resources CFO to its US$4.1B sale to Teck (2007).
Track record
  • Desert Sun Mining (Brennan founder): built Jacobina in Brazil, sold to Yamana in 2006 — a shareholder win (company bio; sale terms not re-verified here).
  • Largo Resources (Brennan president & CEO): financed and built the Maracás Menchen vanadium mine (production 2014); Kurt Menchen (now a Cerrado director) ran Brazil operations. Largo later needed a debt restructuring and heavy dilution in 2015–16 — the build worked, early shareholders were diluted (unverified detail).
  • Sierra Metals: Brennan appointed president & CEO Apr 2015 (https://www.miningweekly.com/article/sierra-metals-appoints-brennan-president-ceo-2015-04-14); tenure ended before 2020 (dates unverified).
  • Ascendant Resources (Brennan executive chairman from Apr 2017, https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2017/04/11/1035874/0/en/Ascendant-Resources-Appoints-Mark-Brennan-as-Executive-Chairman.html): bought El Mochito (Honduras) 2016, sold it in 2020; earned 80% of Lagoa Salgada with a 2023 FS (NPV8 US$147M); permit stalled; merged into Cerrado May 2025 — Ascendant shareholders did not get a win.
  • Cerrado: bought MDN in 2020 and rebuilt it around heap leaching (M&I up >10× to 490 koz by Apr 2024); the stock fell to C$0.14 (Aug 2024) before the gold price and the Monte do Carmo sale (US$60M) took it to C$2+source
  • FY2025 production 50,238 GEO vs guidance raised to 55,000–60,000 in April 2025 (https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/cerrado-gold-increases-2025-production-guidance-amid-operational-expansion; https://www.miningstockeducation.com/2026/04/cerrado-gold-announces-q4-and-annual-2025-financial-results/).
  • Repurchased the Sprott streams Jul 2026 and ended the hedge book Jan 2026 — both shareholder-friendly in a rising gold marketsource

Boards today: Brennan: CEO & Chairman of Cerrado; historically chaired/led Ascendant and Voyager (both now inside Cerrado). Other current public boards not verified. Board of 8 incl. Brennan, Menchen (ex-Largo), Sellars (Red Cloud CFO), Jones, Anzola (ex-Cerrado general counsel, now 'independent'), Campbell, Salomao ×2, Santos.

Fit to this job
Fit is good for what MDN is: the COO commissioned Largo's plant, the CTO has built three gold mines, the Argentine CEO ran MDN before Cerrado. The stretch is the portfolio — one small gold mine plus an iron project needing US$574M+ and a VMS project in a permit fight — run by a financier-founder whose pattern is to assemble, promote and sell rather than operate for a decade.
Skin & pay
3/5 — a ~3.5% founder stake, one token open-market buy, no selling; pay high against the market cap. Brennan holds ~4.97M shares / ~3.5% (~C$11M) — meaningful for a founder, mostly founder stock and grants; one small open-market buy (12,500 shares at up to C$1.98, 28 Jan 2026, ~C$24.8k); no sales found. Insiders in total ~6.8%. Pay: 2023 total US$316k (Simply Wall St, stale); H1 2026 key-management compensation US$5.25M in aggregate (MD&A). 8.37M RSUs + 4.38M options outstanding. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsxv-cert/cerrado-gold-shares/ownership

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Pattern of dated project promises re-dated or ended in a sale: Monte do Carmo (2023 construction → 2025 start-up → sold), Lagoa Salgada OFS/construction decision (slipped twice), Mont Sorcier FS (Q1/Q2 2026 → H1 2027).
  • 2025 production guidance raised mid-year and then missed by ~9% against the low end, with no plain acknowledgement.
  • Key management compensation US$5.25M for H1 2026 (MD&A) at a ~US$226M company — ~4–5% of market cap annualised — while FCF was negative and equity was sold at C$2.50 (cash vs share-based split not verified).
  • Going-concern language and a US$39M working-capital deficit in a company describing 'strong cash flows'.
  • Related-party history: Brennan and Hale-Sanders founded Ascendant and Voyager and then merged both into Cerrado; a former general counsel sits as an 'independent' director.

What the numbers say
  1. Higher gold prices turned Minera Don Nicolas (MDN, Argentina) from break-even into a cash machine: revenue US$100M (FY23) → US$116M (FY24) → US$147M (FY25) → US$118M in H1 2026 alone; operating cash flow US$56M in FY25 and US$29M in H1 2026, gross margin (after depreciation) 40% in H1 2026 vs 9% in FY24. Realised gold US$4,184/oz vs AISC US$1,933/oz in Q2 2026.
  2. The company nevertheless reported a FY25 net loss of US$20M: Argentine income and mining tax (US$23M incl. deferred), fair-value losses on the Sprott streams and note (US$15M) and finance costs swallowed the operating profit. H1 2026 net income was US$22M.
  3. Cash is thin for the size of the business: US$0.4M (Dec 2023) → US$26M (Dec 2024, after the US$60M Monte do Carmo sale to Hochschild) → US$5.7M (Jun 2025) → US$25.3M (Jun 2026). Working capital has been negative every period (US$-39M at Jun 2026) and every set of statements since 2023 carries a going-concern warning. Debt-like obligations (loans, prepay facility, debentures, put liability, Sprott streams and note; leases excluded) were US$93M at Jun 2026, up from US$57M at Dec 2024 after the Ascendant acquisition.
  4. Money went into growth rather than the balance sheet: capex US$20M (FY25) and US$25M (H1 2026, mostly non-sustaining: tailings/leach-pad expansion, underground development, fleet) plus E&E US$15M (FY25) and US$11M (H1 2026). Monte do Carmo is no longer a Cerrado project (sold Nov 2024); the development asset is now the 80%-owned Lagoa Salgada zinc-lead-copper project in Portugal, acquired with Ascendant Resources in May 2025 for 27.7M shares, where permitting is in dispute and the optimised feasibility study has slipped.
  5. Shares 98M (Dec 2023) → 104M (Dec 2024) → 136M (Dec 2025, Ascendant) → 139M (Aug 2026, +3M to Sprott) → ~143M after the Sept 2026 C$10M Eric Sprott placement; a small buyback (1.0M shares) ran in 2026. No dividends. After the quarter the company bought back both Sprott streams and the 10% note for US$31.3M (US$8M cash, 3M shares, US$8M note due 6 Oct 2026, US$12M note due 4 Jan 2027), removing ~US$50M of liabilities at the cost of near-term cash calls.

Thesis

The most permit-complete undeveloped gold project in eastern Canada, with cash in the bank and a construction decision weeks away. NexGold (ex-Treasury Metals) bought Signal Gold in Dec 2024 to pair Goliath (Ontario, EA-approved) with Goldboro (Nova Scotia).

Goldboro then collected every major permit in 2025: Crown Land lease (May), ECCC Schedule 2 (Jul), Industrial Approval (Aug), DFO Fisheries Act authorisations (Oct), on top of the Aug 2022 EA — plus a benefits agreement with the Assembly of Nova Scotia Mi'kmaw Chiefs (Dec 2024) now in implementation. Early-works construction began Sep 17, 2026; the updated FS and a board construction decision are both guided to Q4 2026; 26-month build from a Q1 2027 full start → first gold ~Q2 2029; ~100 koz/yr for 11 years.

Goliath's FS was deliberately paused (Jan 2026) to re-optimise while Goldlund gets 25,000 m of infill — sequenced, not abandoned; sell-side models Goliath lifting group output above 200 koz/yr by ~2032. CEO Kevin Bullock; build lead VP Projects Brian Jackson (ex-Ausenco) — the former COO Jeremy Wyeth left in Aug 2025. Sell-side: NBF Buy C$5.50, Red Cloud Buy C$4.30.

The Gate

The Q4 2026 double reveal: updated capex and the financing package to fund it. Every NPV quoted for Goldboro is built on 2021 costs and US$1,600 gold; the updated FS will almost certainly show a much higher NPV and a much higher capex (industry re-baselining since 2022 has run +30–60%). If capex lands near C$400M+, the C$101M treasury covers only a quarter of it, and the plan leans on the non-binding US$175M Appian credit LOI plus whatever equity or stream fills the gap — on a company that has already sold a 2.9% NSR to Appian (US$24M) until 1.25 Moz.

  1. Goliath is on hold — the "two-mine, 200 koz" story is now one mine plus a study-in-waiting.
  2. Nova Scotia execution — first hard-rock gold mine built in the province in decades, 350-person construction camp, contractor and labour market untested at this scale.
  3. Sprott Streaming obligations on Goliath (share issuances under the amended 2022 agreement) sit on top.

Watch whether the construction decision is unconditional or "subject to financing."

The ~100M warrants are the quiet dilution.

Jurisdiction risk

National / provincial: done. Federal (ECCC Schedule 2, DFO), provincial (EA 2022, Industrial Approval, Crown Land lease, mining lease) and Indigenous (ANSMC Mutual Benefits Agreement, implementation committee meeting through 2026) — the gate that dominates most developers is simply not here.

Local: low. Rural Guysborough County, an historic gold district; Nova Scotia has an anti-mining current (the 2024–25 uranium and fracking debates), but Goldboro is through it and the province granted the lease. Goliath: Ontario EA approved; First Nations engagement ongoing.

Permits done is why the easy re-rate has already happened (+155% in 2025).

Differentiator
  1. Permits done + cash on hand — the one combination almost no gold developer has.
  2. 2.26 g/t open-pit reserve grade — roughly double the typical Canadian open-pit developer, which is what makes a ~C$271M-class build plausible at all.
  3. C$101M, no debt, and an Appian relationship that has already put money in.
  4. A second permitted platform (Goliath, EA-approved) that a producer could bolt on — this is what a mid-tier acquirer buys.

Read it honestly: "permitted and funded to a decision" is also why the remaining upside is the capex-vs-price arithmetic in the updated FS, and that cuts both ways.

Exploration upside

Conversion, not discovery · moves the needle: low–medium. Goldboro RC infill: 61.22 g/t over 12 m in the early-mining area (Aug 2026); Goldlund 2026 infill: 15.21 g/t over 20.1 m, 5.11 g/t over 21.8 m, 9.30 g/t over 11 m. These matter for the updated MRE grade and the starter-pit sequence, not for size. Airborne EM and gravity surveys over 32,000 ha at Goldboro (interpretation ongoing) are the only genuine step-out lever.

At 4.7 Moz M&I the file needs economics more than ounces.

What has to go right

The Q4 2026 double reveal: an updated feasibility study with a capex the company can fund, and a financing package to fund it. Every NPV quoted for Goldboro rests on 2021 costs and US$1,600 gold; the new study will show a much higher NPV and a much higher capex. If capex lands near C$400M or more, the C$101M treasury covers a quarter of it and the rest leans on the non-binding US$175M Appian credit letter plus equity or a stream.

Why the stock is priced where it is

A permitted Canadian gold build with two projects (Goldboro, Goliath), a full treasury and a construction decision pending, priced for the dilution the market expects the financing to bring. The upside is a construction story at US$4,000 gold; the risk is the gap between the study's capex and the money on hand.

What the plan does about it

Buys nothing on hope. The first entry needs the study to clear capex, NPV and funding-plan thresholds and the stock to fall anyway, which is how a re-baselined capex usually trades. The real entry is the financing announcement itself, 4–12 weeks after the study, when the price of the dilution is known. No financing by end-March 2027 is its own signal.

Sizing: every amount is a share of the position you decide to hold in this company, whatever that is (100% = the full position). At €4 an order the fee is small; keep each tranche at €200 or more (fee ≤ 2%), and if a tranche would come out smaller, merge it with the next one. Three or four green → project intact; any dip afterwards is a discount. Two or more red → the project got worse, not cheaper. Stop. Do not buy the dip. Re-run the card first.

Step 2first tranche: 40%
  1. Mostly green and the stock falls ≥ 12% on FS day or within the following week → buy 40% in the market. The discount is driven by the size of the cheque, not by the project.
  2. Mostly green and the stock rises → buy 40% anyway within a week. The dip is not coming; an unconditional decision is worth more than the 15% saved. Don't chase beyond +20%.
  3. Red → nothing.
Step 3second tranche: 60% — on the financing announcement (4–12 weeks after the FS, most likely Q1 2027)

This is the real entry. Buy in the market on the day the bought deal is announced or the next morning, at or near the deal price — the institutions' price without the four-month hold. Read the deal first:

  1. Go (60%): equity ≤ C$120M, a stream ≤ US$100M, the Appian debt binding — total dilution under ~40%. A strategic (a producer) taking a stake at a premium is the best possible signal: buy that day regardless of price.
  2. Caution (30%): equity C$120–200M with no stream and no strategic — dilution 50–75%. Probably still fine, the project is funded, but the re-rate is slower.
  3. No-go (keep the 60%): a bridge or a small raise "to advance detailed engineering" without a full package — they couldn't get the money.
Step 4no financing announced by end-March 2027

They are waiting for the stock to recover so the C$1.92 (average) warrants fund it. Buy the 60% anyway in two 30% pieces, April and June. The overhang is a grind, not a cliff; waiting longer only costs the re-rate.

Step 5once in: sell-or-hold triggers
  1. Sell if the construction decision is withdrawn or the project is put "under review".
  2. Sell half if the stock doubles before first gold (~Q2 2029) — construction stocks re-rate fastest between financing and commissioning; a double on a pre-production developer is worth banking half of.
  3. Otherwise hold to first gold. The thesis is a permitted mine reaching production; don't trade the quarters in between.
PracticalWhere to buy, and the most likely outcome

Main liquidity is TSXV: NEXG; OTCQX: NXGCF; Frankfurt: TRC1 is thin — use TSXV access if the broker offers it and accept the CAD conversion. Most likely single outcome: the FS is fine (capex ~C$400M, decision conditional) and the stock drifts 10–15% lower over two months without a dramatic dip. The plan still works; the average entry is ~C$1.25 rather than C$1.05, and the money was never in the timing — it is in whether the mine gets built.

Plan log: 25 Sep 2026 — plan written at ~C$1.40; Step 0, nothing bought. 26 Sep — marked as pick in tracker and rankings. 1 Oct — Sep 17 release: early-works construction started at Goldboro ahead of the FS; Sep 23: strong Goldlund infill (14.07 g/t / 7 m). Still Step 0 — the FS thresholds are the trigger, and spending before the decision suggests management expects to pass them.

Next Catalyst

Updated Goldboro FS + construction decision (Q4 2026) — the nearest firm catalyst in this file; binding project financing (Appian or other); Goldboro updated MRE; remaining Goldlund infill results and a re-scoped Goliath plan; long-lead procurement awards; first gold ~Q2 2029.

Fit to this job

The build-relevant experience sits with VP Projects Jackson (Ausenco project execution) and chair Gowans (large-company operator). Jurisdiction fit is good (Nova Scotia team carried over from Signal Gold; Mi'kmaq partnership for early works). A high-grade Colombian underground mine that has been "about to" reach commercial production for a year, freshly de-levered by doubling its share count, with the cash from its latest raise sent to a copper explorer

Gate Turning 43 tpd of hand-mined ore into an 834 tpd mechanised mine — on time, on grade, in Titiribí. The PEA's 558% IRR is an artefact of counting only the US$11M of capex not yet spent; what it really says is that the entire value sits in execution: a new portal and 600 m ramp (funded by June's Trafigura upsizing), a plant that has slipped from Q3 to Q4 2026 and now to “by Q1 2027”, and a resource that is 79% Inferred and has never been mined at scale. Sub-gates: (1) security — Suroeste Antioquia had a record 320 homicides in 2025; Titiribí itself had six in Q1 2026 after a February massacre (one in all of 2025), and El Colombiano flags new mining projects as extortion targets; (2) capital allocation — the last C$28.8M of equity was redeployed into a copper explorer rather than Zancudo, while Zancudo's own development is funded by an offtaker's prepayment; (3) costs — cash cost US$2,513/oz in the artisanal phase against a PEA LOM US$2,448 that assumes mechanised mining; silver payability 20–45% on raw ore; (4) a slipping Spanish leg — Aguablanca has moved three times, its US$20M note raised US$7.5M, Lomero's PEA never came.

Not funded for Aguablanca's restart (RNR raised US$7.5M of a US$20M note; US$25M facility pending) or for further ramp capital if grades disappoint — and the last C$28.8M of equity went to Copper Giant, not Zancudo.
Thesis

Zancudo, in Titiribí (Antioquia), is a historic high-grade gold-silver district (worked since the 1700s) that Denarius — an Iacono / ex-Gran Colombia Gold vehicle — is bringing back as a 1,000 tpd underground flotation operation. Early production since Q2 2025 by hand-mining accessible workings and shipping raw ore to Trafigura: H1 2026 6,244 t at 11.4 g/t Au / 237 g/t Ag for 1,563 oz Au + 17.5 koz Ag payable, revenue US$8.4M, gross margin ~40%. The PEA (Mar 2026) shows after-tax NPV5% US$324M, 11-year life at 834 tpd, 465 koz Au + 2.2 Moz Ag payable, AISC US$2,482/oz — on only US$11M of remaining capex because the plant is already under construction; first concentrate is now guided Q4 2026.

On Jul 31, 2026 the company retired C$34.2M of 12% gold-linked convertible debentures (Iacono and Aris Mining were the large holders) by issuing 223.6M shares — share count 213M → 437M — eliminating a US$38.8M working-capital deficit and ~C$157M of future gold-premium obligations.

Three weeks later Trafigura bought 67M units at C$0.43 (C$28.8M; now 14.8%) and the proceeds went, in full, into a 15.3% stake in Copper Giant Resources (the copper file's Mocoa).

Spain: 21.8% of Aguablanca (Ni-Cu, restart slipped to mid-2027, non-recourse financing half-placed), 100% of Lomero (1.9% CuEq Indicated, PEA never delivered) and Toral (maiden 14.8 Mt Inferred Zn-Pb-Ag, Sep 2026). Cash US$18.9M at Jun 30; Trafigura prepay US$16M facility (US$7M undrawn).

The Gate

Turning 43 tpd of hand-mined ore into an 834 tpd mechanised mine — on time, on grade, in Titiribí. The PEA's 558% IRR is an artefact of counting only the US$11M of capex not yet spent; what it really says is that the entire value sits in execution: a new portal and 600 m ramp (funded by June's Trafigura upsizing), a plant that has slipped from Q3 to Q4 2026 and now to “by Q1 2027”, and a resource that is 79% Inferred and has never been mined at scale.

Sub-gates
  1. Security — Suroeste Antioquia had a record 320 homicides in 2025; Titiribí itself had six in Q1 2026 after a February massacre (one in all of 2025), and El Colombiano flags new mining projects as extortion targets.
  2. Capital allocation — the last C$28.8M of equity was redeployed into a copper explorer rather than Zancudo, while Zancudo's own development is funded by an offtaker's prepayment.
  3. Costs — cash cost US$2,513/oz in the artisanal phase against a PEA LOM US$2,448 that assumes mechanised mining; silver payability 20–45% on raw ore.
  4. A slipping Spanish leg — Aguablanca has moved three times, its US$20M note raised US$7.5M, Lomero's PEA never came.

The debenture conversion fixed the balance sheet; it did not fix the mine. Q4's first concentrate is the first hard data point on whether the PEA is a plan or a spreadsheet.
