Valuation Anchor

~0.7× PEA NAV on a 79%-Inferred resource, ~US$1,000/oz Indicated — priced as if the ramp is done. At 834 tpd and ~40 koz/yr the PEA's mid-life years earn ~US$60M of margin at US$4,000; 8–10× that is US$500–600M, which is the analyst target and the bull case.

The bear case: it never reaches 834 tpd, costs stay at US$2,500 in a security-compromised district, and the 573M fully-diluted shares make every further raise a heavier lift. The Spanish portfolio and the Copper Giant stake are real but currently consume attention and capital rather than provide it.

Bucket: grade / discovery / optionality — high grade, no reserves, execution-priced; it does not qualify for cheap defined ounces (Inferred-dominated) and does not yet qualify as a producer (US$8M of H1 revenue, negative operating cash flow).

Shareholder structure
Management & board
Serafino Iacono (Exec Chairman) ~16.0% (80.8M shares after the Trafigura placement; 18.5% at Jul 31) plus 2.44M options and 8.7M warrants. How he got there matters: ~27.6M shares were bought with cash over 2023–25 (market purchases at ~C$0.54, placements at C$0.50 in Mar and Nov 2025, warrant exercises) — then +53.2M shares on Jul 31, 2026 in settlement of C$8.5M of debentures he held (15.2M on conversion, ~37.9M as make-whole for future gold premiums at the NPV price of C$0.81). CEO Restrepo-Solano ~4.75M pro forma; CFO Davies ~0.7M; other directors not disclosed online (circular on SEDAR+ only). 13.7M options outstanding.
Insider activity (12 mo)
Iacono buying with cash, CFO selling. Iacono: 1.85M placement units @ C$0.50 (Nov 2025), 260k in the market @ ~C$0.79 (May 19, 2026), 219k @ ~C$0.60 (Jul 10, 2026, three weeks before the conversion) — consistent, small, and at the lows. CFO Davies exercised 249k options and sold 200k @ ~C$0.83 (Feb 2026, a third of his holding). The July 31 settlement dwarfs all of it.
Strategic & prominent
Trafigura 14.8% (74.6M + 19.2M warrants; 17.9% partially diluted) — offtaker, prepay lender and now the second-largest holder after the Aug 2026 C$28.8M placement at C$0.43; also holds 20% of the Copper Giant offtake. Aris Mining ~11.8% (59.6M; 13.6% at Jul 31) — the Iacono/Giustra-founded producer, holder since the Zancudo vend-in; bought 4M units @ C$0.50 (Nov 2025) and received 36.5M in the debenture settlement; "for investment purposes only." Ruffer LLP ~4.8% (24.0M) — the one notable outside institution, origin undisclosed. Aton Ventures ~2.6% (was 12.2% in Mar 2025, diluted). Frank Giustra is not a disclosed Denarius holder — his link is through Aris and as a co-investor in Copper Giant.
Institutions / retail
Iacono + Trafigura + Aris ≈ 42–43% in three aligned hands; Ruffer ~5%; the rest retail. No formal shareholder agreement disclosed. 504.1M shares; 67.4M warrants + 13.7M options → FD ~585M. AGM turnout 62% (Jun 2026).

Read: The highest insider ownership in the file, and the most ambiguous. Iacono has ~US$37M in the stock and has kept buying with cash at the lows — that is real alignment. But two-thirds of his position arrived on Jul 31 in a settlement he negotiated as a debenture holder, at an effective ~C$0.15, approved by a minority vote; and the three largest holders — chairman, offtaker-lender, affiliated miner — are one network controlling ~42%. High ownership here is as much control as conviction. Read it as: the insiders will not let it fail, and the insiders will decide who gets diluted when it needs money.

Jurisdiction risk

National: turned favourable, unproven. Abelardo de la Espriella won the Jun 21, 2026 runoff (49.7% vs 48.7%), inaugurated Aug 7; Mines minister María Nohemí Arboleda; stated agenda of faster permitting, formalising legal mining and reopening exploration, driven by a 6.4%-of-GDP deficit — the same reframing the copper file applied to Copper Giant. Zancudo's environmental licence (2024) and industrial permit (Oct 2025) are in hand.

Local: the live risk is security, not licence. Suroeste Antioquia: record 320 homicides in 2025, 81 in Q1 2026 (18.6% of the department), Clan del Golfo offshoots and Medellín groups contesting; Titiribí six homicides in Q1 2026 after a Feb 25 massacre. No community opposition or informal-miner conflict found — but a 1,000 tpd operation in a district worked by hand for 250 years is an extortion and invasion target by construction. Board includes a former Procuradora General (Margarita Cabello) — a political-risk hire.

Same national tailwind as Copper Giant; a worse local layer, and Denarius now owns 15% of Copper Giant, so the Colombia exposure is doubled.

Differentiator
  1. Grade, a built plant, and a trading house inside the tent. 6.9 g/t Indicated / 5.6 g/t Inferred with 11 g/t coming out of the hand-mined phase is top-decile for an underground gold developer, and the plant, licence and portal are funded and largely built — the PEA's US$11M residual is real in that narrow sense.
  2. Trafigura as offtaker, US$16M prepay lender and ~15% shareholder — an aligned counterparty that has doubled down twice in 2026.
  3. A clean balance sheet for the first time — no debentures, no gold-premium overhang, US$18.9M cash.
  4. Optionality in three other assets and a listed copper stake, all carried at little inside a US$225M EV.

Read it honestly: the differentiators — Trafigura's embrace and the Iacono/Aris network — are also the concentration and related-party risk: three affiliated holders own ~42%, the offtaker is the lender is the shareholder, and the debenture make-whole (146M shares at an NPV of future gold premiums) went largely to insiders. Same fact, two sides.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, in-mine · moves the needle: medium–high. The thesis needs Inferred → Indicated more than new ounces: 79% of the PEA's material is Inferred. The 2026 programme (15,100 m, 3,200 m brownfield) is producing high-grade intercepts (33 m @ 5.68 g/t; 1 m @ 41.8 g/t) at Las Brisas — good for the grade narrative, not yet a category upgrade. Toral (Sep 2026 maiden) and Lomero add tonnes in Spain that the market gives no credit for and won't until a study exists.

An updated Zancudo MRE with a meaningful Indicated share would do more for the stock than any hole.

Next Catalyst

First concentrate from the 1,000 tpd plant (by Q1 2027) — slipped twice (Q3 → Q4 2026 → by Q1 2027, 23 Oct); Q3 production (late Oct) and Q3 financials (~Nov 13); new portal / 600 m ramp progress; Aguablanca US$25M facility (guided end-Q3 — check) and the mid-2027 restart; an updated Zancudo MRE; Copper Giant's PEA (Q4 2026) as a mark on the C$28.8M stake; the Toral West option.

Open Questions
  • What does the plant actually run at in its first two quarters — and what grade, when mechanised stopes replace hand-picked ore at 11 g/t?
  • How much of the 832 koz Inferred converts, and what does the PEA look like on Indicated-only material?
  • Why send C$28.8M of fresh equity into Copper Giant while Zancudo's ramp is funded by an offtaker's prepay — strategy, or Iacono-network capital recycling?
  • What is the security plan for a mechanised operation in Titiribí after the Feb 2026 massacre, and who bears the cost?
  • Does Aguablanca ever restart on Denarius's balance sheet, or does the 21.8% get sold?
  • With 573M shares fully diluted, what is the next raise — and at what price?
Context & updates
24 Oct 2026 update

The 23 Oct release now says the Zancudo plant will start producing concentrates “by the first quarter of 2027”. The 9 Sep release still said Q4 2026, and before that Q3 2026, so this is the second slip of the same date. The new date sits in the boilerplate and is not called a delay, in line with the habit noted in the Management tab. One more quarter costs time and overhead, but the case for a 3× rests on the ramp to ~800 tpd by end-2027, which this does not yet break. Odds stay 11% and risk stays 4 for now. A repeated slip is one of the sell triggers, so it is flagged. Q3 production, due around 28 Oct, and the Q3 financials (~13 Nov) should show whether commissioning is moving.

6 Oct 2026 update

Listed as a developer although it already sells ore. Zancudo ore goes directly to Trafigura (US$8.4M revenue in H1 2026; Q2 ~43 t/day and ~970 oz payable gold), far below the 500–1,000 t/day plan. The value still rests on commissioning the plant (due Q3/Q4 2026 at the time; now by Q1 2027) and restarting Aguablanca (mid-2027), which are developer milestones — so it is tagged 'early ore sales' and stays on the developer list. Rule: it moves to the producer list once the plant runs near design capacity and covers its own operating costs for two quarters in a row; checked every Saturday.

3 Oct 2026 refresh

No release since 9 Sep. First concentrate from the 1,000 tpd plant is still guided Q4. The Aguablanca US$25M facility, guided for end-Q3, has not been announced (missed). The stock fell 15% to C$0.56 with no news, which lifts the per-share multiples ~18%.

Debenture retirement (Jul 31, 2026)

C$34.2M of 12% gold-linked convertibles (Series 1 C$19.9M @ C$0.45; Series 2 C$14.3M @ C$0.60) retired for 223.6M shares: 67.9M on conversion + 146.5M make-whole (NPV of future gold premiums, settled at C$0.81 VWAP) + fees. Iacono 18.5%, Aris Mining 13.6% post-deal. ISS/Glass Lewis supported; ~C$157M of future obligations avoided; working capital swings from −US$38.8M to +US$12.8M pro forma.

Trafigura placement + Copper Giant (Aug 21, 2026)

67M units at C$0.43 (C$28.81M) with C$0.60 warrants to 2029; Trafigura 14.8%. Same day: 40.0M Copper Giant shares at C$0.72 (C$28.8M) = 15.3%; CEO Restrepo-Solano joins CGNT advisory board. Prepay facility upsized to US$16M (Jun 18).

Q2 2026 (Aug 13)

3,907 t shipped (+67% q/q) at 11.3 g/t Au / 217 g/t Ag; 970 oz Au + 9.7 koz Ag payable; revenue US$4.9M; gross profit US$1.9M; cash cost US$2,513/oz; net income +US$8.3M on a US$15.5M non-cash debenture gain. Cash US$18.9M. Plant first concentrate re-guided to Q4.

Aside

No 2026 production or cost guidance issued. Revenue figures differ between the production release (US$5.1M) and the financials (US$4.9M). Chung's Denarius project holds ~25 filings incl. the PEA and Q1 2026 MD&A — check the going-concern language there; releases don't carry it.

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 4/5 · Candour 2/5 · Skin in the game 5/5

Iacono has built a Colombian underground producer before (Segovia) and owns 16% with real market buying: a team that has done this job. Held at B, not higher, because every Denarius date since 2024 slipped by a year or more and each slip was reported as a fresh target; on 23 Oct the plant date moved again (Q4 2026 → by Q1 2027) in boilerplate. Candour stays 2; a weak Q3 or a third slip would move the grade to C.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

Owns ~16% of Denarius. · Federico Restrepo-Solano (CEO & Director, since CEO 7 Jan 2025; director since Oct 2022): Age 58. Track record
  • Bolivar Gold (co-founder): sold to Gold Fields in 2006 — a 2003-07 cycle win; price not verified this sessionsource
  • Pacific Rubiales/Pacific Exploration & Production (co-chairman): Colombia's largest independent oil producer, restructured under creditor protection in 2016 wiping out equity — the big miss; not verified via fetch this sessionsource
  • Gran Colombia Gold (executive chairman): built Segovia into a profitable underground gold producer after a debt restructuring; became Aris Mining in 2022; Aris now holds 11.8% of Denariussource
  • Denarius Zancudo: Feb 2024 release said production in 2024 'remains on track', plant operational Dec 2024; mining actually started March 2025 and the plant is now guided for Q3/Q4 2026 — ~2 years late (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/199750/ ; https://denariusmetals.com/denarius-metals-announces-start-of-mining-operatio-10014/ ; https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/denarius-metals-announces-second-quarter-and-first-half-2026-production-results-its)
  • Aguablanca (Spain, 50%): restart 'within one year of dewatering' (Feb 2024), 'within next 12 months' (Mar 2025), now mid-2027 target; US$20M notes offering by Rio Narcea launched; US$25M facility unconfirmed as of Sept 2026source
  • Capital structure: C$34.2M convertible debentures (C$0.45 and C$0.60 conversion) plus 189M shares; C$16.7M from warrant exercises early 2026source

Boards today: Iacono: Denarius exec chair; Aris Mining role ended with the 2022 merger (unverified whether he holds other current public boards). CEO Restrepo-Solano: Denarius only verified. Board added two directors June 2026 (Blanco, Al-Ramah).

Fit to this job
Exact fit on paper: Colombian underground narrow-vein gold-silver at small scale with toll/offtake sales is what Gran Colombia did at Segovia, and Iacono's team ran that. Region and permitting (ANLA, Antioquia) known to them. What is NEW: Spain — a nickel-copper restart (Aguablanca) and a polymetallic VMS (Lomero) in a jurisdiction none of them has operated in, funded with JV minority stakes and notes. Execution at Zancudo has been slow despite the fit.
Skin & pay
5/5 — large stake bought with their own money, still buying. Iacono ~80.8M shares / 16.0% (MarketScreener) — includes options exercised for 15M shares (C$8.5M) July 2026 and an open-market buy of 260k shares (C$205k) May 2026; insiders net buyers C$8.7M over 12 months. CFO Davies exercised 249k options Feb 2026. CEO Restrepo-Solano comp US$698k (26% salary) at a ~C$280M market cap — about 0.3%, acceptable. Iacono's own pay not retrieved. Circular not fetched. (https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/DENARIUS-METALS-CORP-111483007/company/ ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/neoe-dmet/denarius-metals-shares/management)

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Pattern of missed timelines: Zancudo plant ~2 years late, Aguablanca restart ~2-3 years late, each slip disclosed as a new target rather than a miss.
  • Three-way founder/affiliate ownership (Iacono 16%, Farringford Foundation 15%, Aris 12%) — related-party dynamics; Aris offtake/toll history.
  • Layered convertibles and notes; equity financed partly by warrant exercises rather than fundamentals.
  • Iacono's history includes the Pacific Rubiales equity wipe-out (unverified this session) alongside real wins.

Next catalyst
~114 holes / ~22,000 m of pending assays through Q4 2026 → column-leach results + maiden MRE Q1 2027 → PEA Q2 2027
Funded to the next catalyst Funded through the MRE, the PEA and most of the 2027 drill season without a raise. A feasibility study (guided 2028–29) and permitting will need another C$50M+ from 2028; the company has raised at rising prices each time (C$0.50 → C$0.95 → C$2.15) and the next raise will likely follow the PEA.
Thesis

Flat is a district-scale, intrusion-hosted bulk-tonnage gold system 40 km north of Donlin, with 206 of 206 holes at Chicken Mountain hitting gold over 3.3 km of strike and free-milling, heap-leachable metallurgy (83–96% column recoveries, preliminary). The team sold Kaminak's Coffee project to Goldcorp for C$520M in 2016 and has raised ~C$113M since Aug 2025, so the company is fully funded through a maiden resource (Q1 2027) and a PEA (Q2 2027) with no raise needed. The bet is that the 2026 40,000 m campaign delivers a multi-million-ounce, open-pit heap-leach resource at a grade the market will pay for, with Black Creek as a second centre.

The Gate

The maiden resource must be large AND above ~0.7 g/t — or the market has already paid for it At C$230M with no ounces, the stock is pricing roughly 2–3 Moz already. Much of the Chicken Mountain tonnage is 0.3–0.6 g/t (e.g. 118 m @ 0.51 g/t, 38 m @ 0.56 g/t in the Sep 2026 batch); the high-grade corridors (36.6 m @ 9.94 g/t, 59 m @ 2.41 g/t) must carry the average. The Q1 2027 MRE and the column-leach results that come with it are the gate: a 3 Moz+ resource at ~0.8 g/t with 80%+ heap-leach recovery re-rates it; a 1.5–2 Moz resource at 0.5 g/t does not. Sub-gate: remote fly-in/barge logistics and a multi-year Alaska federal permit path (Donlin needed a decade) cap what any PEA can show.

DepositNo resource. Chicken Mountain: 3.3 km strike × up to 700 m × 300 m+ depth, 206/206 holes hit gold; maiden MRE Q1 2027.No NI 43-101 resource. Chicken Mountain/Alpha Bowl/Adit: 206 holes to date: 2021–24 programmes (metres not totalled here) + 18,373 m / 125 holes in 2025 + >29,000 m at Chicken Mountain in 2026 — well over 47,000 m in the last two seasons alone, every hole hit gold, >60% ended in mineralization; footprint 3.3 km × up to 700 m × 300 m+ vertical, open in all directions; mapped intrusion 6.5 × 5.6 km with only ~2.3 km² drilled. Best holes: CMR25-084 9.94 g/t over 36.58 m incl. 104.23 g/t over 3.05 m; CMR26-170 (Alpha Bowl) 1.86 g/t over 80.77 m from surface incl. 2.41 g/t over 59.44 m and 11.82 g/t over 10.67 m; Adit 4.05 g/t over 30.48 m; CMR26-163 1.52 g/t over 42.67 m. Bulk-tonnage reality check: CMD26-036 118 m @ 0.51 g/t, CMR26-142 38 m @ 0.56 g/t. Black Creek, 6 km NE: CMR25-059 4.50 g/t over 48.77 m from surface; CMR26-152 5.09 g/t over 21.34 m; CMR26-153 1.89 g/t over 57.91 m. Land: 99,840 acres (92,160 leased from Doyon on a 15-year renewable lease, 7,680 acres state claims), six km-scale intrusions over ~20 km, five with gold; ~1.4 Moz of historical placer gold came out of the drainages. Metallurgy: preliminary ¾-inch column tests 83–96% recovery, low cyanide, no preg-robbing; 2-inch crush columns pending.
NPV : capexn/a — no study. Relevant screen today is EV per future ounce: EV ~US$100–120M means the market is paying ~US$35–60/oz for an assumed 2–3 Moz that does not yet exist.
Valuation Anchor

US$161M cap / ~US$105–120M EV for a pre-resource explorer: rich against Abitibi and Nevada explorers (US$20–60M typical) and already at the level of a 2 Moz Inferred resource at US$50–60/oz. The comparables the company itself shows (Banyan AurMac 7.8 Moz at C$583M, Liberty Gold Black Pine 4.8 Moz at C$740M, Snowline at C$3B) are the ceiling: Tectonic needs 3–5 Moz and a credible PEA to earn a 2–3× from here, and a Snowline-style outcome needs grade it has not yet shown over bulk widths. Cash of C$83M (36% of cap) is the floor.

Shareholder structure

Crescat Capital ~16.5% (post-Mar 2026 raise, company release; Crescat's own site says 21.8% partially diluted) — bought in every raise since 2022 under a pre-emptive right. Doyon Ltd (Alaska Native regional corporation, landowner) 'second-largest shareholder', C$10M+ invested since 2020; was 22.3% in 2022 and 9.9% in Sep 2024, now diluted to an unverified single-digit % after two warrant-free raises. Institutions ~55% per the Oct 2026 deck: Franklin Templeton ~7.5%, ASA Gold & Precious Metals ~6.1%, VanEck ~3.5%, Konwave ~1.8% (Simply Wall St, Oct 2026). Insiders ~1.2%: Eira Thomas 756k sh (0.55%), Tony Reda 506k (0.37%), other directors <0.1% each. Insider trades found: all buys in the Mar 2026 placement at C$2.15 — Thomas 232,500 sh (C$500k), Reda 24,000 (C$52k), J. Armstrong 15,000, Roper 5,000. No open-market buys or sells found.

Read: Crescat and a Native landowner anchor the register and real institutions came in at C$2.15; management's own stake is tiny (~1%) for a founder team and mostly bought in placements, not the market.

Jurisdiction risk

National: USA/Alaska — top-tier rule of law, pro-mining state, Fort Knox and Pogo as analogues; but federal permitting (NEPA/EIS, Army Corps 404) is slow — Donlin, 40 km south, spent ~2012–2018 on its EIS and is still not built. A maiden MRE makes Flat eligible for FAST-41 (company says). Local: the project sits on Doyon Ltd land under a lease Doyon negotiated and Doyon is a shareholder — the strongest possible community position in Alaska; Native village corporations and subsistence users along the Kuskokwim have contested Donlin, so the regional context is not friction-free. Logistics: no road — 4,100 ft gravel airstrip, barge on the Kuskokwim ~6 months a year; a proposed natural-gas pipeline for Donlin would pass nearby (not built).

Landowner-as-shareholder is a real edge; remoteness and a Donlin-length federal permit path are the real costs.

Differentiator

Every one of 206 holes has hit gold across a 3.3 km intrusion, and the landowner is a shareholder. A C$83M treasury (36% of market cap) means the MRE and PEA get delivered without a raise, which is rare for an explorer; the Kaminak team (C$520M exit) has done the discovery-to-sale path once before in a similar jurisdiction.

Scale and funding are proven; grade over bulk widths and the heap-leach case are not.

Exploration upside

District-scale, six intrusions, <7% of the main intrusion drilled · moves the needle: high Chicken Mountain is open in all directions and only ~2.3 km² of a 36 km² intrusion is drilled; Alpha Bowl (820 × 600 m) is the starter-pit candidate and Black Creek, 6 km away, is a second high-grade centre (5.09 g/t over 21 m, 4.50 g/t over 49 m). ~114 holes / ~22,000 m of assays plus regional soils are pending into Q4 2026, so the news flow is dense but the stock has fallen through two assay batches, suggesting the market now wants ounces, not more intercepts.

Next Catalyst

Pending assays from ~114 holes (~22,000 m) through Q4 2026, then column-leach results and the maiden Chicken Mountain MRE in Q1 2027, followed by a PEA in Q2 2027.

Open Questions
  • What average grade and strip ratio does the pit-constrained envelope carry once the 0.3–0.6 g/t bulk material is modelled against the high-grade corridors?
  • Do the 2-inch crush column tests hold 80%+ recovery on fresh (non-oxidized) rock, and what is the oxide/sulphide split in the first resource?
  • What is Doyon's current stake and did it participate in the C$92M raise (not disclosed)?
  • What is the realistic permitting timeline and capex for a fly-in/barge heap-leach in the Kuskokwim, given Donlin's history?

2/5 — small founder stakes (~1% combined), placement buys only, large option grants; not net sellers. Thomas ~756k sh (0.55%), Reda ~506k (0.37%), other directors <0.1% each; ~1.2% in total (Simply Wall St, Oct 2026). Only trades found are placement buys at C$2.15 on 3 Mar 2026 (Thomas C$500k, Reda C$52k, J. Armstrong C$32k, Roper C$11k); no open-market buys or sells found on SEDI summaries. CEO pay ~C$520k (50% salary / 50% bonus-equity) vs C$230M cap — modest in ratio, but the stake is small. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsxv-tect/tectonic-metals-shares/ownership ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsxv-tect/tectonic-metals-shares/management

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Insiders own ~1.2% of a company they founded nine years ago; the CEO holds 0.37% (~C$0.85M) on C$520k total pay. Grants are large: 2.146M options at C$2.10 (Jul 2026) plus 560k at C$2.05 (Oct 2026), DSUs and RSUs.
  • Chair's last executive job (Lucara) ended in a cost overrun and going-concern warning.
  • Promotional release style ('big gold systems leave big footprints', belt-wide ounce counts) with CEO-signed headlines on the best metre; investors should read the tables.
  • Seven years of Doyon-land exploration before the Flat discovery, with heavy dilution (419.9M shares pre-consolidation) — the current share count is clean only because of the 10:1 consolidation.
  • Advance-notice policy drew 21% opposition at the Sep 2026 AGM — minor, but a sign some holders are watchful.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash was C$83.2M at 30 June 2026 (no later company figure) after the C$92.0M gross / ~C$87.1M net March 2026 placement at C$2.15 (Crescat C$14.5M, no warrants); Q2 2026 cash burn was C$11.8M (C$13.5M operating outflow, partly offset by a C$2.1M FX gain on USD cash), but a further C$4.4M of drilling costs were accrued and unpaid at quarter end, so the underlying Q2 spend rate was ~C$16M. With five rigs running to late October, year-end 2026 cash is likely around C$50–55M — roughly four to five quarters of 2026-style spending, enough to fund the Q1 2027 maiden MRE, the Q2 2027 PEA and a 2027 drill season without a raise before late 2027.
  2. Money goes into the ground: exploration expensed rose from C$2.9M (FY24) to C$19.3M (FY25) to C$18.3M in H1 2026 alone (Q2 2026 C$15.6M), plus C$2.7M of capex in H1 2026 for heavy machinery, fuel trucks and camp expansion (PP&E 0.6 → 2.8). Cash overhead (G&A ex-depreciation) is about C$0.6M a quarter in 2025 and C$0.8–1.0M a quarter in 2026 — roughly 10% of cash spend in FY25 and ~9% in H1 2026, down from ~35% in the lean FY24.
  3. Share count on the post-consolidation basis: 33.1M (Dec 2023), 42.0M (Dec 2024), 90.1M (Dec 2025), 134.5M (30 Jun 2026), 136.3M (20 Aug 2026). Net equity raised: C$9.3M FY23, C$4.9M FY24, C$32.4M FY25 (May units at C$0.50 with C$0.75 warrants; August shares at C$0.95), C$88.5M H1 2026. 28.4M warrants (mostly the C$0.75 May-2027 series, ~C$19M if exercised; well in the money at the current ~C$1.69 price, 15 Oct 2026) and 9.0M options outstanding at the MD&A date.
  4. Non-cash items flatter nothing here: share-based compensation was C$1.7M in FY25 and C$1.1M in H1 2026; key-management related-party costs were C$2.0M in FY25 and C$1.8M in H1 2026 (of which SBC C$0.87M, salaries C$0.46M). H1 2026 net loss (C$18.6M) is reduced by a C$2.1M FX gain and C$1.0M interest income on the treasury. The FY24 audit carried a going-concern paragraph; the FY25 audit (26 Feb 2026) does not.
  5. No debt, streams or convertibles; the only non-current liability is a C$0.55M Flat camp restoration provision. Commitments are light: Doyon lease US$50k a year to 2030 then US$100k, plus US$2.5M of exploration per three-year period from 2027; Tibbs and Porterfield US$50k a year. Cash low point was C$1.2M at 31 Mar 2025, three raises and 18 months before the C$95M peak.

Burn · runway
Q2 2026 net loss C$2.87M (exploration C$2.29M, drilling only started 25 Jun). During drilling the stated treasury fell ~C$3M between 22 Sep and 20 Oct — roughly C$3M/month while rigs turn (my estimate). 2026 budget C$9.8M (board-approved Jan 2026).
Next catalyst
Newmont Zone assays (~27 holes drilled, results pending) and the rest of the 14,000 m program through Q4 2026; Dragonfly phase 2 (16 permitted holes), undated.
Funded to the next catalyst Funded through the 2026 program and, at the 2026 budget rate, most of a 2027 season without a raise (C$24M ÷ ~C$10–12M/yr). MD&A: "sufficient financing to cover its projected funding requirements for the ensuing year." A raise is likely only if 2027 is upsized or a resource/PEA program is added — plausibly H2 2027 on whatever the stock does. No going-concern note.
Thesis

Mojave (100%-owned, 5,830 ha, Inyo County) carries a shallow oxide-gold discovery at Dragonfly where every one of the 15 holes reported in 2026 hit gold from or near surface — best 83.82 m @ 3.40 g/t from surface (DF26-031) and 39.62 m @ 5.35 g/t (DF26-020) — with 97% cyanide-soluble gold, the raw material of a heap-leach story. The BLM Record of Decision (8 Apr 2026) ended a permit process that stopped the company for four years, and a C$25.25M raise at C$0.70 (Feb 2026) funds a 14,000 m program through 2026 and probably 2027. The bet is that Dragonfly plus the Newmont Zone (2 km south) grow into a 1 Moz-plus oxide resource that a US producer wants — but there is no resource, no date for one, and a California mine permit would be a far bigger fight than the drill permit was.

The Gate

Turning 240 m of drilled strike into ounces the market will pay for — before the California question comes due Dragonfly's reported holes cover only ~240 m of strike (surface structures run ~1,000 m); the ~27 Newmont holes are unassayed and the company has said no resource in 2026 and given no date after that. Widths are drilled widths in steep structures, so true widths are unknown. At US$117M with zero defined ounces the market already pays roughly US$100/oz for a 1 Moz deposit that does not yet exist on paper. Behind that sits the real gate: Conglomerate Mesa drew 23,800 scoping comments and an organised permanent-protection campaign (Friends of the Inyo); a drill permit took an EIS and ~5 years, and a mine would need far more.

A year ago the stock was C$0.355 at the 52-week low; Jan 14 2026 close C$0.74 on 194.7M shares = C$144M; the C$25.25M LIFE raise at C$0.70 (36.07M shares, closed 10 Feb 2026) plus 30.7M warrant exercises (to 24 Oct 2025) took the share count up 51% in a year. 52-week high C$0.93. Insiders ~5.5%.
Capex / IRRNo study, no capex, no IRR. Nothing can be modelled until a resource exists; the company has not dated one.
NPVNo NPV. No broker or third-party valuation found.
DepositNo resource. Dragonfly: 15 holes over ~240 m strike, all mineralised; best 83.82 m @ 3.40 g/t Au from surface; Newmont 41.15 m @ 1.64 g/t (2021).Mojave, 5,830 ha, 100% K2 (option completed 2025), Walker Lane trend, 3.4 miles east of Keeler. Eastside Gold Trend 6.5 km long. Dragonfly (2026 RC, drilled widths): DF26-031 83.82 m @ 3.40 g/t from surface incl. 19.81 m @ 7.58 g/t (hole ended early in bad ground); DF26-020 39.62 m @ 5.35 g/t from 51.8 m incl. 25.91 m @ 7.14 g/t; DF26-032 28.95 m @ 3.11 g/t incl. 9.15 m @ 8.53 g/t; DF26-023 27.43 m @ 4.08 g/t; DF26-028 53.34 m @ 2.00 g/t incl. 15.24 m @ 5.33 g/t; DF26-030 100.58 m @ 1.01 g/t. Historic DF20-002 45.72 m @ 6.68 g/t; 86.89 m @ 4.02 g/t cited from earlier surface drilling. Structures steeply west-dipping, stacked, across a ~400 m corridor, mostly undrilled; oxide to at least 180 m. Newmont Zone (2 km south): NM20-011 41.15 m @ 1.64 g/t (2021; BHP 1997 and Newmont 1991 drilled it); ~27 K2 holes drilled in 2026, assays pending. Cyanide solubility 97.1% aggregate on 211 samples (>0.1 g/t only, so not representative). Morningstar polymetallic trend (750 m × 2 km, grab samples to 13.3 g/t Au, 2,260 g/t Ag, 3.85% Cu) is under option (US$75k/yr). Wels, Yukon: 7,200 ha, 2023 RC 12 holes/1,961 m, best 34.7 g/t over 1.52 m and 21.33 m @ 1.6 g/t; Go Metals JV, K2 funds to PEA then 90/10. Wolf, Yukon: 21,887 ha staked May 2026, recon only. Si2, Nevada: 8 holes/3,871 m early 2026, no economic grades (best 3.04 m @ 1.29 g/t), JV talks.
NPV : capexn/a — no study. The relevant screen is what the market pays per not-yet-defined ounce.
Valuation Anchor

US$117M for zero defined ounces. If Dragonfly + Newmont end up at 1 Moz oxide, today's price is ~US$117/oz; at 2 Moz, ~US$58/oz. US oxide heap-leach developers with resources have in this gold market traded in a wide band I have not verified here, so treat the anchor as: the stock already discounts a ~1 Moz resource. What is not priced is a 2–3 Moz district — or a California permitting dead-end. Bucket: grade (shallow, high-grade oxide hits are the story), not value.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~5.5% (13.3M shares, Simply Wall St, 1 Sep 2026): John Robins 3.41% (8.25M), Jim Paterson 0.79%, Steve Swatton 0.47%, Chase Taylor-Robins 0.28%, Anthony Margarit 0.17% (418k), Steven Krause 0.08%, Eric Buitenhuis 0.02%, CFO 0.007%. No institution or strategic holder disclosed; no 10%+ holder; the Feb 2026 C$25.25M LIFE raise named no lead investor. Company says insiders exercised "a meaningful portion" of the 40M+ warrants in 2025. 2026 insider trades: Swatton sold ~50–62k shares (Apr and Aug 2026, ~C$0.83–0.88) — small. Last open-market buys: Robins ~94.5k shares at C$0.35–0.36 (May 2025, ~C$33k) and 1M at C$0.15 (Mar 2025, the placement price).

Read: Retail-heavy register with a well-known chairman at 3.4%; no strategic, no fund disclosed, so a 3× needs a producer or institutions to show up — and the CEO's 0.17% is thin.

Jurisdiction risk

National: USA — the current administration is pro-mining and the BLM cited Secretarial Order 3418 ("Unleashing American Energy") in the Mojave Final EIS (company release, 1 Dec 2025). The company has not claimed FAST-41 or any fast-track list; none found. State/local: California, Inyo County, Conglomerate Mesa — one of the most contested exploration sites in the US desert. The Phase 2 drill plan (submitted 2021, accepted complete Mar 2021) was pushed from an EA to a full EIS in Mar 2022 after 23,800 scoping comments; NOI Aug 2023, Draft EIS May 2025, Final EIS Dec 2025, ROD 8 Apr 2026 — the BLM's own Draft-EIS schedule had the ROD by Nov 2025. The ROD reduced the plan (up to 22 drill sites vs 30 proposed; Friends of the Inyo says disturbance fell to under half an acre with helicopter access and cultural monitors — their account, not verified against the ROD). Paiute/Shoshone tribes use the mesa (pinyon harvest); no formal tribal position found. Friends of the Inyo is campaigning for permanent protection.

Drilling is permitted; a mine is a different fight. California is the discount, and it is deserved.

Differentiator

Shallow, high-grade, leachable oxide gold with a permit in hand. Fifteen for fifteen at Dragonfly from surface, 97% cyanide-soluble, and the only EIS-backed exploration ROD on Conglomerate Mesa — which took five years and is now a barrier for anyone else. Discovery Group (Robins/Paterson: Kaminak → Goldcorp C$520M, Great Bear → Kinross ~C$1.8B) runs the capital markets side, and the C$24M treasury means no raise is needed to finish the discovery phase.

The permit and the treasury are real edges; the ounces are still a promise.

Exploration upside

Open along strike and at depth, 6.5 km trend mostly undrilled · moves the needle: high Dragonfly surface structures now run ~1,000 m (a 480 m southward extension mapped in Oct 2026) against ~240 m drilled; the Newmont Zone's ~27 2026 holes are the next read. Flores (12.35 g/t rock, historical trench 43 m @ 3.78 g/t), Gold Valley (27.6 g/t grabs), Stega and Morningstar are untested or barely tested. Here exploration is the thesis, not a bonus: without a resource there is nothing else.

Next Catalyst

Newmont Zone assays (~27 holes, pending as of 20 Oct 2026) and the remaining ~6,000 m of the 14,000 m program through Q4 2026; then Dragonfly phase 2 (16 permitted holes), a bottle-roll metallurgy program and — undated — a maiden resource. Expect a 2027 budget release in January as in 2026.

Open Questions
  • What are the true widths of the steep Dragonfly structures — do 80 m drilled intervals translate to 30 m or 60 m of real thickness?
  • Does the Newmont Zone (41 m @ 1.64 g/t historically) carry Dragonfly-type grades, or is it the lower-grade bulk of the trend?
  • When does K2 commit to a maiden resource, and how many of the 22 permitted sites does it need to get there?
  • What did the ROD actually restrict (helicopter access, acreage, cultural monitoring) and does it cap how fast the trend can be drilled out?
  • Is a mine at Conglomerate Mesa permittable in California at all — and if not, who buys a drilled-out oxide deposit there?

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 4/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 3/5

Robins and Discovery Group have twice sold discoveries to majors, and the team raised the discovery money and delivered the 2026 program on its dates. But K2 itself spent five years waiting, the CEO is unproven and thinly invested, the chairman's attention is spread across six companies, and no one here has permitted a mine in California. Solid, not tier 1 for this specific job.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
John Robins (Executive Chairman & Director (Chairman from the start; Executive Chairman since 16 Mar 2022), since Founder-era; Executive Chairman since 2022): Geologist, 35+ years; co-founder of Discovery Group. Kaminak Gold (Coffee) sold to Goldcorp (C$520M, 2016); Great Bear Resources sold to Kinross (~C$1.8B, 2022); Great Bear Royalties to Royal Gold (C$200M). Also Chairman of Aquitaine Metals; advisor to Kodiak Copper, CopperEx, ValOre, Prospector Metals. PDAC Viola R. MacMillan award 2025. Largest insider at 3.41%. · Anthony Margarit, P.Geo. (President, CEO & Director, since President before 2022; CEO since 16 Mar 2022): 25+ years in exploration at majors and juniors; first CEO job found. Holds ~418k shares (0.17%). H1 2026 fees C$110k plus C$93k share-based pay. · Jim Paterson (Director, since n/a): Co-founder and principal of Discovery Group; 28 years of capital raises, M&A and listings. Chairman of ValOre Metals and Targa Exploration. 0.79%. · Eric Buitenhuis, M.Sc., P.Geo. (VP Exploration & QP, since Mar 2022): Kaminak Gold from 2011 (Coffee delineation), then Goldcorp after the 2016 takeover. 0.02%. · Jessica Van Den Akker, CPA, CA (CFO & Corporate Secretary, since 2025 (her company's fees start in 2026; prior CFO's fees end in 2025)): Ex-CFO Kore Mining, Hive Blockchain, GlobalBlock, Fiore Management; paid through her company (C$60k H1 2026). · Carolyn Clark Loder (Director, since n/a): Ex-Manager Mineral Rights & Public Lands at Freeport-McMoRan; former President of the California Mining Association; National Mining Hall of Fame. Track record
  • Robins/Discovery Group: Kaminak Gold (Coffee, Yukon) sold to Goldcorp for ~C$520M in 2016 — win (https://k2gold.com/corporate/management/; company release 10 Feb 2026 notes Kaminak was a Discovery Group company)
  • Robins: Great Bear Resources sold to Kinross for ~C$1.8B (2022) and Great Bear Royalties to Royal Gold (C$200M) — win; advisors Chris Taylor and Rita Bennett came from Great Bearsource
  • K2 itself: optioned Mojave in 2019/2020, drilled discovery holes in 2020 (DF20-002 45.72 m @ 6.68 g/t), then lost four years (Mar 2022–Apr 2026) to the BLM EIS; shifted to Si2 (Nevada) in 2022, which produced no economic grades in 2026 — a long stall owned plainly, no hidden loss (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/117150; https://k2gold.com/k2-gold-drills-extensive-disseminated-mineralization-and-gold-silver-epithermal-quartz-veins-at-si2-project/)
  • Financing: C$1.045M at C$0.15 (Mar 2025, insiders in), 30.7M warrants exercised to Oct 2025, C$25.25M LIFE at C$0.70 (Feb 2026, non-brokered, oversubscribed/upsized twice from C$15M) — raised the discovery money before the ROD, at rising prices (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/283480; https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/276432)
  • Margarit: first CEO role; delivered the 2026 program on the dates given once the permit arrived (budget Jan 5, mobilise Jun 16, drilling Jun 25, assays from Aug 18) (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/279439; https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/302818)

Boards today: Robins: Executive Chairman K2, Chairman Aquitaine Metals, advisor to four more Discovery Group juniors. Paterson: K2 director plus Chairman of ValOre and Targa. The Discovery Group model is a shared bench across many juniors — marketing (Rita Bennett) and capital are pooled; K2 gets a slice of attention, not a full-time chairman.

Fit to this job
Stage: drilling a discovery towards a maiden resource — fits Buitenhuis (Coffee delineation) and Robins/Paterson (financing discoveries into sales). Deposit: shallow oxide gold in structures; Joey Wilkins (ex-Coeur Great Basin exploration director) adds Nevada-style oxide experience. Region: California permitting is the odd one — Loder (ex-Freeport lands, ex-California Mining Association president) is the fit, and the ROD shows it worked. New for them: nobody on this team has permitted or built a mine in California; Discovery Group's wins were sales of Canadian discoveries, so the natural ending is the same here.
Skin & pay
3/5 — meaningful chairman stake (3.4%), partly bought at market and via warrants; CEO stake thin; no selling by the people who matter, small sales by a former CEO. Insiders ~5.5% (13.3M shares, 1 Sep 2026). Robins 8.25M shares (3.41%, ~C$5.7M at C$0.69): 1M bought at C$0.15 in the Mar 2025 placement, ~94.5k open-market at C$0.35–0.36 (26 May–2 Jun 2025), plus warrant exercises in 2025 (company: insiders exercised 'a meaningful portion'). Margarit 418k (0.17%); Paterson 1.9M (0.79%). Swatton net seller 2026 (~50–62k shares, small). Pay: CEO fees C$110k/half-year + SBC — modest in cash; total key management comp C$739k H1 2026 against a ~C$167M cap. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsxv-kto/k2-gold-shares/ownership; https://www.insiderscreener.com/en/company/k2-gold-corp; Q2 2026 MD&A.

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Executive Chairman who chairs/advises six other juniors, a first-time CEO with 0.17% of the shares, and a CFO paid through her own company — a shared-bench structure.
  • Key management compensation more than doubled in H1 2026 (C$739k vs C$335k), mostly share-based; 8.195M options at C$0.70 granted 24 Jun 2026 (3.4% of shares) the day before drilling began. Advertising/marketing C$595k in H1 2026.
  • Drill releases carry small internal inconsistencies (7.51 vs 7.58 g/t in the 20 Oct headline/table; 4.03 vs 4.08 on 9 Sep; Newmont 1.64 vs 1.69 g/t) — sloppy, not deceptive.
  • Share count up 51% in a year; the C$0.70 placement has no hold period, and the stock has sat at or below C$0.70 since mid-October — overhang.
  • Director Swatton (ex-CEO) sold small amounts in Apr and Aug 2026 at C$0.83–0.88; no insider open-market buying found since May 2025.
  • Combative public language towards the BLM in 2022 ('absurd', 'political interference') from a company that still needed the same office for its permit.
Promises vs delivery

2021-03'Significant permitting milestone' — BLM accepted the amended Phase 2 Plan of Operations as complete; Phase 2 drilling expected to follow under an EAMar 2022: BLM required a full EIS instead; K2 suspended Mojave work, called the decision 'absurd' and 'political interference', and changed CEO. Drilling did not restart until June 2026 — five years after the 'milestone'. The slip was said plainly, the cause was outside the company, but the tone was combative rather than measured.source

Funded to the next catalyst Funded through the C$9M fall programme and into early 2027 (est. ~C$10–13M cash at year-end 2026 at the H1 pace — my estimate, not guided). The 2027 drill programmes plus a PEA will need another raise, probably H1 2027 on a ~C$200M cap; flow-through at a premium has been the pattern (C$3.40 FT vs C$2.45 common in Feb 2026).
Thesis

Maple Gold owns 100% of Douay (~4.1 Moz Indicated+Inferred: 3.5 Moz open-pit at 0.77–1.31 g/t plus 0.6 Moz underground) and Joutel (1.1 Moz at ~4.1–4.5 g/t underground, Agnico Eagle's old Eagle-Telbel mine), 35 km apart in Québec's Abitibi, after unwinding its 50/50 JV with Agnico in Dec 2024. A new team (CEO Kiran Patankar since Aug 2023) has raised ~C$37M since Aug 2025 at rising prices, drilled ~32,000 m in winter 2026, lifted the resource 70–77% in April 2026 and is now drilling 25,000 m at Joutel to grow the high-grade ounces ahead of an internal scoping study and a possible PEA in 2027. The market cap of ~US$150M pays ~US$29/oz for all ounces and ~US$165/oz for the Indicated ones.

The Gate

Proving the ounces are worth mining: a PEA that works on 0.77 g/t Douay pit material plus a Joutel underground restart No economic study has ever been published on the combined project; 83% of the ounces are Inferred and most of them sit in the Douay Porphyry zone at 0.74 g/t, which only becomes a mine at today's gold price with a cheap, large central mill. The company must turn the winter and fall drilling into Indicated ounces and an internal scoping study (2026) into a PEA (guided 'potential 2027'). Sub-gates: (1) the Agnico Eagle back-in — Agnico can take 50% of Douay/Joutel at a construction decision for 200% of Maple's spend since Dec 2024 plus C$12M, which halves the asset a buyer other than Agnico would be bidding for; (2) ~32 Douay winter holes and the Morris holes have been unreported since June 2026; (3) a 2027 raise is likely before any PEA.

Valuation Anchor

~US$29/oz on 5.2 Moz total, ~US$165/oz on the 905 koz Indicated, EV ~C$195M. That is cheap per total ounce only because 2.7 Moz are 0.77 g/t Inferred pit material; paying for the Indicated plus the 1.1 Moz high-grade Joutel ounces (~US$75/oz on those 2.0 Moz) is a fair resource-stage price for the Abitibi, not a bargain. Peers with a PEA (e.g. Abitibi 1–3 Moz developers) trade at roughly US$50–120/oz on M&I; Maple has to convert and study before it can be re-rated onto that scale, and the Agnico 50% back-in means a buyer is effectively bidding for half the project.

Shareholder structure

Agnico Eagle ~12.5–13.7% (largest holder; topped up by buying 662,780 shares in the market after the Feb 2026 offering to stay at ~13.7% partially diluted); Franklin Templeton ~8.3–9.5% (C$7M lead order in the Sep/Oct 2025 LIFE, maintained pro rata in Feb 2026); Michael Gentile ~8.4% (private placement Aug 2025, early warrant exercise C$2.3M at C$0.85 in Mar 2026); CDPQ ~2.5%; Spartan Fund ~2.4%. Insiders ~1.5% (Patankar ~0.69%, ~510k shares); insiders bought 96,700 shares at C$2.45 in the Feb 2026 placement and Patankar bought 10,000 at C$2.65 in the market in Jun 2026; no insider sales found. ~71% general public (Simply Wall St, Oct 2026).

Read: Three serious holders (a major, a big fund, a known junior-mining investor) all added at higher prices in 2026; management's own stake is small but all bought.

Jurisdiction risk

National/provincial: Québec, Abitibi — top-tier. Douay sits on the Casa Berardi deformation zone with road access, Hydro-Québec power nearby and Agnico's own Joutel mine infrastructure history 35 km away; Joutel is a past-producing site with existing permits and reclamation bonds that transferred with the Eagle purchase. Local: low; no community opposition found. The Matagami–Joutel area borders Cree (Eeyou Istchee) traditional territory and a mine permit would need an agreement — not yet in evidence (unverified).

Jurisdiction is not the risk here; grade and the Agnico back-in are.

Differentiator

Agnico Eagle is both the biggest shareholder and the holder of a 50% back-in, which makes Maple a quasi-captive development vehicle for Agnico's Abitibi pipeline. That cuts both ways: it guarantees a serious partner at construction and an obvious acquirer, but it caps what any other bidder would pay.

5.2 Moz for US$150M in Québec is scale; the question is how much of it is real at a mining grade.

Exploration upside

481 km² district, Joutel open along strike and at depth · moves the needle: medium-high Joutel is where the stock moves: winter holes hit 19 of 22 targets, extended high-grade up to 450 m beyond the old workings, and none of it is in the MRE; the 25,000 m fall programme targets the gap between the Eagle and Telbel shafts and conversion of Inferred. Douay adds tonnes easily (1.0 g/t over 138 m step-outs) but not grade. Morris (VMS, 3 holes) is a side bet with results overdue.

Next Catalyst

A stream of Joutel fall-programme assays through Q4 2026, then an updated resource (undated) feeding scoping studies and a possible PEA in 2027. Watch for the ~32 unreported Douay winter holes and Morris assays.

Open Questions
  • What exactly triggers and prices the Agnico Eagle Construction Option (200% of spend since Dec 2024 + C$12M) — and does Agnico intend to exercise or to buy the company instead?
  • Why have ~32 of 46 Douay winter holes and the Morris holes gone unreported since June 2026 — lab backlog or weak results?
  • Can Douay's 0.77 g/t Inferred pit material carry a central mill at today's Québec costs, or is the real project Joutel underground plus the 731 koz Douay Indicated starter?
  • Which two TSX-V companies did Patankar run in 2015–18 and what happened to their shareholders?

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 2/5

A genuine two-year turnaround (JV unwound, five raises at rising prices, MRE on time) by a team that has not yet delivered a study or a sale as principals; small but cash-bought insider stakes; one unexplained assay silence.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Kiran Patankar (President, CEO & Director, since Interim CEO Aug 2023, permanent Nov 2023; at Maple since Mar 2021 (SVP Growth Strategy 2021–22, CFO 2022–23)): Geological engineer (Colorado School of Mines) + Yale MBA; mining investment banker 2007–14 (Macquarie, Mackie Research); President/CEO of two unnamed TSX-V gold companies 2015–18. Independent director of Onyx Gold since 2023. Age not stated. · Dustin Isaacs (Independent Chair, since Jan 2026): Chief Legal Officer of Turquoise Hill Resources 2013–23 through the C$4.3B Rio Tinto buyout; ex-M&A lawyer; Québec Bar. · Ian Cunningham-Dunlop (EVP (Qualified Person), since n/a (also EVP of Onyx Gold)): Led exploration at Eskay Creek (Homestake/Barrick) 1997–2003; HighGold (Johnson Tract), NewCastle Gold, True Gold (Karma), Fronteer (Long Canyon). · Pascal Lessard (VP Exploration, since Feb 2026): 30+ years at Glencore/Xstrata/Falconbridge; runs the site. · Alex Rodriguez (SVP Corporate Development & Strategy, since Jul 2026): Ex-VP Corp Dev O3 Mining (C$204M sale to Agnico Eagle, Mar 2025); ex-Volcan, VerAI. · Nick Furber (CFO, since n/a): ~10 years CFO of Dynasty Metals & Mining; ex-PwC. · Marc Legault (Independent Director, since n/a (board refreshed Aug 2025/Jan 2026)): 34 years at Agnico Eagle, retired 2022 as SVP; explored the Casa Berardi belt and Joutel mine complex early in his career. · Gérald Riverin / Darwin Green / Chris Adams (Independent Directors (Technical Chair / director / Audit Chair), since n/a): Riverin: Troilus discovery, ex-Inmet, Cogitore, Yorbeau (Douay area). Green: founder/CEO HighGold (sold to Contango ORE 2024), Exec Chair Onyx Gold. Adams: ex-head of Mining Finance Americas, Macquarie.
Track record
  • Patankar: joined Maple Mar 2021 as SVP, CFO 2022–23, CEO from Aug 2023 — the Dec 2025 shareholder letter itself admits 'historical underperformance' and a reset begun 'two years ago'; the stock bottomed around C$0.08 pre-consolidation (~C$0.80 post) in 2024 before the turnaroundsource
  • Patankar as CEO: unwound the Agnico 50/50 JV to 100% ownership (announced Jun 2024, closed Dec 2024) at the cost of a 1% NSR and a 50% back-in; cut overhead >50%; raised ~C$9.6M (early 2025), C$5M (Aug 2025, 10:1 consolidation), C$13M (Oct 2025 at C$1.20), C$16M (Feb 2026 at C$3.40 FT/C$2.45) plus ~C$6M warrants — each at a higher price; stock +224% in 2025 (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/234639; https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/284118)
  • Patankar 2015–18: President/CEO of two TSX-V gold companies, unnamed in every company document found — outcome for those shareholders not verifiedsource
  • Cunningham-Dunlop: Eskay Creek exploration lead 1997–2003 (E.A. Scholz Award 2003); Fronteer's Long Canyon (sold to Newmont 2011) — wins as a geologist, not as a CEOsource
  • Rodriguez: O3 Mining VP Corp Dev through the C$204M Agnico sale (Mar 2025) — directly relevant to the likely ending heresource
  • Green: built and sold HighGold Mining to Contango ORE (Jul 2024) — one completed junior exit on the boardsource

Boards today: Patankar: Maple CEO + Onyx Gold independent director. Cunningham-Dunlop is EVP of both Maple and Onyx Gold; Green is Exec Chair of Onyx and on Contango ORE and Evergold boards — an Onyx/HighGold cluster shares the bench. Chair and CEO are separate (Isaacs chair since Jan 2026).

Fit to this job
Stage: resource growth toward a first study — fits a banker-geologist CEO with a strong technical bench (Eskay Creek, Glencore, Agnico 34 years). Deposit: Abitibi gold, including the exact Joutel camp Legault worked. Region: Québec — Riverin and Legault are Abitibi natives. New for them: nobody on the executive team has taken a project through a PEA/FS to construction as CEO; the corporate-development hire (Rodriguez) signals the plan is a transaction, not a build.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake (~1.5% insiders, CEO ~0.7%) but all cash-bought at market or placement prices, no selling; modest pay. Insiders ~1.5% in total; Patankar ~0.69% (~510k shares, ~C$1.5M), bought 20,400 at C$2.45 in the Feb 2026 placement and 10,000 at C$2.65 in the market (10 Jun 2026); six other insiders bought 96,700 shares in total at C$2.45 in Feb 2026; officers/directors took 77,268 units in the Sep 2025 placement. No insider sales found. CEO total pay ~C$533k (60% salary) on a ~C$215M cap — modest. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsxv-mgm/maple-gold-mines-shares/ownership; https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/284118

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Four months of silence on ~32 Douay holes and the Morris programme while Joutel results were promoted.
  • Share-based compensation to related parties jumped to C$1.13M in Q2 2026 (C$0.22M a year earlier); G&A C$2.1M in Q2 vs C$0.8M in Q3 2025 — overhead is rising with the share price.
  • Patankar's 2015–18 CEO roles are never named — unusual for a bio that cites '>C$3B of transactions'.
  • Patankar was CFO/SVP during the 2021–23 decline the company now calls 'historical underperformance'; the turnaround is his, but so was part of the slide.
  • Agnico Eagle is simultaneously largest shareholder, royalty holder and back-in holder — alignment with minority shareholders at a construction decision is not guaranteed.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash rose from C$3.2M at 30 June 2025 (the low point) to C$27.3M at 31 March 2026 after three raises in seven months (Sep 2025 C$5.0M, Oct 2025 C$13.0M, Feb 2026 C$16.0M, mostly flow-through at a premium) plus about C$6.6M of warrant exercises, and stood at C$23.4M at 30 June 2026; the discrete Q2 2026 operating burn was C$7.0M (Q1 C$5.0M), so at the Q2 rate the runway is roughly 10 months, i.e. into Q2 2027, and with a 'fully funded' C$9M fall Joutel program plus more Douay drilling in H2 the company should end 2026 with roughly C$9–11M and need another raise in H1 2027.
  2. Spending has shifted decisively into the ground: exploration expensed went from C$3.8M (FY23) and C$3.5M gross (FY24) to C$9.4M gross in FY25 and C$11.0M in H1 2026 alone (Douay 7.4, Joutel 2.5, Morris 0.9); cash overhead was about C$1.3M in H1 2026 against C$11.9M of operating outflow, so overhead is now ~11% of cash spend, down from ~50% in FY23 (G&A C$4.0M vs exploration C$3.8M) and ~40% in FY24.
  3. Reported G&A nevertheless doubled year on year in H1 2026 (C$3.2M vs 1.3M) because share-based payments jumped to C$1.8M (C$1.4M in Q2 alone, with key-management SBC of C$1.1M in the quarter); total SBC including the exploration portion was C$2.2M in H1 2026, and cash-settled RSUs cost C$0.24M in Q2.
  4. Share count (post-consolidation) grew from 34.0M at Dec 2023 to 45.5M at Dec 2024, 62.2M at Dec 2025 and 74.2M at 24 Aug 2026 (fully diluted 82.2M); roughly C$44M net has been raised since the start of 2024 (FY24 9.0, FY25 17.4, H1 2026 20.9 incl. C$6.1M warrants). Michael Gentile's early warrant exercise in March 2026 accounts for most of the Q1 2026 warrant cash.
  5. Reported losses are flattered by non-cash flow-through premium amortisation (C$2.9M in FY25, C$0.9M in H1 2026); the FT premium liability was C$4.5M at 30 June 2026 and C$15.0M of eligible exploration remains to be spent by 31 Dec 2027 (minimum C$3.4M by 31 Dec 2026). Every annual audit carries a going-concern paragraph. No debt or streams (only C$0.8M of office/vehicle leases); Agnico Eagle holds a 1% NSR and a 50% back-in option on Douay/Joutel after the Dec 2024 JV unwind, and the Eagle property was fully acquired in July 2026 (final cash payment + 55k shares).

Maple EXPENSES all exploration (statement of loss line 'exploration and evaluation expenses'), so 'exp' carries the drilling spend (shown NET of Quebec mining exploration tax credits, which the company nets into the same line: FY24 −0.33, FY25 −2.06 (of which 2.04 in Q2 2025), 2026 nil) and 'exp_cap'/'ee' are zero/null; only office equipment and right-of-use assets are capitalised ('ppe'). 'ga' = G&A excluding share-based payments (includes depreciation and directors' fees); 'sbc' = share-based payments within G&A only (SBC charged to exploration stays in 'exp'). 'other' = non-cash amortisation of the flow-through share premium (a gain) plus small items. Lease payments are shown under 'debt_out'; there are no borrowings (a C$40k CEBA loan was repaid in 2024). Shares were consolidated 1-for-10 on 8 Sep 2025; ALL share counts here are post-consolidation (pre-Sep-2025 counts divided by 10). 'spend': overhead = cash G&A (G&A − SBC − depreciation); ground = operating cash outflow − overhead (so it absorbs working-capital swings and tax-credit refunds).

Thesis

Berenguela, at 4,200 m in Puno, is a carbonate-replacement Ag-Cu-Mn-Zn deposit worked from 1906 and optioned by ASARCO, Silver Standard and Valor before Aftermath bought it from SSR Mining (2020; final payment made early, Nov 2025; 100% owned, no remaining payments). The Nov 2025 MRE — 439 holes, open-pit constrained — gives M&I 51.6 Mt @ 74 g/t Ag, 5.7% Mn, 0.63% Cu, 0.33% Zn (122.5 Moz Ag, 2.93 Mt Mn, 717 Mlb Cu), Inferred 14.3 Mt.

The plan is a hydrometallurgical plant: sulphuric/SO2 reductive leach → copper by SX/EW → zinc precipitate → manganese sulphate crystallised to 99.9% HPMSM (battery-grade) → silver by cyanidation of the residue; bench tests show 95% Mn and 89–95% Ag extraction. A PFS with DRA Global / SENET started Feb 2026 and is guided for Q1 2027 — no PEA was done. Cash C$21.8M, no debt, ~C$14M/yr burn; Eric Sprott owns ~24% and wrote the whole Nov 2024 raise.

Phase 3 drilling (90 holes) returned 48.5 m @ 438 g/t Ag / 2.2% Cu / 24.9% Mn and 70 m @ 230 g/t; Phase 4 is testing Copper East and a 2 km skarn anomaly. A US critical-minerals subsidiary with retired USMC generals on its advisory board is chasing DPA / DOE / EXIM money for the HPMSM.

Chile: Challacollo (35 Moz Ag Indicated, permitted DIA, drilling restarted Jul 2026 after the contractor quit) and Cachinal (15 Moz, DIA approved Jul 2026, the 2023 sale never closed).

The Gate

Whether a four-product hydromet plant at 4,200 m makes money — and the answer is mostly a manganese-sulphate price, not a silver price. On the company's own NSR model, manganese is ~75% of value, silver ~13%, copper ~11%. So the PFS (Q1 2027) is really an HPMSM feasibility question: reagent supply (sulphuric acid and SO2 trucked or made on site), acid consumption (never disclosed), plant location and throughput trade-offs, and an offtake market for high-purity manganese sulphate that is thin, China-dominated and price-volatile. Six years after optioning the asset there is no capex, NPV or IRR; SSR's original PFS deadline (Nov 2025) was missed and waived.

Sub-gates
  1. Puno — the most anti-Fujimori region in Peru (86% Sánchez in June), site of the Jan 2023 Juliaca killings and the 2011 "Aymarazo" that cancelled Bear Creek's Santa Ana; a September drill permit was delayed over "incorrect identification of indigenous groups"; consulta previa and water permits are undisclosed.
  2. Funding — C$20M of working capital covers the PFS, not a feasibility study or a plant; another raise in 2027 is near-certain on a stock down ~39% YTD.
  3. Alignment — officers and directors have been steady sellers for a year while Sprott is the only buyer.

If you want silver exposure, this is the wrong vehicle: the silver is a by-product credit on a manganese project. If you want a Western-Hemisphere HPMSM option with 122 Moz of silver attached, it is the only one listed.

Valuation Anchor

Cheapest silver ounces in the file on paper (~US$1.2/oz M&I) and the least meaningful number in it. Price the company as what it is: a pre-study manganese-sulphate project with 122 Moz of silver and 717 Mlb of copper as credits, in Puno, with a plant nobody has costed.

The bull case is a PFS that shows a US$300–500M capex plant making ~US$150–250M/yr of margin across four products at spot, with US government critical-minerals money de-risking the build — at which point a US$165M market cap is a fraction of NPV.

The bear case is a PFS whose economics hinge on an HPMSM price that Chinese oversupply sets, at a capex a C$20M company cannot fund.

Bucket: grade / discovery / optionality — defined tonnes, but no study and the wrong metal for the "cheap defined ounces" test. Silver-price scenarios barely move it; HPMSM price and PFS capex do.

Read: One man owns a quarter of the company and has bought every time it needed money; the people running it own ~1% and have sold at every price from C$1.00 down to C$0.60. The 'insider-aligned 35%' figure that circulates in promotional coverage is Sprott plus management — read it as Sprott. Related-party fees (~C$1.8M cash + C$2.6M stock in FY26) on a C$14M burn are high for a company with no study.

Jurisdiction risk

National: freshly favourable, thin margin. Keiko Fujimori won the Jun 7, 2026 runoff by 49,641 votes, inaugurated Jul 28; a US$33B mining-investment target, 240 authorisations in 2026, permitting fast-track, 40% of royalties to host communities — analysts call it a 12–24-month window.

Local: the worst in this file after Concordia and Titiribí, for different reasons. Puno voted 86% for Sánchez (the resource-nationalist); Aymara groups at Ilave vowed in June not to recognise a Fujimori win, invoking the Jan 2023 Juliaca killings (18 dead; state of emergency to Sep 2023); the 2011 "Aymarazo" cancelled Bear Creek's Santa Ana project outright. Berenguela is 6 km from Santa Lucía with rail to Matarani and grid power — good infrastructure — and has surface-access agreements and a renewed drilling EIA; but a September authorisation was held up over indigenous-group identification, and consulta previa, water rights and a construction EIA are undisclosed. Chile (Challacollo, Cachinal): DIAs approved, low risk, no funding.

National tailwind, regional headwind: Puno is where Peru's mining conflicts have been settled by force, twice in fifteen years.

Differentiator
  1. The only listed Western-Hemisphere HPMSM project with a silver-copper deposit wrapped around it. 2.93 Mt of manganese in M&I, bench-proven to 99.9% battery-grade sulphate, at a moment when US policy (DPA, DOE, EXIM, DFC) is paying for non-Chinese battery inputs — the advisory board of retired generals and an ambassador is aimed squarely at that.
  2. A large, measured, 100%-owned, royalty-light resource with no payments left — 439 holes, Measured category, open-pit shape, rail and power at the door.
  3. Eric Sprott at ~24%, who funded the company alone in Nov 2024 and took half the Dec 2025 raise — the deepest-pocketed anchor of any junior in either file.
  4. A COO (Danny Keating) who ran Giyani's HPMSM project and a technical director with 22 years at First Quantum — the right résumés for the flowsheet.

Read it honestly: the differentiator (manganese) is why the silver name is misleading and why the economics can't be judged by anyone who follows silver — and Sprott's 24% is both the floor and the reason every future raise is priced by one man's appetite. Same fact, two sides.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, but conversion is done · moves the needle: low–medium. The resource is already Measured + Indicated; Phase 3 (90 holes) produced spectacular silver intercepts (48.5 m @ 438 g/t; 11.4 m @ 1,042 g/t; 4.95 m @ 882 g/t) that improve the model but don't change the category or the metal mix. Phase 4 targets — Copper East (156 m @ 1.12% Cu, 290 g/t Ag previously) and the 2 km SW skarn anomaly — are the genuine upside: a copper-rich extension would rebalance value away from manganese, which is what the equity needs. Chile: 2,000 m at Challacollo, results pending.

More silver ounces add nothing here. More copper would.

Next Catalyst

Berenguela PFS (Q1 2027) — capex, NPV and the HPMSM price assumption; Phase 4 Copper East and SW Intrusive assays (Q4 2026); Challacollo results; any US critical-minerals grant, loan or offtake; a financing (likely 2027, likely Sprott-led); permitting milestones — consulta previa, water.

Open Questions
  • What HPMSM price does the PFS assume, and what does NPV look like at a stressed (Chinese-oversupply) price?
  • Acid and SO₂ consumption and supply at 4,200 m — trucked from where, at what cost per tonne?
  • Is consulta previa complete, and who are the correctly identified indigenous groups?
  • Does the SW skarn or Copper East deliver enough copper to make this a Cu-Ag project with a Mn credit rather than the reverse?
  • Why has the share price fallen 39% in a silver bull market while drilling delivered — is the market saying "not a silver stock" or "no study"?
  • What does Sprott do at the next raise — and what happens to the equity if he doesn't?

  1. Cash was C$21.8M at 31 May 2026, with no term deposits left; at the latest quarterly burn of C$4.2M that is about 15 months of runway.
  2. Operating outflow rose from C$5.4M in FY24 to C$14.2M in FY26; expensed exploration was C$9.1M while cash G&A jumped to C$5.8M, about 39% of spending.
  3. Shares outstanding grew from 233.3M in May 2024 to 350.0M in September 2026, up 50%, after C$25.0M raised in FY25 and C$26.1M in FY26, all equity.
  4. The Berenguela purchase from SSR Mining was paid off in cash instalments of C$4.4M in FY25 and FY26; no bank debt, convertibles or streams remain.
  5. Related-party fees to officers and directors were C$1.5M cash plus C$2.6M in shares in FY26, and the statements still carry a going-concern note.

Thesis

Big Ridge owns 100% of Hope Brook, a brownfield gold mine on Newfoundland's south coast with 16.2 Mt @ 2.32 g/t Au Indicated (1.2 Moz, of which 1.0 Moz @ 2.14 g/t is pit-constrained) plus 2.2 Mt @ 3.25 g/t Inferred (231 koz), at a US$1,750 price deck. The company consolidated the project from First Mining in 2024–25, has a strategic backer (Michael Gentile, ~15% basic / 19.9% partially diluted) and raised C$7.0M in July 2026 for drilling and a PEA by SGS. The story is a re-start study on existing infrastructure at a gold price more than double the resource deck, then resource growth along a 5 km strike to the southwest.

The Gate

A PEA that shows a real mine at a sensible capex, and getting it out at all The PEA was promised for Q1 2026 (Sep 2025), then H1 2026 (Nov 2025, Jan 2026), then 'nears completion' (Apr 2026); by Sep 2026 the company only says it is 'working on' it, with no date. Hope Brook's pit grade is 2.14 g/t in a moderately refractory, pyrophyllite-silica system that historically recovered 79–90% and shipped a copper-gold concentrate; the study has to show that a restart (pit plus underground, with ore sorting) pays at a capex a C$180M company can finance. The market already pays ~US$81/oz for 1.43 Moz with no economics, so a thin PEA would hurt more than a good one helps.

Historical mine (1987–97) processed ore through an on-site mill with gold recoveries of 78.8–89.8% and a 22% Cu / 34 g/t Au concentrate in 1992; recent met work gives 26–30% Cu concentrates at 270–539 g/t Au. Ore sorting test (Jul 2025, 69 kg) rejected 27.8% of mass and 73% of visually barren material — small-sample, preliminary.

That was a 43% Indicated-ounce increase on the 2021 estimate after ~20,000 m of 2021–22 drilling. The Phase I holes were long and modest: 0.47 g/t over 87 m (HB-22-198), 0.56 g/t over 56 m (HB-22-194), 17.5 g/t over 1 m (HB-22-193). Mineralisation sits in the Main and 240 Zones along the Cinq Cerf deformation zone; 2023–24 geophysics and sampling outlined several kilometres of targets to the southwest (Chetwynd, Cinq Cerf). The 2026 programme (from Jun 2026) is infill/step-out at the 240 and Main Zones plus ~2,000 m of geotechnical and hydrogeological drilling for the PEA. Land package size not stated in any release found. Site has a 28-person camp, 1,100 m airstrip, dock and a substation on the provincial grid.
NPV : capexn/a — no study
Valuation Anchor

At US$116M the market pays ~US$81/oz for 1.43 Moz of all-category resource, or ~US$97/oz on Indicated alone, for a project with no economic study. That is the top of the range for pre-PEA Canadian gold developers and reflects the brownfield infrastructure, the Gentile sponsorship and the gold tape. The nearest comparable is Maritime Resources (Hammerdown, Newfoundland), a permitted, producing-stage project sold to New Found Gold for C$292M in 2025 — Big Ridge is already at ~60% of that with no study or permit.

Shareholder structure

Michael Gentile ~15.3% basic / ~19.9% partially diluted after the Jul 2026 placement (18.1M of 23.3M units); he also bought ~877,000 shares on market at ~C$0.27 on 7 Mar (year not stated on the source; consistent with 2026). Management and directors ~3% (CEO Bandrowski 1.1%, CFO Kirke 0.58%, Bates 0.57%, Tintor 0.34%, Mazur 0.24%, Pint 0.16%). PowerOne Capital Group participated in the Jul 2025 placement (amount not disclosed). First Mining Gold's 36.5M shares were sold in Mar 2024 to a group of mostly existing shareholders (buyers and price not disclosed). No institutional holders found; insiders net buyers of ~C$361k over 12 months per Simply Wall St.

Read: One large financier-sponsor (Gentile) and a thin management stake; no major and no visible fund base.

Jurisdiction risk

National: Canada, Newfoundland & Labrador — a mining province that permitted and built Valentine (Calibre/Equinox) in 2023–25 and Hammerdown; the province co-funded Big Ridge's 2023 work through its Junior Exploration Assistance programme. Local: Hope Brook is a past-producing, previously permitted mine site 85 km east of Port aux Basques with grid power and a dock; environmental baseline work was completed in 2024 and a project registration was being prepared. The company cites 'strong social license' but names no Indigenous agreement (the south coast falls within Qalipu/Mi'kmaq asserted territory — engagement status unverified). New COO James Powell ran regulatory and government affairs at Valentine.

Low-risk jurisdiction with a brownfield site; permitting is a 2–3 year process, not a gate, provided the PEA justifies it.

Differentiator

<b>A real mine site, not a greenfield target:</b> 752 koz produced, a mill pad, grid substation, airstrip, dock and camp already exist, and 1.2 Moz is Indicated at a price deck of US$1,750 when gold is ~US$4,180. The permitting and infrastructure hurdles that sink most 1–2 Moz juniors are smaller here.

The edge is restart optionality at today's gold price; the weakness is that the market has already priced most of it before a study.

Exploration upside

5 km of strike to the southwest, open at depth · moves the needle: medium The 2026 programme is mostly infill and geotechnical work for the PEA, with step-outs at the 240 Zone (deeper, higher-grade) and below the current model. Geophysics in 2023–24 outlined several kilometres of targets along the Cinq Cerf deformation zone toward Chetwynd, untested by drilling. Phase I (2021–22) hit wide low-grade intervals rather than new high-grade shoots, so doubling the resource would need a new zone, not just extensions.

Next Catalyst

First 2026 drill assays (none out after four months) and the PEA, both undated. The company presents at the Gentile forum in London on 19 Oct 2026 and a European roadshow 20–23 Oct.

Open Questions
  • Why has the PEA slipped from Q1 2026 to no date, and what has changed in scope (open pit only? sorting? copper concentrate?) — or is it waiting for the geotechnical drilling?
  • Does First Mining's 1.5% NSR and C$2M production payment survive the 2025 buy-out of the 20%, and are there other royalties on the ground?
  • What is the land package, and does the company hold the full 5 km Cinq Cerf strike and the Chetwynd ground it keeps citing?
  • Who bought First Mining's 36.5M shares in Mar 2024 and at what price — is there an overhang?
  • With two full-time employees, who is actually running the PEA and the drill programme day to day?
Context & updates
19 Oct 2026 update

Metallurgy: the 2026 test program (BaseMet, directed by Canenco) reports ~88% overall gold recovery and 90% copper recovery with a ~24% copper, ~300 g/t gold concentrate on ~1.08 g/t feed. That removes some of the recovery risk in the gate (the old mine recovered 79–90%), but the PEA promised for Q1 2026 is still undated; the release only says the company will now work on its process design. Odds and risk unchanged.

Added to the tracker at the owner's request. First assessment: risk 3/5, chance it works ~25%, odds of a 3× ~10%, room for a second 3×: partly. Management B.

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 2/5 · Skin in the game 2/5

Deal-making has been good (cheap consolidation of Hope Brook, raises at rising prices, a real mine-builder added to the board), but the one dated technical promise — the PEA — has been re-dated three times without acknowledgement (Q1 2026 → H1 2026 → "nears completion" → undated) and no technical results have come out in 2026. Unproven at delivering studies; B with a candour watch.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

Has run Big Ridge from the 2021 First Mining earn-in to 100% ownership. Comp ~C$347k incl. ~37% stock/options (Simply Wall St); Yahoo shows C$131k cash pay. · James Powell, P.Eng (Chief Operating Officer, since 23 Mar 2026): Ex-VP Regulatory & Government Affairs, Valentine Gold Mine (NL); chair of Mining Industry NL; 25+ years civil/geotech/environmental. 300k options at C$0.32. · Paul Robinson, PhD, P.Geo (VP Exploration, QP, since 2023): Joined the exploration team in 2023; QP on all releases. Holds 0.04%. · James Kirke, CPA, CA (CFO, since n/a): Holds 0.58%; cash pay ~C$102k. · Nick Tintor (Chairman (director since Oct 2020), since Chair Jun 2021): Negotiated the Hope Brook earn-in; prior Newfoundland gold experience (not detailed). Holds 0.34%. · Garett Macdonald, P.Eng, MBA (Director, since 15 Sep 2026): Ex-President & CEO Maritime Resources (took Hammerdown to first gold; sold to New Found Gold for C$292M in 2025); VP Ops/GM Hemlo Mining Corp; Rainy River, Curraghinalt FS, Placer Dome. · Kristina Bates, Richard Mazur, Paul Pint (Directors, since Pint since 2023; others n/a): Backgrounds not found in releases. Holdings 0.57% / 0.24% / 0.16%. · Michael Gentile (Strategic shareholder (~15% basic, 19.9% partially diluted), since 2024–25): Bastion Asset Management; junior-mining financier with top positions in ~35 companies and six board seats; runs the investor forums Big Ridge markets at.
Track record
  • Bandrowski/Tintor: earned 51% then 80% of Hope Brook from First Mining (2021–Mar 2024) after renegotiating the spend down by ~C$6M, then bought the final 20% for C$3M cash + 7M shares (Jul 2025) — delivered, and cheaplysource
  • Resource grew 43% in Indicated ounces (844 koz → 1.2 Moz) on ~20,000 m of 2021–22 drilling, though at a lower grade (4.77 → 2.32 g/t) from a lower cut-offsource
  • Share price C$0.125 (Jul 2025 placement) → C$0.57 (Oct 2026), with three raises at rising prices (C$0.125, warrant exercise ~C$0.20, C$0.30) — shareholders have done well in the gold tapesource
  • PEA: commenced Sep 2025 with a Q1 2026 target; still not delivered by Oct 2026 — the one dated technical promise, missedsource
  • Macdonald (new director): built and sold Hammerdown (Maritime → New Found Gold, C$292M, 2025) — the only person on the team with a completed mine-buildsource

Boards today: Bandrowski: Big Ridge only (per releases). Macdonald: executive at Hemlo Mining Corp plus this board. Gentile sits on six boards (not Big Ridge's). Two full-time employees per Yahoo profile — the company is run through consultants and SGS.

Fit to this job
Stage: resource-to-PEA on a brownfield restart — needs a study manager and a permitting lead. Fit: CEO is a finance/CFA person, good at deals and raises (the earn-in and buy-out were well structured) but not a mine builder; the 2026 hires (Powell for permitting, Macdonald for building) fill that gap on paper. Deposit/region: Robinson and Burke have Hope Brook history (Coastal Gold); Powell knows the NL regulator. New for them: delivering a study on time — the first PEA has already slipped.
Skin & pay
2/5 — CEO ~1% and officers under 2% combined, origin unverified; the real buyer is the outside sponsor, not management. CEO Bandrowski ~1.1% (~C$2.0M at C$0.57), origin of the stake (purchase vs grants) not verified; other officers/directors ~1.9% combined. Insiders net buyers of ~C$361k over 12 months (Simply Wall St) — mostly Gentile (>10% holder) on-market at ~C$0.27 and in placements at C$0.125 and C$0.30. CEO total comp ~C$347k (37% equity) vs a C$181M cap — modest. Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsxv-brau/big-ridge-gold-shares/management

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • PEA re-dated twice and then left undated, each time in a release that reads as business as usual; the Apr 2026 'nears completion' has now run six months.
  • 4.3M officer options at C$0.45 vested immediately on 1 Jul 2026, days before a C$0.30 placement closed; director options (Macdonald) also vest immediately.
  • Two full-time employees for a company marketing a PEA-stage restart; execution rests on consultants.
  • Boilerplate referring to 'Caprock's shares' in the forward-looking section of every release since 2025 — sloppy disclosure hygiene.
  • Marketing cadence (Gentile showcases, PDAC, Atlanta, European roadshow) outpaces technical news: zero drill or study results in 2026 to date.
