What the numbers say
  1. Cash went from a near-empty C$0.21M at 30 June 2025 (negative working capital, going-concern paragraph) to C$3.55M at 31 March 2026 plus C$2.68M of Caprock Mining shares held as marketable securities; since then C$0.24M of warrant/option exercises (Apr–May 2026) and the C$7.0M unit placement closed 7 July 2026 (23.3M units @ C$0.30, full warrant @ C$0.46 to July 2029, Gentile took 18.1M units → 19.9%) have come in. At the Q3 FY26 operating burn of C$0.41M a quarter the treasury would last years, but the 2026 program (IP survey from June, drilling from mid-June 2026, PEA and environmental/geotech studies) will lift spending to an estimated C$1.5–2.5M a quarter, so the roughly C$9–10M of cash after the July raise is about 12–18 months of runway — the next raise is likely in H2 calendar 2027, earlier if drilling is expanded.
  2. Overhead dominates: over the eight quarters cash G&A ran a steady C$0.2–0.3M a quarter (C$1.0M a year: salaries C$0.54M, office C$0.11M, IR C$0.11–0.18M, professional fees C$0.1M) while expensed exploration fell from C$2.2M in FY24 to C$0.85M in FY25 and only C$0.53M in the nine months to March 2026 — cash overhead has exceeded money into the ground in six of the last eight quarters. Reported G&A is inflated by non-cash share-based compensation of C$1.65M in 9M FY26 (DSU/RSU liabilities revalued as the share price rose from C$0.05 to ~C$0.30), with equity-based awards still C$1.6M of liabilities at 31 March 2026.
  3. The big ticket was the acquisition of the remaining 20% of Hope Brook from First Mining (closed 30 July 2025): C$3.0M cash plus 7.0M shares (C$1.17M), taking E&E assets from C$5.47M to C$9.65M. In FY24 C$1.22M of optioned Newfoundland properties were written off after the company missed vendor payments.
  4. Dilution has been heavy and cheap: 136.6M shares at June 2023, 198.2M at June 2024 (51.4M for the Gold Island merger, which supplied C$3.8M of cash), 229.6M after the C$0.05 placement of Sept 2024, 278.6M after the C$0.125 unit placement of July 2025, 293.4M at 31 March 2026 after 13.2M warrant exercises, ~294.3M by late May 2026 and about 318M after the July 2026 placement (per stockanalysis). Cash raised in equity since July 2023 is only about C$16M (FY24 0 excl. Gold Island cash, FY25 1.5, 9M FY26 7.8, July 2026 7.0), with 32.1M warrants (7.5M @ C$0.20 to Jul 2027, 23.3M @ C$0.46 to Jul 2029, finder warrants) and ~10M options still outstanding.
  5. Q3 FY26 showed net income of C$1.5M, but it is entirely a C$2.65M non-cash gain from reclassifying the Caprock Mining stake (Destiny project optionee, which must also deliver 350k shares, C$0.25M cash and C$0.75M of exploration by 31 Dec 2026) to fair value; the Caprock shares are the only liquid asset besides cash. No debt, streams or convertibles; related-party items are limited to management salaries (C$0.44M in 9M FY26), director fees and cash-settled DSUs to directors (C$0.09M in FY25).

Statements are in Canadian dollars (not thousands); figures here are C$ millions, one decimal. Big Ridge EXPENSES exploration (statement-of-loss line 'exploration expense'), so 'exp' carries the field spend and 'exp_cap' is zero; 'ee' = capitalised exploration and evaluation assets (Hope Brook acquisition costs). Share-based compensation is reported INSIDE G&A in the filings; here 'ga' = G&A less SBC, and 'sbc' is shown separately (it is volatile because cash-settled DSU/RSU liabilities are re-marked to the share price, producing credits in some quarters). 'spend.overhead' = cash G&A (G&A less SBC and amortisation) plus any cash settlements of DSUs/RSUs. Acquisition cash for Hope Brook (Q1 FY26) is counted in 'ground'. The Gold Island cash acquired in FY24 is shown under 'acq' (the filing puts it under financing). Office-lease liabilities (≤C$41k) appear as 'debt' in FY24–Q3 FY25 only and round to 0.0.

Gate Does the bulk sample deliver grade — and is the underground as continuous as the model says? The 2027 question remains: C$46M of secured debt comes due Dec 2027 and the April-2024 debentures (C$3.1M) mature ~Apr 2027, so repayment still depends on bulk-sample gold sales (deck: free cash flow Q2 2027) or a refinancing; the new money narrows that gap rather than closing it.
Thesis

Galleon owns 100% of West Cache, 13 km west of Timmins: 4.05 Mt @ 3.63 g/t Indicated (472 koz) and 11.8 Mt @ 2.87 g/t Inferred (1.09 Moz) at a 1.6 g/t cut-off (P&E, Jan 2022), with a maiden PEA (after-tax NPV5 C$240M, IRR 26.7% at US$1,700 gold). In 2025 it raised C$91.5M (C$30M equity at C$0.60, C$15.5M convertibles, a C$46M Pan American secured facility), bought back the 3% Newmont NSR, and in 2026 built the box cut, portal and hydro line and started ramp development toward a permitted 86,500 t bulk sample that the company models at ~8.1 g/t / 22,600 oz, to be toll-milled 40 km away at Pan American's Bell Creek. If the bulk sample delivers anything near that grade, the gold alone (~C$130M gross at today's price) repays the debt, and an updated PEA (Hard Rock Consulting, engaged Oct 2026) can carry 2026 drilling that extended Zone #9 to >500 m vertical.

The Gate

Does the bulk sample deliver grade — and is the underground as continuous as the model says? The whole 2026–27 story rests on 86,500 t from four Zone #9 stopes grading ~8.1 g/t against a resource that averages 3.6 g/t Indicated; a sample that comes in at 4–5 g/t still makes money at US$4,000 gold but kills the 'self-funding' narrative and leaves C$46M of prime+7% secured debt due December 2027. Sub-gates: (1) the Bell Creek toll-milling MOU (Aug 2025, definitive agreement 'in the near term') is still only an MOU 14 months later; (2) the 2022 PEA is stale on costs — capex C$150M and AISC US$987/oz are 2021 numbers — so the updated PEA has no date and could show much higher capex; (3) a going-concern note sits in every filing despite the 'fully funded for 2026' message, and the Pan American facility matures 24 months after Dec 2025.

DepositInd 4.05 Mt @ 3.63 g/t (472 koz) + Inf 11.8 Mt @ 2.87 g/t (1.09 Moz) at 1.6 g/t cut-off, underground (eff. 10 Jan 2022)West Cache (100%, ~11,600 ha, >5 km strike, 13 km west of Timmins on the Porcupine-Destor): Indicated 4,051 kt @ 3.63 g/t = 472 koz; Inferred 11,788 kt @ 2.87 g/t = 1,088 koz (1.6 g/t cut-off, P&E, eff. 10 Jan 2022). Zone #9 is the high-grade core: 2026 holes WC-26-237 16.07 g/t over 9.25 m (within 4.07 g/t over 40.9 m), WC-26-241 6.80 g/t over 19.45 m (within 4.72 g/t over 29.05 m), WC-26-239 6.25 g/t over 10.2 m, WC-26-246 2.52 g/t over 26.5 m; the corridor now spans >500 m vertical, open up- and down-dip. 36 holes of an 18,000 m programme drilled by 7 Oct 2026 (21 holes/11,000 m by end-July). Metallurgy: up to 98% recovery (SGS, 2024). Company says <10% of the property is drill-tested; 3% Newmont NSR repurchased Dec 2025 (C$11M).
NPV : capex2022: NPV(after-tax)/capex 1.6× at US$1,700. At today's gold the ratio would be far higher, but capex must be re-based first.
Valuation Anchor

At ~US$131M basic (EV ~US$135M after C$32M cash and ~C$29M debt) the market pays ~US$85/oz on 1.56 Moz, or ~US$280/oz Indicated — mid-range for an Ontario underground developer, and roughly 0.5–0.8× the stale 2022 after-tax NAV before any gold-price uplift. The price also embeds the bulk sample: 22,600 oz at US$4,180 is ~C$130M gross, 70% of the market cap, if the 8.1 g/t model holds. Peers: Emperor (Québec, 1.46 Moz Inferred) ~US$40/oz; Timmins-camp producers Pan American (Bell Creek/Timmins West) are the natural buyer.

Shareholder structure

Pan American Silver 14.6% basic (19.8M sh; 19.6% fully diluted with 9.4M warrants and the C$8M convertible; approved as control person May 2026, 99.8% in favour). Eric Sprott ~14% (19.0M sh; was controlling shareholder Jan 2020; bought C$3M at C$0.60 Dec 2025). Management and board ~4% (Russell 1.76M sh = 1.3%; Kofman, Agustina, Buchan, Hobart, O'Neil small). Deck also names Michael Gentile and family offices; institutions ~2% (BMO AM 1.3%, Timelo 0.85%). Insiders bought ~C$0.33M in the Dec 2025 placement and small open-market lots (Russell C$4.4k Nov 2025 and May 2026; Agustina C$6.9k May 2026). No insider sales found.

Read: Two deep-pocketed anchors (a major and Sprott) own ~29%, which de-risks financing but also caps the public float and makes a Pan American takeout the likely end-game.

Jurisdiction risk

National: Canada, Ontario — tier-one; Timmins is a century-old camp with Bell Creek mill 40 km away. Local: mining lease registered 2022; advanced-exploration closure plan accepted for filing Apr 2025 (C$1.39M financial assurance); Category 2 and 3 water permits Mar 2026; hydro line energised Apr 2026. Permitting took 2022–25 (first bulk-sample permit updates Aug 2022), which is the main reason the bulk sample is two years behind the 2024 plan.

Low jurisdiction risk; the permitting delay is history, not a live threat.

Differentiator

A funded, permitted underground bulk sample at a 1.56 Moz Timmins deposit with a major as lender, 15–20% shareholder and mill partner. Few C$200M gold developers are already underground with a mill 40 km away and no royalty on the resource area.

The strategic backing is the edge; the stale 2022 study and the grade gap between sample (8 g/t) and resource (3.6 g/t) are the weaknesses.

Exploration upside

Zone #9 open >500 m vertical, <10% of 11,600 ha drilled · moves the needle: medium-high 2026 infill/step-out drilling (18,000 m planned, 36 holes by Oct) has confirmed the Zone #9 high-grade core down-dip and extended the corridor to >500 m vertical with intercepts like 16.07 g/t over 9.25 m; step-outs around the core return 1–2.5 g/t over 18–26 m. Soil sampling and geophysics (2025) outline new targets along >5 km of strike. Resource growth is plausible but the near-term value is conversion to Indicated for the updated PEA, not a new discovery.

Next Catalyst

Ramp development to the first Zone #9 stope and the start of bulk-sample extraction (undated; the company will 'provide updates as development advances'), then a definitive toll-milling agreement with Pan American's Bell Creek mill and first gold sales; the updated PEA (initiated 6 Oct 2026) has no date.

Open Questions
  • What grade and tonnage does the first stope actually deliver versus the 8.13 g/t / 22,600 oz model, and when is first ore trucked to Bell Creek?
  • How much has been drawn on the Pan American facility since the C$11M December draw, and what does the all-in cost of the underground development (Aki-Dumas contract) look like against the C$67M available?
  • Will the updated PEA re-base capex and AISC to 2026 costs, and does it convert enough Inferred to Indicated to support a feasibility study in 2027?
  • Why is a C$46M facility maturing December 2027 the right capital structure for a company whose updated study is undated — refinancing or equity before then?

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 4/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 3/5

Russell has built a Timmins mine before (Black Fox) and has carried West Cache from shell to ramp with Sprott and now Pan American behind him, but Apollo ended in a debt crisis and dilution and Fire River ended with the creditor; the bulk sample is two years behind the 2024 plan and the toll-milling deal is 14 months past 'near term'. Capable, persistent, not yet proven to protect shareholders through a build.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

R. David Russell (President, CEO & Chairman, since CEO of Pure Nickel/Galleon since Jan 2019; director >12 years before that): Mining engineer (Montana Tech). Founder, President & CEO Apollo Gold 2002–Jun 2010 (built Black Fox, Timmins camp, into production 2009); earlier VP/COO Getchell Gold (sold to Placer Dome 1999), VP US Ops LAC Minerals, Hecla, Independence. Track record
  • Russell: Apollo Gold 2002–2010 — put Black Fox (Timmins camp) into commercial production May 2009 on a US$70M Macquarie/RMB project facility, but missed the US$9.3M (Sep 2009) and US$6.0M (Dec 2009) repayments, hedged 250,420 oz at ~US$876, reported a 2009 net loss of US$61.7M, put Montana Tunnels on care and maintenance and sold it for notes, and merged with Linear Gold at C$0.40/share in June 2010 (became Brigus, later bought by Primero). A mine built, shareholders diluted hard (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000938113/000114420410013956/v177510_10k.htm; https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachrichten-2019-01/45699961-pure-nickel-provides-corporate-update-296.htm)
  • Russell: Fire River Gold (Nixon Fork, Alaska) — non-executive chair, interim CEO from Jun 2012; operations suspended Jun 2013 and the mine assets passed to creditor Waterton in 2014 — loss (https://sedar-filings-primary.thecse.com/00027349/1206272343020603.pdf; https://groundtruthalaska.org/articles/NixonForkMine/)
  • Russell/Galleon: took Pure Nickel from a shell (Jan 2019) through the Explor merger (Dec 2019) to a West Cache discovery (Zone #9, 2020), resource (2021), PEA (Jan 2022), mining lease (2022), closure plan (Apr 2025), C$91.5M of 2025 financing with Pan American and Sprott, and ramp development (Sep 2026) — delivered, with Sprott's support throughoutsource
  • Share price C$0.24 (early 2025) to C$1.37 (Oct 2026) while shares doubled from 68M to 136M — shareholders who held through have done well in this cyclesource

Boards today: Russell: combined Chair+CEO at Galleon; no other current public roles found. Directors Kofman, O'Neil, Hobart, Nanna — outside roles not checked.

Fit to this job
Stage: ramp development and bulk sample at an underground Timmins deposit — exactly what Russell did at Black Fox 70 km east, and the Apollo-era financing troubles are the cautionary half of that experience. Deposit: orogenic underground gold, Timmins — yes. Region: Ontario — yes. The bench is thin: no COO since Jun 2024; underground execution rests on contractor Aki-Dumas and Pan American's services agreement.
Skin & pay
3/5 — meaningful stake bought largely in placements at C$0.60, small open-market adds, no selling; not large against a C$187M cap. Russell 1.76M shares (~1.3%, ~C$2.4M) — bought C$50k at C$0.60 in the Dec 2025 placement and ~C$4.4k open-market lots in Nov 2025 and May 2026; management and board ~4% fully diluted (deck); insiders put C$3.3M into the Dec 2025 placement (incl. Kofman C$100k, Agustina C$100k, Buchan C$51k). No sales found. Options 10.0M (C$0.19–0.98). Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Combined Chair+CEO; small board; no COO since 2024 at the moment the company goes underground.
  • Key-management pay C$3.0M for six months to May 2026 (C$1.18M cash, C$1.82M share-based) on a ~C$150–190M company; C$1.8M owed to officers (likely deferred pay — unverified).
  • Going-concern note in every filing while messaging says 'fully funded'; C$2.5M of accrued penalties and Part XII.6 taxes (flow-through) on the books.
  • Pan American is lender, mill owner and 15–20% shareholder — alignment, but also a position to buy the company cheaply if the bulk sample stumbles.
  • The bulk-sample grade (8.13 g/t) is a non-43-101 stope model more than double the resource grade; the company has never said what a disappointing grade would mean.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash went from C$0.5M at 28 Feb 2025 (working-capital deficit C$3.8M, debenture interest being paid in shares) to C$32.1M at 31 May 2026 after C$15.5M of convertible debentures in Jul–Aug 2025, the C$30M unit placement of 4 Dec 2025 (C$28.3M net; Pan American Silver took 18.75M units) and an C$11M first draw on the C$46M Pan American credit facility. The discrete Q2 FY26 (Mar–May 2026) outflow was C$10.3M (operating 2.5, capitalised development/drilling 6.9, facility interest and fees 0.6, Golden Trove instalment 0.3), so the 31 May balance covers roughly three quarters at that rate — to about February 2027 — before counting the C$35M undrawn facility; underground ramp development started 21 Sep 2026, so the burn is rising, and payables already stood at C$8.2M (C$1.8M of it owed to officers).
  2. Where the money went in the first half of FY26 (Dec 2025–May 2026): C$11.0M to buy back the 3% NSR (debt-funded), C$8.2M into the ground (box cut, surface works, permitting, 11,000 m of drilling), about C$3.0M of operating outflow against C$2.0M of cash G&A (the rest is HST receivable and prepaid build on construction spend), and C$1.4M of facility fees, interest and transaction costs. Cash overhead has doubled year on year (6M G&A ex-SBC C$2.0M vs C$1.0M) and share-based compensation jumped to C$2.0M in the half (C$1.6M in Q1 alone); key-management remuneration was C$3.0M for the six months.
  3. This is a leveraged developer, not a clean explorer: C$27.4M of carrying debt at 31 May 2026 (C$15.9M of convertible debentures in four series at C$0.165–0.45, C$10.6M drawn on the Pan American facility at prime + 7% = 11.45% maturing 30 Dec 2027, C$0.9M vendor take-back mortgage with C$300k instalments from 17 Oct 2026) plus a C$2.5M CRA penalty/Part XII.6 provision that accrues interest. Finance and accretion expense was C$2.7M in the half, more than the cash G&A; the 2024 debentures (C$2.8M) are current and secured by stockpile gold.
  4. Dilution: 63.5M shares at Nov 2023, 67.2M at Nov 2024, 77.3M at Nov 2025, 135.6M at 29 Jul 2026, with 34.4M warrants (C$0.185–0.75), 10.0M options and debentures convertible into roughly 55–60M more shares; fully diluted the count is about 240M. Pan American Silver is a related party and approved control person (AGM 20 May 2026), with its Dec 2025 participation under OSC review because minority approval was not obtained.
  5. Unusual items: the CRA has reassessed flow-through renunciations inherited from the 2019 Explor amalgamation (shortfalls of about C$3.8M for 2011–13 and C$2.3M for 2016–17; Tax Court appeal pending); the FY25 result was flattered by a C$0.75M gain on selling a royalty for US$700k when cash was near zero; every annual audit (Doane Grant Thornton) carries a going-concern paragraph; FY24 included a C$1.1M swing in the fair value of the debenture conversion derivative. An updated PEA was commissioned from Hard Rock Consulting on 6 Oct 2026 with no completion date.

A 204 koz gold-antimony deposit with a 17% IRR PEA, 95% of a 2 Moz historic goldfield, and an undrilled target 3 km from OceanaGold's 17 g/t WKP — priced at US$480/oz AuEq, three weeks before an election (7 Nov 2026) that could revoke the fast-track it depends on

Gate Whether New Zealand's fast-track survives the 7 November election — and whether a 204 koz, 5.5-year, 17%-IRR deposit is a mine or a resource. The 1News-Verian poll of Sep 23–27 has the left bloc (Labour 28, Greens 16, TOP 6) at 65 seats against 59 for the governing right; the Greens have pledged to revoke fast-track approvals and oppose mining on conservation land, and Auld Creek's access adit sits on DOC land. A change of government lands before Rua's panel decision (~Q2 2027). Sub-gates: (1) the economics — NPV US$42M on US$133M of capex at the base deck is a 0.3× project; it only clears the Rule bar at spot gold and a US$27,000/t antimony price that has since halved in China (US$13,300) and is US$19,250 in Europe; mineable shapes in the PEA are 22–27% below the headline ounces and it relies on Inferred; (2) the vein system — 0.6 m at 136 g/t AuEq headlines against a 3.7 g/t Inferred bulk grade: nuggety, narrow, orogenic; the MRE update must convert Inferred to Indicated, not just add ounces; (3) the treasury — C$29.6M at June against a C$17–20M/yr burn and 9,000 m at Glamorgan; the company itself guides C$10–15M by Q2 2027 and 'may need to secure additional financing' — a raise is coming, probably on Glamorgan results or the PFS; (4) the Siren overhang — Siren Gold holds 11.4% in escrow releasing through November and has started selling (700k @ C$1.15, Aug 27); (5) antimony marketing — a separate Sb concentrate to four unnamed metal traders, unproven at scale.

Partly funded to the next catalyst Funded through the MRE, the PFS, the fast-track application and the first Glamorgan programme — not beyond mid-2027. The MD&A says it: 'may need to secure additional financing.' Expect a C$15–30M raise in H1 2027, timed to Glamorgan results or the PFS, ideally before the Siren block is fully out. The mine (US$133M) is a separate question two years away.
Thesis

Rua consolidated the Reefton Goldfield (South Island; >2 Moz produced historically at 9–50 g/t) by buying Siren Gold's assets in Nov 2024 for A$20M in shares, taking its ground from 34,000 to ~125,000 ha. The flagship is Auld Creek, a gold-antimony orogenic system 3 km south of Reefton: MRE (Feb 2026) Indicated 54 koz + Inferred 150 koz AuEq at 3.7–5.7 g/t, ~1 km of strike, >500 m deep, open in every direction; and a PEA (Apr 2026): 250 ktpa underground, 5.5 years, ~27 koz AuEq/yr, capex US$133M, AISC US$1,850, after-tax NPV5% US$42M and IRR 17% at US$3,300 Au / US$27,000/t Sb, US$113M and 36% at US$4,700. Antimony (~30% of revenue; a listed critical mineral) is recovered by non-cyanide flotation into a separate concentrate. 2026: 19,600 m drilled at Auld Creek with up to six rigs — 0.6 m @ 82.9 g/t Au + 24.8% Sb (136 g/t AuEq), 2.9 m @ 38.8 AuEq, 32 m @ 2.4 AuEq, first visible gold — 18 holes pending; updated MRE Q4 2026 targeting >300 koz AuEq and a PFS in December; second Reefton deposit (Alexander River / Big River / Supreme, ~340 koz Inferred) into a hub-and-spoke plan Q1 2027. Permitting via the Fast-track Approvals Act: Auld Creek referred by the Minister Jul 29, 2026; substantive application October; decision ~Q2 2027 — OceanaGold's WKP went through in ~112 days. Glamorgan (North Island): 46 km², never drilled, >4 km of Au–As soil anomalies and >40 g/t rock chips, 3 km from WKP (1.46 Moz @ 17.3 g/t); nine pads approved Aug 4; 9,000 m with two rigs from Q4 2026, results Q2 2027.

Cash C$29.6M (Jun 30) after a C$33M raise at C$1.10 in January (no warrants; Franklin Templeton 6%); TSX and NZX listings Feb 2026. CEO Rob Eckford (ex-Aris CFO), chair Oliver Lennox-King (Roxgold, Teranga; 6% holder), COO Simon Henderson (credited with the WKP discovery). Stock C$1.37 (10 Oct 2026), roughly double a year ago; consensus target C$2.37.

The Gate

Whether New Zealand's fast-track survives the 7 November election — and whether a 204 koz, 5.5-year, 17%-IRR deposit is a mine or a resource. The 1News-Verian poll of Sep 23–27 has the left bloc (Labour 28, Greens 16, TOP 6) at 65 seats against 59 for the governing right; the Greens have pledged to revoke fast-track approvals and oppose mining on conservation land, and Auld Creek's access adit sits on DOC land. A change of government lands before Rua's panel decision (~Q2 2027).

Sub-gates
  1. The economics — NPV US$42M on US$133M of capex at the base deck is a 0.3× project; it only clears the Rule bar at spot gold and a US$27,000/t antimony price that has since halved in China (US$13,300) and is US$19,250 in Europe; mineable shapes in the PEA are 22–27% below the headline ounces and it relies on Inferred.
  2. The vein system — 0.6 m at 136 g/t AuEq headlines against a 3.7 g/t Inferred bulk grade: nuggety, narrow, orogenic; the MRE update must convert Inferred to Indicated, not just add ounces.
  3. The treasury — C$29.6M at June against a C$17–20M/yr burn and 9,000 m at Glamorgan; the company itself guides C$10–15M by Q2 2027 and 'may need to secure additional financing' — a raise is coming, probably on Glamorgan results or the PFS.
  4. The Siren overhang — Siren Gold holds 11.4% in escrow releasing through November and has started selling (700k @ C$1.15, Aug 27).
  5. Antimony marketing — a separate Sb concentrate to four unnamed metal traders, unproven at scale.

Two gates on one card: an election that could close the permitting door, and a study that says the flagship is marginal without the antimony price it was written at.

Satellites: Supreme 0.9 m @ 26.9 g/t; Caledonian 4.0 m @ 6.9 g/t. Glamorgan: no drilling yet — 4,137 soils, Au–As anomalies over >4 km (Sutcliff 1.3 km, Wires Ridge 2.1 km, Tairua 1.6 km), rock chips >40 g/t Au and >200 g/t Ag, CSAMT done.
NPV : capex0.3× at the base deck; ~0.9× at spot — fails the Rule test at base, marginal at spot. IRR 17% fails the 25% bar at base, passes at spot. EV per AuEq ounce: ~US$480 on 204 koz; ~US$290 on the ~340 koz district total — expensive for Inferred-heavy narrow-vein ounces, cheap only if the Q4 MRE lands at >300 koz and Glamorgan hits. Compare Santana (Bendigo-Ophir, 2.34 Moz, PFS NPV A$1.5B, decision Oct 29) for what the market pays a NZ developer with a real study.
Valuation Anchor

~US$480 per AuEq ounce on a 204 koz resource; a PEA whose NPV at spot roughly equals the EV; and an undrilled Glamorgan worth, on the market's arithmetic, nothing. That last point is the case: at C$164M the market pays for Auld Creek plus optimism, and Glamorgan — 3 km from a 1.46 Moz, 17 g/t deposit that OceanaGold just consented, found by the same geologist who is Rua's COO — is the free option.

The re-rate path: Q4 MRE >300 koz with Indicated conversion → PFS with a better base case → fast-track decision Q2 2027 → Glamorgan's first holes (results Q2 2027). Any one of those is 1.5×; Glamorgan hitting WKP-style grade is the multi-bagger, and nothing else on the card is.

The bear case starts on Nov 7: a Labour-Greens government revokes or stalls fast-track, the PFS confirms a 17% IRR, Siren finishes selling, and the company raises at C$0.90 in mid-2027 to drill Glamorgan anyway.

Bucket: grade / discovery / optionality — the Argenta archetype with a study attached: the study says 'marginal', the district says 'maybe'.

Shareholder structure
Management & board
D&O ~8.0%. Chair Oliver Lennox-King 6.88M shares / ~6% — C$2.3M bought over twelve months incl. C$1M in the Jun 2025 placement and 1.39M shares at C$0.18 in Oct 2024; the largest insider. CEO Rob Eckford 581k shares + 2.2M options; bought 19,000 in Jul 2026. COO Simon Henderson (WKP discovery). 7.66M options at C$0.60–1.43. Interim CFO Darren Prins (Sep 2026, CFO on leave).
Insider activity (12 mo)
Net buyers. Lennox-King's placement participation and open-market buys; Eckford 19k (Jul 2026); insiders took 1.53M shares in the Jun 2025 raise. No insider selling found. The selling is the Siren Gold block: 700k @ C$1.15 on Aug 27 with escrow releases through November.
Strategic & prominent
Siren Gold (ASX) 11.4% — vendor paper, not strategic, and selling. Konwave 7.2%, Franklin Templeton 6.05%, Mackenzie 2.3%, IG 1.0%, ICM and Libra named. Eric Sprott and Peter Marrone are cited as holders by one promotional outlet only — no filing found; treat as unverified and <10%. No OceanaGold, Evolution or other producer; no Rule, McEwen, Palisades or Crescat position found.
Institutions / retail
Company: institutions >40% post-January; filings-based: institutions ~11%, Siren 11–12%, insiders ~8%, retail ~69%. 115.6M shares, FD ~125M; a ~6:1 consolidation in 2024–25. 2,153 registered holders at NZX listing.

Read: A chair who has put C$2.3M of his own money in at prices from C$0.18 to C$1.10 is the strongest insider signal in the small-cap set here, and the CEO is buying, not selling. Against that: the largest holder is a vendor with an escrow calendar, the 'Sprott' name attached to this stock in promotional coverage has no filing behind it, and the company has had to answer for paid promotion once already. Read the register, not the newsletters.

Jurisdiction risk

National: the most mining-friendly New Zealand in a generation — for five more weeks. The coalition's Fast-track Approvals Act 2024 delivered OceanaGold's WKP consent in ~112 days (Dec 2025); the Crown Minerals Amendment Act 2025 changed the regulator's purpose from 'manage' to 'promote' and created Tier-3 gold permits; the Minerals Strategy targets NZ$2–3B of mineral exports by 2035; the Conservation Amendment Bill (in committee) would ease disposal of conservation land. Auld Creek was referred into fast-track on Jul 29, 2026 (stage 1 of 6); substantive application October; ~six-month panel; decision ~Q2 2027. The election is Nov 7. The latest poll has the left bloc ahead 65–59; the Greens have pledged to revoke fast-track approvals and oppose mining on conservation land; NZ First wants ministerial veto powers back. Auld Creek's surface is private farmland and Ngāi Tahu forestry, but the access adit is on DOC land, and a minister has previously declined a mine extension in the nearby Victoria Conservation Park.

Local: Reefton is pro-mining (a gold town whose residents lobbied DOC to keep a mine road open in 2025); no iwi opposition found at Reefton. Glamorgan is the reverse — ~15,000 ha of public conservation land in the Coromandel, Coromandel Watchdog's home ground (they fought WKP for a decade and called the fast-track 'stacked against communities, iwi and environment'); Māori consultation was scheduled for March 2026 with no position published.

Two projects, two licences: Reefton is the easy one and Glamorgan is the hard one — and Glamorgan is where the upside is.

Differentiator
  1. Control of a 2 Moz historic goldfield — >95% of Reefton — with a defined deposit, a PEA, six rigs and a permitting path a major has just proven.
  2. Antimony — ~30% of Auld Creek's revenue from a critical mineral with no Western primary supply, which is either a strategic premium or a marketing problem; the PEA assumes the former.
  3. Glamorgan — the last undrilled epithermal target next to WKP, held by the team that found WKP; nothing else in this file has a discovery target with a 17 g/t neighbour.
  4. A clean structure — 116M shares, no investor warrants in the last two raises, Franklin and Konwave on the register, insiders net buyers, the chair with C$2.3M of his own money in.
  5. Timing — MRE, PFS, fast-track application and first Glamorgan holes all land inside the next six months.

Read it honestly: the flagship's study is the weakest economics in the file, and the differentiator that matters (Glamorgan) has no drill hole in it yet.

Exploration upside

Discovery-driven · moves the needle: very high — it is the thesis. Reefton: 19,600 m in 2026, 18 holes pending, Q4 MRE targeting >300 koz AuEq with Indicated conversion; satellites Supreme, Caledonian, Alexander River, Big River, Murray Creek, Capleston feeding a hub-and-spoke plan from Q1 2027. Glamorgan: 9,000 m, two rigs, from Q4 2026, ~US$5M, results Q2 2027 — the first drill test of >4 km of surface anomalies 3 km from WKP. A WKP-style intercept (tens of g/t over metres) is the only path to a multiple that does not depend on gold.

Glamorgan's start already slipped from Q2 to Q4 2026. The first three holes will say more about this stock than the next three years at Auld Creek.

Next Catalyst

Oct 2026: remaining Auld Creek assays; substantive fast-track application. Q4 2026: first Glamorgan drilling; Siren escrow fully released (Nov). Nov 7: NZ general election. Nov 13: Q3 financials. Nov–Dec: updated MRE (>300 koz target) + PFS. Q1 2027: second Reefton deposit into the plan. Q2 2027: Glamorgan results; fast-track panel decision; project-financing talks and, realistically, an equity raise.

  • If the government changes on Nov 7, what happens to a referred-but-undecided fast-track application — grandfathered, stalled, or revoked?
  • Who are the four antimony offtake groups, and what does a Western Sb concentrate actually fetch versus the China price?
  • When does the company raise, at what price, and does Siren's 11.4% come out first?
  • What is Glamorgan's first-pass drill plan — depth, target, how many holes before a go/no-go?

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 2/5 · Candour 2/5 · Skin in the game 3/5low confidence

The chairman's exits and C$2.3M of market buying are real; the executives guided an Auld Creek resource they then missed by a wide margin and called a 17%-IRR study 'positive'. Candour 2.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Robert Eckford (CEO & director, since Apr 2024): Ex-CFO of Aris Gold (Caldas Gold) which merged into Aris Mining 2022; company bio says 'co-founder and CFO of Aris Mining' · Oliver Lennox-King (Non-executive Chairman, since 2024): Ex-chair Fronteer Gold (sold to Newmont ~US$2.3B, 2011) and Roxgold (merged into Fortuna ~C$1.1B, 2021); chair Pangea Goldfields, Aurora Uranium · Simon Henderson (COO & director, since 2024): NZ exploration geologist, orogenic/epithermal specialist; local stakeholder relationships · Simon Delander (VP Risk, Stakeholder & Regulatory Affairs, since unverified): Ex-VP at Endura Mining (formerly Federation Mining, Snowy River NZ) — ran its permitting
Track record
  • Lennox-King: two large exits as chairman — Fronteer to Newmont (2011, top of cycle) and Roxgold to Fortuna (2021, mid-cycle); Roxgold actually built and ran Yaramokosource
  • Eckford: finance executive (CFO Aris Gold/Caldas, Marmato Colombia), not a mine builder or discoverer; first CEO role (https://ruagold.com/team/; https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsx-rua/rua-gold-shares/management)
  • Rua formed 2024 (Reefton Resources + Siren Gold merger, per prior knowledge — unverified); NZX secondary listing Feb 2026; Auld Creek PEA May 2026: after-tax NPV5 US$42M, IRR 17%, capex US$133M, 5.5-yr life, ~27koz AuEq/yr at US$3,300 goldsource
  • Auld Creek accepted into NZ fast-track approvals (Jul 2026); PFS targeted Q4 2026, permits Q2 2027source
  • Director Richard Thomas was COO of Aris Mining; Tyron Breytenbach was SVP Capital Markets at Aris — the board is an Aris alumni groupsource

Boards today: Eckford: 1 (Rua). Lennox-King: Rua chair plus other chairmanships (Pangea Goldfields, Aurora Uranium) — at least 3, exact count unverified. Breytenbach is CEO of Lithium Africa Resources.

Fit to this job
Stage: early explorer with a thin PEA, aiming to become a small gold-antimony producer in New Zealand. The chair's wins came from large discoveries sold to majors, not from building small mines; the CEO is a CFO by trade. Nobody on the executive has built or run a mine in New Zealand; the NZ permitting experience is Delander (Endura/Federation) and Henderson's local network. New for them: everything from PFS to permitting under NZ's fast-track regime, antimony marketing, and a 5.5-year-life project whose economics barely clear a 17% IRR at US$3,300 gold.
Skin & pay
3/5 — meaningful stake, mostly founder stock or grants; not selling. Eckford ~0.54% (~C$0.8M); chairman Lennox-King bought ~C$2.3M of shares in the market over the trailing 12 months — the best open-market buying signal in this batch. CEO total comp 2025 C$664k (40% salary, 60% bonus/stock/options) — high for a C$150M explorer. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsx-rua/rua-gold-shares/management. Circular not fetched.

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Resource delivered at roughly a quarter of the ounces guided three months earlier
  • CEO comp C$664k at a ~C$150M market cap (0.4% of cap) with 60% in equity awards
  • CEO owns only 0.54% — alignment comes from the chair, not the CEO

Thesis

Santa Ana is one of the few primary-silver resources of real grade left in a junior: 1.79 Mt @ 519 g/t AgEq Indicated plus 2.35 Mt @ 369 g/t Inferred (57.8 Moz AgEq, 13 vein systems, 130,000 m drilled), with a dozen more known veins undrilled on a 17 km corridor and a stated 100 Moz goal. The market is paying ~US$1.7/oz AgEq (US$97M cap) with silver at ~US$61 and the resource priced at US$40, because the veins are narrow, the project is in Tolima, and the first PEA has yet to start (the company says it begins after the end-October 2026 technical report). If the PEA (early 2027) shows a small 800–1,000 tpd underground mine making money at anything near today's prices and the social situation in Falán calms, the re-rate is from a very low base.

The Gate

Getting a narrow-vein mine permitted and accepted in Falán, Tolima The resource is real; the gate is social and regulatory. Falán, which hosts the core veins, was declared an Área de Protección para la Producción de Alimentos (APPA, ~12,900 ha) by the Agriculture Ministry in February 2026, and campesinos have run a blockade of the subsidiary Minerales Santa Ana at Santa Filomena since 27 May 2026. The company holds exploration-stage concession contracts (HFL-151 valid to 2040); on 15 Oct 2026 the mining agency (ANM) approved the work plan (PTO) for a 40 t/d pilot mine on La Porfía, and the environmental study is filed with CORTOLIMA (licence hoped for early 2027). The pilot's cost and funding are not given. Sub-gates: (1) the PEA must show the 0.9 m veins can be mined at a sensible cost (the MRE already assumes US$65–110/t mining); (2) cash — ~C$15M at 1 Aug 2026 against ~C$5M a quarter of burn, so a raise is due before or around the PEA.

Cut-offs 95 g/t (long-hole) and 130 g/t (cut-and-fill), 79:1 AgEq, recoveries 96.3% Ag / 98.5% Au into a 4,187 g/t Ag concentrate. Best 2026 holes: DH637 2.30 m @ 1,760 g/t Ag + 5.14 g/t Au (2,214 g/t AgEq) at Las Maras; DH652 0.22 m @ 5,196 g/t Ag; DH648 5.28 m @ 188 g/t AgEq incl. 0.4 m @ 2,693 g/t at the new 'Shoot 7'; DH613 0.34 m @ 2,559 g/t AgEq at Morena; DH604 0.80 m @ 1,405 g/t AgEq at Aguilar. Land: >28,000 ha of titles and applications in the Mariquita district, 17 km corridor titled (11 concession contracts in Falán and Frías; HFL-151 to Apr 2040). Also Mallama (Nariño, indigenous consulta previa pending) and Oribella (Antioquia) — non-core.
NPV : capexn/a — no study. The screen today is EV/oz by category: ~US$1.5/oz AgEq on all ounces (US$97M less ~US$8M cash ÷ 57.8 Moz), ~US$3/oz on Indicated.
Valuation Anchor

~US$1.5–1.7/oz AgEq in the ground is at the bottom of the silver-developer range (peers with PEAs and friendlier addresses trade at US$3–8/oz). The market is pricing Colombia-plus-blockade and the narrow veins, not the grade. At today's ~US$61 silver the Indicated rock is worth ~US$1,000/t in situ against ~US$160/t of all-in site cost in the MRE assumptions, so a PEA at even US$45–50 silver should show wide margins; the discount is whether anyone believes it can be built in Falán. Bucket: grade.

Shareholder structure

Eric Sprott (2176423 Ontario) 91.7M shares / 18.6% — bought mostly in placements (C$5M at C$0.35 in Oct 2025, led the Mar 2025 offering, earlier buys); Jupiter Fund Management 42.9M / 8.7% (C$15M at C$0.35, Oct 2025); ALPS 1.4%; other institutions small; retail ~70%. Management and board own very little: Hebert ~1.7M (0.35%), Nishi 130k, Sujir 100k, Harris ~50k per Simply Wall St (unverified), Bruggeman 1M inducement shares vesting plus 1M options at C$0.36. Insider trades in 2026 are all sales near the highs: Nishi 370k at C$0.48–0.50 (Jan–Feb), VP Exploration Hernandez Pineda 135k at C$0.60 (Jan, exercised at C$0.16); no open-market buys found. At the Jan 2026 AGM ~36% of votes were withheld from every director and 37% voted against the option plan.

Read: Two deep-pocket holders own 27% and set the price of any raise; management has almost no cash in the stock and sold into the January peak.

Jurisdiction risk

National: Colombia under the Petro government (to Aug 2026) was hostile to new mining; a new government took office in August 2026 and media report it repealed ten restrictive mining resolutions in September 2026 (unverified). Concession contracts run exploration → construction → exploitation; a PTO goes to the ANM and an environmental licence to CORTOLIMA (under 2 Mt/yr) or ANLA. Outcrop is still in exploration (HFL-151 valid to 2040); the PTO for a 40 t/d pilot was approved by the ANM on 15 Oct 2026 and the environmental study is with CORTOLIMA (licence hoped for early 2027). Local: Tolima is the department that stopped AngloGold's La Colosa by consulta popular (Cajamarca, 2017). Falán was declared an APPA (food-production protection area, ~12,897 ha) by MinAgricultura Resolution 052 in Feb 2026; a tutela by >1,000 campesinos against it was dismissed in Jan 2026, and local press alleges Minerales Santa Ana helped collect the signatures. Campesinos have blockaded company vehicles and staff at Santa Filomena since 27 May 2026; the company (29 May statement in Colombian press) rejected 'violence and threats' and said it would attend a 6 June community meeting. The mayor of Falán and the Tolima governor oppose the APPA. A community leader was killed in 2023 amid mining-related disputes. The company reports ~130 employees, 85% local, and 170 land-use agreements in 2025.

This is the discount: Colombia plus an active local conflict, and none of it appears in the company's own 2026 releases as far as I could find.

Differentiator

Grade and district scale in silver. 519 g/t AgEq Indicated inside mining shapes is rare in a listed junior, the veins carry bonanza shoots (DH637 2.3 m @ 2,214 g/t AgEq; DH652 5,196 g/t Ag), metallurgy is simple (96%/98.5% recovery to a high-grade concentrate), and 12 known veins are still undrilled on a 17 km corridor. Two serious holders (Sprott 18.6%, Jupiter 8.7%) and a CEO who chaired AbraSilver through its re-rate add credibility to the capital-markets side.

The same narrow veins that give the grade make this a selective, higher-cost underground mine — the PEA will show how much of the headline grade survives.

Exploration upside

District-scale, 12 undrilled veins, open along strike · moves the needle: medium The 2026 programme (35,000 m, four rigs) keeps finding new shoots by structural prediction (Shoot 7 at Santa Ana, no surface expression) and new veins (Morena, Aguilar N). But the 2023–26 yield was ~283 oz AgEq per metre and the Indicated grade fell; the company's 100 Moz goal needs ~95,000 more metres (~C$40M, 2–3 years) by its own arithmetic. Growth is believable; it is also expensive and has already been partly priced into a US$97M cap.

Next Catalyst

NI 43-101 technical report for the Sep 2026 MRE by ~29 Oct 2026; remaining 2026 assays through Q4; PEA results early 2027 (CEO guidance in interviews); FY2026 results ~mid-Dec 2026; pilot-plant permitting; a financing.

Open Questions
  • What does the PEA assume for mining width, dilution and cost on 0.9 m veins — and does the mined grade stay above ~400 g/t AgEq?
  • Is the Santa Filomena blockade still in place, which veins does it affect, and what does the Falán APPA designation legally mean for an exploitation licence on existing titles?
  • What does the 40 t/d pilot mine and plant cost, and who funds it — the company has not said?
  • Who will fund the next C$10–20M — Sprott and Jupiter again at a lower price, or a strategic (Coeur, Hochschild, Pan American) that wants Colombian silver?
  • Why did ~36% of votes withhold from every director in January 2026, and has the board addressed it?
Context & updates
15 Oct 2026 update

Colombia's mining agency (ANM) approved the technical work plan (PTO) for concession HFL-151: a pilot underground mine and plant of up to 40 t/d on the La Porfía vein. The environmental study has been filed with CORTOLIMA; the company expects the licence in early 2027 and targets first pilot production in 2027. This closes one regulatory sub-gate (the PTO was missing), but the pilot is small, its cost and funding are not given, and the release does not address the APPA food-protection area over Falán or the Santa Filomena blockade. A PEA for a medium-scale mine starts after the resource technical report (due end of October). Odds unchanged at ~12%.

Management review
Creal weaknesses: slipped dates, thin fit or thin candourTrack record 3/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 2/5 · Skin in the game 1/5

A new CEO with a real re-rate behind him (AbraSilver) and a Chair who knows Colombia, but the record at this company is a slipped and softer resource, directors selling at the top, a large grant package on the day of the CEO change, related-party fees, a protest vote at the AGM, and a local conflict that is in the Colombian press and not in the company's releases. Real weaknesses, not yet a pattern of failing shareholders; Bruggeman gets a clean sheet for the PEA.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

Fit to this job
Stage: resource-to-PEA, first mine study — Bruggeman has financed and promoted exactly this stage (AbraSilver) but has never built a mine; Harris, now Chair, is the engineer with Colombian operating experience. Deposit: narrow-vein underground silver in Colombia — the team has no narrow-vein mine-building record; the PEA consultant will matter. Region: Colombia yes (Harris, Alvarez, Torres, Colombian subsidiary with ~130 staff); the Falán social problem is the test and it is unsolved. New for them: permitting an exploitation project under an APPA designation.
Skin & pay
1/5 — under ~0.5% held by management, grants not purchases, directors net sellers at the highs while the company was promoting. Thin. Management and board hold well under 1% in aggregate on my reading (Hebert ~1.7M shares, Nishi 130k, Sujir 100k, Harris ~50k per Simply Wall St — unverified; Bruggeman 1M inducement shares vesting over a year plus 1M options at C$0.36, none bought). 2026 insider activity is all selling: Nishi 370k at C$0.48–0.50 (Jan–Feb), Hernandez Pineda 135k at C$0.60 (Jan) after exercising at C$0.16; Hebert sold ~1.4M in 2025 at C$0.20–0.21. Sprott's 18.6% and Jupiter's 8.7% are strategic blocks, not management skin. Pay: key management C$1.46M for nine months to May 2026 against a C$138M cap. Red flags
  • A six-month resource slip that was re-dated in passing, followed by a lower-grade result and a 20% fall.
  • Directors and the then-VP Exploration sold stock at C$0.48–0.60 in Jan–Feb 2026, within weeks of the high; no insider has bought in the market in 2026 as far as found.
  • The Falán APPA designation, the dismissed tutela (with press allegations the subsidiary helped collect signatures) and the Santa Filomena blockade do not appear in the company's own disclosure as far as I could find.
  • ~36% withhold on every director and 37% against the option plan at the Jan 2026 AGM — a protest vote the company did not explain.
  • Related-party fees of C$1.07M in nine months (legal, corporate services) on a company spending C$2.9M of G&A; key-management pay C$1.46M in nine months (~C$1.95M a year, ~1.4% of the cap) plus a large April 2026 grant package.
  • Two VPs resigned on the day of the CEO change.

A very high-grade, very small silver deposit that four larger companies drilled and walked away from — now re-drilled at 45,000 m a year on Giustra and Elsztain money, with the market pricing it at ~US$1.50 per Indicated ounce

Gate Proving there is a mine here, not just a vein — and doing it before the money runs out. Yaxtché's 3.2 Mt is a 6-year mine at 1,500 tpd; Golden Minerals' 2018 PEA put the NPV at US$45M, and neither Hochschild, Golden nor Barrick chose to build it. The updated MRE is guided H1 2027 and any economic study ~Q4 2028 — a long runway on ~C$2.3M/month of burn against ~C$24M, which means a financing in 2027 on a stock that has fallen 61% from its February high with C$0.80 LIFE paper and C$0.60 warrants underwater. Sub-gates: (1) tonnage — 45,000 m has to turn Mani-Copan and the step-outs into tens of millions of new ounces, not just spectacular metre-intervals; (2) concentrate quality — historic concentrates carried As/Sb/Bi penalties and recovery varied by zone; the Sep 2026 tests are encouraging but not locked-cycle; (3) altitude and logistics — 4,800 m, 50–200 mm of rain, seasonal access, Puna water; (4) the sellers — both strategic holders and two directors have been net sellers since Sep 2025 (data-vendor sourced, unverified against SEDI), and nobody inside bought in 2026.

Thesis

El Quevar, at 4,800 m in Salta's Puna, was found by Apex Silver (2004), advanced by Hochschild, Golden Minerals (2009–24) and Barrick (earn-in 2020–24, US$6M spent, withdrew) — 414 holes and >US$100M of inflation-adjusted spend — before Argenta (ex-Butte Energy) bought 100% for US$3.5M cash, no royalty to the vendor, in Oct 2024.

What it bought is Yaxtché: 2.93 Mt @ 482 g/t Ag for 45.3 Moz Indicated + 4.1 Moz Inferred — grade among the highest of any undeveloped silver resource, tonnage among the smallest — plus a 100-person camp, a 1,250 m decline, roads, water permits and an approved exploration EIA.

The thesis is that the previous owners explored 3–5% of a 57,000 ha property looking for a bulk-tonnage system, and that a high-grade vein-and-breccia district is what is actually there: the 2025/26 programme (25,500 m since May 2025, upsized three times to 45,000 m for 2026) has extended Yaxtché ~270 m and found Mani-Copan (4,982 g/t over 7.5 m, 500 m south), a Au-Cu system at Carmen (0.57 g/t Au + 0.58% Cu over 44 m), and 20+ untested targets. Sep 2026 metallurgy: 95% average rougher recovery, concentrates to 14,857 g/t.

Cash C$30M at Jun 30 (working capital ~C$24M by Sep), no debt, C$60M raised since inception; Frank Giustra ~7.5–10%, Eduardo Elsztain (IRSA/Cresud) ~9–10%. Red Cloud target C$1.70; stock C$0.455.

The Gate

Proving there is a mine here, not just a vein — and doing it before the money runs out. Yaxtché's 3.2 Mt is a 6-year mine at 1,500 tpd; Golden Minerals' 2018 PEA put the NPV at US$45M, and neither Hochschild, Golden nor Barrick chose to build it. The updated MRE is guided H1 2027 and any economic study ~Q4 2028 — a long runway on ~C$2.3M/month of burn against ~C$24M, which means a financing in 2027 on a stock that has fallen 61% from its February high with C$0.80 LIFE paper and C$0.60 warrants underwater.

Sub-gates
  1. Tonnage — 45,000 m has to turn Mani-Copan and the step-outs into tens of millions of new ounces, not just spectacular metre-intervals.
  2. Concentrate quality — historic concentrates carried As/Sb/Bi penalties and recovery varied by zone; the Sep 2026 tests are encouraging but not locked-cycle.
  3. Altitude and logistics — 4,800 m, 50–200 mm of rain, seasonal access, Puna water.
  4. The sellers — both strategic holders and two directors have been net sellers since Sep 2025 (data-vendor sourced, unverified against SEDI), and nobody inside bought in 2026.

Every prior owner's exit is data. The bull case has to explain why Barrick, with US$6M in and a 70% earn-in, walked in April 2024.

Rule screen applies only when a study exists; when it does, run it on the tonnes sensitivity, not the price.
Valuation Anchor

~US$1.5 per Indicated ounce — computable, and the whole debate is whether the denominator is real. If the 2026 programme lifts the resource to 70–100 Moz at similar grade and a 2028 study shows a modest-capex underground mine (the camp, decline and permits already exist), then at US$50+ silver the NPV is plausibly US$500M–1B and today's EV is 10–15% of it — the Red Cloud C$1.70 case.

If tonnage stays near 3–4 Mt, this is a US$100M company with a high-grade vein that three majors declined, waiting for a study in 2028. Unlike Aftermath, the silver-price columns do move this name — it is the purest silver exposure in the developer set.

Bucket: grade / discovery / optionality — Indicated ounces but no study, and the value case rests on discovery, not on what is defined.

Frank Giustra (Fiore) ~7.5–10% — 13.6% at the Oct 2024 listing (C$0.15 placement + loan warrants), bought up to 15.1% in the market by Jan 2025, then diluted/trimmed to 9.9% post-Jan 2026 LIFE (MarketScreener 7.5%). Eduardo Elsztain (IRSA / Cresud) ~9–10% — 25M shares @ C$0.20 (May 2025) + 6.25M units @ C$0.40 (Aug 2025), board seat; 9.7% post-LIFE. Institutions: Konwave ~2.8%, Sprott Asset Management ~2.5%, Ninepoint ~2.5%, Radcliffe ~2.3%. Willem Middelkoop (Commodity Discovery Fund) strategic advisor since Nov 2024, fund holding undisclosed. No Eric Sprott personal, Rule, Gentile, Palisades or Crescat found.
Institutions / retail
Backers ~17–20%; institutions ~10–15%; HNW ~13%; insiders ~2%; retail ~46–70% depending on source. 290.3M shares; FD 340.8M. No 10%+ holder after Jan 2026.

Read: Two famous names put real cash in at C$0.15–0.40 and have been quietly reducing since the stock went to C$1.17 — that is the honest version of 'backed by Giustra and Elsztain'. Management's own stake is options. Nobody inside bought the 61% drawdown. The register is a 2024–25 vote of confidence and a 2026 vote of patience, at best.

Jurisdiction risk

National: the best it has been in a generation. Milei's coalition won the Oct 2025 midterms; export duties on mining cut to 0% (Aug 2025); Decree 482/2026 restored the 1993 Mining Investment Law's stability certificate and VAT refunds; RIGI has approved ~US$9B including AbraSilver's Diablillos next door (El Quevar itself is likely below the US$200M RIGI threshold and has filed under the 1993 law); capital controls largely lifted; a US$20B US Treasury swap line behind the peso. The Apr 2026 glacier-law reform narrowed protection and handed periglacial oversight to provinces — relevant at 4,500–5,100 m and being litigated.

Provincial / local: strong. Salta is the Fraser Institute's top Latin American jurisdiction (2024), hosts Taca Taca, Rincón and Diablillos, and owns the surface rights (seven easements granted). Kolla community engagement documented and positive; 80% Salta workforce; no conflict found. The real local constraints are physical — altitude, water (permits for 60 m³/day), seasonal access, power 20 km away.

This is the mirror of Aftermath: national and regional politics are the tailwind; geology and the balance sheet are the risk.

Differentiator
  1. Grade — 482 g/t Indicated is exceptional — inside a district almost nobody has explored. Prior owners drilled 3–5% of 57,000 ha chasing bulk tonnage; Argenta is finding high-grade shoots (Mani-Copan) and a separate Au-Cu system (Carmen) with the first systematic surface programme (3,000+ talus samples, 720 km of ground mag).
  2. Infrastructure bought for US$3.5M — camp, decline, roads, water permits, EIA, magazine, gas and HV lines within 20 km — that would cost several times the purchase price to replace.
  3. Two backers with names and cheque-books — Giustra (Fiore) from the listing, Elsztain (IRSA/Cresud, Austral Gold) with a board seat since May 2025 — and a Red Cloud/Raymond James syndicate that has raised C$38M in two bought deals.
  4. Pure silver — no AgEq arithmetic, no by-product deck; it is the cleanest silver-price torque among the developers.

Read it honestly: the differentiator (grade in narrow, high-grade shoots) is why tonnage is small and why the three previous owners, who wanted scale, left. And the two backers have been reducing, not adding, since the stock peaked — the names are a vote from 2024–25, not 2026.

Exploration upside

Discovery-driven · moves the needle: very high — it is the thesis. 45,000 m in 2026 (two rigs; 40% resource expansion, 60% discovery); >25,500 m and 89 holes since May 2025. Yaxtché extended ~270 m; Mani-Copan is a new high-grade zone 500 m south; Carmen a Au-Cu system 350 m NE; Argentina target 1.5 km out; 20+ targets from mag and surface sampling. The next MRE (H1 2027) is the first time the drilling gets counted. Watch the ratio of metre-intervals to ounces — bonanza grades over 1 m add headlines, not tonnes.

Argenta needs tonnes more than grade; every release should be read for width × continuity, not peak g/t.

What has to go right

One number: how many tonnes the Q1 2027 resource adds to 45 Moz Indicated at 482 g/t. The 2026 programme (45,000 m) has to turn Yaxtché's extensions and the new Mani–Copan zone into ounces, and the locked-cycle metallurgy (Oct–Nov 2026) has to confirm the 95% rougher recoveries. Then a 2027 financing that is not punitive.

Why the stock is priced where it is

Below every financing since the C$0.20 Elsztain placement of May 2025, with no study, a small deposit (3.2 Mt) and economics not before 2028. The market has already discounted the dilution that a 2027 raise brings; the backers (Fiore / Giustra, Cresud / Elsztain) have been trimming, not adding.

What the plan does about it

Buys a small piece of the drill results now, because the price has already paid for the raise and assays are flowing. The main piece waits for the resource to read green on tonnes, grade and category; the last piece goes in at the price the institutions set in 2027, not above it.

What to watchPrice C$0.30Updated Yaxtché resource, Q1 2027 (CEO: March)Locked-cycle metallurgy, Oct–Nov 2026Any TSXV announcement: "private placement", "bought deal", "LIFE", "strategic"Early-warning or SEDI filings by Fiore (Giustra) or Cresud (Elsztain)

Sizing: every amount is a share of the position you decide to hold in this company, whatever that is (100% = the full position). At €4 an order the fee is small; keep each tranche at €200 or more (fee ≤ 2%), and if a tranche would come out smaller, merge it with the next one. Not advice; my read written down in advance so that on the day I compare numbers against thresholds I set beforehand, not against the price move.

Step 1starter: 30% now — drill results are flowing and the price has already discounted the dilution

Buy 30% with a limit order at or below C$0.36 on the TSXV. Reason: at ~US$1.5 per Indicated ounce the market is already pricing the 2027 raise and a resource that disappoints; the remaining 2026 assays (40–70% of holes pending at each release) and the locked-cycle metallurgy arrive before the raise, and each is a free look at the tonnage question. Only 30% now because the two best holders have been trimming and nobody inside bought the fall — the plan does not know more than they do; it only knows the price they sold at (C$0.61–0.94) is far above today's.

  1. Falls to the C$0.30 alert with no news? Fill the 30% there if it has not filled, and nothing more. Below C$0.30 the next raise prices in the twenties and the warrant overhang (18.75M at C$0.60) is irrelevant — the only thing that matters is Step 2.
  2. A financing announced before the resource? Skip ahead to Step 4 and apply its rules; the raise price becomes the Step 1 limit for anything unfilled.
  3. Runs above C$0.50 on assays alone? Don't chase. Spectacular metre-intervals are what the previous three owners also had; wait for the tonnes.
Step 2the updated resource (guided Q1 2027): read four numbers and one sentence before doing anything
WhatGreenRed
Total ounces≥ 70 Moz (the CEO's own 70–75 Moz target, from 49 Moz today)< 55 Moz — a year of 45,000 m added grade, not a deposit
Tonnes≥ 6 Mt (roughly double the 3.2 Mt that three owners judged too small)< 4 Mt, whatever the grade
Grade≥ 350 g/t kept while tonnes grow — the mine-plan grade stays high< 250 g/t at the same cut-off: growth bought by diluting the vein
Category≥ 60% Indicated, Mani-Copan carried as a separate domainmostly Inferred; Mani-Copan and the step-outs not yet in the estimate
The sentence"a preliminary economic assessment has been commissioned" / a study brought forward from 2028"further drilling is required to define" / the 2028 study date unchanged

Three or four green → the gate is open: at US$3–4 per ounce on 70–90 Moz the share is worth 2–3× today's price after the dilution still ahead, and more if silver holds. Two or more red → the three owners who left were right about the size. Stop. Do not buy the dip, and sell the starter if the ounces are below 55 Moz. Re-run the card — without tonnes this is a high-grade vein with a 2028 study and a raise to fund the wait.

Step 3second tranche: 40% — on the resource, not before it
  1. Mostly green and the stock falls or goes nowhere on the day or within the following two weeks → buy 40% in the market. A resource at target met by a flat tape is the market waiting for the financing; the plan is happy to own the tonnes while it waits.
  2. Mostly green and the stock rises → buy 40% anyway within two weeks; don't chase beyond +30% from the pre-release price — above that the next raise is being priced in and Step 4 will get a better level.
  3. Mixed (two green, two red) → 20% only, and the second 20% becomes a Step 4 tranche. Mixed usually means the tonnes came but mostly Inferred; the price for that is the 2027 raise.
  4. Red → nothing, and apply Step 2's sell rule to the starter.
Step 4third tranche: 30% — the 2027 financing, at the institutions' price

A C$20M+ raise in 2027 is near-certain (working capital ~C$24M in September against ~C$2.3M a month). It is the one event with a price attached, so the last tranche waits for it:

  1. Giustra and Elsztain take their pro-rata or more, at or above the market price → buy 30% on the announcement day at or within 5% of the issue price. The two sellers of 2026 turning into buyers is the signal this plan most wants; the price on the day is secondary. A LIFE offering is open to Canadian retail, not to a German account, so the market on the day is the entry.
  2. Raise at a discount of more than 15%, or with a full warrant, and the backers absent → halve it: 15% at the issue price, 15% held for a lower print. Bought deals with full warrants on TSXV silver explorers have a pattern of trading below issue for months.
  3. Silver drawdown instead: if silver falls 20%+ and the stock 30%+ with the resource already green and no raise announced, deploy the 30% into it — the fall is the metal, the tonnes are still there.

If the raise lands before the resource (a bought deal on strong assays), Step 4 moves ahead of Step 3 and its tranche shrinks to 20%; the resource keeps the larger one.

Step 5overrides — events that change the plan whatever step it is at
  1. Buy the remaining tranches that day: a producer or major takes ≥ 10% at a premium or signs an earn-in (a Barrick-type party coming back is the strongest possible answer to "why did Barrick leave"); or a resource above 90 Moz with the grade kept.
  2. Stop adding and review: an early-warning filing showing Fiore or Cresud below 5%; the CEO leaves; the locked-cycle tests confirm As/Sb/Bi penalties that the Sep 2026 rougher tests did not show; the Supreme Court suspends the April 2026 glacier-law reform (the card's 18 Oct watch item — it would raise the permitting bar for any mine plan at 4,800 m); or working capital below C$8M with no raise announced.
  3. Sell everything: the resource is red and the next raise prices below C$0.30 — small deposit, cheap paper, no study until 2028.
Step 6once in: sell-or-hold triggers
  1. Sell if by end-2027 the resource is under 60 Moz and the economic study has not been brought forward from Q4 2028; the thesis was tonnes by 2027, not metres forever.
  2. Sell half if the stock triples before any economic study. Vein stories re-rate hardest on hope; a triple on a resource alone is worth banking half of, and the other half rides to the study.
  3. Otherwise hold through the study. The purest silver exposure in the file; if silver is higher and the tonnes are real, the study is where the NPV gets written down and the multiple earned. Don't trade the Carmen gold-copper holes in between.
PracticalWhere to buy, currency, and the most likely outcome

Liquidity is on the TSXV (AGAG) in CAD; the OTCQX line (AGAGF) is usable for a US-dollar account but wider. Use limit orders — the spread at C$0.35 is often a cent (~3%) and the book thins on down days. Canadian placements come as a same-day announcement rather than an ASX-style halt, so Step 4 means reading the terms at the open and acting that day. Most likely outcome (my read, not a forecast): a resource in Q1 2027 of 60–75 Moz with more of the growth in grade and Inferred than in Indicated tonnes — a "mixed" Step 2 — followed by a C$20–25M raise at C$0.35–0.50 with the backers taking pro-rata. That gives a 2–3× case only if silver holds above US$50 and the study is pulled forward; it is why the plan keeps a tranche for the raise rather than spending it all on the resource. The failure mode is a resource that reads well and adds few tonnes; the plan's job is to make sure that outcome costs the 30% starter, not the whole position.

Next Catalyst

Ongoing 2026 assays (40–70% pending at each release) through Q4; locked-cycle metallurgy and concentrate specs (next 45–60 days from Sep 21); IP/CSAMT geophysics and new target drilling; updated MRE H1 2027; a financing in 2027; environmental baseline (Ausenco) complete; economic study ~Q4 2028.

Open Questions
  • Why did Barrick walk in April 2024 after US$6M and a 70% earn-in — what did they conclude about scale?
  • How many ounces does the 2027 MRE add, and at what tonnage — is this a 50 Moz or a 100 Moz deposit?
  • Do the As/Sb/Bi penalties that hit historic concentrates reappear in locked-cycle tests?
  • Who funds 2027 — Giustra and Elsztain again, or the market at a lower price?
  • What does a 1,500 tpd underground mine at 4,800 m cost to build and run — and has anyone re-run the 2018 PEA at today's silver price?
  • Is Carmen a distraction or a second deposit?

Metallurgy (Sep 21, 2026)

Blue Coast Research: 13 of 15 variability samples averaged ~95% rougher recovery (max 99%); cleaner tests 96% recovery to a 14,857 g/t concentrate from a 381 g/t head. Locked-cycle, mineralogy and base-metal specs next.

Programme scale-up (2026)

Summer programme upsized 12–15,000 m → 25,000 m (Feb) → 45,000 m (Jul; Sep deck says "up to 40,000"). Key hits: QVD-469 446 g/t / 28 m in a 120 m step-out (Jul 6); Mani-Copan QVD-433 4,982 g/t / 7.5 m (Feb 23); Carmen Au-Cu (Jan).

Financings

Oct 2024 C$15.3M @ C$0.15 (listing); May 2025 C$5M @ C$0.20 to Elsztain; Aug 2025 C$15M bought deal @ C$0.40 + ½ warrant @ C$0.60 (Red Cloud) + C$2.5M Elsztain pro-rata; Jan 2026 C$23M LIFE @ C$0.80, no warrants (Red Cloud / Raymond James). C$60.5M raised since inception; Jun 30 cash C$30.1M.

Nothing beyond exploration has been done by this team: no resource update, PEA or permitting led by them yet (the 49.4 Moz resource is the 2024 inherited one). Giustra ~10% (bought in market to 15.09% of 169M shares by Jan 2025, since diluted to ~10% of ~290M shares and trimming in 2026); Elsztain Group ~10%, also trimming; together ~17–20%. Management ~2% in total (deck, Feb 2026). CEO Marias 0.22% (~C$348k). Insiders net buyers of ~C$479k over 12 months (SimplyWall.st) — mostly options exercises. CEO comp C$531k (50% salary / 50% bonus-options) at a ~C$200-290M market cap — on the high side for an explorer CEO 1.5 years into the role. Circular not fetched.   • The money came from two financiers, Giustra (~10%) and Elsztain (~10%), both net sellers in 2026 — the register that funded the story is reducing while the drill bit is asked to prove it.
  • CEO is a first-time public-company CEO with unverified prior history.
  • Three financings in 16 months; CFO holds no shares; director Harder sold option shares (Feb 2026).

Thesis

A micro-cap sitting on a very large drill database in the Abitibi, trying to re-cut an old underground deposit as an open-pit starter + underground story. Emperor optioned Duquesne West from Globex/Duparquet Assets (Oct 2022), rebuilt the geological model with AI-assisted targeting, and more than doubled the historical 727 koz to 1.46 Moz.

The 2025/26 programme (66 holes, 20,479 m, on budget) plus 7,884 m of resampled historical core is meant to (a) thicken the pit-shell lenses near surface and (b) convert Inferred to Indicated ahead of an updated 43-101 and a PEA.

Second leg: Lac Pelletier, 4 km from Rouyn-Noranda, contiguous with Agnico Eagle's Wasamac (2.2 Moz M&I) on the same shear — acquired for assumed closure liabilities (~C$305k in bonds) plus a purchase from Maritime; it carries a granted 1,000 tpd underground extraction permit. CEO John Florek (P.Geol); C$11.1M LIFE raise Oct 2025 (oversubscribed) funded the season.

The Gate

Turning a 100%-Inferred, historically-underground deposit into a bankable open-pit case — does the near-surface envelope carry enough grade at a workable strip ratio once properly modelled? Free/visible gold and bonanza intervals make the grade nuggety; APEX had to use ordinary kriging with locally-varying anisotropy to get continuity, and nothing is yet Indicated.

Sub-gates
  1. The option isn't done — C$10M cash + 15M shares + C$12M exploration over five years to Duparquet Assets (50% Globex); year-3 paid Jan 2026, year-4 due Jan 2027.
  2. Treasury — the Oct 2025 C$11.1M has largely been spent on the season, so a PEA and the 2027 option payment almost certainly mean another raise on a ~C$65–95M cap.
  3. Disclosure hygiene — an Oct 2025 release mis-stated the resource grade as 5.42 g/t and needed a same-day correction, the company moved to semi-annual reporting in Jun 2026, and assay turnaround has slipped twice on lab backlogs.

Lac Pelletier's closure-plan approval was guided end-June → now "before end of Q3" — watch for a third slip.

Valuation Anchor

~US$40/oz on Inferred ounces (US$60M ÷ 1.46 Moz; ~US$35–50/oz across the mcap range). Cheap-looking against Abitibi peers with Indicated resources, but the Inferred discount is deserved: nothing here can go into a reserve yet.

The honest anchor is EV per future Indicated ounce — if half converts, you are paying ~US$80/oz for the credible part, which is fair rather than cheap.

Dilution overhang is structural: 15M option shares + C$10M of option cash + a PEA to fund. Lac Pelletier is carried at roughly nothing and is the free option.

Bucket call: grade / discovery / optionality, not "cheap defined ounces", because the ounces aren't defined to the standard the cheap bucket requires.

Rick Rule — "invested in 2025" per company deck, size undisclosed (presumably the Oct 2025 LIFE). Institutions / retail
Institutions ~7%, insiders ~6.5%, retail ~86%. No 10%+ holder, no control block. 196.1M shares; 28.8M warrants + 17.4M options → FD 242.3M.

Read: The two names that matter here both put cash in at the bottom: McEwen has averaged up across three placements and Rule chose it in 2025. Management's ~6% is real money on a ~C$65M cap but small in absolute terms. The retail-heavy register is why the stock moves 10%+ on a drill hole — and why a financing will be priced to whoever shows up.

Jurisdiction risk

National / provincial: as good as it gets. Québec, Abitibi — road, hydro, Rouyn-Noranda labour, labs at Val d'Or, a permitting regime the whole industry knows.

Local: low. Duquesne West is 10 km from Duparquet in the historic camp; Lac Pelletier sits inside Rouyn-Noranda city limits, but as a past-producing mine site with an existing extraction permit and closure plan, not a greenfield fight. No organised opposition known.

Jurisdiction is not the discount here — geology and balance sheet are.

Differentiator
  1. Data density per dollar of market cap. ~143,000 m of drilling (much of it inherited) on a ~US$60M company is unusual — most peers at this cap have a fraction of that, so the resource-growth story is about re-modelling and infill, not blind step-outs.
  2. High-grade shoots inside a bulk envelope — 61.5 g/t over 15 m and 369.6 g/t over 2.4 m are real, and free gold was not previously recognised or targeted, which is optionality a 1.69 g/t average understates.
  3. A permitted second asset — Lac Pelletier's 1,000 tpd extraction permit, existing portal and underground development, on Agnico's Wasamac shear, is a rare thing for a micro-cap to own (subject to the liability transfer closing).

Read it honestly: the bonanza lenses are the differentiator and the reason the resource is hard to model and still all Inferred — the same fact seen from two sides. And "AI-driven exploration" is marketing until the Indicated tonnes show up.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, better tonnes near surface · moves the needle: high. 21.3 m @ 3.0 g/t from 64 m (DQ26-43) and 24.1 m @ 2.6 g/t from 45 m incl. 7.1 m @ 7.5 g/t (DQ26-52) sit ~400 m apart — that continuity is the starter-pit argument. Deep bonanza shoots (15 m @ 61.5 g/t at ~400 m; 20.1 m @ 5.0 g/t; 35.9 m @ 3.1 g/t) are underground material, not pit material. 107.7 m @ 0.5 g/t is the bulk-envelope argument. Only ~45% of the season's assays (incl. historical core) reported as of Sep 9 — the rest lands through Q4.

Here exploration is not a bonus: conversion to Indicated and the pit-shell grade are the thesis.
