What has to go right

Two things set the value, and neither is a drill hole. The financing, near-certain in H1 2027 when the January option payment and a PEA both need money, has to come from the people who already own it, at a fair price, for the things that create a first NAV. Then the Duquesne West resource update has to say how much of the 1.46 Moz is real enough to mine from surface: Indicated ounces, a pit shell, a grade that survives top-cutting.

Why the stock is priced where it is

Everything is Inferred, the PEA is undated, the flagship is still an option from Globex, and the register is ~86% retail, so the next placement will be priced to whoever shows up. The stock is 90% above the October 2025 placement on bonanza intercepts; metre-intervals are not Indicated ounces.

What the plan does about it

Does not pay up for drill holes. Most of the money waits for the two events: the placement, bought in the market at or near the institutions' price without their four-month hold; and the resource, bought only if it reads green on Indicated ounces and a starter pit. The starter exists only because a bonanza hole can gap the stock 30% and a 0% position has nothing to add to.

What to watchPrice C$0.32 (€0.203)Any CSE release: "private placement", "LIFE", "bought deal", "option"Duquesne West resource update, Q1–Q2 2027Lac Pelletier resource, end-Q1 2027Year-4 Globex option payment, due Jan 2027

Sizing: every amount is a share of the position you decide to hold in this company, whatever that is (100% = the full position). At €4 an order the fee is small; keep each tranche at €200 or more (fee ≤ 2%), and if a tranche would come out smaller, merge it with the next one. Not advice; my read written down in advance so that on the day I compare numbers against thresholds I set beforehand, not against the price move.

Step 1optional starter: 20% — only on a no-news drawdown

Buy 20% only if the stock trades at or below C$0.32 (€0.203 / US$0.228) with no adverse news — roughly the level before the September drill-hole pop, and the price at which the CEO's own market buys (C$0.165–0.175) would still be doubling. Otherwise nothing before the raise. Reason for the small size: on a retail-heavy register (~86% retail) the next placement will be priced to whoever shows up, and that price is likely to be at or below the market on the day, so there is little to gain by being early and a 20% dilution to lose. The starter exists only because a bonanza intercept near surface can gap the stock 30% on a Tuesday, and a 0% position has nothing to add to.

  1. Runs above C$0.50 (€0.317) on assays alone? Let it run. Metre-intervals are not Indicated ounces; the raise, when it comes, will be below that.
  2. Falls below C$0.25 (€0.158) with no news? Hold the starter, do not add — a no-news fall into a financing means the placement is being priced, and the placement is Step 2.
Step 2the financing (H1 2027, most likely around the January option payment): read four things before doing anything
WhatGreenRed
Size≥ C$8M — enough for the option payment, the PEA and a drill season together< C$5M: a bridge that buys six months and a second raise
Priceat or above C$0.35 (€0.222) and within 10% of the 20-day average — no half-price papera 20%+ discount, or a full warrant on top of the discount
WhoMcEwen (Evanachan) takes his share again, or Rule's fund is named; any insider participationno named backer; a broker-led unit deal to new retail
Use of proceeds"option payment, resource update and PEA" in that order"general working capital" with no programme named, or the option renegotiated into more shares

Three or four green → the money came from the people who already own it, at a fair price, for the things that create the first NAV. Two or more red → the register is being refilled at a discount with nothing dated to show for it. Stop. Do not buy on the day. Hold the starter if any; re-run the card after the resource.

Step 3second tranche: 40% — at the placement price, on the announcement
  1. Mostly green → buy 40% in the market on the day of the announcement or the next morning, at or within 5% of the placement price. A LIFE offering is open to Canadian retail only, so the market after the release is the entry for a German account; the institutions' price without the four-month hold is as good as this gets.
  2. Mostly green but the stock gaps 20%+ above the placement price → 20% now, 20% held for a pull-back within four weeks; deploy at the four-week mark if it never comes.
  3. Red → nothing. Reassess at Step 4; a discounted raise usually keeps the stock near the issue price for weeks, so Step 4 will offer the same or better.
Step 4third tranche: 40% — the Duquesne West resource update (deck: Q1–Q2 2027): read four numbers and one sentence
WhatGreenRed
Indicated≥ 500 koz Indicated (a third of the 1.46 Moz converted)< 250 koz Indicated — the nugget effect won
The pita stated pit-constrained resource ≥ 600 koz at ≥ 1.3 g/t inside a pit shell with strip ≤ 8:1no pit shell stated, or pit ounces < 400 koz / strip > 12:1
Gradeoverall ≥ 1.5 g/t after top-cutting< 1.2 g/t — the bonanza holes were carrying the average
Total ounces≥ 1.6 Moz (growth plus conversion)< 1.2 Moz — the re-model shrank it
The sentence"PEA commissioned", with a named engineer and a date"further infill required" / PEA still undated
  1. Four or five green → buy 40% within two weeks, whatever the tape. This is the first moment the ounces have a confidence category the market can value; at ~US$80/oz for credible ounces it is still cheap.
  2. Three green → 20%, the rest on the PEA.
  3. Two or more red → nothing, and sell the starter if the pit ounces are the problem. A high-grade underground deposit with no open-pit starter is a different, smaller company than the one this plan was written for.

If the Lac Pelletier resource (end-Q1 2027) lands first with a compliant 200 koz+ at > 3.5 g/t and a dated plan to use the extraction permit, that is a reason to keep going, not to buy: the second asset is the free option, not the thesis.

Step 5overrides — events that change the plan whatever step it is at
  1. Buy the remaining tranches that day: Agnico Eagle or another producer takes a stake, options Lac Pelletier, or bids for the company — the one buyer that makes the Wasamac-shear story real; or a resource update above 2 Moz with ≥ 40% Indicated.
  2. Stop adding and review: the Globex option is renegotiated into more shares or a longer earn-in (the flagship is not yet owned); the resource update slips past June 2027 with no date; a second disclosure error; McEwen reported selling.
  3. Sell everything: the option lapses, or a raise below C$0.25 (€0.158) with a full warrant and no backer — cheap paper on an unowned asset.
Step 6once in: sell-or-hold triggers
  1. Sell if the PEA (deck: later 2027) shows an after-tax NPV below C$150M at ≤ US$3,000 gold or an IRR below 20% — the open-pit starter did not work, and the underground ounces need a bigger company to mine them.
  2. Sell half if the stock doubles before the PEA. A double on an Inferred resource is the retail register doing what it does; bank half, let the rest ride into the study.
  3. Otherwise hold through the PEA. The thesis is conversion plus a starter pit on a 143,000 m database; the study is where that becomes a number. Don't trade the step-out holes in between.
PracticalWhere to buy, currency, and the most likely outcome

Liquidity is on the CSE (AUOZ) in CAD, and it is thin — days with a few hundred thousand shares. Frankfurt (9NH) quotes it in EUR but the market maker's spread on a name this size can be 5% or more; price any EUR limit off the Toronto close converted at the day's rate, and prefer the CSE line if the broker offers it. Use limit orders only. At €4 an order the fee is irrelevant; the spread is the cost. Most likely outcome (my read, not a forecast): a C$8–12M LIFE placement in Q1 2027 at C$0.30–0.40 (€0.19–0.25) with McEwen in, followed by a Duquesne West resource that converts about a third to Indicated with a smaller starter pit than the company's conceptual Phase 1 implies — "three green" at Step 4, not five. That path gives a 1.5–2× from today if gold holds; the 3× the rankings give ~10% odds to needs the pit to work and a PEA before the end of 2027. The plan is built so that the usual micro-cap path — a raise, a decent resource, an undated study — puts 60% of the position in at fair prices, and the bad path risks only the 20% starter.

Management review

Unproven: first-time CEO mine geologists on modest pay with no broken promises found; a serial-founder chairman and an optioned flagship.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
John Florek (President & CEO, director, since Nov 2022): M.Sc., P.Geo; ex-Superintendent of Geology Detour Lake (Kirkland Lake Gold), senior geologist Barrick Hemlo, Placer Dome; director McEwen Inc. · John Williamson (Chairman (independent), since unverified): Founder of Metals Group; says he has founded 20+ companies and raised C$1B+ · John Labrecque (VP Exploration, since ~2025): 26 yrs; Hemlo 'Developer of the Year' 2008 · Sean Mager (CFO & director, since ~2020): Co-founder Metals Group
Track record
  • Florek: a mine geologist (Detour, Hemlo) in his first CEO role; no prior company run or sold foundsource
  • Williamson/Metals Group: claims 20+ companies founded — individual outcomes not verifiable from company material; the pattern (many small shells) is the risk to checksource
  • Under Florek: maiden MRE at Duquesne West Jul 2025, 1.46Moz at 1.69 g/t (doubling the 727koz historical); acquired Lac Pelletier 2025; C$11M LIFE financing Oct 2025; 10–15km drill program 2025–26 with strong hits incl. 15m at 61.5 g/t (Jun 2026) (https://www.gbreports.com/contents/john-florek-2/; https://www.newsfilecorp.com/company/8461/Emperor-Metals-Inc.)
  • Duquesne West is held under option from Duparquet Assets (50% Globex); third-year renewal Jan 2026 cost C$1.0M cash + 3.26M shares (C$600k) — the company does not own its flagshipsource

Boards today: Florek: 2 (Emperor CEO, McEwen Inc. director). Williamson: multiple Metals Group companies — count unverified.

Fit to this job
Explorer stage, Abitibi gold — the CEO and VP Exploration are Abitibi/Ontario mine geologists (Detour, Hemlo), which is the right fit for resource growth and open-pit conceptual work. Nobody on the executive has run a public company to an exit, completed a PEA, or built a mine. New for them: converting the resource into a PEA (talked about for 2026, not yet delivered) and securing the optioned ground.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake (~6% insiders, CEO ~1.6%), partly bought at market at the lows (CEO 253,500 sh at C$0.165–0.175); no selling by the CEO. Florek ~1.58% (~US$1.2M); insider buying/selling not found. CEO total comp ~US$206k (64% salary) — modest and proportionate to a ~US$77M market cap. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/materials/otc-emau.f/emperor-metals/management. No circular fetched.

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

  • Flagship is optioned, not owned; annual payments of C$1M+ cash plus shares

What the numbers say
  1. Cash fell to C$0.25M in January 2025 and was C$1.0M at 31 July 2025; a C$11M LIFE offering in October 2025 left working capital of about C$5.4M by September 2026.
  2. Overhead dominates: in H1 FY26 G&A was C$0.7M against C$0.5M of capitalised exploration, and investor promotion is the single biggest expense line.

  4. Shares outstanding grew from 103.5M in July 2024 to 196.1M in September 2026, up 89%; the Lac Pelletier purchase was paid largely in shares and the LIFE deal added 44M.
  5. Recurring flow-through financings produce non-cash gains that flatter the reported loss; no debt or streams, only small leases.

Thesis

IMPACT has mined silver at Zacualpan since 2006 without ever booking a reserve, and the 2026 silver price turned a marginal operation into a cash machine: H1 2026 revenue C$53.1M and gross profit C$29.1M against C$20.5M and C$3.2M a year earlier, with C$52.2M cash and no debt at 30 June. The market pays almost nothing for it — enterprise value ~C$35M (US$25M) against trailing EBITDA of ~C$28M — because the second mine (Plomosas, bought 2023 for US$6M) is being shut after two impairments, grades swing quarter to quarter (251 g/t in Q1, 207 g/t in Q2), costs rose 9% per ounce, and management has a 27-year record of diluting rather than compounding. The bet is a re-rating from ~1× to even 4–6× EBITDA plus silver beta, with a small gold-feed Capire restart (H2 2027) as the only growth project.

The Gate

Prove the Q1 2026 quarter was the new normal, not a grade spike Q1 2026 (251 g/t, 268 koz Ag, C$17.4M operating cash flow) was followed by Q2 (207 g/t, 221 koz AgEq, C$1.1M operating cash flow). The company publishes no guidance, no reserve and no AISC, so the only test is each quarter's print. The Q3 results (due ~late November, carrying a ~C$4.3M Plomosas impairment) must show that Kena and Carlos Pacheco grades hold above ~200 g/t and that gross profit converts into cash. Behind that sits the credibility gate: a CEO since 1999 with 0.18% of the shares, a share count up 30% in a year, and a zinc mine that went from 'restart over the coming quarters' (March 2026) to care and maintenance (October 2026).

Risk score4/5Permanent loss is limited by C$52M of net cash (60% of the market cap) and a mine that is profitable at today's silver — not a 5. Not a 3 because there is no reserve or resource behind the production, grade swung 20% in one quarter, unit costs rose 9% y/y, the only growth project (Plomosas) was written off within three years, the share count grew 30% in a year, and the same CEO has run the company for 27 years while the stock is lower than in 2011 at twice the silver price. The loss path is 'cheap stays cheap' plus a silver pullback on a 2.1-beta stock.
Market cap16 Oct 2026: ~US$61M (C$0.25 · ~C$87.4M on ~349.5M shares). Market cap C$87.4M (US$61M) at C$0.25 on 349.5M shares, 16 Oct 2026; 52-week range C$0.21–0.60 (January 2026 high ~€0.36 ≈ C$0.55). Raises: C$5.0M in May 2025 at C$0.18–0.20 (units with C$0.24–0.26 warrants; Trafigura C$1.75M, Palisades C$1.1M); C$16.0M bought-deal LIFE on 17 Sep 2025 at C$0.36 (44.4M units, one full warrant at C$0.45 to 17 Sep 2027); warrant exercises C$4.9M in Q1 2026 and C$1.4M in Q2 2026. Share count +30% y/y; Plomosas was bought in April 2023 for US$3M cash + 11.44M shares.
ValuationEV = C$87.4M cap − C$52.2M cash + C$0.1M debt = C$35.3M (US$24.7M). TTM EBITDA C$27.6M (stockanalysis) → EV/EBITDA ≈ 1.3×. Q2 2026 annualised: Zacualpan gross profit C$10.8M − Plomosas loss C$2.0M − overhead ~C$1.85M = C$7.0M/q → C$28M/yr → 1.3×; with Plomosas on care and maintenance the Q2 run-rate is ~C$36M/yr → ~1.0×. At ~US$58 silver and the derived AISC, 0.95 Moz × (58 − 31) = US$25.7M EBITDA → EV/EBITDA ~1.0×.
Growth / studyNo economic study. Zacualpan has operated since 2006 without an NI 43-101 reserve or resource; Capire (restart planned H2 2027) has only a 2016 Inferred resource and no costed plan.
ReservesNone. The company states its production decisions are not based on NI 43-101 resources or reserves (corporate presentation, Sep 2023). Mine life therefore undefined: Zacualpan has produced ~14 Moz Ag over ~20 years from 200+ km² with four underground mines and one open pit feeding a 500 tpd plant. Capire: NI 43-101 Inferred 1,786,000 t @ 79 g/t Ag, 1.22% Zn, 0.54% Pb (4.5 Moz Ag, 48 Mlb Zn, 21 Mlb Pb; Mine Development Associates, 2016). Plomosas: JORC 2012 (Dec 2021, by seller Consolidated Zinc) Indicated 215 kt @ 13.5% Zn, 6.3% Pb, 34 g/t Ag; Inferred 772 kt @ 13.1% Zn, 3.0% Pb, 19 g/t Ag — never classified under NI 43-101, mine now going to care and maintenance.Zacualpan: 100%-owned 200+ km² district in Estado de México, mined since 2006 (~14 Moz Ag, >C$370M revenue) from four underground mines (Guadalupe, San Ramon, Kena, Noche Buena) and one open pit into the 500 tpd Guadalupe plant — all without an NI 43-101 reserve. 2026 grade lift came from the Kena vein and the Carlos Pacheco vein at Noche Buena (restarted late 2025, 4 km from the mill). Best 2026 holes: Z26-09 6.55 m @ 1,333 g/t Ag (incl. 5.45 m @ 1,519 g/t) and 3.95 m @ 939 g/t Ag, 2.95 g/t Au (15 Jun 2026); 0.61 m @ 114.5 g/t Au, 1,295 g/t Ag, 1.10% Cu within 9.49 m @ 9.79 g/t Au, 212 g/t Ag (21 Apr 2026). Capire (16 km SW): Inferred 1.79 Mt @ 79 g/t Ag, 1.22% Zn, 0.54% Pb (2016) with a 200 tpd pilot plant on care and maintenance. Plomosas (Chihuahua, 3,019 ha, ~6 km structure): JORC 2021 ~1 Mt at ~13% Zn, impaired C$8.8M (2025) and ~C$4.3M (Q3 2026), plant moving to care and maintenance.
DividendNone paid.
Valuation Anchor

At US$61M market cap with US$36.5M cash the market pays ~US$25M of enterprise value for a mine that made C$29M gross profit in H1 2026 — ~1× trailing EBITDA, against 6–8× for discounted silver producers and 10–15× for Aya or Avino. The discount prices in no reserve, grade volatility, Plomosas' write-offs, 27 years of dilution under the same CEO, and the suspicion that Q2's C$1.1M operating cash flow (not Q1's C$17.4M) is the true conversion rate. Stated the other way: the cash alone is worth C$0.15 of the C$0.25 share price.

Shareholder structure

Insiders ~0.5% (stockanalysis); CEO Fred Davidson 0.18% (617,750 shares), VP Exploration George Gorzynski 0.09% (simplywall.st / marketscreener). Institutions ~6% (stockanalysis). Strategic/notable: Trafigura (concentrate trader, long-standing partner) and Palisades Goldcorp took lead orders in the May 2025 placement (stakes not disclosed, each under 5%); the Sep 2023 deck named Sprott, GR Asset, BCV, Commodity Discovery, EOP and Crescat as holders (20% combined then, not verified today). Float ~348M of 349.5M shares. Insider trades in 2025–26: no SEDI data could be loaded; simplywall.st showed insiders as net sellers over the prior 12 months (as of Aug 2026) with no buys.

Read: A retail-held float with almost no insider or strategic ownership — nobody at the table owns enough to care about the share price.

Jurisdiction risk

National: Mexico — the 2023 mining-law reform (shorter concessions, tighter water rules, no new concessions under the current government) matters little for a brownfield with 20-year-old concessions, but any Capire permit falls under the Sheinbaum administration; 7.5% mining royalty plus 0.5% on precious-metals revenue; peso strength and union wage settlements were named as Q2 cost drivers. Local: Zacualpan has been mined by IMPACT for 20 years with no reported community blockade; Chihuahua (Plomosas) carries cartel-security risk common to the state, but the mine is being mothballed anyway.

Mexico risk is real but secondary here — the company's problems are its own.

Differentiator

The cheapest silver producer in the tracker on any cash-flow measure: ~1× EV/EBITDA and a ~19% trailing free-cash-flow yield, with cash equal to 60% of the market cap. No other name offers a re-rating leg that large before any help from the silver price. The flip side is that it is cheap for reasons that have not changed in 20 years.

Deep value with a credibility problem, not a growth story.

Exploration upside

District-scale veins, high-grade hits, no resource · moves the needle: medium Carlos Pacheco (Noche Buena) is giving the best intercepts in the company's history — 6.55 m @ 1,333 g/t Ag and a gold-rich zone (114.5 g/t Au over 0.61 m) — and is already in the mill feed, which is what lifted 2026 grades. The company has never converted 20 years of drilling into a reserve, so exploration shows up only as next quarter's grade, never as a valuation number. Two consultant geologists and two staff geologists were added in June 2026; no 2026 metre or budget figure is published.

Next Catalyst

Q3 2026 results (~late Nov): whether grade held above ~200 g/t after Carlos Pacheco ore entered the feed, how much of the gross profit became cash, and the final Plomosas impairment. Then Capire: metallurgy, permits and a capital decision through 2027 for an H2 2027 start.

Open Questions
  • Why did Q2 operating cash flow collapse to C$1.1M on C$8.7M gross profit (tax, working capital, Plomosas severance)? The MD&A was not fetched.
  • Is the 2026 grade (207–251 g/t vs 163 g/t in 2025) a vein-specific window at Kena/Carlos Pacheco or a durable step-up — without a reserve there is no way to know.
  • What does the Capire restart cost, what gold recovery does the circuit achieve, and does the company finally publish an economic case before spending?
  • Total cash sunk into Plomosas since 2023 (US$6M purchase + capex + ~C$13M of impairments + operating losses) and whether a sale or toll-milling deal recovers any of it.
  • Will the ~C$52M cash be returned (buyback/dividend) or spent on more acquisitions by a team that owns 0.2%?

Management review
Creal weaknesses: slipped dates, thin fit or thin candourTrack record 2/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 2/5 · Skin in the game 1/5

Kept a marginal mine alive for 20 years and did deliver the 2026 grade shift, but the record for shareholders is dilution without appreciation, an acquisition written off in three years, a 'temporary' closure that was not, and no guidance, reserve or cost standard to be measured against. Not a D: no self-dealing or hidden loss found, and the Plomosas facts were disclosed, if buried.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

Frederick (Fred) W. Davidson (President & CEO, director (previously also Chairman), since CEO since 1999/2000 (simplywall.st: Aug 1999; marketscreener: 30 Apr 2000)): Chartered accountant, UBC MBA 1970. Founder and CEO of Energold Drilling 1994–2019; CEO of Great Republic Mining 2021–2024; earlier CFO of Redhawk Resources and TOTAL Energold; director of Wheaton River Minerals. Owns 617,750 shares (0.18%). 2025 pay C$756k (77% salary). · George Gorzynski, P.Eng. (VP Exploration, director, Qualified Person, since ~2004 (22 years on the board per simplywall.st)): Owns ~0.09%. Signs the technical disclosure; an independent QP (Victor Jaramillo) was added June 2026. · Jerry Huang (CFO and Investor Relations, since not verified): Listed as CFO on 2023 deck and 2025 releases. · Armando Alexandri (COO, since not verified (on the Sep 2023 deck)): Runs Mexican operations; current status not confirmed on a 2026 document. · Board (Victor Tanaka (30 yrs), Richard Mazur (33 yrs), Robert Lishman (10 yrs), Jose Antonio de Olmedo (5 yrs), Janet Meiklejohn (2 yrs); George Gorzynski and Fred Davidson, since average tenure 16.4 years (simplywall.st)): Three independents have served 10–33 years — independence in name.
Track record
  • Davidson has run IMPACT since 1999/2000. Shares outstanding ~349.5M today vs 276.95M in Sep 2025 (+30% in a year) and roughly 60–70M in 2011–12 (unverified); the share price (C$0.25) is below its 2011 level (>C$1) with silver at nearly twice the 2011 price (https://wwww.stockwatch.com/News/Item/Z-C!IPT-3732504/C/IPT?fmt=orig ; https://stockanalysis.com/quote/tsxv/IPT/statistics/).
  • Zacualpan has produced ~14 Moz Ag and >C$370M revenue in ~20 years without long-term debt — a mine kept alive through two silver bear marketssource
  • Plomosas: bought April 2023 for US$6M (US$3M cash + 11.44M shares, plus a 12% NPI to the seller) with a plan to 'restart in the near term then expand through 2023–24'; underground mining suspended March 2026 after 'development intensity and variability in grade and tonnage' made it uneconomic; C$8.8M impairment in 2025, ~C$4.3M more in Q3 2026; plant to care and maintenance Oct 2026 (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/161140 ; https://impactsilver.com/investors/news/impact-silver-announces-temporary-suspension-of-underground-mining-at-plomosas/ ; https://impactsilver.com/investors/news/impact-silver-outlines-capire-gold-opportunity-and-plomosas-operating-and-exploration-update-1/).
  • 2026 operations delivered: Q1 2026 record revenue C$31.2M and net income C$11.3M, H1 gross profit C$29.1M, cash C$52.2M at 30 June — the Kena/Carlos Pacheco grade shift the company promised in April 2026 did happensource
  • Raised C$16.0M at C$0.36 in Sep 2025 and C$5.0M at C$0.18–0.20 in May 2025 — the stock now trades below both prices (https://wwww.stockwatch.com/News/Item/Z-C!IPT-3732504/C/IPT?fmt=orig ; https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/248661).
  • Energold Drilling, which Davidson founded and ran 1994–2019, ended in creditor protection in 2019 (unverified — from memory, not fetched)source

Boards today: Davidson: IMPACT (CEO/director); no other current public executive role found (Great Republic Mining ended Aug 2024). Gorzynski: IMPACT only, as far as found.

Fit to this job
Exactly the same job for 20 years: small-scale underground silver mining and flotation milling at Zacualpan — they know the district better than anyone. What they have not done is build a reserve, publish a cost standard, or make an acquisition work (Plomosas). The Capire restart (a 200 tpd plant they already own, 16 km away) is the same kind of work, not a step up.
Skin & pay
1/5 — 0.18% CEO stake, pay ~0.9% of market cap a year, no buys found, net sellers. Davidson 617,750 shares = 0.18% (~C$150k at C$0.25); Gorzynski ~0.09%; all insiders ~0.5%. 2025 CEO pay C$756k (salary C$585k) ≈ 0.9% of the market cap per year, i.e. the CEO earns his whole stake every three months. No open-market buys found in 2025–26 (SEDI not loaded; simplywall.st: net sellers over the prior 12 months as of Aug 2026). Sources: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsxv-ipt/impact-silver-shares/management ; https://ca.marketscreener.com/insider/FREDERICK-DAVIDSON-A04QW9/ ; https://stockanalysis.com/quote/tsxv/IPT/statistics/

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Plomosas closure announced under a 'Capire Gold Opportunity' headline; the March 2026 'temporary' suspension became permanent in six months.
  • No production guidance, no cost guidance, no AISC, no reserve in 20 years of operation — shareholders cannot hold management to anything.
  • CEO of 27 years owns 0.18%; pay C$756k on an C$87M company; board independents with 10–33-year tenures; insiders net sellers with no buys found.
  • Share count +30% in a year; both 2025 financings now under water.
  • Headlines are consistently year-over-year percentages ('756%') chosen off a near-zero base.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash rose from C$8.3M at December 2023 to C$52.2M at June 2026 with no debt (only C$0.1M of leases). Of the C$28.5M added in the first half of 2026, C$18.5M came from operations, C$11.2M from warrant exercises and C$4.1M from cashing in a GIC; operating cash flow fell to C$1.1M in Q2 2026 because C$7.6M of 2026 tax instalments were paid in the quarter.
  2. Revenue grew from C$20.8M in FY23 to C$31.9M in FY24 and C$48.5M in FY25, and H1 2026 alone brought C$53.1M as silver prices rose; gross margin went from -7% in FY24 to 21% in FY25 and 55% in H1 2026 (65% in Q1, 40% in Q2). The business lost money every year from 2023 to 2025 (net losses of C$12.4M, C$9.8M, C$10.3M) and earned C$14.1M in H1 2026.
  3. Spending is modest for a producer: capex C$2.0-2.6M a year in FY24-25 (C$5.7M in FY23), exploration C$2.8-4.6M a year, all expensed rather than capitalised, and G&A C$4.2-4.5M a year, which fell from 20% of revenue in FY23 to 9% in FY25 and 5% in H1 2026.
  4. Shares outstanding rose 64% from 213.6M (December 2023) to 349.5M (June 2026): C$12.0M of equity was raised in 2023, C$8.7M in 2024 and C$22.0M in 2025 (including a C$16.0M bought deal at C$0.36 in September 2025), plus C$6.3M of warrant exercises in H1 2026. At 20 August 2026 there were still 93.6M warrants outstanding, 26.2M of them at C$0.35 expiring 19 October 2026 and 46.3M at C$0.45 expiring September 2027.
  5. Unusual items: an C$8.8M impairment of the Plomosas zinc-lead mine in Q4 2025 and a further ~C$4.3M non-cash impairment flagged for Q3 2026 after underground mining there was suspended in March 2026; C$1.2M of share-based compensation booked in Q4 2025 on a 4.8M option grant; the FY2024 statements restated earlier periods (previously capitalised costs were expensed, so Q3 2024 figures shown here are the restated ones where available); and an income-tax charge of C$10.0M on C$24.1M of H1 2026 pre-tax profit (41%).

Thesis

Freegold Mountain is a large, road-accessible land package (~200 km² along 30 km of the Big Creek Fault, km 82 of the government-maintained Freegold Road, 70 km from Carmacks) that Northern Freegold / Triumph has held since 2006, with more than C$40M of historical work and a Feb 2020 resource of 791 koz Au Indicated (1.0 Moz AuEq) + 707 koz Au Inferred (1.09 Moz AuEq) across Nucleus (oxide-capped, 0.65 g/t), Revenue (Cu-Au-Mo porphyry, 0.38 g/t) and Tinta Hill (Ag-rich veins). Goldcorp took 19.9% in 2017; a Zijin-linked fund took 9.8% in 2018; a 2013 PEA (superseded) showed an after-tax NPV of C$358M at US$1,455 gold on US$500M of capex. Then nothing: the last drill hole was in 2021 (6,615 m; best N21-02 46 m @ 0.54 g/t oxide), the company hit C$2,252 of cash in September 2024 with C$364k owed to management, did a 1-for-10 consolidation (Dec 2022), and has since raised C$9.3M in three non-brokered unit placements (C$0.20, C$0.30, C$0.50) to reach C$5.2M cash at Jun 30, 2026. 2025 exploration spend: C$253k (mapping; the 'Proton Zone' vein showing). 2026 H1: C$124k. Meanwhile it bought a silver property in Utah (Coyote Knoll: US$150k + 4M shares + US$3M in year four), plans an IP survey in BC, and floated a spin-out. Executive Chairman and 'interim' CEO John Anderson since 2019; no analyst coverage; no news release since June 12.

The company's own 2026 outlook offers mapping, sampling and "first-pass drill planning" with no budget, no metres and no timeline for an updated MRE.

Valuation Anchor

~US$17/oz AuEq — the lowest number in the file, and the least informative. Cheapness per ounce is only a signal when something is being done to convert or grow the ounces; here the last five years of spending went to overhead, promotion, a Utah silver property and a BC geophysics plan.

The bull case is purely arithmetic: a 2 Moz AuEq resource in the Yukon, road-accessible, with a Goldcorp/Newmont and Zijin pedigree, re-studied at US$4,000 gold, is worth many multiples of US$35M — and Western Copper's Casino project next door is why the road exists at all.

The bear case is the company as it actually operates: three placements in eighteen months to fund G&A, a warrant overhang of 34.8M, and a flagship that gets mapping while cash gets spent.

Bucket: grade / discovery / optionality — optionality is the operative word, on someone else eventually doing what this company has not.

Shareholder structure

Executive Chairman / interim CEO John Anderson ~4.8M shares / ~6.6–8% — built through placements (3.5M units in the Jan 2023 raise pre-consolidation, 250k units Nov 2025, 500k units Jun 2026) plus options; the one insider consistently writing cheques. Other directors and officers hold 10k–136k each. 6.9M options at C$0.27–0.58, 4.75M of them granted May 2025 with immediate vesting.
Insider activity (12 mo)
The CEO buys placements; everyone else sells. Anderson: 250k units @ C$0.30 (Nov 2025), 500k @ C$0.50 (Jun 2026). Corporate secretary Moroney sold ~104k shares at C$0.68–0.84 (Feb–Jun 2026); new director Cowley sold 50k at C$0.46–0.61 (Apr–May 2026) — two months after joining the board. One small buy by Schreiner (10k, Sep 23, 2026). Net insider selling ~C$74k in the recent three-month window on a C$48M company.
Strategic & prominent
None current. Goldcorp's 19.9% (2017) became Newmont's and was diluted to 3.45% by 2023 and below the reporting threshold since; the Zijin-linked fund's 9.8% (2018) has vanished from every holder list; Palisades' 9.5% (2021) is sub-2%. Konwave (Gold 2000) ~2.6% is the only institution. The Michael Gentile '~8%' in newsletter coverage is unfiled. No Sprott, Rule or Crescat. Related-party: director Paul Cowley's company billed C$143k in H1 2026 (consulting + share-issuance costs).
Institutions / retail
Institutions ~2.7%, insiders ~7%, retail ~90%. 72.5M shares; FD 114.3M — 34.8M warrants (C$0.175–0.55, to 2027–29) and 6.9M options; the Jun 2026 placement's 10.8M shares come free Oct 13, 2026. 1-for-10 consolidation Dec 2022. No lead broker on any raise since 2023; finders' fees and finder warrants on each.

Read: The strategic register that made this name interesting in 2017–2020 — Goldcorp, a Zijin fund, Palisades — has been diluted out of existence, and no one with a name has replaced them. What remains is a CEO who funds his own placements, a retail float, a warrant overhang equal to half the shares, and officers selling small amounts into every rally. The company's own ownership claims do not reconcile with the filings; treat the filings as the truth.

Jurisdiction risk

National / territorial: tier-one on paper, degraded in practice since Eagle. The Yukon Party won a majority in Nov 2025 on faster permitting, legislated timelines and a new minerals act — but the act is targeted for 2028, and the Eagle Gold heap-leach failure (Jun 2024; cleanup C$377M by Sep 2026; 50+ review-board recommendations, 27 still due by spring 2027) produced a territorial halt on licensing new heap-leach facilities and a rewrite of mine-waste guidelines — directly relevant to a Nucleus oxide heap-leach concept. The Yukon Geological Survey itself says Eagle "negatively impacted investors choosing to risk capital on early-stage projects in the Yukon."

Local: unaddressed. Freegold sits in Little Salmon/Carmacks First Nation traditional territory; the company discloses no exploration or cooperation agreement with LSCFN (engagement is a citizen-owned environmental contractor and a 2021 office hire); LSCFN declared a mining moratorium around Claire Lake in Apr 2026 (location relative to Freegold not established) and its chief has criticised the minerals-legislation process. The Freegold Road upgrade beyond km 82 — the company's stated infrastructure advantage — was de-funded in Mar 2025 when the Gateway money moved to the Dempster; it now depends on Casino's YESAB timeline.

Yukon is the reason a 0.58 g/t resource can be called 'tier-one'; post-Eagle Yukon is the reason its likely mining method is on hold.

Differentiator
  1. Two million AuEq ounces on a government road for US$35M — with a Casino-scale neighbour that will bring infrastructure whether Triumph does anything or not.
  2. The land package — 200 km² along 30 km of a productive structure with 20+ zones, WAu breccia and Blue Sky intercepts that were never followed up; if the Dawson Range gets re-rated by Casino's build, this is one of the largest positions in it.
  3. A clean-ish balance sheet for once — C$5.2M cash, no debt, management debts repaid.
  4. The historical validation — Goldcorp at 19.9%, a Zijin fund at 9.8%, Rio Tinto once optioning the BC ground — which says the geology was worth a major's money in 2017–19, even if none of them stayed.

Read it honestly: every differentiator is something that happened to the company, not something it did — the road, the neighbour, the 2017 placement. The only thing it controls, exploration, is the thing it has not done.

Exploration upside

Nothing drilled since 2021 · moves the needle: potentially very high, currently zero. The 2026 plan is mapping and sampling with 'first-pass drill planning' — no metres, no budget. Targets that would matter if tested: WAu breccia at depth, Blue Sky, Revenue's underground high-grade block, the Nucleus oxide cap for a heap-leach case (now regulatorily fraught), and the 2025 Proton Zone showing. A December 2025 newsletter floated RC drilling of Nucleus oxides and re-assaying WAu for tungsten (~15 Mlb W, non-43-101); nothing has been reported. Andalusite Peak (BC) gets an 11.8 line-km IP survey; Coyote Knoll (Utah) a 26-hole permit — the money is going away from the flagship.

The next drill hole at Freegold will be the first in five years. Until it exists, exploration upside is a slide, not a programme.

Next Catalyst

Any drill programme at Freegold (undated, unbudgeted); the June placement's hold expiry (Oct 13, 2026) — 10.8M shares free to trade; Yukon heap-leach guideline rewrite (spring 2027); Casino (Western Copper) permitting progress as a district read-through; Coyote Knoll drilling H2 2026; a possible spin-out; the next placement.

Open Questions
  • Why has a company holding 2 Moz AuEq not drilled it since 2021 — and what, specifically, is the 2026 budget for Freegold versus Utah, BC and G&A?
  • Who actually owns the stock — is the '37% management, board and key shareholders' claim reconcilable with the 6.9% insiders and 2.7% institutions that filings show?
  • What does Nucleus look like as a heap-leach project under the post-Eagle Yukon rules, and is there a non-heap-leach case?
  • Is there any agreement, or any conversation, with Little Salmon/Carmacks First Nation?
  • What happens to the share price when 10.8M June-placement shares and 34.8M warrants meet a stock that trades 20–250k shares a day?
  • Is the asset worth more to Western Copper, or to anyone building in the Dawson Range, than to its current owner?

Yukon after Eagle

Victoria Gold heap-leach failure Jun 24, 2024; receivership; Yukon loans C$185M drawn; cleanup C$377M projected by Sep 2026; Independent Review Board (Jul 2025): 'preventable', 50+ recommendations; new heap-leach licensing halted; guidelines revised to spring 2027; Boroo exclusivity on the asset extended to ~Oct 2026. Yukon Party majority Nov 3, 2025 (Premier Dixon); new minerals act targeted 2028; Freegold Road upgrade de-funded Mar 2025.

Aside

No news release since Jun 12, 2026. The '~8% Michael Gentile' holding cited in Dec 2025 newsletter coverage has no early-warning filing behind it and is treated here as unverified. The 2013 PEA is sometimes quoted at 'C$650M NPV' (pre-tax) — the after-tax figure was C$358M.

News releases · September 2026 – October 2026

No release in September 2026 – October 2026 (as of 1 Oct 2026). Last release: Triumph Gold Announces Closing of Private Placement June 2026 (12 Jun 2026).

Links go to the company's own site · all releases · grey notes are my read of whether a release changes this card.

Management review
Creal weaknesses: slipped dates, thin fit or thin candourTrack record 2/5 · Fit 2/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 3/5

Fifteen years on one property under an interim CEO, serial small placements and no stage advance: a pattern of capital consumed without progress.

Effect on the odds: chance it works 25% → 20%, odds of a 3× 7% → 6%.

People
John Anderson (Executive Chairman & Interim CEO, since Chairman since 2011 (on board since ~2009); interim CEO since Sept/Oct 2019): Age 62. Capital-markets background (Bema Gold IR, Manulife corp dev); founded Deep 6 PLC, American Eagle Oil & Gas, Aquastone Capital gold fund. Has been 'interim' CEO for ~7 years. · Jesse Halle, P.Geo. (VP Exploration, since unverified (quoted as VP Exploration since at least 2021)): Managing director of Halle Geological Services (contractor); porphyry Cu-Au work at Casino, Copper Mountain. Wife Emily Halle is project manager from the same firm. · Rakesh Patel (CFO, since Sept 2017): Part-time; audit partner at DMCL. · Marty Henning, P.Geo. (Principal Geologist, since unverified): 10 years at New Afton block cave.
Track record
  • Anderson: capital-markets/IR career; the companies he founded (Deep 6 PLC, American Eagle Oil & Gas) have no verifiable mine-building or sale outcome foundsource
  • Triumph/Freegold Mountain: ~2 Moz AuEq resource at Revenue-Nucleus already cited in 2020; same resource still the pitch in 2025 — no study, no resource growth found in 6 years (https://investingnews.com/ceo-interviews/triumph-gold-president-director-tony-barresi-freegold-mountain-update-dawson-range-yukon/ ; https://www.stocktitan.net/news/TIGCF/triumph-gold-updates-shareholders-on-operations-engages-market-maker-vfbsh4otjr8u.html)
  • Former president Tony Barresi said in March 2020 the company was 'positioning ourselves as a takeout target'; no takeout happened, Barresi gone, Anderson interim CEO since 2019source
  • Serial small financings: $1.94M at $0.30 (Nov 2025), $3.75M raise (earlier), market maker hired at $6,500/month (May 2025) (https://investingnews.com/triumph-gold-closes-1-93-million-private-placement/ ; https://resourceworld.com/triumph-gold-raising-3-75-million-for-yukon-project/)
  • Board average tenure 12.5 years; Strub and Anderson on board since 2011; Sparks since 2017; only one new director (Cowley, June 2025)source

Boards today: Anderson: Triumph (exec chair + interim CEO); other current public boards not verified. Director Paul Cowley is CEO of two other juniors (Phenom Resources, Indigo Exploration). Director Marco Strub sits on several other juniors (Canada Zinc Metals etc.).

Fit to this job
Team is a capital-markets chairman plus contract geologists. Explorer-stage fit is adequate for a porphyry/epithermal Yukon target (Halle, Henning have porphyry Cu-Au experience). Nobody on the executive has taken a project through PEA/PFS or built anything. Company has been exploring the same property since the Northern Freegold days (2000s) without advancing stage — the 'job' here is simply finding something new, and 15+ years of trying has not produced it.
Skin & pay
3/5 — meaningful stake, mostly founder stock or grants; not selling. Anderson holds ~4.87M shares (~8.0% per MarketScreener; SimplyWall.st says 6.6%), built partly through placements (250k units Nov 2025 = C$75k). Other directors hold <0.3% each. SimplyWall.st flags 'significant insider selling' of ~C$63-74k in the last 3 months (names not verified). CEO comp C$313k, 100% salary (SimplyWall.st) — ~0.65% of a C$48M market cap; modest in absolute terms. Circular not fetched; figures are third-party aggregations. (https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsxv-tig/triumph-gold-shares/management ; https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/TRIUMPH-GOLD-CORP-49477449/company/)

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Interim CEO for ~7 years; no permanent operator hired.
  • Same ~2 Moz AuEq resource marketed for 6+ years with no study or growth — stage never advanced.
  • Immediate-vesting option grants (4.75M at $0.27, May 2025) at a ~C$48M company.
  • Strategy drift: Yukon gold explorer announcing it is 'evaluating silver project acquisitions'.
  • Board refreshment: only one new director in 3 years; average tenure 12.5 years.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash went from near zero to C$5.21M at 30 June 2026 after three placements; at the H1 2026 burn of C$0.73M a quarter that is about 7 quarters.
  2. That burn contains almost no drilling: the permitted 26-hole Coyote Knoll program and the Andalusite Peak IP survey are not yet in the numbers.
  3. Overhead dominates: FY2025 G&A was C$1.49M against C$0.67M spent in the ground, so about two-thirds of cash went to overhead, led by corporate communications.
  4. Shares outstanding rose from 42.8M in December 2024 to 72.1M in June 2026, up 69%, after C$9.3M of unit placements; 34.8M warrants remain.
  5. No debt, but share-based pay was C$1.31M in FY2025, related-party payables exceeded cash for most of 2024–2025, and the statements carry a going-concern note.

Amounts in C$ millions. Because Triumph's figures are very small (statements are in whole dollars, most quarters < C$1M), values are given to TWO decimals rather than one so that the spend chart is not all zeros. Exploration here is mostly EXPENSED (exploration expenditures + property investigation in the income statement); only property acquisition costs and the exploration deposit are capitalised (cf.exp_cap). spend.overhead = operating cash outflow not explained by expensed exploration (i.e. cash G&A incl. working-capital moves); spend.ground = expensed exploration + capitalised acquisition/deposit cash.

Funding & next catalyst
Cash
C$14.56M at 30 Jun 2026 (Q2 MD&A); ~C$11.75M in mid-Oct 2026 after C$1.9M of warrant exercises (14 Oct 2026 release; the 31 Aug figure was C$11.9M per the Oct deck, C$12.9M on the capital-structure page)
Debt
No debt. C$712,500 of deferred compensation owed to the CEO (due 1 Jan 2028, deferrable); flow-through spending obligations from the Jan and May 2026 raises (amounts not disclosed)
Burn · runway
H1 2026 operating cash outflow C$6.14M; Q2 exploration C$2.34M, net loss C$2.94M. Two rigs since July so H2 is heavier - likely C$3-4M a quarter in the field season
Next catalyst
Gold Rock and Mud Lake North assays through Q4 2026; Hyndman drilling guided for fall 2026
Funded to the next catalyst Funded for the 45,000 m 2026 programme ('fully funded', company Jun-Sep 2026) and the MD&A says twelve months of operations. At the current pace cash lasts into mid-2027; a flow-through raise in H1 2027 is likely, and the pattern (Jan and Apr/May raises in 2025 and 2026) says so. Both majors have top-up rights and have used them.
Thesis

Dryden has stitched together ~90,000 ha of the old Gold Rock camp 30 km east of Dryden, Ontario, and in three seasons has turned three known structures into 15 mineralized structures and ~10 high-grade zones, with the best hole to date 7.88 g/t over 12.70 m near surface (Sep 2026). Alamos (vendor, 10.3%) and Centerra (9.9%, with a top-up right) sit on the register and both followed in the May 2026 raise. The company says openly it is building something a major would buy rather than a mine, and it is deferring a resource until the system is big enough; the bet is that two rigs and a fully funded 45,000 m programme in 2026 produce the scale that makes one of those majors move.

The Gate

Show continuity and tonnage, not just high-grade intercepts Every headline so far is a drilled core length with true width unknown, in narrow shear veins with bonanza sub-metre sections. The company has >34,000 m of core and no resource, deliberately. Until it publishes an estimate, or a major converts its stake into a deal, the market has nothing to anchor on except the next assay. The 2026 two-rig programme (deeper step-outs at Elora/Big Master, first holes at Mud Lake North, Hyndman in the fall) is where that case has to be made.

Valuation Anchor

At ~US$38M the market is paying for a drill story: no ounces, no NAV, so any per-ounce comparison is impossible. The anchor is what two majors paid: Centerra C$0.23 (Dec 2024), C$0.32 (Apr 2026) and C$0.452 (May 2026); Alamos C$0.452 (May 2026). Today's C$0.235 is roughly half the last strategic price. Peers at the same stage in Ontario (pre-resource, major-backed) trade US$30-150M; Dryden sits at the low end after a 50% slide from January.

Shareholder structure

Company page (31 Aug 2026): Alamos Gold 10.32% (25,413,326 sh, from the Manitou property payments plus 2.41M sh bought in May 2026), Centerra Gold 9.87% (Dec 2024 placement, top-ups Apr 2026 and 2.305M sh May 2026, investor-rights agreement with a participation right), Delbrook Capital 9.57%, EuroPac Gold Fund 5.02%, management and insiders 4.82%, Sprott Asset Management 3.01%, Eric Sprott 1.62%, Rob McEwen 1.35%, Robert Quartermain 0.41%, other institutions 12%, public float 42%. CEO Wasser ~4.9M sh (~2%), CFO Kelly ~1.55M, President Kolb 200,000 (Simply Wall St / MarketScreener holdings, Jul 2026).

Read: Two majors at ~10% each, both still buying, plus Sprott, McEwen and Quartermain - a strong register for a US$38M explorer; insiders are modest at ~5%.

Jurisdiction risk

National: Canada / Ontario - top-tier, flow-through funding available, Ontario exploration tax credits used in 2026. Local: Gold Rock camp 30 km east of Dryden on the Trans-Canada corridor with historic mines (past mining to ~80 m at >5.5 g/t per the company), roads, power and a mining workforce. The company says it has 'collaborative First Nations relationships' and engages Indigenous Nations; drill permits have come through (Mud Lake permit received Jul 2026, about six weeks after submission; Hyndman permitting under way). On 16 Oct 2026 the company signed an Early Exploration Agreement with Eagle Lake First Nation (a release, terms not reviewed). No dispute or delay found.

Low risk; the only local item to watch is permitting pace for the newly staked Hyndman ground.

Differentiator

Two majors on the register before a resource exists. Alamos (the vendor) and Centerra both hold ~10% and both topped up in 2026 at prices above today's; Centerra's investor-rights agreement gives it a standing participation right. On the ground, the company has gone from three known structures to 15, with high-grade zones repeating along ~1 km of strike and now blind structures (Elora 2, Paymaster) found at depth.

The register is better than the geology is proven - useful, but the majors have bought cheap optionality, not the company.

Exploration upside

District-scale, two rigs, blind structures at depth · moves the needle: high Gold Rock has grown to ~1 km x 750 m of stacked structures with two plunges controlling high-grade shoots; the September 2026 hole (7.88 g/t over 12.70 m at 65 m) is the first that reads like open-pit material, and management now talks about evaluating open-pit potential. Beyond Gold Rock there are Mud Lake North (visible gold, assays pending), Hyndman (12 km till corridor, drilling guided for fall 2026), Sherridon and Lost Lake. The 2026 programme is 45,000 m across two rigs, the largest the company has run.

Next Catalyst

A steady flow of Gold Rock assays from two rigs through Q4 2026, the first Mud Lake North assays (three holes, visible gold in one), and the start of fall drilling at Hyndman. No resource is scheduled; a financing is likely in H1 2027.

Open Questions
  • What are the true widths? Every intercept is a core length, and the bonanza grades are in 0.4-1.9 m sections inside 4-15 m halos of 1-3 g/t.
  • How long will the company defer a resource, and will the majors wait? With >34,000 m drilled a maiden estimate is possible; without one the stock has no floor.
  • Does Hyndman become a second system or stay a till anomaly with 0.5-2 m hits? The first six holes were modest.
  • What does Alamos want? It is the vendor, keeps a 1% NSR and a C$2M resource bonus, and has bought in two financings - a buyer, or a passive holder?

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 3/5

One real exit (Ely Gold, 2021) and a clean, well-backed financing record; field dates mostly met; but no resource after three seasons by choice, a thin board, heavy marketing and several corrections. Solid and unproven at this exact job.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Clarence (Trey) Wasser (CEO & Director, since Founder; CEO since the company's formation (pre-IPO 2022-23; listed 10 Jan 2024)): Ex-President, CEO and Director of Ely Gold Royalties, which he grew from a small royalty company and sold to Gold Royalty Corp in 2021 (C$1.46/sh, ~42% premium, C$84M cash cap plus up to 41.5M GRC shares - implied ~C$290M, derived). Consolidated ~400-480 km2 at Dryden over ~18 months. Holds ~4.9M shares (~2%). Has deferred C$712,500 of his own pay, due Jan 2028. · Maura Kolb, M.Sc., P.Geo. (President (runs geology; QP), since 15 Apr 2023): Structural geologist, ~15 years; ex-Director of Exploration at Treasury Metals; eight years in Red Lake with Goldcorp, Newmont, Evolution and Battle North. The public face on technical releases; speaker at Mining Forum Americas Sep 2026. Holds 200,000 shares. · Scott Kelly (CFO & Director, since n/a): Holds ~1.55M shares (0.64%). CFO also sitting on a four-person board. · Anna Hicken, M.Sc., P.Geo. (VP Exploration, since n/a): Runs the regional programme (mapping, till, HMC). Holds 50,000 shares. · Jason Jessup / Gary Baschuk (Independent Directors, since Baschuk elected 8 Jul 2026): Baschuk: geologist, 40+ years incl. Barrick. Jessup holds 580,000 shares. Christina McCarthy left the board Jul 2026 to become CEO of Nuvau Minerals; stays as advisor. Advisors: Darin Wagner, Stephen Kenwood, Ben Frieman.
Track record
  • Wasser: Ely Gold Royalties sold to Gold Royalty Corp, Jun 2021, C$1.46/sh, ~42% premium, C$84M cash cap + up to 41.5M GRC shares - a win for Ely holderssource
  • Wasser: Dryden Gold assembled ~400 km2 pre-IPO (2022-23), optioned the Manitou/Alamos ground Apr 2022 and completed 100% in Mar 2025 by paying the last C$1M in 8.57M shares at C$0.1167, making Alamos the largest holdersource
  • Dryden raised C$3.38M from Centerra at C$0.23 (Dec 2024), C$1.85M at C$0.425 (Jan 2026) and C$9.6M at C$0.41-0.452 (May 2026) with Centerra and Alamos following - financing executed at rising prices until the 2026 slidesource
  • Kolb: Treasury Metals (Goliath, Ontario) exploration director and Red Lake mine geology - relevant Archean high-grade experience; no prior resource authored as a public-company president foundsource
  • Field delivery: second rig promised for early July 2026 and mobilised in July; Mud Lake permit and first holes delivered within the season; deeper Gold Rock holes promised 'this summer' (May) reported 31 Augsource

Boards today: Wasser: Dryden CEO and director; no other public executive role found (Gold Royalty board seat from 2021 - current status unverified). Kelly: CFO and director. Board is four people, two of them executives - thin independence for a company spending C$10M+ a year.

Fit to this job
Stage: pre-resource district explorer - fits Wasser's background as a consolidator/dealmaker (royalties, land) and Kolb's as a structural geologist in Archean gold camps. Deposit: shear-hosted high-grade Ontario gold - Kolb's Red Lake and Treasury years fit exactly. Region: NW Ontario - yes, team is local. New for them: neither has taken an exploration project through a maiden resource or a sale as the operator; the stated plan (sell to a major) is what Wasser knows how to do, but it needs ounces first.
Skin & pay
3/5 — CEO ~2% mostly founder stock plus C$712k of deferred fees left in the company; no selling found; no open-market buying found either. Wasser ~4.9M sh (~2%, ~C$1.15M at C$0.235), Kelly ~1.55M, Jessup 580,000, Kolb 200,000, Hicken 50,000; company says management and insiders 4.82% (31 Aug 2026). No open-market buys or sells found (Simply Wall St shows insufficient data; SEDI not checked). Key-management pay H1 2026 C$499k incl. C$118k share-based (annualised ~C$1.0M, ~1.7% of market cap) - modest; the CEO has deferred C$712,500 of his fees to Jan 2028, which is cash left in the company. Insiders may have taken CFT shares in May 2026 (release flagged MI 61-101) - amounts not disclosed.

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Four-person board with the CEO and CFO as half of it; only 16.75% of shares voted at the 2026 AGM.
  • Heavy promotion for the size: Bunt Capital C$15-16.5k a month plus options, Epstein Research, Streetwise and Market One sponsorships, Rocks & Stocks sponsored content - the register is strong but so is the marketing budget.
  • Three disclosure corrections in 2026 (finders' fee, claim count, marketing fee) - sloppy rather than dishonest.
  • Headline wording stretches: 'true depth of 330 metres' in a headline while the body says true widths are unknown; 'two new discoveries' for single-hole 0.75 g/t and 0.36 g/t intercepts (Jul 2026).
  • 6% finders' fees on parts of the May 2026 raise.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash was C$14.6M at 30 June 2026 after the C$9.6M (gross) May 2026 placements with Centerra and Alamos, and C$11.9M at 31 August per the October deck; the discrete Q2 burn was C$3.5M but the two-rig summer program runs at well over C$2M a month, and with C$11.0M of the C$17.5M 2026 budget spent by late September the company should enter 2027 with roughly C$6–8M, so another raise in H1 2027 looks likely.
  2. Exploration is expensed, which makes the overhead split visible: in H1 2026 C$4.1M went into the ground against C$2.3M of G&A (overhead about 35% of cash spend), and investor relations alone was C$1.6M, up from C$0.6M a year earlier and now the largest overhead line (Bunt Capital at C$16.5k a month plus other marketing contracts).
  3. The share count has tripled: 82.8M at December 2023, 149.5M at December 2024, 213.1M at December 2025 and 246.4M at 31 August 2026; roughly C$40M net has been raised since the December 2023 RTO (FY23 6.5, FY24 8.3, FY25 13.9 incl. C$6.1M of warrant exercises, H1 2026 11.5), the bulk of it flow-through at a premium.
  4. Reported losses are flattered by non-cash flow-through premium recoveries (C$1.9M in FY25, C$0.9M in H1 2026); the FT premium liability was C$1.9M at 30 June 2026 and every annual audit carries a going-concern paragraph. C$0.7M of deferred compensation to a related party has been accrued but not paid.
  5. No debt or streams: only C$0.4M of office leases (an unusual C$0.39M lease payment in Q4 2025 as the ROU asset was rebuilt). Property growth was paid mostly in shares (Manitou 8.6M shares + C$1.05M cash in Q1 2025; Tremblay; Lost Lake option Aug 2026), and of the 14.15M warrants at C$0.18 expiring 2 Oct 2026, 10.57M were exercised for C$1.90M gross (14 Oct 2026 release); the rest lapsed, leaving no warrants and ~251.2M shares.

Thesis

Solstice has consolidated 57 km² of the Temagami greenstone belt (southern Abitibi) around two things: its own 2025–26 Red Cedar hits (8.52 g/t over 3.5 m; 59.4 g/t over 0.5 m with visible gold) and, since 15 Sep 2026, the Leckie Gold Zone — a 160 m shaft on five levels with >23,000 m of historic drilling where 62% of 133 assayed holes carry ≥3 g/t over ≥1.5 m, mostly within 250 m of surface. The bet is that relogging the old core and a Q4 2026 drill program turn Leckie into a maiden resource of a few hundred thousand ounces fast and cheaply, with Red Cedar and 50 IP targets as the growth story. Michael Gentile (~13.5%) and the board (~30%) own it; the market cap is US$23M.

The Gate

Turning a historic underground vein zone and narrow drill hits into continuous ounces — with almost no cash. The width comes from the historic Leckie data (4.85 g/t over 17.1 m, 7.24 g/t over 10.45 m) which no QP has verified and which the company itself says needs confirmation drilling. The Q4 2026 program has no stated metres or budget, cash was C$0.83M at 31 Mar 2026 and the C$0.65M September placement went to the C$0.6M Leckie cash payment, so the next drill program is not funded. A raise, probably at or near C$0.10–0.12, comes first.

Valuation Anchor

US$23M buys a brownfield vein zone with an old shaft and a big historic database, narrow but high-grade own hits, 57 km² of Abitibi-belt ground and a tight register — but no ounces and no cash. It is a cheaper, earlier and worse-funded version of Dryden Gold (US$41M, no resource, two majors on the register) and well below Emperor (US$59M, 1.46 Moz Inferred). If Leckie yields a 0.3–0.6 Moz maiden resource, Ontario resource-stage peers at ~US$40–80/oz imply US$15–50M — i.e. the current price already assumes a resource of that size.

Shareholder structure

Insiders and board ~30%: Michael Gentile ~13.5% (35.8M via Integritas Financial Consulting + 1.5M direct; 16.76% in Jan 2025 after open-market buying at ~C$0.011; diluted since), director Blair Schultz ~9.9% (27.3M), chairman David Adamson ~5.5% (15.1M), CFO Mark Laycock 0.25%, CEO Pablo McDonald 0.18% (0.5M). Institutions ~0.3% (Timelo). Board collectively held 38.8% in Jan 2025 per the company. Insiders took C$96k of the Mar 2025 raise, ~C$117k of the Oct 2025 raise, some of the Mar 2026 warrant exercises and C$53k of the Sep 2026 placement. No insider selling found (Simply Wall St: net buying ~C$294k over 12 months).

Read: A Gentile-controlled register with a chairman who owns 5.5% and a CEO who owns almost nothing; the backers keep writing small cheques, no one is selling, and no major or fund is present.

Jurisdiction risk

National: Canada/Ontario — top-tier, Mining Act permits and ESA in place; the company calls Strathy 'fully permitted' for exploration and holds stripping-plan approval at Red Cedar (stripping permits were 'in progress' in Jun 2026). Local: Temagami, ~1 km from the Trans-Canada Highway, with a historic shaft and road access; winter/ice access needed for some Leckie down-dip targets. The Temagami area is the traditional territory (n'Daki Menan) of the Temagami First Nation / Teme-Augama Anishnabai, whose land claim history is long (the 1973 land caution held up development for two decades); consultation is a standard duty here, not an exotic risk. No community opposition reported by the company.

Ontario at its most ordinary: the jurisdiction will not be the gate; the rocks and the treasury will.

Differentiator

A historic underground gold zone bought for C$0.6M cash plus 2M shares, next to its own visible-gold hits. Leckie gives Solstice >23,000 m of drilling and a shaft it did not pay to drill, which is why a maiden resource could come quickly; Gentile's ~13.5% stake, bought on the market at a cent, gives it a patient anchor shareholder. Against that it is the smallest, least-funded company in this group.

Edge is cheapness and data, not size or money.

Exploration upside

Brownfield vein zone + 50 IP targets · moves the needle: high (from a US$23M base) The near-term upside is confirming the historic Leckie widths and grades with modern holes and extending them along the Leckie Fault toward the 'Leckie-type' polymetallic hit 600 m east; the 43 new claims cover the undrilled fault intersection and ~10 km of the Link Lake deformation zone. Red Cedar's visible-gold veins are high grade but sub-metre so far and need stripping and channel sampling to show continuity. From a US$23M cap a single 10 m+ intercept at 5 g/t in Solstice's own hole would re-rate the stock; the data integration and 3D model (Oct 2026) is the step that ranks the targets.

Next Catalyst

Audited FY2026 (June) accounts by late Oct 2026 showing the cash position; a financing and the C$0.10 warrant expiry (30 Oct 2026); then the Q4 2026 drill program at Leckie/Red Cedar with first assays likely Q1 2027.

Open Questions
  • How many metres and what budget is the Q4 2026 program, and is it funded — or does drilling slip to Q1 2027 behind a raise?
  • Do modern holes reproduce the historic Leckie widths (10–17 m at 5–7 g/t) or only the sub-metre veins Solstice has hit so far?
  • Will the company publish a maiden Leckie resource in 2027, and how much of the historic core can be used after relogging and re-assay?
  • What happened to the 2025 check-assay discrepancies (up to 331% on six high-sulphide samples) — resolved or still open?
  • Does Gentile keep buying at C$0.10+ or was his conviction a one-cent trade?

Track record
  • Adamson: founded Rubicon Minerals (1996) and led it through the Phoenix (F2) discovery in Red Lake; co-recipient of the discovery award. He stepped down as CEO at end-2012 and was non-executive chairman 2013–14; the 3.3 Moz 2013 PEA resource built on that drilling was cut ~88% in 2016 after a US$700M build under later management, and the company restructured before Battle North was sold to Evolution for C$343M in 2021 — a discovery win whose later resource failed after he left (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_North_Gold; https://www.newswire.ca/news-releases/mike-lalonde-to-transition-to-president-and-ceo-effective-january-1-2013-511346271.html)
  • Adamson: CEO of NewCastle Gold to Jul 2016; NewCastle merged into Equinox Gold in 2017 — neutralsource
  • Solstice under Adamson's chairmanship (since 2017): listed with the Nunavut Qaiqtuq/KGP project, drifted to a ~C$3M market cap by Jan 2025 — a long loss carried alongside shareholders (he holds 5.5% and has bought in placements), then pivoted to Strathy in 2024source
  • McDonald/Adamson: two drill programs in 2025–26 (3,120 m and 3,087 m) delivered on the guided size and reported within ~3.5 months; Red Cedar discovery Aug 2025; Leckie acquisition negotiated and closed Aug–Sep 2026 for C$0.6M + 2M shares (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250813744249/en; https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/press-releases/2026/09/15/)
  • Financing record: C$1.15M (Mar 2025, C$0.035–0.049), C$1.12M (Oct 2025), C$0.45M warrants (Mar 2026), C$0.65M (Sep 2026, C$0.06) — small raises at rising prices, insiders in every one (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20250401429815/en/; https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/press-releases/2026/09/08/)

Boards today: Adamson: Solstice chair only (per MarketScreener). Gentile: five other junior boards plus an advisory role — Solstice competes with his other names for his attention and capital. McDonald: Solstice only.

Fit to this job
Stage: pre-resource explorer with a brownfield vein zone — fits Adamson's Red Lake discovery background and McDonald's exploration-management career. Deposit: Archean orogenic vein gold in Ontario — exactly Adamson's field. Region: Ontario — yes. New for them: McDonald has never run a public company or taken a project to a resource; neither has built a mine, which is not needed yet. The skill the company most needs now — raising C$3–5M on a micro-cap — rests on Gentile's network.
Skin & pay
4/5 — large stake across the board (~30%), the largest holder bought at market and insiders join every raise; held back from 5 because the CEO owns almost nothing and Adamson's block is mostly founder paper. Gentile ~13.5% (open-market buyer at ~C$0.011 in Jan 2025, plus placements); Schultz 9.9%; Adamson 5.5% (15.1M shares, partly founder stock, has taken placement shares); CEO 0.18% (0.5M shares, options at C$0.05–0.10); CFO 0.25%. Insiders bought C$96k (Mar 2025), ~C$117k (Oct 2025), part of the Mar 2026 warrant exercises and C$53k (Sep 2026); no sales found. Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Treasury run to near zero repeatedly (US$127k cash at 30 Sep 2025, negative equity that quarter; C$0.83M at 31 Mar 2026) with a going-concern note; drill programs are announced before they are funded.
  • Executive and director compensation of C$552k for nine months (C$270k share-based) against a company that had under C$1M of cash and a C$3–25M market cap over that period; CEO salary C$200k while the cap was ~C$3M in early 2025.
  • Eight years under the same chairman with ~95%+ shareholder loss before the 2025 pivot; the 'discovery' credential (Rubicon/Phoenix) is also the deposit whose resource later collapsed, although after his tenure.
  • Disclosure hygiene: the Jun 2026 release's table (3.09 g/t) and footnote (3.64 g/t) disagree on the same intercept; the 2025 hole count in text (13) does not match the table (15); check-assay discrepancies left open.
  • The headline Leckie widths are historic and unverified; the company's own holes have never cut more than 3.8 m.

  1. Cash was C$833,734 at 31 March 2026 (filed Q3 FY26 interims; the vendor feed's 597K for the same date is in US$, not C$) against a quarterly operating outflow of about C$0.3M — roughly eight months of runway at that date; the February–June 2026 Strathy drill program ran through the June quarter, so cash at 30 June 2026 (FY26 year end, statements due 28 Oct 2026) was probably well under C$0.5M, and the C$650K raised in September 2026 was explicitly earmarked for the C$600K Leckie cash payment, leaving the Q4 2026 Leckie drill campaign unfunded without another placement.
  2. The company lives hand to mouth: cash has swung between C$0.1M (Dec 2024, Sep 2025) and C$0.8M (Mar 2025) around small placements — C$1.15M at C$0.035–0.049 in Mar 2025, C$1.12M at C$0.06–0.085 in Oct 2025, C$0.45M of C$0.05 warrant exercises in Mar 2026 and C$0.65M at C$0.06 in Sep 2026 — roughly C$3.4M gross raised in 18 months, all of it spent as it arrived; total equity was negative (−C$8K) at 30 Sep 2025 and C$0.4M at 31 Mar 2026.
  3. Overhead takes a large share of a very small budget: the three top officers' pay alone (CEO C$200K, Executive Chairman C$90K, CFO C$86K in FY25) is about C$0.38M a year, against total operating expenses of roughly C$0.9M in FY25 and C$1.2M in the nine months to March 2026 — overhead is around 40% of spend, and exploration ('ground') is only meaningful in the two drilling quarters (Apr–Jun 2025, Jan–Mar 2026).
  4. Share count growth: roughly 209M in mid-2024, about 237M after the March 2025 placement, 253.1M at November 2025, 262.4M at 31 March / 1 July 2026 and about 275.2M after the September 2026 placement (10.8M) and Leckie shares (2.0M) — up about a third in two years at prices of 3.5–8.5 cents, with 13.4M options and 5.7M C$0.10 warrants (expiring 31 Oct 2026; in the money at the C$0.12 October 2026 price) outstanding.
  5. Everything is expensed — total assets equal current assets, there are no capitalised mineral properties despite the Strathy option (final C$35K payment accelerated in Aug 2026), the C$40K patented-claim purchase (Mar 2026) and the C$600K Leckie purchase (Sep 2026); the only liability of note is a C$43K long-term item (likely a lease or small loan, nature unverified) and payables that jumped to C$0.26M at March 2026. Insiders (directors and officers hold ~40%, Michael Gentile 16.8% in Jan 2025) take 10–17% of each placement; related-party pay and FT-premium accounting make the quarterly loss figures lumpy (Mar 2025 quarter loss only C$43K).

Gate Getting a drill rig turning — and a first hole that justifies a second raise The company has told the market Pinnacles was 'fully permitted and ready for immediate drilling' since Sep 2024 (under Great Pacific) and again at listing in Apr 2026, and its Sep 2026 deck carries two drill dates (Q2 2026 and H2 2026); as of 18 Sep 2026 it is still 'moving from evaluation to field work planning' and had spent C$35k on exploration in the half-year to 31 Jul. Thesis

A ~US$18M shell with ~C$5.9M cash sitting on most of the Walhalla–Woods Point goldfield, 150 km east of Melbourne, where Cohens Reef produced ~1.48 Moz at ~32 g/t from a single shoot mined to 1,120 m and the rest of the belt has almost no modern drilling (73 historic holes near Cohens, ~5 across the other ~520 km² when Fosterville South staked it in 2020). The case is a Fosterville-style re-look at an old high-grade field by people who were at Fosterville (VP Exploration Owen Greenberger) and Sunday Creek (director Lisa Gibbons). The first test is a permitted greenfield target, Pinnacles (400 m × 1,100 m gold-in-soil over an aplitic dyke; channels 81.6 m @ 1.02 g/t and 18 m @ 3.28 g/t), followed by repeat structures around Cohens Reef.

The Gate

Getting a drill rig turning — and a first hole that justifies a second raise The company has told the market Pinnacles was 'fully permitted and ready for immediate drilling' since Sep 2024 (under Great Pacific) and again at listing in Apr 2026, and its Sep 2026 deck carries two drill dates (Q2 2026 and H2 2026); as of 18 Sep 2026 it is still 'moving from evaluation to field work planning' and had spent C$35k on exploration in the half-year to 31 Jul. The gate is a maiden program that returns a drill intercept the market will pay for, before the ~C$5.9M treasury is eaten by overhead. Behind that sits the geological question: Cohens Reef was one rich shoot on one shear; nobody has shown there is a second one, and the dyke-hosted targets are a different, lower-grade style.

Historic production ~1.51 Moz @ 33.6 g/t across the licences (GeoVic 2020), ~1.48 Moz of it from Cohens Reef.No mineral resource; the Oct 2025 NI 43-101 technical report states none. Cohens Reef (Walhalla EL7297): ~1,479,851 oz from 1.43 Mt at 32.2 g/t Au, a laminated quartz-carbonate reef in the ~50 m-wide Cohens shear, ~1,500 m strike, mined to ~1,120 m; historic drilling at depth includes 4.25 m @ 11.15 g/t Au from 258.4 m, and a 2007 Goldstar campaign returned best results of 5–12 g/t. Longfellows Reef, 1 km west, has 1.5 km of old workings and grab samples quoted as '200 m at 4.95 g/t' and '75 m at 4.1 g/t' (the release does not say how these lengths were derived). Pinnacles (EL7307): greenfield, a 400 m × 1,100 m gold-in-soil anomaly (soils to 1,140 ppb) over an aplitic dyke with disseminated sulphides at surface; channel sampling 81.6 m @ 1.02 g/t Au and 18.0 m @ 3.28 g/t Au; rock chips to 26.3 g/t; permitted for drilling. Land: ~1,230 km² across nine exploration licences (Kevington EL8538, Enoch's Point EL7219, Loch Flyne EL6363, Harbinger EL7215, Woods Point EL6321, Pinnacles EL7307, Walhalla North EL7289, Walhalla EL7297, Cooper's Creek EL7300) — down from the '1,400 km²' quoted in 2024–25; the MD&A itself gives two different licence counts. Modern drilling across the belt is almost nil: 73 mostly shallow holes near Cohens Reef (3 deeper than 200 m, deepest 537 m) and ~5 holes elsewhere as of 2020.

Valuation Anchor

At ~US$13.5M EV the market is paying for an option on a first drill program, not for ounces. Peers: Victorian explorers with a discovery hole (Southern Cross Gold/Sunday Creek, Great Pacific's own Lauriston 8 m @ 105 g/t) re-rated to US$100M+ on a few holes; pre-drill Victorian ground with historic high-grade production typically trades US$10–30M. Walhalla sits at the bottom of that band, below its C$0.20 financing price, which is the fair reading of six months with no rig.

Shareholder structure

Individual insiders ~0.78% (1.66M shares: CFO Shorter 650k, Carew 511k, Moore 500k; Simply Wall St, Sep 2026) — all four named officers/directors together own less than 1%. Franklin Templeton ~2.5% (5.32M), IG Investment ~0.1%; the rest is the Great Pacific shareholder base (152.3M shares distributed) plus the C$0.20 placement holders. Insiders hold 10.0M options and 6.0M RSUs (7.5% of the company) against 0.8% in stock. No strategic holder. No SEDI filings found showing open-market buys since listing.

Read: Nobody at the top has meaningful stock; the exposure is through options and RSUs granted at and after listing.

Jurisdiction risk

National: Australia — stable, royalty 2.75% of net market value in Victoria (state), plus the 2% GPAC NSR. Local: Victoria is slow but improving — Resources Victoria's FY2025-26 report shows median exploration-licence grant time 231 days (from 405), initial work plans median 50 days, but 76 exploration applications still pending and competing-application cases averaging 777 days. Drilling on an EL needs either a low-impact exploration notice under the Code of Practice or an approved work plan, landholder consent or compensation agreement, Crown-land consents (much of the Walhalla ground is state forest/Crown land) and a rehabilitation bond. Walhalla township is a heritage-tourism village and the Thomson catchment supplies Melbourne's water, so any Cohens Reef work near town will draw community and water-catchment scrutiny; Pinnacles is the company's permitted entry point. Victoria does have a path through: Fosterville, Sunday Creek's exploration-decline permitting (which new director Gibbons ran) and Costerfield.

Permitting is a timeline risk, not a wall; Pinnacles is permitted, Cohens Reef near town is the harder ask.

Differentiator

The ground, not the company: this is most of a 2 Moz-class, +25 g/t historic goldfield in one set of hands, with almost no modern drilling and a permitted target. The team additions in Sep 2026 (Greenberger from Fosterville's Lower Phoenix/Swan team, Gibbons from Sunday Creek) are the right kind of Victorian people. Against that, the corporate parent treated it as a non-core asset for five years and spent almost nothing on it.

Great ground that two owners in a row have not drilled — the question is why.

Exploration upside

District-scale, almost undrilled · moves the needle: high (if a rig ever turns) ~1,230 km² with 420+ historic workings and 54 producing mines; nine licences; Pinnacles permitted and the only target with a modern surface dataset. Cohens Reef splays and repeat structures along the shear are the high-grade idea; dyke-hosted targets along the Woods Point corridor (Morning Star-style) are the bulk-tonnage idea. Any decent intercept from a US$18M base would be a large move; the risk is that the first holes test a 1 g/t dyke rather than a reef.

Next Catalyst

A dated maiden drill program (Pinnacles, then Cohens Reef repeats) — the company said 'near term' on 18 Sep 2026 after RSC's data review; first assays would then be the first real catalyst, plausibly H1 2027.

Open Questions
  • Why has nobody drilled Pinnacles in the two years it has been 'ready for immediate drilling' — budget, access, or a weaker target than the slides suggest?
  • How much of the C$5.9M goes into the ground in FY2027 versus consultants and listing costs, and how many metres does phase 1 actually contain?
  • Is there any modern structural evidence for a second Cohens-type shoot, or is the 'repeat structures' idea entirely conceptual?
  • What are the Morning Star/Woods Point licence terms and expenditure commitments across nine ELs, and are any up for renewal or partial relinquishment in 2027?
