Management review
Creal weaknesses: slipped dates, thin fit or thin candourTrack record 2/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 2/5 · Skin in the game 1/5

A Vancouver spin-out shell whose first CEO lasted three months, with a drill-ready target it has promised for two years and not drilled, insiders under 1%, and inconsistent disclosure. The Sep 2026 Victorian hires (Greenberger, Gibbons) are genuinely good and keep this from a D; a dated program and a rig would move it to B.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Steve Jukes (CEO & Director, since Jul 2026): Mechanical engineer; founded mining advisory JukesTodd (advised Newmont, Gold Fields, Rio Tinto, SSR), then Global Head of Mining & Minerals at Turner & Townsend after it bought JukesTodd. Project experience is study/build-side (Winu, Gibraltar, Moose River, Cerro Verde, Çöpler, Sepon). Non-exec director Dover Castle Metals; AMEC board. First time running a listed grassroots explorer. Paid through Oakmont Minerals Pty Ltd (C$11,366 in the ~10 days of Q2). · Samantha Shorter, CPA (CFO & Director, since listing, Apr 2026): Principal at Red Fern Consulting (13 yrs), ex-Davidson & Co; outsourced CFO for several Vancouver juniors. Red Fern billed C$70,000 in the half-year. Holds 650k shares (0.31%). · Owen Greenberger (VP Exploration, since Sep 2026): ~20 yrs Australian exploration; ~8 yrs at Fosterville on the Lower Phoenix/Swan/Eagle discovery team; Geology & Exploration Manager at Kirkland Lake Gold (Victoria, 1,600 km², >$30M budgets); Morning Star mine. The one person with the exact deposit-and-district background. · Mick (Michael) Carew, PhD (Director, Strategic Advisor (CEO Apr–Jul 2026), since incorporation 2025): Geologist; ex-VP Corp Dev Great Pacific Gold (the parent), ex-CEO Gama Explorations (Oct 2022–Aug 2023, lithium pivot, left after ~10 months) and Midex Resources; ex-Haywood mining analyst; director of K92 Mining since Jan 2024. Carew Management Consultancy billed C$40,000 in the half-year. Holds 511k shares (0.24%). · Lisa Gibbons (Director, since Sep 2026): Geologist, 35+ yrs; ex-Normandy (Oberon, Hyperion, Groundrush, McPhillamys); GM then Head of Community & External Affairs at Southern Cross Gold (Sunday Creek permitting incl. exploration decline); chairs MCA Victoria exploration working group. · Michael Moore, P.Geo (Director & QP (not independent), since listing): 35+ yrs exploration, BC-registered; signs the technical disclosure. Director fees C$7,500/half-year. Holds 500k shares. · Harp Gosal (Director of Capital Markets & Communications, since 2026): IR; ex-NexGen Energy, Founders Metals. · Jamie Burns (Director (deceased Aug 2026), since listing): Death announced 12 Aug 2026; 500k RSUs vested on death.
Track record
  • Jukes: career in advisory and project delivery for majors; no record found of leading an exploration company to a discovery or a salesource
  • Carew: Gama Explorations CEO Oct 2022 – Aug 2023; acquired Muskox lithium and raised C$5.4M, then stepped down to advisor and left the board with no reason givensource
  • Carew: as VP Corp Dev at Great Pacific Gold the Walhalla ground sat undrilled 2020–2025 while GPAC drilled Lauriston and PNG; GPAC then spun it out for C$1.5M cash plus a 2% NSRsource
  • Greenberger: part of the Fosterville Lower Phoenix/Swan discovery team (company statement; individual contribution not verifiable)source
  • Gibbons: ran Sunday Creek's Victorian exploration and decline permitting at Southern Cross Gold — a direct, recent Victorian permitting winsource
  • Company: listed 29 Apr 2026 with C$7.0M at C$0.20; shares C$0.12 on 9 Oct 2026; exploration spend C$35k in the six months to 31 Jul 2026 against C$498k cash operating outflowsource

Boards today: Jukes: Walhalla CEO + Dover Castle Metals NED + AMEC board. Carew: Walhalla director + K92 Mining director + consulting to other juniors. Shorter: outsourced CFO (Red Fern) with other client companies. Moore: director/QP. Gibbons and Greenberger newly joined. The CEO, CFO and lead geologist are all part-time or newly arrived; the operating bench is the Sep 2026 hires.

Fit to this job
Stage: grassroots-to-first-drill explorer — the CEO's background is studies and construction for majors, which is the wrong end of the lifecycle; the fit comes from Greenberger (exact: Victorian orogenic gold, Fosterville, Morning Star) and Gibbons (exact: Victorian permitting and community). Deposit type: high-grade reef/dyke orogenic gold — Greenberger yes, others no. Region: Victoria — Greenberger, Gibbons yes; Vancouver corporate side no. New for them: running a Victorian field program on a C$6M budget from Vancouver.
Skin & pay
1/5 — under 1% in stock, options and RSUs only, no open-market buying found; large share-based pay against a tiny cap. Insiders ~0.78% (1.66M shares; Shorter 650k, Carew 511k, Moore 500k — Simply Wall St, Sep 2026); Jukes' holding not disclosed. No open-market buys found since listing. Exposure is via 10.0M options at C$0.20 and 6.0M RSUs. Cash pay is modest in absolute terms (~C$120k of related-party fees in the half-year), but share-based pay of C$1.52M in six months is ~6% of today's market cap. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/cse-wau/walhalla-gold-shares/ownership and the Jul 2026 MD&A.

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Insiders own ~0.78% in stock but hold 16.0M options/RSUs (7.5% of the company) granted within four months of listing; share-based compensation C$1.52M in the half-year against C$35k of exploration.
  • Historic production is quoted three different ways across company documents (1.51 Moz @ 33.6 g/t; 1.68 Moz @ 37.9 g/t; 2.2–2.3 Moz @ 25.3 g/t) and the land is quoted as 1,400 km² then 1,230 km²; the MD&A gives two different licence counts; the website team page still shows four lorem-ipsum placeholder entries.
  • CEO change three months after listing; the listing CEO (Carew) was VP Corp Dev of the parent that never drilled the ground.
  • All executive pay flows through related-party consultancies (Carew Management, Oakmont Minerals, Red Fern) — normal for a Vancouver shell, but the company has no employees on the ground in Victoria beyond the Sep 2026 hires.
  • Director/QP Michael Moore is not independent and signs all technical disclosure; no independent technical review since the Oct 2025 43-101 report.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash went from C$0 (a C$1 shell) at 31 Jan 2026 to C$6.75M at 30 Apr 2026 after the FinCo amalgamation brought in C$5.30M of cash plus a C$1.49M placement at C$0.20, then fell to C$5.91M at 31 Jul 2026 after repaying the A$340k promissory note to Great Pacific (C$0.34M) and C$0.5M of operating outflow; at the Q2 cash burn of ~C$0.5M per quarter the treasury covers roughly three years, but the planned 7,500 m phase-2 drill program has not started and will change that.
  2. Almost nothing has gone into the ground yet: C$35k of exploration was expensed in the six months to 31 Jul 2026 against C$0.46M of cash overhead (consulting, professional, management, listing fees), so overhead is ~93% of spending; the C$1.5M purchase of the project from Great Pacific was settled by FinCo and never touched the company's cash.
  3. The reported H1 FY27 loss of C$2.0M is three-quarters non-cash: 10M options at C$0.20 vested in full on listing (C$1.51M expense) plus the start of a 6M RSU grant (C$0.48M fair value, C$11k expensed so far).
  4. Shares outstanding went from 152.3M at the spin-out to 212.5M after the amalgamation (52.6M FinCo shares, 7.4M placement, 0.14M finder's shares) and have not moved since; there are no warrants, 10M options and 6M RSUs. 118.3M shares were escrowed at listing and are released in tranches, the last 29.6M on 13 Dec 2026.
  5. Related parties took C$0.13M of fees plus C$0.40M of share-based pay in H1 FY27; the founding CEO (Carew) was replaced by Steven Jukes in July 2026, a VP Exploration and a new director were added in September 2026, and Great Pacific keeps a 2% NSR on the project.

How to read a card. The bucket colour on the left is the archetype. The gate is the single thing that has to go right; the differentiator is what the company has that peers don't. When those two are the same fact seen from two sides, that's usually the most honest thing to know about the name.

Reminder on cross-company comparisons: NPV/capex figures sit on each project's own metal-price deck and discount rate, and AuEq/AgEq use different price assumptions per company — read the anchors as shapes, not decimal-precise rankings. Market caps for CSE/TSXV names move 10–30% on single releases; verify live before anchoring. This is research shorthand, not investment advice.
